## Explained the tunnel dead-reckoning trick; bigger badge, smaller car, marker hidden before the first fix (this session)

Christer re-ran bv-export after the self-healing duration change and reported a long, silent delay before "trip already exists" appeared - confirmed this was exactly the one-time full-archive ffprobe pass `load_or_compute_duration()` now does during trip detection (`front_recordings` covers the *whole* archive, not just the requested trip, since `TripBuilder.build()` calls `recording_duration` on essentially every recording while walking gaps). Flagged that this scan is currently silent and offered either a progress indicator or narrowing the self-heal to just the requested range - Christer didn't pick either yet, so both remain open follow-ups, not implemented this session.

Separately, watching a real map.mp4 render, Christer had three requests and one question:

1. The satellite badge (11px radius) is too small/hard to read - "even 100% bigger."
2. The default red-car marker (a bundled 128x128 PNG, rendered at native resolution - the only sizing it ever had) is too big - "make it half that size."
3. The marker correctly clamps to the first known fix during a leading GPS gap, but shouldn't be visible at all until real coordinates exist for the first time.
4. Why does the camera pan through a tunnel with no GPS signal - is bv-export guessing?

Answered (4) directly before touching code: yes, it's a guess - `interpolate_position()` draws a straight line between the last real fix before the gap and the first real fix after it, extrapolating constant speed and course across the whole silent stretch (with circular course interpolation for the 0/360 wraparound, but still just a linear guess, not measured data). This is exactly why the satellite badge exists - to mark that guess as a guess even though it renders identically to a live position otherwise.

Confirmed three decisions before implementing 1-3 via AskUserQuestion: badge 100% bigger (not 50%); the marker's 0.5x scale applies generally to whatever marker image is in play, bundled red car or a custom `--map-icon` alike, not just the bundled asset; and the "hide before first coordinates" behavior covers only the strict leading gap (before the trip's very first real fix) - the marker keeps showing (clamped/interpolated, as before) through a trailing gap or a mid-trip tunnel, since Christer's wording was specifically about *never yet having* a position, not every case the badge already goes dark for.

**Implementation, `map_render.py`.** `GPS_BADGE_RADIUS_PX` doubled from 11 to 22. The satellite glyph inside `_draw_gps_badge()` was originally drawn with fixed pixel offsets (2.5, 3, 3.5, 4, 6) independent of the radius - just doubling the radius would have left the same tiny glyph adrift in a bigger circle, not the "more detail" Christer actually asked for. Reworked every glyph dimension to scale off `GPS_BADGE_RADIUS_PX` relative to the original 11px baseline (`scale = GPS_BADGE_RADIUS_PX / 11.0`), so the glyph itself grows proportionally with the badge and stays self-scaling if the radius ever changes again. `render_frame()` gained a new `show_marker: bool = True` parameter - `if position is not None and show_marker:` now gates the entire marker-drawing block (custom image, arrow, or plain dot alike), independent of `show_gps_badge`, so the two can differ (a trailing/mid-trip gap: badge off, marker still shown) or agree (leading gap: both off).

**Implementation, `map_video.py`.** New `MARKER_IMAGE_SCALE = 0.5` constant, applied once right after `marker_image_path` is loaded (`marker_image.resize(...)`, `Image.LANCZOS`) - once per render, not per frame, since the marker image itself never changes mid-render. Applies uniformly to the bundled red car and any custom `--map-icon`, which also fixes a real, if minor, pre-existing inconsistency: a custom icon used to render at whatever size its own source file happened to be saved at, with nothing normalizing it against the map canvas at all. In the per-frame loop, `before_first_fix = timestamp < positioned[0].timestamp` (a strictly stronger condition than `live_fix`/`show_gps_badge`, which also fires for the *trailing* and mid-trip cases) is computed alongside `live_fix` and passed through as `show_marker=not before_first_fix` on every `render_frame()` call.

**Tests.** `test_map_render.py`: three new tests - `show_marker=False` suppresses a custom marker image, the default (`True`) still shows it, and `show_marker=False` also suppresses the plain-dot fallback (no `marker_image`/`heading`). The existing badge-corner-position test already derives its expected coordinates from `GPS_BADGE_RADIUS_PX` itself, so it needed no changes for the size bump. `test_map_video.py`: four new tests - the marker image is actually resized to half its loaded dimensions before being handed to `render_frame()`; `show_marker` is `False` for the frame before the first real fix and `True` once it's covered; `show_marker` stays `True` throughout a trailing gap; and `show_marker` stays `True` throughout a mid-trip signal-loss gap even though `show_gps_badge` goes `False` for some of the same frames. All 19 tests in `test_map_render.py` (up from 16) and all 46 in `test_map_video.py` (up from 42) pass by hand via the project's harness (one pre-existing, unrelated `monkeypatch`-signature harness limitation in `test_map_render.py`, same as noted in earlier sessions).

**Visual verification.** Rendered a real synthetic 10-fix trip end-to-end with a 5-second leading gap and a bundled red-car marker, pulled frames at t=0s (inside the leading gap) and t=6s (just after the first fix) with real ffmpeg, and looked at both directly: the t=0 frame shows a completely blank map (no car, no badge) despite the position technically being clamped to the first fix underneath; the t=6 frame shows the red car at roughly half its old on-screen footprint with a clearly bigger, more legible satellite glyph in the corner - both exactly as intended.

**Docs.** Updated `--map-icon`'s row and the satellite-badge paragraph in `docs/man/bv-export.md`: noted the marker's 0.5x scale, spelled out the tunnel dead-reckoning behavior in plain terms (straight line, constant speed/course, not measured), and added a new paragraph distinguishing the marker's leading-gap-only hide from the badge's broader off-conditions.

Not yet run through the project's own pytest suite, and not yet confirmed against Christer's real archive - worth him re-rendering a real trip's map.mp4/map_zoom video and checking the badge/car sizing reads well in practice, and that the car really does stay hidden until his own GPS actually locks on at the start of a real trip. The self-healing duration scan's silent-during-a-long-run UX (progress indicator vs. narrowing the scan to the requested range) is still an open question from earlier in this session, unresolved either way.

## Scoped duration self-healing to the trip(s) being exported; added --duration-heal-archive (this session)

Direct follow-up to the open question from the entry above. Christer: "it should ask the overwrite question before selfhealing and only self heal recording[s] to this trip unless a --option to do the whole archive." I flagged the real tension first: trip *detection* needs a recording's real duration to decide where trips split - that's exactly why self-healing exists (it fixed a real mis-split bug earlier this session), so scoping it down necessarily trades away some detection accuracy for recordings nobody's asked to export yet. Christer, after hearing that trade-off, confirmed accepting it: "I get it it's a Catch 22 moment. Just scan the included recordings unless an option --xxx_all is present then scan the whole archive."

**Implementation, `bv_export.py`.** The archive-wide `TripBuilder(...).build()` call - which walks every recording in the archive to decide trip boundaries, regardless of the requested `--timestamp`/`--from`/`--until` range - now uses `read_duration_seconds` (cache-only, no ffprobe) instead of `load_or_compute_duration` for that pass, by default. This is the actual fix for the long silent delay: detection is back to reading whatever's already cached, same speed as before self-healing existed, so the first "trip already exists?" prompt isn't blocked on unrelated archive-wide work anymore.

Once `trips` (the filtered list actually being exported) is known, a small loop at the top of each trip's own turn in the export loop - `for recording in trip: load_or_compute_duration(recording)` - self-heals only that trip's own recordings, right before `folder_name_for_trip()` (which reads `trip.end_timestamp`, hence the last recording's real span) computes its folder name and before its own overwrite prompt. Scoped exactly to "this trip," per Christer's ask; a harmless no-op (all cache hits) on any recording already healed by an earlier pass. `dry_run` skips this entirely, consistent with everything else it doesn't touch.

New `--duration-heal-archive` flag (`duration_heal_archive: bool = False` on `bv_export()`) restores full archive-wide self-healing for a run that wants maximum detection accuracy over a fast first prompt. Implemented as its own explicit pass - `for recording in front_recordings: load_or_compute_duration(recording)` - run once up front, rather than just handing `load_or_compute_duration` to `TripBuilder` the way the original (pre-this-session) implementation did. That distinction mattered: `TripBuilder.build()`'s own gap-walking loop only ever calls `recording_duration` on a recording playing the role of `previous` in a consecutive pair, which means the chronologically *last* recording in the whole archive is never looked up at all (nothing follows it to trigger that lookup) - caught by a test that would otherwise have silently passed with that one recording left unhealed even under the "heal the whole archive" flag. Rejected together with `--no-duration` (`raise SystemExit(...)` at the top of `bv_export()`, mirroring the existing `LexicalTimeParser` error-handling pattern in the same function) - there's nothing to heal against with duration data turned off entirely.

**Tests, `test_bv_export.py`.** Five new tests: a two-trip archive with `--timestamp` scoped to just the first trip confirms only that trip's recordings get a `.duration.txt` written, not the second trip's; the same setup with `duration_heal_archive=True` confirms *both* trips' recordings get healed (this is the test that caught the last-recording gap above); `--no-duration` together with `duration_heal_archive=True` raises `SystemExit`; and two `main()`-level tests confirming `--duration-heal-archive` defaults to `False` and flips to `True` when given. All 91 tests in the file (up from 86) verified passing by hand via the project's harness, in four batches - the same 3 pre-existing, unrelated `--stitch-mirror-size/zoom/pan` default-value failures noted in the previous self-healing entry are still present and still unrelated (confirmed then via `git stash` against the untouched commit; not re-verified this round since nothing touching those tests changed).

**Docs.** `docs/man/bv-export.md`: added `--duration-heal-archive` to the synopsis and the Trip detection options table, reworded `--no-duration`'s row to say it skips reading/computing/writing entirely (not just "ignoring" the file), noted both new-flag-relevant lines are `bv-export`-only (`bv-ls --trips` doesn't heal at all, same as `--max-parking-duration`), and added a paragraph spelling out the new scoped-by-default/heal-whole-archive-if-asked behavior and its accuracy trade-off. `bv_export()`'s own docstring rewritten to match, including the "why an explicit archive-wide pass, not just handing the function to TripBuilder" reasoning. `--no-duration`'s argparse help text updated to point at `--duration-heal-archive`.

Not yet run through the project's own pytest suite, and not yet confirmed against Christer's real archive - worth him re-running `bv-export` on his real archive (already mostly healed from the earlier full-archive pass this session) and confirming the first "trip already exists?" prompt now appears quickly, that a trip's own `.duration.txt` files get written as it's processed, and that `--duration-heal-archive` still does the full archive-wide pass when he wants it.

## rearview_mirror's --stitch-map panel now defaults to a side matching the trip's own geometry (this session)

Christer, watching a rendered rearview_mirror export: "in rearview mirror mode wi put the map under the video. Maybe we should have the approach that if a trip is mainly north-south we put it to the left of the video, whats your thought." I agreed and explained why: `side_by_side`/`top_down` already nest their map panel perpendicular to the camera stack's own shape (a tall stacked column gets the panel on the left, a wide stacked row gets it underneath, so the final frame doesn't turn into a ribbon) - `rearview_mirror` never had an equivalent rule since it's a single full-frame camera, not a stack, so there's no camera shape to counter. Christer's idea gives it one anyway: counter the *map panel's own* natural shape instead - a north-south trip's map renders tall and narrow (fits a left column), an east-west trip's renders wide and short (fits underneath). Confirmed with him before implementing; he said yes.

**Implementation, `stitch.py`.** New `_default_rearview_mirror_map_side(fixes)`, placed right after `pick_stitch_layout()` since it reuses the exact same `bounding_box_for_fixes()`/`aspect_ratio_of()` geometry check (`aspect_ratio_of(bbox) < 1.0` -> north-south -> `"left"`; otherwise, or no GPS data to compute a bbox from at all, -> `"down"`, matching `rearview_mirror`'s old static default as the safe fallback). `_DEFAULT_MAP_SIDE_FOR_LAYOUT` (the static side_by_side/top_down dict) dropped its `"rearview_mirror": "down"` entry entirely, replaced with a comment pointing at the new function - the call site in `_stack()` (where `map_fixes` was already in scope, no new plumbing needed) now special-cases `layout == _MIRROR_LAYOUT` before ever consulting the dict, and an explicit `map_side` still overrides either path exactly as before.

A real surprise while writing the integration test: I'd assumed a sharply north-south trip, now defaulting to `"left"`, would hit `_REARVIEW_MAP_PANEL_MAX_FRACTION`'s 30% cap the same way it used to hit it on the *height* axis for the old `"down"` default - it doesn't. `_map_panel_dimensions()`'s free-axis formula for `"left"`/`"right"` is `comp_height * trip_ratio` (height is the *matched* axis there, not free) - for a sharply north-south trip `trip_ratio` is tiny, so that product comes out far *below* even the general 20% floor (`_MIN_MAP_PANEL_FRACTION`), not above the 30% ceiling. The cap only ever bound on the *height* axis, which is exactly the axis `"left"` placement no longer frees up. First draft of the test asserted the wrong number (192, the 30%-of-width figure) before actually running it and seeing 128 (the 20%-of-width floor) instead - fixed by working through `_map_panel_dimensions()`'s real formula rather than assuming symmetry between the two sides, and rewrote the test's own comment to explain why the floor binds here, not the ceiling.

**Tests.** Three new direct tests for `_default_rearview_mirror_map_side()` (north-south -> left, east-west -> down, no GPS data -> down). One existing integration test (`test_stitch_cameras_rearview_mirror_map_panel_is_capped_at_30_percent`) renamed to `..._defaults_to_left_for_a_north_south_trip` and corrected to the real 20%-floor numbers above (width `640 + 128`, height unchanged at `480`) - its old assertions (`height == 480 + 144`) were exercising the pre-this-session static `"down"` default, which the same fixture no longer reaches. Added a new companion test, `..._honors_an_explicit_side`, using the *same* north-south fixture with an explicit `map_side="down"` to keep the original 30%-height-cap scenario covered under deliberate override rather than losing that coverage entirely. Confirmed no other test file (`test_trip_export.py`, `test_bv_export.py`) combines `rearview_mirror` with `map_mode`/`--stitch-map`, so nothing else needed updating. All 121 tests in `test_stitch.py` (up from 118) verified passing by hand via the project's harness, across nine batches - the same 2 tests already flagged in an earlier session as unable to finish within this sandbox's per-call time budget (`..._scale_shrinks_the_map_panels_own_render_size`, `..._scale_shrinks_the_output_preserving_aspect_ratio`, two full real `map.mp4` renders each) still weren't run, confirmed unrelated by code review (this diff doesn't touch `--stitch-scale` at all). The two existing `side_by_side`/`top_down` map-panel-default tests were re-run and pass unchanged, confirming those two layouts' own behavior is untouched.

**Docs.** `docs/man/bv-export.md`'s `--stitch-map-side` row rewritten to describe `rearview_mirror`'s new geometry-based default separately from `side_by_side`/`top_down`'s unchanged static one.

Not yet run through the project's own pytest suite, and not yet confirmed against Christer's real archive - worth him re-running `bv-export --stitch --stitch-layout rearview_mirror --stitch-map` on a real north-south trip and confirming the map panel now renders on the left rather than underneath, and that an east-west trip (or an explicit `--stitch-map-side`) still behaves as before.

## --include-parking: skip mid-trip Parking footage by default, replace with a transition clip (this session)

Christer's last open item from his stitch-map-side request: "A last option --include-parking, if present then we include parking files as is in the middle of a trip otherwise we skip them with a nice transition or a 3 second video that you or I can create that clearly shows that we skip parking video like a 'No parking' sign or something else."

Before writing any code, asked three scoping questions via `AskUserQuestion` rather than guessing: (1) which Parking recordings the skip applies to - he picked "only ones strictly mid-trip," confirming a Parking recording that opens or closes a trip has nothing to transition from/to on one side and should always stay untouched; (2) who creates the placeholder image - he picked "both, I'll generate one procedurally, and you'll try to create a better one," which settled the design toward an image-based override (like `--map-icon`) rather than a pre-rendered video override, since the placeholder has to be re-encoded per trip's own resolution/frame rate anyway (see below) - a still image sidesteps that entirely, a pre-made video wouldn't; (3) whether the trip's own `audio.aac` should also swap in matching silence for a skipped recording - he confirmed yes, "keeps stitch.mp4's audio in sync."

**Why a placeholder can't just be one bundled file.** `concatenate_media()` (media.py) uses ffmpeg's concat demuxer with `-c copy` - a pure stream copy, no re-encoding - so every source has to already match its neighbours' own codec/resolution/frame rate (video) or codec/sample rate/channel count (audio) exactly. A trip's own front/rear resolution and frame rate (and audio sample rate/channels) vary by camera and archive, so a single shipped placeholder video could never guarantee a match. Solved by rendering the placeholder fresh, per trip, from a still image - `render_parking_transition_video()` (new `parking_transition.py`) probes whichever real recording it's standing in for and encodes a matching clip via `ffmpeg -loop 1 -i <image> -t 3 -r <matched fps>` (reusing `encode_with_nvenc_fallback()`, the same NVENC-then-CPU path `map_video.py`/`gsensor_video.py`/`stitch.py` already use). `render_parking_transition_silence()` does the audio equivalent via `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i anullsrc=...`, matched to sample rate/channel count. `ParkingTransitionCache` memoizes both by their own matched-property key (`(width, height, frame_rate)` / `(codec, sample_rate, channels)`) for the life of one `export_trip()` call, so a trip with several skipped Parking recordings at the same camera resolution only pays for one real render of each, not one per occurrence.

**The default image.** `render_parking_transition_image()` draws a dark frame with a red "prohibited" icon (a plain circle + diagonal slash) and a "PARKING FOOTAGE SKIPPED" caption, in the same red accent (`(230, 57, 70)`) the map badge/marker/route already use elsewhere in this project. First draft put a letter "P" inside the circle - looked right in isolation, but the diagonal slash crossed the P's own stem in a way that read as an "R" instead once actually rendered and viewed (caught by generating and looking at real preview PNGs at both 640x480 and 1920x1080 before wiring anything else up, not assumed from the code). Dropped the letter entirely - the caption text already spells out "parking" in full, so the icon only needs to carry "prohibited," and a plain slashed circle reads unambiguously at any size. `--parking-transition-image PATH` lets Christer supply his own picture instead (fitted/padded, not stretched, to each trip's own resolution via `_fit_and_pad_image()` - same letterboxing approach `stitch.py`'s own map-panel fitting already uses) - deliberately no "none" literal the way `--map-icon`/`--stitch-mirror-icon` have, since there's no procedural-vs-bundled toggle here: the procedural frame already *is* the default, there's nothing to opt out of back to.

**Implementation, `trip_export.py`.** `_concatenate_asset()` gained `include_parking`/`parking_transitions` parameters. Building `sources` now walks `trip.recordings` by index (not a plain comprehension) so it can tell "strictly mid-trip" (`0 < index < last_index`) apart from "opens or closes the trip" per recording; a mid-trip Parking recording with `include_parking=False` gets `_parking_transition_source()`'s placeholder substituted in its exact sequence position instead of its own file - silence for `Asset.AUDIO`, the rendered clip for anything else. If a placeholder can't be produced (a `MediaToolError` probing/encoding it), that recording's contribution to that one asset is dropped entirely rather than falling back to the real Parking footage Christer explicitly asked to have skipped - the same "missing asset contributes nothing" behavior every other gap in this pipeline already has. `export_trip()` only spins up a `ParkingTransitionCache` (backed by a `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()`) when `not include_parking and trip.has_parking_footage` - most trips have no Parking footage at all, so this stays a no-op for them - scoped tightly around just the front/rear/audio `ThreadPoolExecutor` block via `try/finally`, since no later phase (map/gsensor/stitch, subtitle merging) reads from it.

**Implementation, `bv_export.py`.** New `--include-parking` (`store_true`, default `False`) and `--parking-transition-image PATH` flags, forwarded straight through to `export_trip()`. `include_parking=False` is the new default behavior end to end, matching Christer's own framing ("if present then we include... otherwise we skip").

**Real-data verification, not just unit tests.** Before writing the formal test suite, built a real synthetic 3-recording trip (drive / 30-second Parking timelapse / drive) with actual ffmpeg fixtures and ran `export_trip()` against it directly: confirmed `front.mp4` came out exactly 7 seconds (2s + 3s placeholder + 2s), not 34 seconds, and pulled a frame from the middle of the result with ffmpeg to visually confirm it really was the placeholder graphic, not the real Parking footage. Re-ran the same trip with `include_parking=True` and got the full 34 seconds back. Also confirmed a Parking recording that opens or closes the trip is left untouched either way. For audio specifically, hit a real ffmpeg quirk worth recording: `ffprobe`'s quick `format=duration` estimate for a raw AAC elementary stream concatenation came back wrong (`2.2s` for what should have been `~5s`) with an "Estimating duration from bitrate, this may be inaccurate" warning - decoding the file to WAV and re-checking showed the real content was all there (`~5.06s`, packet counts matched exactly). This is a pre-existing characteristic of how this project's `audio.aac` files already work (raw ADTS streams, no container-level timestamps), not a bug introduced here - but it meant the test suite had to check decoded duration, not `ffprobe`'s reported one, for anything touching `audio.aac`.

**Tests.** New `test_parking_transition.py` (14 tests) covers the image/video/silence renderers directly (correct dimensions/frame rate/sample rate/channels, a non-blank rendered frame, graceful `None` from `probe_audio_properties()` on an unreadable file) and `ParkingTransitionCache`'s memoization (same properties reuse the same file; different properties render separately; a bad audio source degrades to `None` rather than raising). `test_trip_export.py` gained 6 tests: the mid-trip swap itself (front.mp4 duration reflects the 3s placeholder, not the real 6s Parking clip), `include_parking=True` preserving the original behavior, a Parking recording at the trip's start or end staying untouched in each direction, the audio-silence swap (verified via decode, per the ffprobe quirk above), and the `--parking-transition-image` override actually being used. `test_bv_export.py` gained 3 tests for the new flags' CLI wiring (`include_parking` defaults `False`, flips `True` when given, `parking_transition_image` forwarded verbatim). All 14 new `test_parking_transition.py` tests, all 62 tests in `test_trip_export.py` (up from 56, 4 pre-existing `capsys`-harness skips unrelated to this change), and all 94 tests in `test_bv_export.py` (up from 91) verified passing by hand via the project's harness - the same 3 pre-existing, unrelated `--stitch-mirror-size/zoom/pan` default-value failures noted in earlier sessions are still present and still unrelated (re-confirmed via `git stash` this session, not just assumed from precedent).

**Docs.** `docs/man/bv-export.md`: new "Parking footage" options subsection (between "Trip detection" and "Map") explaining `--include-parking`/`--parking-transition-image` and the per-trip re-render/caching mechanism, synopsis line updated, and the `front.mp4`/`rear.mp4` row in the OUTPUT table noted the default skip behavior.

Not yet run through the project's own pytest suite, and not yet confirmed against Christer's real archive - worth him re-running `bv-export` on a real trip that includes mid-trip Parking footage and confirming the transition clip reads clearly, the rest of the trip's audio stays in sync afterward, and (if he follows through on making his own placeholder) that `--parking-transition-image` picks it up correctly.

## Add --parking-transition-clip: a real video, not just a still image, for the parking placeholder (this session)

Direct follow-up to the entry above. Christer uploaded six of his own "No Parking" clips (`No_Parking.mp4` through `No_Parking6.mp4`) and asked "Maybe they should be without sound. Please show me yours." Probed all six first: 1920x1080, 24fps, ~3.04s, each with its own AAC audio track. Five of the six read as AI-generated puppet/claymation-style clips (a distinctive tell: garbled sign text like "AIIME" in one of them, a classic text-rendering artifact of video-generation models); the first looked different in kind - real actors in a realistic urban scene, which reads as possibly-existing footage rather than something generated from scratch. Flagged that distinction directly rather than silently treating all six the same way: recommended steering clear of that one specifically if it didn't originate as Christer's own generated content, since baking someone else's copyrighted footage into a personal export pipeline is a real risk the AI-generated ones don't carry.

Showed Christer the actual placeholder frame this project renders by default (regenerated at 1920x1080 to match his own resolution for a fair side-by-side) - the plain dark-background red "prohibited" circle with "PARKING FOOTAGE SKIPPED" caption from the previous session. Answered the sound question directly: yes, strip it - `front.mp4`/`rear.mp4` are video-only containers throughout this whole pipeline (audio always lives in its own separate `audio.aac`), so a clip with an embedded audio track would need that track stripped before ffmpeg's concat demuxer would even accept it alongside video-only neighbours.

Also flagged, before writing any code, that the existing `--parking-transition-image` only accepts a still picture, not a video - his files are real ~3-second clips, which the current design couldn't use directly. Asked via `AskUserQuestion` whether to add proper video-clip support or just extract one still frame instead; Christer picked adding real video support.

**Implementation, `parking_transition.py`.** `render_parking_transition_video()` gained a `clip_path` parameter that takes priority over `image_path` when both are given (never raises - the CLI layer is what actually rejects giving both, see below). New `_render_from_clip()` builds one ffmpeg command that does everything at once: `-stream_loop -1 -i <clip> -t <duration>` loops the source indefinitely and then cuts the *output* to exactly `PARKING_TRANSITION_DURATION_SECONDS` regardless of whether the source is shorter or longer than that (verified both directions with real fixtures: a 1-second source loops to fill a requested 2-second output; a 3-second source trims to a requested 1-second output) - one code path instead of branching on "loop vs. trim". `-r <frame_rate>` re-times to the target trip's own frame rate, `-an` strips any audio track, and `-vf scale=...,pad=...` reuses the exact same fit-and-pad idiom `stitch.py`'s own `_fit_and_pad()` already uses for the map panel (scale to fit without distorting aspect ratio, then pad to the exact target size) - copied rather than imported, since `_fit_and_pad()` builds a filter-graph *fragment* for a multi-input `-filter_complex` graph (stitch.py's own composition), while this needed a plain single-input `-vf` filter string; same idiom, different call shape. `ParkingTransitionCache` gained a matching `clip_path` field, threaded through to `render_parking_transition_video()` exactly like `image_path` already was - no other change needed since the caching key (video width/height/frame_rate) doesn't care which source produced the cached file.

**Implementation, `trip_export.py`/`bv_export.py`.** `export_trip()` gained `parking_transition_clip: Path | None = None`, threaded into `ParkingTransitionCache(...)`'s construction. `bv_export()` gained the matching CLI-facing parameter, plus a new `--parking-transition-clip PATH` flag - and, unlike the library-level function (which silently lets `clip_path` win if both are somehow given), the CLI layer explicitly rejects giving both `--parking-transition-image` and `--parking-transition-clip` together with a `SystemExit`, the same "ambiguous flag combination -> clear rejection" pattern `--duration-heal-archive`/`--no-duration` already established - since at the CLI, "which one wins" is much more likely to be a real mistake than a deliberate choice.

**Real-data verification against Christer's own clips, not just synthetic fixtures.** Ran `render_parking_transition_video()` directly against `No_Parking3.mp4` (a real, clearly legible "NO PARKING" sign shot, one of the five AI-generated ones) requesting a 640x480 output - confirmed via `ffprobe` the result matched exactly (640x480, requested frame rate, no audio stream), and pulled a frame with `ffmpeg` to look at directly: correctly letterboxed (source is 16:9, target 4:3), no distortion, clearly the right content. Then ran a full synthetic `export_trip()` end to end (drive / 20s Parking timelapse / drive) with `parking_transition_clip` pointed at that same real clip - `front.mp4` came out exactly 7 seconds (2s + 3s placeholder + 2s) with no warnings, and a frame pulled from the middle of the *actual concatenated export* showed Christer's own clip content, correctly scaled to the trip's 320x240 resolution - confirming the whole pipeline, not just the isolated renderer function.

**Tests.** `test_parking_transition.py` gained 6 tests (up to 20 total): a custom clip with its own embedded audio and mismatched resolution gets scaled/padded/re-timed with the audio stripped; a clip shorter than the target duration loops to fill it; a clip longer than the target duration trims; `clip_path` takes priority over `image_path` when both are given to `render_parking_transition_video()` directly; and two `ParkingTransitionCache`-level equivalents (uses the clip for every render, clip wins over image). `test_trip_export.py` gained 2 tests (up to 64): the clip override actually gets used (verified via decoded duration and an explicit "no audio stream" check on the result), and clip-over-image priority holds through the full `export_trip()` call, not just the isolated renderer. `test_bv_export.py` gained 3 tests (up to 96): `parking_transition_clip` defaults to `None` and forwards verbatim when given, and `bv_export()` raises `SystemExit` when both `--parking-transition-image`/`--parking-transition-clip`-equivalent kwargs are given together. All new tests pass; the same 3 pre-existing, unrelated `--stitch-mirror-size/zoom/pan` default-value failures are still present, still unrelated (nothing in this diff touches those flags).

**Docs.** `docs/man/bv-export.md`: synopsis line updated to show `--parking-transition-image`/`--parking-transition-clip` as mutually exclusive (`|` between them, matching the existing `--stitch-gsensor-pos | --stitch-gsensor-xy` convention), new `--parking-transition-clip` row in the Parking footage options table, both rows noted the "rejected together" relationship.

Not yet run through the project's own pytest suite, and not yet confirmed against Christer's real archive - worth him picking whichever of his six clips he actually wants to use (or a still frame from one, if he'd rather keep it simple) and confirming `--parking-transition-clip` on a real trip looks and sounds right end to end.

## Bundle Christer's 6 Kling clips as the random default parking-transition source (this session)

Direct follow-up to `--parking-transition-clip` above. Christer uploaded all six of his own "No Parking" clips again with a two-part message: "Here are my examples of no parking videos. Maybe they should be without sound. Please show me yours." - answered the sound question the same way the previous entry already had (strip it, `front.mp4`/`rear.mp4` are video-only throughout this pipeline), and showed him the plain procedural placeholder frame this project renders by default.

He then asked directly: "All of my No parking videos are AI generated(Kling). Should i put them in the projects images folder or have you already included them?" - this resolved the one open concern from the previous session (whether `No_Parking.mp4`, which looked like real-actor footage rather than the other five's more obviously AI-generated look, might be third-party content) - Kling (Kuaishou's AI video generator) is confirmed capable of photorealistic output, so all six are his own generated content, not a copyright risk. Verified the actual bundled-asset location before answering his folder question (`grep`'d `DEFAULT_MAP_ICON_PATH`/`DEFAULT_MIRROR_ICON_PATH` to confirm `src/blackvue/export/assets/`, not the top-level `images/` folder he was asking about, which turned out to be his own unrelated staging area).

Asked via `AskUserQuestion` whether one clip should become the new bundled default (replacing the plain procedural frame) or stay opt-in via `--parking-transition-clip`. Christer's answer changed the scope of the question: "I want them to be randomly inserted if not specified." - not one new default, but a random pick from all six, whenever neither `--parking-transition-image` nor `--parking-transition-clip` is given.

**Bundling.** All six clips copied into `src/blackvue/export/assets/` as `no_parking_1.mp4` through `no_parking_6.mp4` (~31MB total; confirmed via `ffprobe` each is 1920x1080, 24fps, ~3.04s, with its own AAC track - to be stripped by `_render_from_clip()`'s existing `-an` flag whenever actually used, same as any other `--parking-transition-clip` source). `pyproject.toml`'s `package-data` glob for `blackvue.export` extended from `["assets/*.png"]` to `["assets/*.png", "assets/*.mp4"]` - without this, `pip install .` would silently drop the new files, same reasoning already documented there for `mirror.png`/`red_car.png`. New `DEFAULT_PARKING_TRANSITION_CLIPS` tuple in `parking_transition.py` (right after `PARKING_TRANSITION_DURATION_SECONDS`) points at all six paths.

**Where the randomness lives.** Kept the existing "CLI has its own opinionated default, library stays neutral" split (`--map-icon`/`--stitch-mirror-icon`'s precedent) rather than pushing a random default into `export_trip()`/`parking_transition.py` itself - `export_trip()` still defaults to the plain procedural frame when nothing at all is given, so this project's own test suite and any other direct caller of `export_trip()` isn't surprised by a randomized default it never asked for. The actual pick lives in `bv_export.py`'s own per-trip loop, right before each `export_trip()` call: `random.choice(DEFAULT_PARKING_TRANSITION_CLIPS)`, but only when `not include_parking and parking_transition_image is None and parking_transition_clip is None` - an explicit override always wins, and `--include-parking` means nothing is ever transitioned so there's nothing to pick.

Deliberately resolved *per trip*, not once for the whole run and not per individual skipped recording. Once-per-run would lock every trip in a multi-trip export into showing the same clip; per-recording would need `ParkingTransitionCache`'s existing resolution-based memoization key redesigned (it currently reuses one rendered file for every recording at the same width/height/frame_rate within a trip, which is what keeps a trip with several skipped Parking recordings cheap). Per-trip is the middle ground: real variety across an archive export, without touching the cache's own design or slowing down a trip with many skipped recordings. Documented directly in a code comment at the resolution site, not just decided silently.

**Verification.** Built a synthetic 3-recording archive (drive 2s / Parking-mode 20s / drive 2s) and ran `bv_export()` directly with no override flags - `front.mp4` came out exactly 7 seconds (2s + 3s placeholder + 2s, confirming a substitution happened, not the real 20s Parking footage), and a frame pulled from the middle of the result and viewed directly showed a real "No Parking" sign shot - one of the six bundled clips, not the plain procedural frame. Re-ran the same export 8 times in a row (still with no override flags) and hashed a frame from each result: 6 distinct hashes across the 8 runs, matching all six clips in the pool being reachable, with two repeats - expected from 8 independent draws out of 6 options, not a bug.

**Tests, `test_bv_export.py`.** Five new tests (96 -> 101): the default random pick draws from exactly `DEFAULT_PARKING_TRANSITION_CLIPS` (verified by monkeypatching `random.choice` to record its own argument and return a fixed value, then checking the exact object handed to `export_trip()`'s own `parking_transition_clip` kwarg - `export_trip()` itself monkeypatched to just capture kwargs rather than actually render, since these tests are about *which* clip bv-export resolves, not the lower-level render already covered by `test_parking_transition.py`/`test_trip_export.py`); `random.choice()` is never called at all when `--parking-transition-image`, `--parking-transition-clip`, or `--include-parking` is given (each asserted via a fake `random.choice` that raises if called); and a fresh pick happens per trip, not once for the whole run (a two-trip archive, `random.choice` monkeypatched to cycle through two different clips, confirms the two trips get different picks). All 101 tests in `test_bv_export.py` pass by hand via the project's harness, across two batches. The existing 20 tests in `test_parking_transition.py` and 64 in `test_trip_export.py` were re-run unchanged and still pass - neither file needed updates, since `DEFAULT_PARKING_TRANSITION_CLIPS`/the random pick are entirely `bv_export.py`'s own concern, not `export_trip()`'s or the renderer's. The same 3 pre-existing, unrelated `--stitch-mirror-size/zoom/pan` default-value test failures noted in every session since they first appeared are still present in `test_bv_export.py` (confirmed unrelated: byte-identical to the already-committed HEAD version of those three tests, and they compare against `stitch.py`'s neutral library defaults rather than `bv_export.py`'s own deliberately different opinionated CLI defaults - a pre-existing test bug, not something this session's diff touches or introduces).

**Docs.** `bv_export()`'s own docstring paragraph on parking transitions rewritten to describe the random-per-trip default instead of "the procedural frame is the default." `--include-parking`/`--parking-transition-image`/`--parking-transition-clip`'s argparse help text updated to match. `docs/man/bv-export.md`'s "Parking footage" section: the `--include-parking` row's placeholder description changed from "a still frame reading 'PARKING FOOTAGE SKIPPED'" to "one of six bundled 'no parking' clips picked at random per trip"; both override rows dropped their old "Default: a bundled dark frame..." wording (no longer accurate - the procedural frame is now only reachable via `--parking-transition-image none`... actually not even that, there's no explicit "use the plain frame" opt-out anymore, only "use my own image/clip instead of the random pick") and a new paragraph spells out the per-trip random-pick behavior and why it's per-trip.

Not yet run through the project's own pytest suite, and not yet confirmed against Christer's real archive - worth him running a real multi-trip `bv-export` (no override flags) and confirming the parking placeholder actually varies between trips, reads clearly as one of his own six clips, and that the ~31MB repo size increase from bundling them is acceptable to him going forward.

## Add the procedural frame to the random pool, --parking-transition-standard, and clarify the 3-second-clip trim (this session)

Direct follow-up, three more requests in one message after being told about task #89's fix: "I think your clip should be in there to[o]. There should also be an -- option to have no clips, but instead an obvious standard transition and if an external clip is added only the first 3 seconds should be imported." The `AskUserQuestion` tool failed twice with a stream error before I could get a clarifying round in - proceeded with my own best-judgment interpretation of each point instead of blocking further, flagged clearly below for Christer to correct if any of it reads wrong.

**"Your clip should be in there too."** Read as: the plain procedural "PARKING FOOTAGE SKIPPED" frame this project already draws by default should be one of the random pool's own possible outcomes, not just a thing reachable by explicitly opting out. New `RANDOM_PARKING_TRANSITION_POOL` in `parking_transition.py`: `DEFAULT_PARKING_TRANSITION_CLIPS + (None,)` - a 7th entry, `None`, standing in for the procedural frame. This reuses an existing sentinel rather than inventing a new one: `render_parking_transition_video()`/`ParkingTransitionCache` already treat `clip_path=None` (with no `image_path` either) as "draw the plain procedural frame," so `random.choice()`'s result can be handed straight through as `trip_parking_transition_clip` with zero special-casing - if it lands on `None`, that's already exactly what makes `export_trip()` draw the plain frame on its own. `bv_export.py`'s per-trip resolution now draws from `RANDOM_PARKING_TRANSITION_POOL` instead of `DEFAULT_PARKING_TRANSITION_CLIPS` directly. Verified with a real 2000-draw statistical check (`random.choice()` over the real pool, no mocking): all 7 outcomes reachable, roughly evenly distributed (`None` landed ~295/2000, matching the ~285-average of the other 6).

**"An option to have no clips, but instead an obvious standard transition."** New `--parking-transition-standard` flag (`parking_transition_standard: bool = False` on `bv_export()`) - when given, skips the random pick entirely and always uses the plain procedural frame, for a run where none of the six personal clips should potentially show up. Implemented as literally just skipping the `random.choice()` block - `trip_parking_transition_clip`/`parking_transition_image` are already `None` at that point, which is already the "draw the plain frame" condition, so no new code path was needed to actually produce the frame, only to skip the randomness. Rejected pairwise together with `--parking-transition-image`/`--parking-transition-clip` (extended the existing single `if a and b: raise` check into a small list-based version that names whichever two-or-more of the three were actually given, so the error message stays specific rather than generic).

**"If an external clip is added only the first 3 seconds should be imported."** Checked this against the existing `_render_from_clip()` implementation before changing anything: `-stream_loop -1 -i <clip> -t <duration>` already does exactly this for any clip at or above the fixed 3-second duration - the loop always restarts from the source's own frame 0, and `-t` (an output option) caps the result, so a longer clip's output is already nothing but its own first 3 seconds, never a middle or end segment. This was already true and already tested (`test_render_parking_transition_video_trims_a_clip_longer_than_the_duration`) - no code change needed for that case. Left the one genuinely ambiguous case - a clip *shorter* than 3 seconds - unchanged (still loops back to its own start to fill the remaining time) rather than guessing Christer wants that changed too: shortening the output there would break the fixed-duration audio/video sync guarantee he explicitly asked for earlier ("keeps stitch.mp4's audio in sync"), and his wording ("first 3 seconds... imported") reads most naturally as being about a clip *at least* 3 seconds long, which is also the case his own six clips (~3.04s each) actually fall into. Added an explicit paragraph to `_render_from_clip()`'s own docstring spelling this out (both directions), and reworded the CLI help text/man page for `--parking-transition-clip` accordingly ("Its own first 3 seconds are used if it's longer than that; looped to fill the full 3 seconds if it's shorter.") so the documented behavior is unambiguous even though nothing in the render logic itself changed.

**Tests, `test_bv_export.py`.** Six new tests (101 -> 107): the default random pool is exactly `RANDOM_PARKING_TRANSITION_POOL` (not just `DEFAULT_PARKING_TRANSITION_CLIPS`); a `random.choice()` result of `None` flows through to `parking_transition_clip=None`/`parking_transition_image=None` on `export_trip()` (the "picked the procedural frame" path); `--parking-transition-standard` skips `random.choice()` entirely; and `--parking-transition-standard` is rejected together with each of `--parking-transition-image`/`--parking-transition-clip` (two tests), plus `main()`-level default-`False`/flag-flips-`True` coverage. The two existing random-pool tests that referenced `DEFAULT_PARKING_TRANSITION_CLIPS` as the exact pool `random.choice()` was called with were updated to expect `RANDOM_PARKING_TRANSITION_POOL` instead (the picks themselves are unchanged - `pool[0]` is still `DEFAULT_PARKING_TRANSITION_CLIPS[0]`, so those assertions didn't need touching). All 107 tests in `test_bv_export.py` pass by hand via the project's harness. `test_parking_transition.py` (20) and `test_trip_export.py` (64) re-run unchanged and still pass - the docstring-only change to `_render_from_clip()` doesn't affect either file's own tests.

## Road-type coloring and street-name labels for map rendering (this session)

I couldn't find a matching prior commitment when Christer said "Our earlier talk you said you might be able to makes the map better" - no such promise appears anywhere in this file. Asked him directly what "better" meant; his answer was terse: "street names road colors." Read as: the flat gray-line map (`map.mp4`, `map_zoom_*.mp4`, and the `--stitch-map` panel all share this same rendering code) should style roads by OSM `highway=*` type and label streets by their OSM `name`.

**Where the tag data comes from, `osm_roads.py`.** Checked Overpass's own default output verbosity before writing anything: `_overpass_query()`'s `out geom;` statement already returns full tags (Overpass's default "body" verbosity includes tags - only an explicit `out skel geom;`/`out ids geom;` would suppress them), so `_parse_overpass_payload()` discarding tags was a pure parsing omission, not a query limitation. No query change and no cache-format migration needed - even already-cached `.osm_cache/*.json` files already contain the tags and work immediately once re-parsed. `Road` extended with `highway: str = ""` and `name: str | None = None`; `_parse_overpass_payload()` now reads `element.get("tags") or {}` and populates both fields. Confirmed backward-compatible against `test_osm_roads.py`'s existing `_SAMPLE_PAYLOAD` fixture, which has no `"tags"` key at all on any element - `.get("tags") or {}` degrades to `highway=""`/`name=None`, matching every existing test's assertions (none of which touch `.highway`/`.name`).

**Styling and labeling, `map_render.py`.** New `_ROAD_STYLE_BY_HIGHWAY` table (19 OSM `highway=*` values mapped to a `(color, width)` pair - motorways/trunks thickest and most saturated, residential/service roads down to the old flat gray, footways/paths thinnest) with `_DEFAULT_ROAD_STYLE = (ROAD_COLOR, 2)` as the fallback for anything unmapped or tagless, which is exactly the old flat behavior - so a cached pre-tag render or an untagged way never looks different from before. Flagged directly in the code comment that this specific palette is my own first pass, not yet checked against Christer's own taste, since "road colors" was as specific as his request got.

Street names: `_LABELED_HIGHWAY_TYPES` (8 "major" types - motorway through tertiary, plus their `_link` variants) are eligible for a label; minor/service/footway types never get one, to keep a rendered frame legible rather than cluttered. Real OSM data splits one physical street into many separate way segments (one per intersection), so labeling every segment would repeat the same name several times along one street - solved with a `labels_by_name: dict[str, (point, length)]` collected during the line-drawing pass, keeping only the longest on-screen segment per distinct name and drawing it once, at that segment's midpoint, in a second pass after all lines are drawn (so a label is never overdrawn by a later crossing road). Labels use `draw.text(..., anchor="mm", stroke_width=2, stroke_fill=BACKGROUND_COLOR)` for a halo/outline effect - Pillow's `stroke_width`/`stroke_fill` (available since Pillow 6.2; project requires >=10.0) reads more legibly over crossing roads than a plain flat-color label would. A `_MIN_LABELED_ROAD_LENGTH_PX = 40` threshold skips labeling a way segment too short on-screen to read anyway. New shared `_draw_roads(draw, proj, roads)` helper replaces what had been two near-identical inline loops (one in `render_base_map()`, one in `render_frame()`'s no-`base_image` branch) - both now call the one function.

**Real bug found and fixed as a prerequisite, not scope creep: `_load_font()`.** The two-font-size need (default size for the existing speed/timestamp text, a smaller `_ROAD_LABEL_FONT_SIZE = 12` for road labels) exposed that `_load_font()`'s original single-slot `_CACHED_FONT` global ignored its own `size` parameter after the first call - any second call with a different size would silently get back the wrong-sized font. Rewrote to a dict cache, `_CACHED_FONT_BY_SIZE: dict[int, ImageFont.ImageFont]`, keyed by size - matching the pattern `parking_transition.py`'s own `_load_font()` already uses. This was a real latent bug (would have bitten any future second font size, not just this feature), not something invented to justify touching the file.

**Tests.** `test_load_font_only_opens_the_font_file_once` referenced the now-renamed `_CACHED_FONT` global directly via `monkeypatch.setattr` - updated to `_CACHED_FONT_BY_SIZE`. New `test_load_font_caches_separately_per_size` covers the actual bug fixed above: two different sizes return two different (fake) font objects, and a repeated size reuses its own cached one, not the other size's. All 20 tests in `test_map_render.py` pass by hand via the project's harness (a `monkeypatch`/`tmp_path`-aware harness, matching the pattern already used for `test_stitch.py`/`test_bv_export.py`). `test_osm_roads.py` (21 tests - no harness existed yet for this file this session, so I wrote one following the same pattern) and `test_map_video.py` (46 tests, its existing harness already supported `monkeypatch`/`tmp_path`) both re-run unchanged and still pass - neither `Road`'s new optional fields nor `_draw_roads()`'s internal styling change either file's own public-API assertions. Did not re-run all of `test_stitch.py`'s 121 tests this session (already fully verified against the letterbox-removal change directly above, in the same sandbox-timeout-constrained batches) - `_render_map_panel()` calls into this rendering code only through `render_map_video()`'s existing signature, which this diff doesn't touch, so no new risk there.

**Real-data verification.** Built six synthetic `Road` objects spanning motorway/primary/residential (x2, same name, different lengths)/footway/an unrecognized `highway` value, rendered via `render_base_map()`, and viewed the output frame directly: motorway rendered thickest and most saturated, primary a lighter/thinner orange, the two same-named residential segments produced exactly one "Storgatan" label (on the longer of the two, as designed), the footway and unmapped-type roads both rendered as plain thin gray lines with no label (footway because it's not in `_LABELED_HIGHWAY_TYPES`, the unmapped type because it fell through to `_DEFAULT_ROAD_STYLE`), and the halo/stroke around each label kept it legible where it crossed other lines.

**Docs.** No `docs/man/bv-export.md` changes - checked its "road data" mentions and none of them describe road appearance in a way this would contradict.

Not yet run through the project's own pytest suite, and not yet confirmed against Christer's real archive - worth him rendering a real trip's `map.mp4` and telling me directly whether the color palette and which streets get labeled actually match what he had in mind, since "street names road colors" didn't specify either.

## Bound trip detection to the requested range instead of scanning the whole archive (this session)

Christer: "how does bv-exort scan for duration, i believe it takes to long time." Walked through the actual flow with him first: trip *detection* itself only reads whatever `.duration.txt` cache already exists (no ffprobe), but it ran across the *entire archive* on every single run regardless of how small the actual `--timestamp`/`--from`/`--until` request was - a deliberate, previously-accepted tradeoff (see the "Trip-stats/geocoding/letterbox" and self-healing entries above) to never silently truncate a trip that merely overlaps a requested window. Confirmed via `AskUserQuestion` that his own usage is plain `bv-export` (no `--duration-heal-archive`) and that it's slow on *every* run, not just first-time probing - surprising, since a cached recording's `.duration.txt` read is cheap disk I/O, not ffprobe. Rather than guess further, asked whether to instrument first, speed up ffprobe, or check the cache - his actual answer wasn't any of those three: "from time range, seek backwards until start found, then forward until end is found." A real, specific algorithm proposal, not a selection from the offered options.

**The real cost.** `TripBuilder.build()` is a pure function over whatever recordings it's handed - it was never inherently archive-wide. `bv_export()` just always handed it the *entire* archive's front-video recordings, then threw away every trip outside the requested range after the fact. So exporting one day out of a large, growing archive still meant detecting (and duration-checking) every trip that ever existed, every run.

**Confirmed the algorithm with Christer** before implementing (`AskUserQuestion`, both answered): grow a search window outward from the requested range until both trip boundaries are *proven* (a real gap found on each side), rather than scanning everything - yes, that's it. And `--duration-heal-archive` (previously "ffprobe the whole archive during detection") should become bounded too, not stay archive-wide - "make it bounded too."

**Implementation, `trip_builder.py`.** New `TripBuilder.build_for_interval(recordings, interval, *, reasons=None)`, reusing `build()` internally rather than duplicating its gap/bridge/parking-cap logic: seed a slice of `recordings` to just the ones whose own `id.value` falls inside `interval` (`LexicalTimeParser`'s own `TimeInterval`, already used for the existing post-hoc "does this trip touch the range" filter), run `build()` on it, then check whether the earliest/latest trip that actually *touches* `interval` (not just the first/last trip in the built list - an early design mistake, see below) still starts/ends exactly at the slice's own edge. If so, that boundary isn't proven - there could be more of that trip just outside the slice - so the slice grows (margin starts at 4, doubles each retry - a "galloping search") and `build()` runs again. Repeats until both boundaries land on a real, `build()`-confirmed gap, or the slice can't grow further (already spans the whole archive - the correct degenerate fallback for one giant trip, or for `interval` matching the "whole archive" sentinel LexicalTimeParser produces when none of `--timestamp`/`--from`/`--until` are given).

**A real design bug caught before it shipped, worth naming.** My first version checked whether *the very first trip in the built list* touched the window's left edge - but `build()` unconditionally makes whatever recording it's handed first the start of trip #1, by construction, so that check was trivially true any time the window didn't already start at index 0, regardless of whether a real gap existed nearby. Traced through by hand with a concrete example (a decoy earlier trip sitting between the window's edge and the actual target trip) before writing a line of test code, which is what surfaced it: the fix was checking the *interval-relevant* trip specifically, not structurally the first trip in the list - once corrected, the check is a genuine, non-trivial proof (the target trip's own first recording no longer sits at the window's edge once a real predecessor gap has been crossed), confirmed against a hand-traced multi-trip scenario before it went anywhere near the real test suite.

**A second gap, caught by an existing test.** `build()`'s own gap-walking loop never calls `recording_duration` on a window's *last* recording (nothing follows it to trigger `_end_timestamp()` - the same documented gap that used to justify `--duration-heal-archive`'s separate archive-wide eager-heal loop for the chronologically last recording in the whole archive). Under the new bounded design this meant a recording landing right on the final window's own edge could go unhealed even under `--duration-heal-archive`, which isn't the clean guarantee that flag is supposed to make. Fixed by having `build_for_interval()` explicitly call `self.recording_duration` on every recording in its own final window before returning, not just the ones `build()`'s internal gap logic happened to need - harmless for the default cache-only reader (`read_duration_seconds` has no side effect), and closes the edge case for `load_or_compute_duration`.

**Wiring, `bv_export.py`.** Swapped the unconditional `TripBuilder(...).build(front_recordings)` for a check: `interval` matching the exact "whole archive" sentinel (`"00000000_000000"`/`"99999999_999999"`, what `LexicalTimeParser` produces when none of `--timestamp`/`--from`/`--until` are given) still calls `build()` directly; anything else calls the new `build_for_interval()`. Removed the old standalone `for recording in front_recordings: load_or_compute_duration(recording)` eager-heal loop entirely - `--duration-heal-archive` now just means passing `load_or_compute_duration` itself as the `recording_duration` callable into the bounded search, instead of the cache-only `read_duration_seconds`, so only whatever the search actually touches gets ffprobed. The separate per-trip self-heal loop right before each trip's own overwrite prompt (unchanged, still runs whenever `duration=True` regardless of `duration_heal_archive`) already guaranteed every recording in the trip actually being exported gets healed, so nothing needed to change there. Rewrote `bv_export()`'s own docstring paragraph and `docs/man/bv-export.md`'s "Trip detection" prose and `--duration-heal-archive` row to describe bounded detection instead of the old archive-wide scan.

**Tests.** 9 new tests in `test_trip_builder.py` against a synthetic multi-trip archive, every one checked against a real `build()` call over the *entire* archive as ground truth rather than a hand-picked expected shape: a middle trip recovered correctly when seeded by only its own middle recording (forcing growth both directions within the same trip); the first and last trips in the archive; an interval matching zero recordings (returns `[]`); a `--from`/`--until`-style range spanning four trips at once; the whole-archive sentinel producing an identical result to `build()` in one pass; `reasons` populated for the trip actually returned; every recording in the final window getting healed under a side-effecting `recording_duration` (the edge-case fix above, verified directly); and a 50-trip archive where the bounded search reads under a quarter of the duration lookups a full scan would (structural proof of the actual speedup, not just correctness). Two new `test_bv_export.py` tests: `--duration-heal-archive` still heals a two-recording archive that happens to fit inside the bounded window's first pass (the *existing* test, re-verified unchanged - it turned out to already hold once the last-recording healing gap above was fixed, no test edit needed); and a new one proving the actual bounded-not-archive-wide claim - ten separate trips 30 minutes apart, only the first requested, `--duration-heal-archive` given, the tenth (unrelated) trip's `.duration.txt` never gets created. All 108 tests in `test_bv_export.py` and all 41 in `test_trip_builder.py` pass. `test_trip_export.py` wasn't re-run - it operates on an already-built `Trip` object, never touches `TripBuilder` or detection at all, so it's structurally unaffected by this diff.

**Real-data verification.** Built a real 5-trip synthetic archive (real ffmpeg files, 2 recordings per trip, 30-minute gaps between trips) and ran `bv_export()` directly requesting only the middle (3rd) trip: exactly one folder got created (`trip_20260720_100800_20260720_101000`), only that trip's own 2 recordings got a `.duration.txt` written (none of the other 8 recordings across the other 4 trips), and the exported trip's own `trip.log` membership section showed the real gap reasoning ("gap since 20260720_093600_N was 1920.0s, over the 310.0s ... threshold") - confirming `reasons` still flows correctly end-to-end through the new bounded path, not just at the `TripBuilder` unit level.

Not yet confirmed against Christer's real archive - worth him re-running a normal `bv-export --timestamp <day>` (no other flags) on the archive that felt slow, and telling me whether it's actually faster now. If it's still slow, the bottleneck is somewhere else entirely (archive listing/parsing itself, disk I/O on whatever the archive is stored on, or something in the concatenation/render steps rather than detection) and worth a fresh, instrumented look rather than assuming this fix was the whole story.

## Make the parking-transition clip pool opt-in instead of default (this session)

Christer, unprompted, reflecting on an earlier session's work: "do you think i was carried away when adding the 3 seconds clip and make them default." Gave an honest answer rather than just reassurance: yes, somewhat - three mutually-exclusive CLI flags, ~31MB of bundled personal video assets, and ~10 tests had accreted around what's fundamentally a 3-second cosmetic placeholder, and the real overreach wasn't the clips existing but making the random pick the *default* - a personal export tool showing a different one of his own AI-generated clips each run, unannounced, isn't the kind of predictable behavior a default should have. Offered to revert the default to the plain frame and make the whole clip pool opt-in instead, keeping everything already built usable on request. Christer: "yes do that."

**The rename.** `parking_transition_standard: bool = False` (bv-export's own `--parking-transition-standard`, "skip the randomness, always plain frame") became `parking_transition_random: bool = False` (`--parking-transition-random`, "opt into the randomness, don't just use the plain frame") - an inversion, not just a rename. The per-trip resolution condition in `bv_export()` flipped from `and not parking_transition_standard` to `and parking_transition_random`: a trip only ever gets a `random.choice(RANDOM_PARKING_TRANSITION_POOL)` pick now when the flag is explicitly given, never by default. The three-way mutual-exclusion check (`--parking-transition-image`/`--parking-transition-clip`/now `--parking-transition-random`) is otherwise unchanged - still only one placeholder source at a time, still rejected pairwise.

**Nothing about the underlying mechanism changed** - `RANDOM_PARKING_TRANSITION_POOL` (six clips + `None` for the plain frame, each a 1-in-7 outcome), `ParkingTransitionCache`, the 3-second fixed duration, the image/clip override system - all untouched. Only which flag turns the randomness *on* changed, and what happens when nothing at all is given. `export_trip()`'s own default (the plain frame) was already correct and untouched throughout every version of this feature - `bv_export()`'s own CLI-layer default now finally matches it exactly instead of diverging from it, closing the gap the "CLI has its own opinionated default, library stays neutral" comment already flagged as a deliberate divergence in the previous version.

**Docs/comments.** Rewrote `bv_export()`'s own docstring paragraph, all three `argparse` help strings (`--include-parking`'s description of what replaces skipped footage, `--parking-transition-image`/`--parking-transition-clip`'s "instead of the default X" wording, and the new `--parking-transition-random` entry itself), `docs/man/bv-export.md`'s synopsis and options table, and `parking_transition.py`'s own comment above `DEFAULT_PARKING_TRANSITION_CLIPS` - all now describe plain-frame-by-default with an explicit opt-in, and the comment in `parking_transition.py` directly narrates the reversal itself (briefly the default, reconsidered, now opt-in) rather than pretending this was the design from the start.

**Tests, `test_bv_export.py`.** Renamed the four `parking_transition_standard`-keyed tests (rejection-pairwise x2, `main()` default/flag-set x2) to `parking_transition_random`, inverting the CLI flag string and kwarg but keeping their own assertions' shape (still "defaults False," still "flag sets True," still "rejected together with image/clip"). Split the old `test_bv_export_picks_a_random_bundled_clip_by_default` into two: `test_bv_export_leaves_the_plain_frame_by_default` (no flags at all - asserts `random.choice()` is never even called, a stricter check than the old test could make, since previously the assertion had to allow for the random path being the live one) and `test_bv_export_picks_a_random_bundled_clip_when_random_flag_given` (the old test's real logic, now behind explicit `parking_transition_random=True`). `test_bv_export_random_pool_can_land_on_the_procedural_frame` and `test_bv_export_picks_a_fresh_random_clip_per_trip` both updated to pass `parking_transition_random=True`, since neither test's premise (a random pick actually happening) holds anymore without it. Deleted `test_bv_export_skips_the_random_pick_when_parking_transition_standard_is_true` outright - its assertion ("no pick happens when told not to randomize") is now just what the *default* already does, fully covered by the new `test_bv_export_leaves_the_plain_frame_by_default`, so keeping a separate test for the old opt-out flag's absence would have been redundant. Net test count unchanged (108): one test replaced by two, one deleted. All 108 pass, confirmed in three batches via the project's harness.

**Real-data verification.** Ran a real synthetic trip (drive/Parking/drive) through `bv_export()` with no override flags at all - `front.mp4` came out exactly 4 seconds (matching the fixed 3-second placeholder plus the two short drive segments), and a frame pulled from the middle of the result, viewed directly, shows the plain "PARKING FOOTAGE SKIPPED" procedural frame with its red no-parking icon - not one of the six bundled clips. Confirms the default really did revert end to end, not just at the kwarg level.

Not yet confirmed against Christer's real archive - worth him running a real export with no override flags and confirming the plain frame is what shows up now, and a separate run with `--parking-transition-random` confirming his own clips are still reachable exactly as before when he actually wants them.

## Add a second g-sensor visualization: a strip-chart with playhead (`gsensor_graph.mp4`) (this session)

Christer attached a screenshot of the official BlackVue SD Card Viewer app's own g-sensor panel and asked for "another gsensor view, like the bottom panel in this picture" - a horizontal strip chart with colored line traces scrolling/spanning a timeline, distinct from this project's existing circular dot-gauge (`gsensor.mp4`). He later added the intended use case unprompted: "I think this telemetry view is extra nice when you have a rearview video with the map to the left then you have space at the bottom for this view" - i.e. a `--stitch` layout with rearview mirror + map on the left and this graph filling a bottom strip.

Investigated the existing dot-gauge pipeline first (`gsensor_reader.py`/`gsensor_render.py`/`gsensor_video.py`) so any new design would reuse its shape rather than diverge for no reason. Confirmed three genuinely open design questions via `AskUserQuestion` before writing any code, per Christer's own stated preference earlier this session ("Asking questions in discussion is fine - Christer prefers that over guessing"):

1. **Graph motion.** Scrolling window (chart itself scrolls under a fixed playhead) vs. static whole-trip overview with the playhead sweeping across it. Christer picked **static overview, moving playhead** - the opposite of what I'd flagged as "recommended," which was a useful reminder not to over-weight my own guess.
2. **Layout scope.** A new dedicated `--stitch` layout combining rearview mirror + map + graph strip vs. a general bottom panel addable to any layout. Christer picked the **new dedicated layout** - matching the specific "rearview + map left, graph strip bottom" composition he described, not a generic add-on.
3. **Build order.** Standalone video first (mirroring how the dot-gauge itself shipped in two stages historically - task #44 standalone, task #61 `--stitch` wiring later) vs. both in one pass. Christer picked **standalone first**.

This session's scope is just item 3's first half: the standalone `gsensor_graph.mp4` renderer and its own opt-in `bv-export` flag. The dedicated `--stitch` layout (item 2) is intentionally deferred to a follow-up task, not built yet.

**New modules, mirroring the dot-gauge's own two-file split.** `blackvue.export.gsensor_graph_render`: `baseline_for_samples(samples) -> (x, y, z)` (median per axis - same reasoning as the dot-gauge's own `baseline_for_samples()`, extended to z since the strip chart plots all three axes, not just x/y), `scale_for_samples(samples, baseline=...)` (shared vertical scale across all three axes, so their relative magnitudes stay comparable rather than each auto-scaling independently), `render_base_frame(samples, baseline, scale, total_seconds, ...)` (draws the three X/Y/Z traces once across the whole width plus a zero-line and time-tick labels - everything that's fixed for the whole trip), and `render_frame(base_image, elapsed_seconds, total_seconds, ...)` (returns a copy of the base image with a vertical white playhead line composited at the current elapsed-time position). `blackvue.export.gsensor_graph_video`: `render_gsensor_graph_video(samples, destination, *, fps=5, duration_seconds=None)` - renders the base frame exactly once, then loops only the cheap playhead composite per output frame, before handing the sequence to the same shared `media.encode_frame_sequence()` the dot-gauge uses. Because the chart itself never changes frame to frame, this needed none of `gsensor_video.py`'s own `_advance_search_index()`/`_interpolate_from_index()` machinery (built there specifically to fix an O(samples × frames) hang in *per-frame* sample interpolation) - there's no per-frame sample lookup here at all, just direct arithmetic from elapsed time to a pixel x position.

**Visual design choices, made without a question since they're small/reversible.** Same chroma-key green background as the dot-gauge (imported directly from `gsensor_render.BACKGROUND_COLOR` rather than redefined, so both g-sensor overlays key out identically). Three trace colors chosen to avoid green (a green trace would key out with the background) and to stay distinct from each other and from the black zero-line/tick text: X red (`(230, 57, 70)`, matching the dot-gauge's own accent color for a little visual continuity), Y blue (`(69, 123, 157)`), Z amber (`(241, 196, 15)`). Playhead is white, 3px wide - the one color guaranteed to read against all three trace colors and the black axis line alike. Canvas is `960x220` - short and wide ("the bottom panel"), not the dot-gauge's own `480x480` square. Time-tick labels reuse `map_render.py`'s own `_load_font()` pattern (cached-by-size TTF lookup with a `DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf` candidate list, falling back to PIL's built-in default font) rather than a fresh implementation, formatted as `MM:SS` to match the reference screenshot's own `00:52`-style labels; tick spacing picked from a small "round number" candidate table (1/2/5/10/15/30/60/120/300/600/900/1800/3600 seconds) aiming for roughly 6 ticks, the same kind of approach most charting libraries use rather than dividing evenly into an unreadable interval.

**Wiring, mirroring `--gsensor-video`/`render_gsensor` exactly.** New `render_gsensor_graph: bool = False` parameter on both `export_trip()` and `bv_export()`, a new `gsensor_graph_video: Path | None` field on `ExportResult`, and a new `--gsensor-graph-video` CLI flag (`dest="render_gsensor_graph"`) - fully independent of `--gsensor-video`: either, both, or neither can be given, since this is a separate file (`gsensor_graph.mp4`), not a replacement for the dot-gauge. Same `duration_seconds` handling as the dot-gauge (falls back to the last sample's own offset if not given, otherwise uses the trip's real concatenated video duration so a trailing gap in g-sensor data doesn't leave the graph out of sync), same `--debug` phase-timing stderr line, same `trip.log` step logging, same `MediaToolError`-to-warning handling. Deliberately **not** wired into `--stitch` yet - that's the dedicated-layout follow-up from design question 2 above.

**Tests.** New `test_gsensor_graph_render.py` (15 tests): base-frame sizing, flat chroma-key-green background, graceful handling of fewer than two samples, each axis drawn in its own distinct color (verified by computing the exact expected pixel via the same `_time_to_x`/`_value_to_y` helpers the renderer itself uses, not a hand-picked coordinate), the playhead actually changing pixels and landing in the right column, `scale_for_samples`/`baseline_for_samples` extended-to-three-axes behavior (mirroring the dot-gauge's own existing test shapes), and the tick-interval/tick-format helpers. New `test_gsensor_graph_video.py` (6 tests): fewer-than-two-samples and zero-duration both return `None` and write nothing, a real end-to-end ffmpeg render with `ffprobe`-verified duration, the `duration_seconds` trailing-gap-extension behavior, the samples-derived-duration fallback, and a regression guard confirming `render_base_frame()` is called exactly once per export regardless of frame count (the actual point of the base/playhead split - a monkeypatched call counter around the real function). Two new `test_bv_export.py` tests: `--gsensor-graph-video` produces `gsensor_graph.mp4` (and confirms `gsensor.mp4` is *not* also produced, proving the two flags are independent), and no flag produces neither file. All 110 tests in `test_bv_export.py` (108 existing + 2 new) and all 21 new render/video tests pass.

**Sandbox note.** No `pytest` available in this environment (no network to install it either) - built a small standalone test-runner harness (`/tmp/run_bv_export_batch.py`, not checked into the repo) that imports a test file directly via `importlib`, calls every `test_*` function, and provides minimal `tmp_path`/`monkeypatch`/`capsys` fixture stand-ins (including `monkeypatch.setattr("dotted.module.attr", value)`'s two-argument string form) plus a tiny `pytest.raises`/`pytest.fixture` shim module, since `test_bv_export.py` itself imports `pytest` directly. Same category of throwaway harness this project has needed before for real ffmpeg-based batch verification.

**Real-data verification.** Built a real synthetic archive (a real 6-second ffmpeg front video plus 6 seconds of synthetic sinusoidal g-sensor samples at 10Hz) and ran `bv_export(..., render_gsensor_graph=True)` end to end: `gsensor_graph.mp4` came out at 6.2s (matching `front.mp4`'s own 6.0s within the "+1 frame" rounding the dot-gauge's own duration tests already tolerate). Pulled a frame at the 3-second mark and viewed it directly: three distinct-colored sine-like traces span the full width, six evenly-spaced `MM:SS` tick labels run along the bottom, and the white playhead sits exactly at `00:03` - confirming the static-overview-with-moving-playhead design (Christer's own pick, question 1 above) renders as intended, not just at the unit-test level.

Not yet shown to Christer - worth him running `bv-export --gsensor-graph-video` on a real trip and confirming the strip chart itself reads well at realistic g-sensor magnitudes (this session's verification used synthetic sine waves, not real driving data), before starting the follow-up `--stitch` layout work (design question 2: a dedicated rearview-mirror + map + graph-strip layout).

## Make the g-sensor graph a selectable, vertical-capable `--stitch` panel instead of a dedicated layout (this session, direct follow-up)

The previous entry's own "not yet built" item was a dedicated `--stitch` layout combining rearview mirror + map + graph strip - Christer's own design pick at the time. Before I even reported back, he corrected the premise: "You hung when asking me a question.
