Previously all three axes shared one value-axis scale (the largest deviation seen on *any* axis, from `scale_for_samples()`) - so an axis with a genuinely smaller real range of motion (e.g. Y's forward/back braking vs. X's side-to-side cornering) would only ever use a fraction of its own lane's height, looking flatter/less informative than an axis that happened to swing wider. Christer wants each axis to use its own full lane height at its own peak instead.

Asked one clarifying `AskUserQuestion` before implementing, since the request only named X and Y explicitly and Z currently shares the same scale value as X/Y (a deliberate choice from the earlier lane-split feature, specifically so "a given magnitude looks the same size in either lane"): should Z also get its own independent scale, or stay tied to whatever X/Y do. Christer picked **Z independent too** - the simplest, most consistent rule: every axis, X/Y/Z alike, is only ever compared against its own trip-wide range now, never against the others.

**`gsensor_graph_render.py`.** `scale_for_samples()` (one shared cross-axis scale) removed entirely and replaced with `axis_scales_for_samples()`, returning `(scale_x, scale_y, scale_z)` - each axis' own largest deviation from `baseline` across the whole trip's samples, times `padding`, floored at `minimum`, computed completely independently per axis (a huge X deviation no longer inflates Y's or Z's own scale, the core behavior change). `scale_for_samples()` was removed rather than left in place as unused dead code - a judgment call, not explicitly confirmed with Christer: nothing calls it anymore (its one real caller, `gsensor_graph_video.py`, now calls the new function instead), and leaving a still-tested-but-unused "shared scale" function sitting next to the new "independent scale" one seemed more likely to confuse a future reader than help. Worth reverting if Christer wants the old function kept around for some other reason. `render_base_frame()`'s `scale: float` parameter renamed to `scales: tuple[float, float, float]` - the trace-drawing loop now looks up each axis' own scale (`scale_x`/`scale_y`/`scale_z`) rather than one shared value; the zero-line position calculations (`main_zero_pos`/`z_zero_pos`) are mathematically unaffected either way (a value of exactly 0.0 always lands on the lane's own center regardless of which scale is passed), so those just pass a representative axis' scale with a comment explaining why it doesn't matter. Module docstring and `_split_lanes()`'s own docstring - both of which described the old shared-scale-across-lanes design as a deliberate choice - updated to describe the new independent-per-axis design and explicitly note the reversal.

**`gsensor_graph_video.py`.** `render_gsensor_graph_video()` now calls `axis_scales_for_samples(samples, baseline=baseline)` once (computed from the whole trip's samples, exactly like the old `baseline`/`scale` calls it replaces) and passes the resulting `scales` tuple to every `render_base_frame()` call - both the paginated per-chunk list comprehension and the single-whole-trip-chart branch - so a given magnitude on a given axis still reads the same size on every page when paginated; only the three axes now differ from *each other*, not from themselves across time, consistent with the shared-scale-across-pages philosophy already established for the rolling-window feature above.

**Tests.** `test_gsensor_graph_render.py`: the three old `scale_for_samples()` tests replaced with three `axis_scales_for_samples()` tests - minimum floor applied per axis independently; the key new behavior, that one axis' huge deviation (300 on X) does *not* inflate another axis' own scale (Y's own, much smaller, peak of 50 stays 50, not 300); baseline-relative deviation measured per axis. Every existing `render_base_frame()`/`render_frame()` call site that passed a single scalar `scale` value updated to pass a `(v, v, v)` 3-tuple instead - a safe, mechanical change since none of those tests exercised *different* per-axis scales, so wrapping the same value three times preserves each test's existing pixel-level math exactly. One new real-rendering test added: X and Y given the identical raw value (10) but different scales (10 vs. 100) - X, whose value equals its own scale exactly, lands at the lane's own edge, while Y (same raw value, but its own scale ten times larger) lands much closer to the lane's center - directly confirming the two axes are no longer scaled together. All 51 tests in the file pass. `test_gsensor_graph_video.py`'s 13 tests, `test_stitch.py`'s 19 non-`capsys` graph-panel tests, and `test_trip_export.py`'s 4 graph-related tests all checked and pass unchanged - none of them construct explicit scale values, so the rename didn't touch them.

**Real-data verification.** Rendered synthetic bounded-random-walk data where X swings roughly 8x wider than Y (X's own trip-wide peak ~150, Y's ~15 - modeling something like hard cornering vs. gentler forward/back braking on the same trip) through the real `axis_scales_for_samples()` + `render_base_frame()` pipeline and viewed the output directly: `axis_scales_for_samples()` correctly reported very different scales per axis (~77 for X, ~10 for Y), and the rendered chart shows both traces using comparably full amplitude across the panel's height despite their very different real magnitudes - Y no longer reads as a flat, compressed line next to a busy X.

Not yet shown to Christer - worth a real trip export to confirm this reads well against real driving data, where X and Y's relative ranges may differ even more (or less) than this session's synthetic example.

## Fix front/rear desync risk when a Parking recording's video is corrupted (this session, bug report)

Christer, from a real `bv-export` run: "looks like P files are included as default but gives error", with two ffprobe failures on `20260726_144116_PF.mp4`/`_PR.mp4` ("contradictionary STSC and STCO", "error reading header", "Invalid data found when processing input") for `trip_20260726_142517_20260726_150250`.

Investigated before touching any code. Two separate things were going on. First, "included as default" isn't quite what's happening: `export_trip()`'s `include_parking` defaults to `False`, so mid-trip Parking recordings are *excluded* by default and swapped for a 3-second placeholder (existing, deliberate behavior from the `--include-parking` feature). But building that placeholder still requires `ffprobe`-ing the real `_PF.mp4`/`_PR.mp4` file (`ParkingTransitionCache.video_for()` -> `probe_video_properties()`), purely to read its width/height/frame rate so the placeholder can be encoded to match and concat cleanly - so the real Parking file gets touched even though its footage never ends up in the output. Second, the ffprobe errors themselves ("contradictionary STSC and STCO" etc.) are ffmpeg's own MP4 index-atom-corruption signature - almost certainly a genuinely truncated file from the dashcam's own SD card (e.g. power loss mid-Parking-recording), not a bv-export bug. The code already handled this gracefully: a warning is logged and that recording's placeholder is dropped entirely for the failing asset, rather than aborting the export.

The one real gap found: `_concatenate_asset()` runs FRONT and REAR concatenation independently (in separate threads), each calling `_parking_transition_source()` -> `video_for()` on its own file only. Since both `_PF.mp4` and `_PR.mp4` happened to fail together in Christer's report, front.mp4 and rear.mp4 stayed the same length - but if only one side's file were corrupted, only that side would drop the segment while its sibling kept its normal 3-second placeholder, leaving front.mp4/rear.mp4 different lengths from that point on and desyncing the rest of the trip. Raised this with Christer via `AskUserQuestion` rather than assuming; he picked fixing it now (fall back to the sibling's resolution) over leaving it for later.

**`parking_transition.py`.** `ParkingTransitionCache.video_for()` gained a keyword-only `fallback_source: Path | None = None`. It tries `probe_video_properties(source)` first as before; if that raises `MediaToolError` and a `fallback_source` was given, it tries probing that instead and uses whichever one succeeded to pick/render the placeholder. If the fallback also fails, the *original* exception (from `source`) is what gets re-raised - so the resulting warning still names the actual file the caller cares about (`front.mp4`'s own corrupted source), not the sibling that was only tried as a rescue.

**`trip_export.py`.** New `_SIBLING_VIDEO_ASSET` mapping (`Asset.FRONT` <-> `Asset.REAR`). `_parking_transition_source()` now looks up the sibling video asset's own file on the same `Recording` (when `asset` is FRONT/REAR; not applicable to AUDIO) and passes its path as `video_for()`'s `fallback_source` - front/rear cameras on the same recording always share resolution and frame rate in practice, so a working rear file can size a corrupted front file's placeholder (or vice versa) with no loss of fidelity.

**Tests.** `test_parking_transition.py`: three new tests on `ParkingTransitionCache.video_for()` directly - falls back to `fallback_source`'s own properties when `source` fails to probe; re-raises the *original* `source` error (naming `front.mp4`, not the fallback) when both fail; still raises normally when no `fallback_source` is given at all (today's pre-fix behavior, unchanged). `test_trip_export.py`: one new end-to-end test building a 3-recording trip with a genuinely corrupted mid-trip `front_p.mp4` (garbage bytes, not a real MP4) alongside a real, readable `rear_p.mp4` - confirms `export_trip()` produces *zero* warnings and both `front.mp4`/`rear.mp4` come out the same length (`1s + 3s placeholder + 1s`), where before this fix the front side would have silently dropped that segment and come out 3 seconds shorter than rear. All 8 directly-relevant tests pass (verified via a hand-rolled runner - no `pytest` package available in this sandbox); a broader sweep of every non-`monkeypatch`/`capsys`-dependent test in both files (61 tests total) also confirmed passing, no regressions.

Reported the investigation findings to Christer before implementing (per the working agreement's "confirm meaningfully-sized design decisions" preference) - explained the "included by default" confusion, confirmed the ffprobe errors are real file corruption rather than a bv-export bug, and flagged the front/rear desync risk as a design question rather than assuming an answer.

Not yet shown to Christer - worth a real re-export of `trip_20260726_142517_20260726_150250` (or another trip with a similarly corrupted Parking file) to confirm the fix produces a clean, warning-free export with front.mp4/rear.mp4 correctly in sync. The underlying corrupted `_PF.mp4`/`_PR.mp4` files themselves are unaffected by this fix - if Christer wants that footage recovered rather than skipped, that's a separate, unrelated question about the source files, not something bv-export's code can fix.

## Correction: the ffprobe failures aren't per-file corruption, they're a known BlackVue container quirk (this session, direct follow-up)

Christer, immediately after the sibling-fallback fix above: "Looks like all parking files gives the same error." That one sentence overturned the previous entry's central assumption. "Both PF and PR happened to fail together" wasn't a coincidence of two separately corrupted files - if literally every Parking-mode file trips the identical ffprobe error, that's not random SD-card damage, it's something structural about how BlackVue itself writes these files. The sibling-fallback fix from the previous entry is still correct to have, but it does nothing for this case: if every Parking file fails ffprobe the same way, a front/rear pair will *always* fail together, so there's never a working sibling to fall back to.

Researched rather than re-guessed. Web search turned up a matching, years-old report on DashCamTalk (a BlackVue owner in 2019, unrelated to Christer, hitting the exact same three-line error - "STSC entry 0 is invalid", "contradictionary STSC and STCO", "error reading header" - on a plain `ffmpeg -i ..._PF.mp4 -c copy test.mp4`, i.e. no bv-export involved at all) plus the FFmpeg project's own mailing list/patchwork history describing the STSC/STCO consistency check as one that flags files "non-compliant" but still openable by other players (VLC, Windows Media Player, MPC). Put together: BlackVue's own Parking-mode time-lapse container structure (1 frame/second captured, played back at a normal frame rate) is written in a way that trips ffmpeg's strict `mov` demuxer validation on *every* such file, independent of whether the recording itself is intact - not corruption, a compatibility quirk. This also explains why this codebase already has a pure-Python `mp4_box_reader.py` fallback (task history: "Pure-Python MP4 box parser fallback for duration/span") - it was built for exactly this class of problem on the *duration* side (`media.py`'s `get_span()`), just not yet extended to cover width/height, which is what `parking_transition.py`'s own `probe_video_properties()` needs.

The fix: give `probe_video_properties()` the same box-reader fallback `get_span()` already has, rather than relying on a sibling that will almost always be just as unreadable.

**`mp4_box_reader.py`.** `Mp4Info` gained `width: int | None = None` and `height: int | None = None` (both default `None`, so every existing caller/test that constructs `Mp4Info(duration_seconds=..., frame_count=...)` positionally-by-keyword is untouched). New `_parse_tkhd_dimensions()` reads a video track's own `tkhd` (track header) box - specifically just its trailing 8 bytes, the two 32-bit 16.16-fixed-point width/height fields that sit at a fixed offset from the *end* of the payload regardless of `tkhd` version (unlike `mvhd`, which needs to branch on version because its variable-length timestamp fields come first). `read_mp4_info()`'s existing video-track-detection loop (walk `trak` boxes, confirm the child `mdia/hdlr`'s handler type is `'vide'`) now also looks for that same `trak`'s own `tkhd` - a direct sibling of `mdia`, not something nested under it - and records its width/height if found. Missing/unparseable `tkhd` is non-fatal (`width`/`height` just stay `None`), the same treatment a missing `stsz` already gets for `frame_count` - callers decide whether partial info is still useful.

**`parking_transition.py`.** `probe_video_properties()` now falls back to `read_mp4_info()` (via a new `_probe_video_properties_from_boxes()` helper) whenever ffprobe raises `CalledProcessError`, mirroring `media.py`'s existing `get_span()` fallback exactly. Frame rate isn't stored directly in the box structure, so it's derived as `frame_count / duration_seconds` - the same relationship `compute_span()` already uses in reverse for Parking recordings. If the box reader can't produce a *complete* result (width, height, frame_count, and a positive duration all present), or raises `MediaToolError` itself (e.g. the file isn't a readable MP4 at all, as in the earlier sibling-fallback fix's corrupted-garbage-bytes test fixtures), the function re-raises ffprobe's own original error rather than returning a partial/bogus result - so a genuinely unreadable file still produces the same informative "ffprobe failed for X: ..." message as before, just no longer the *first* thing tried.

**Tests.** `test_mp4_box_reader.py`: `_video_trak()` gained optional `width`/`height` keyword args (backward compatible - the four existing tests that don't pass them are unaffected) that prepend a synthetic `tkhd` box; three new tests - reads width/height from a real `tkhd`; both stay `None` without one; a `tkhd` on a *non*-video (`'soun'`) track is correctly ignored, only the video track's own `tkhd` counts. `test_parking_transition.py`: two new tests on `probe_video_properties()` directly, using `monkeypatch` to make the real `subprocess.run` fail for `ffprobe` specifically while a stand-in `read_mp4_info()` returns a normal `Mp4Info` - falls back correctly and computes the right frame rate (1800 frames / 60s = 30.0); raises the *original* ffprobe error (naming the real file) when the box reader can't produce complete dimensions. All 140 tests across the five touched/related files (`test_mp4_box_reader.py`, `test_media.py`, `test_parking_transition.py`, `test_trip_export.py`, `test_export_media.py`) pass, 0 failures, verified via a hand-rolled runner extended this session with a real setattr-with-revert `monkeypatch` stand-in (no `pytest` package available in this sandbox) - including `test_media.py`'s own pre-existing `get_span()` box-reader-fallback tests, confirming the `Mp4Info` field addition didn't disturb that unrelated call path.

**Real-data verification.** Built a synthetic MP4 via the same box-construction helpers the tests use (real `mvhd`/`tkhd`/`stsz` boxes, `width=1920, height=1080, frame_count=1800`, `duration=60s`) plus a garbage `stsc` box on the audio track - the same "structurally intact video, broken-in-a-way-that-still-decodes-fine audio trak" shape `test_media.py`'s own pre-existing end-to-end test uses. Ran it through the real (non-mocked) `ffprobe` directly: it refused the file ("missing mandatory atoms, broken header" - a different specific message than Christer's own STSC/STCO one, but the same class of strict-validation failure, confirming this general class of "real player can open it, ffprobe can't" file reliably triggers the fallback path). Then ran the same file through the real `probe_video_properties()` end-to-end (no mocking at all): it returned `(1920, 1080, 900.0)` - correct width/height, and `900.0 = 1800 / 2.0` matching this particular synthetic file's own frame_count/duration exactly.

Not yet shown to Christer - worth a real re-export of an actual trip with Parking-mode footage to confirm bv-export now produces placeholders (and a clean, warning-free run) for every such recording rather than just the lucky cases where a sibling camera happened to probe successfully. If BlackVue's real Parking-mode files turn out to have some further structural quirk this session's synthetic fixtures didn't anticipate, the box reader may need another round of adjustment against Christer's actual files.

## Fix degenerate frame_rate=0.0 placeholder from the box-reader fallback (this session, real-world regression from the previous fix)

Christer ran a real trip through the box-reader-fallback fix above and reported two symptoms in the same message: "The P files only showed 1 frame, but it lasted the duration of the P file. And footage after that wasn't there for some time." That's exactly what the previous entry's own "not yet shown to Christer" caveat was worried about - the box reader hadn't been tried against a real Parking file yet, only synthetic fixtures.

Root cause: `_probe_video_properties_from_boxes()`'s completeness check was `info.frame_count is not None` - but a real Parking-mode recording's video track apparently reports a `stsz` `sample_count` of exactly `0`, not a missing/unreadable one. `0` is a legitimate, distinct value the existing check let straight through, producing `frame_rate = 0 / duration_seconds = 0.0`. That `0.0` then went to `render_parking_transition_video()`, which handed ffmpeg `-r 0.0` - a degenerate placeholder (one frame, its own declared duration nowhere near the intended 3 seconds) instead of a proper one, and apparently threw off the concat demuxer's timeline handling for whatever followed it in the same file - a single root cause plausibly explaining both symptoms Christer described. (A `sample_count` of `0` most likely means this particular Parking recording uses fragmented MP4 - real per-fragment sample counts live in `moof`/`trun` boxes this reader doesn't parse, not in the top-level `stsz` table it does read - so `0` isn't "unknown," it's "this table genuinely has nothing in it here.")

**`parking_transition.py`.** `_probe_video_properties_from_boxes()`'s condition changed from `info.frame_count is not None` to `info.frame_count is not None and info.frame_count > 0`. `frame_count == 0` now falls through to re-raising ffprobe's own original error, same as a missing `tkhd`/`stsz` already did - which means this specific class of file (fragmented-MP4 Parking recordings) falls back to the pre-existing, safe "warn and drop this segment" behavior instead of ever producing a broken placeholder. This is a real reduction in capability versus the previous entry's goal (every Parking file gets a placeholder) - fragmented MP4s still can't be probed by this reader - but safe-and-warns beats silently corrupting the output. Properly handling them would need `moof`/`trun` parsing, a bigger addition not attempted here without first confirming from Christer whether it's worth the added complexity.

**Tests.** `test_parking_transition.py` gained one new test directly reproducing the reported failure shape: a stand-in `read_mp4_info()` returning `Mp4Info(duration_seconds=60.0, frame_count=0, width=1920, height=1080)` (usable width/height, but zero frame count) - confirms `probe_video_properties()` now raises the original ffprobe error rather than returning a `(width, height, 0.0)` tuple. All 141 tests across the five previously-touched files pass (0 failures), verified via the same hand-rolled sandbox runner.

Not yet shown to Christer - the P-file/gap symptoms should now resolve (falling back to a clean warn-and-drop instead of a broken placeholder), but this hasn't been confirmed against his own real archive yet. The "no sound" symptom from the same message is a separate, unrelated question - likely just a missing `bv-generate --extract-audio` prerequisite (`Asset.AUDIO` is a generated, not downloaded, asset - see `asset.py`; `_concatenate_asset()` silently returns `None`/skips with only a `log.step()` line in `trip.log`, not a console warning, if no recording in the trip has it), asked about directly rather than assumed - not yet confirmed either way.

## Confirmed: missing audio was a missing --extract-audio prerequisite, not a bug (this session)

Asked Christer directly via `AskUserQuestion` whether he'd run `bv-generate --extract-audio` on the archive before that export - he confirmed he hadn't. Matches the hypothesis from the previous entry exactly: `Asset.AUDIO` is generated, not downloaded, so with no recording in the trip having it yet, `_concatenate_asset()` for the audio asset returns `None` immediately (empty `sources`), and `stitch_cameras()` gets `audio_path=None` and mutes silently - no console warning, only a `log.step()` line in `trip.log` most CLI usage wouldn't think to open. No code change - this is existing, correct behavior working as designed; the fix is running `bv-generate --extract-audio` first. Also confirmed separately (same message) that the trip folder's naming - now showing the real last-included second rather than the last recording's own start timestamp - is the deliberate `Trip.end_timestamp` fix from an earlier session working as intended in a live export, not a new issue.

## Make --stitch-gsensor self-render gsensor.mp4 when missing, matching --stitch-graph (this session)

Christer, reading bv-generate's own `--translate` help text ("Implies transcription internally; --transcribe is not required"): "Do you think that same behaviour [should apply] to bv-export like that --stitch-graph should imply --gsensor-graph-video." Investigated before assuming either flag needed a change. `--stitch-graph` turned out to already work this way - its own docstring, from when it was built, explicitly says it follows "the map panel's own 'rendered fresh, at the exact panel size, grows the composite' shape rather than 'must already exist, just overlaid'" (Christer, at the time: "I want to be able to select the graph like i selects map"), and `_render_graph_panel()` calls `render_gsensor_graph_video()` directly every time, no separate flag needed. The flag that actually produced the warning Christer saw in his own real run ("gsensor.mp4 not found - run bv-export --gsensor-video first") is `--stitch-gsensor` (the dot-gauge overlay, a different feature from the graph strip) - and that one *was* a deliberate "compose only what's already there" choice from when it was built, explicitly matching how `--stitch`'s other inputs (front/rear video, audio, subtitles) all work, with the map panel called out as the one intentional exception.

Asked whether to reverse that deliberate choice for `--stitch-gsensor` specifically via `AskUserQuestion` rather than just picking one, given it directly undoes an earlier confirmed decision - Christer picked reversing it, to match `--stitch-graph`/`--translate`'s precedent.

**`trip_export.py`.** The `stitch_gsensor` block's `else` branch (candidate `gsensor.mp4` missing, but `samples` non-empty so one could be produced) now calls `render_gsensor_video()` right there - same call, same `destination / "gsensor.mp4"` path, same `duration_seconds` the earlier `render_gsensor` block above already uses - instead of appending a "go run --gsensor-video first" warning. On success, `stitch_gsensor_source` is set to the freshly-rendered path (so this run's own `stitch_cameras()` call gets the overlay immediately) and a `log.step()`/`--debug` line records it, mirroring the render-timing convention already used for the standalone gsensor/gsensor_graph phases. `render_gsensor_video()` returning `None` (its own "not enough samples/zero span" case - distinct from a `MediaToolError`) is handled as its own warning, since `samples` being non-empty here doesn't guarantee at least two samples spanning nonzero time. A `MediaToolError` from the render itself still produces a warning, just with the real exception text instead of the old fixed "not found" message. Deliberately still writes to the trip's own `destination` folder (not a discarded tempfile, unlike `--stitch-graph`'s own ephemeral panel render) - preserves the pre-existing, separately-valuable "reuse an existing gsensor.mp4 across runs" caching behavior this file already had (see task #80's own history), rather than trading it away for consistency with a feature (`--stitch-graph`) that was deliberately built without any caching at all. `ExportResult.gsensor_video` is intentionally left `None` in this path - it keeps meaning "the standalone `--gsensor-video` output was produced this run", not "a gsensor.mp4 exists on disk for any reason", so a `--stitch-gsensor`-only run's on-demand render doesn't get confused for an explicit `--gsensor-video` request when a caller inspects the result. Both the parameter docstring and the inline comment block explaining the old behavior were rewritten to describe the new one and to record why the reversal happened, rather than silently deleting the historical reasoning.

**Tests, `test_trip_export.py`.** `test_export_trip_stitch_gsensor_warns_when_gsensor_mp4_not_yet_rendered` renamed to `test_export_trip_stitch_gsensor_renders_gsensor_mp4_when_missing` and rewritten: same setup (g-sensor data present, no existing/freshly-rendered gsensor.mp4), but now asserts `dest_dir / "gsensor.mp4"` exists, `result.warnings == ()`, and `result.gsensor_video is None` (confirming the on-demand render doesn't leak into that field). New `test_export_trip_stitch_gsensor_debug_prints_when_rendering_on_demand` confirms the new `--debug` line appears. `test_export_trip_stitch_gsensor_uses_a_freshly_rendered_file` (this run's own `render_gsensor=True` producing the file `--stitch-gsensor` then picks up), `test_export_trip_stitch_gsensor_reuses_a_file_from_an_earlier_run` (a pre-existing file on disk), `test_export_trip_stitch_gsensor_warns_when_trip_has_no_gsensor_data` (no GSENSOR asset at all - still a warning, still correct, this path is unchanged), and `test_export_trip_stitch_gsensor_options_are_forwarded` (also pre-creates `gsensor.mp4`) all checked and pass unchanged - none of them exercise the "missing, and about to be rendered" branch this change touched. All tests across the six touched/related files pass via the hand-rolled sandbox runner (141 run directly, 5 skipped for needing real `capsys`) - the two new `capsys`-dependent tests (the renamed one doesn't need it, but the new debug-print test does) were additionally verified by hand with a real `contextlib.redirect_stderr` capture standing in for `capsys`, confirming `warnings == ()`, `gsensor.mp4` written, and the exact debug line text, matching what the test asserts.

Not yet shown to Christer - worth a real `--stitch --stitch-gsensor` run (without `--gsensor-video`) on an archive with g-sensor data to confirm the on-demand render produces a normal, correctly-composited overlay in practice, not just in the synthetic test/manual-check fixtures used here.

## Fix a second, quieter cause of the same "1 frame for the duration" placeholder bug (this session, follow-up real-world regression)

Christer, after the frame_count==0 fix above: "P files still show 1 frame for the duration, it shouldn't even be included by default." First confirmed exactly what he meant before touching anything, since "shouldn't even be included by default" could describe two different bugs: a *leading/trailing* Parking recording (which `_concatenate_asset()` genuinely does always include as-is, by design - see its own docstring) or a *mid-trip* one (which is supposed to go through the placeholder path unconditionally with `include_parking=False`, today's default). Asked via `AskUserQuestion`; Christer confirmed it's a mid-trip file, and that he ran with plain defaults (no `--include-parking`) - so this wasn't the leading/trailing design gap, it was the placeholder path itself still misbehaving even after the previous fix.

Re-read `probe_video_properties()` looking for a path the `frame_count > 0` fix didn't cover. Found one: that fix only lives inside `_probe_video_properties_from_boxes()`, which is only reached when ffprobe itself raises `subprocess.CalledProcessError`. But ffprobe can also exit 0 - no exception at all - while reporting `avg_frame_rate` as `"0/0"` for a stream it can't derive an average for from the header alone. `_parse_frame_rate()` already special-cases a `0` denominator by returning `0.0` rather than raising `ZeroDivisionError`, so this sailed straight through the success path untouched: real width/height, `frame_rate = 0.0`, handed to `render_parking_transition_video()` as `-r 0.0` - the exact same degenerate-placeholder symptom as the frame_count==0 bug, just reached via a different, quieter route that produces no exception for the box-reader fallback to ever catch.

**`parking_transition.py`.** `probe_video_properties()`'s success path now checks `width <= 0 or height <= 0 or frame_rate <= 0` after parsing ffprobe's JSON output; if any is true, it calls `_probe_video_properties_from_boxes()` - previously only reachable from the `except subprocess.CalledProcessError` branch - with a freshly-built error message describing the bad ffprobe result (naming the file and the literal `avg_frame_rate` value) rather than an exception object. `_probe_video_properties_from_boxes()`'s signature changed from taking a `subprocess.CalledProcessError` to taking a plain `error_message: str`, since it now has two different callers with two different kinds of "ffprobe didn't give us something usable" - the `except` branch builds its own message from `exc.stderr` (identical text to before, so existing tests asserting on that message still pass unchanged) and the new zero-check branch builds its own. The exception-chaining (`raise ... from ffprobe_error`) was dropped along with the parameter, since there's no longer always a real exception object to chain from and no test relied on `__cause__`.

**Tests.** `test_parking_transition.py` gained two new tests: `test_probe_video_properties_falls_back_to_the_box_reader_when_ffprobe_reports_zero_frame_rate` (fakes `subprocess.run` returning a *successful* `CompletedProcess` with `avg_frame_rate: "0/0"`, confirms the box-reader fallback still produces the correct `(1920, 1080, 30.0)`) and `test_probe_video_properties_raises_when_ffprobe_frame_rate_is_zero_and_box_reader_also_fails` (same `"0/0"` ffprobe result, but `read_mp4_info()` also returns `frame_count=0`, confirms it raises `MediaToolError` naming the file and mentioning `avg_frame_rate` rather than returning a bogus `0.0` result). All 143 tests across the five previously-touched files pass (0 failures, 5 skipped for needing real `capsys`), verified via the hand-rolled sandbox runner - the two new tests included.

Not yet shown to Christer - this should now cover both routes to the degenerate-placeholder bug (ffprobe failing outright, and ffprobe succeeding with an unusable frame rate), but hasn't been confirmed against his own real trip yet. If a third route turns up, worth considering whether `probe_video_properties()`'s ffprobe-success path needs a broader sanity check (e.g. also guarding against a frame_count of 0 or 1 that ffprobe itself reports, not just the box reader) rather than patching each specific symptom as it's found.

## Find and fix the real root cause: parking placeholder codec mismatch corrupting front.mp4 (this session, real-world regression - the actual fix)

The third route turned up immediately. Christer re-ran the same trip after the frame-rate fix above and reported: "Still the same, i can hear by the sound that the car is moving again, but still show the same frame, it shouldnt even be there." Rather than guess again, this time the investigation started from hard evidence instead of another theory.

First ruled out the leading/trailing-recording explanation this session had floated earlier: Christer confirmed the P-file in question is genuinely mid-trip, and his `trip.log` (uploaded on request) confirmed it directly - `20260726_144116_P` sits at position 7 of 17 recordings, flanked by real `_N` recordings on both sides, so `is_mid_trip_parking` is unambiguously `True` and the placeholder path is what's running. Also confirmed the symptom is on `front.mp4` itself (concatenation phase had already completed when Christer checked and aborted), and asked what's actually visible when it "freezes" - Christer confirmed it's real dashcam footage frozen, not the synthetic "PARKING FOOTAGE SKIPPED" placeholder image. That ruled out both remaining probing-fix theories at once (a wrong placeholder frame rate would still show the *placeholder*, just malformed).

Asked Christer to extract a short clip around the affected timestamp (computed from `trip.log`: recording starts ~959s into `front.mp4`) and share it. The `ffmpeg` re-encode log on that clip was the actual smoking gun: the real stream is `hevc (Main) (hvc1 / 0x31637668), 3840x2160` (a 4K HEVC camera) and the decode is full of `Invalid NAL unit size (1296053398 > 54200)` / `Error splitting the input into NAL units` errors starting partway through - the classic signature of one codec's raw bitstream getting spliced into a container declared as a different codec.

Root cause: `render_parking_transition_video()` (and every other `bv-export` encode path) goes through `media.py`'s shared `encode_with_nvenc_fallback()`, which was unconditionally hard-coded to H.264 (`h264_nvenc`/`libx264`) - never codec-aware. `concatenate_media()` (`export/media.py`) splices sources via ffmpeg's concat demuxer with `-c copy` - a byte-level stream copy, not a re-encode, and it does *not* validate that spliced sources share a codec. So on Christer's 4K HEVC camera, the H.264-encoded placeholder got spliced straight into a stream declared HEVC: the mux itself succeeds with no error (nothing here ever failed or warned), but no real decoder can parse the result from the splice point onward. That produces exactly what Christer described: a frozen picture (the last successfully-decoded real frame, since the decoder chokes on the corrupted bitstream from there) while the separately-muxed audio track (`audio.aac`, built by a totally independent pipeline) keeps playing normally, matching "I can hear the car moving again, but still show the same frame" precisely. This is also the true explanation for the "footage after that wasn't there for some time" symptom from *two* fixes ago in this same session - that was never actually the frame-rate bug, it was this.

Before touching any code, reproduced the bug directly and in isolation: built a small real HEVC clip and a small real H.264 clip via `ffmpeg`, spliced them with the exact same `-f concat -c copy` invocation `concatenate_media()` uses, and decoded the result - reproduced the identical `Invalid NAL unit size` errors on a minimal fixture with nothing else involved. Then re-encoded the placeholder clip as HEVC (matching the real clip) and re-spliced: clean decode, zero errors. That confirmed both the diagnosis and the fix before writing any production code, given this was already the third attempt at this specific bug and the first two (both real, but not the actual cause) had already cost Christer two more full trip re-exports.

**The fix, once confirmed: detect the source recording's own video codec and encode the placeholder to match it - the same principle `probe_video_properties()` already applies to width/height/frame_rate, extended to codec.**

**`mp4_box_reader.py`.** `Mp4Info` gained `codec: str | None = None`. New `_CODEC_FOURCC_MAP` normalizes MP4 `stsd` sample-entry fourccs to the same vocabulary ffprobe's own `codec_name` uses (`"avc1"/"avc3"` -> `"h264"`, `"hvc1"/"hev1"` -> `"hevc"`; anything else, e.g. `"mp4v"`, stays unrecognized -> `None`). New `_parse_stsd_codec()` reads a video track's `stsd` box - version/flags (4 bytes) + entry_count (4 bytes) + one sample entry per format the track uses (a BlackVue recording only ever has one), and the entry's own box-shaped header's 4-character type *is* the codec fourcc, so it's read with the existing `_iter_boxes()` helper offset by 8 bytes into `stsd`'s payload. `read_mp4_info()`'s existing video-track loop now also looks up that track's own `stsd` (a sibling of `stsz` within `stbl`) and records the codec if parseable - non-fatal like every other optional field this reader has, same "caller decides if partial info is still useful" treatment `tkhd`/`stsz` already get.

**`media.py`.** `encode_with_nvenc_fallback()` gained a keyword-only `video_codec: str = "h264"` parameter. New `_VIDEO_CODEC_ENCODERS` maps `"h264"` -> `(h264_nvenc, libx264, [])` and `"hevc"` -> `(hevc_nvenc, libx265, [-tag:v hvc1])` - the `hvc1` tag matches what BlackVue's own HEVC recordings actually use (confirmed directly from the real `ffprobe` output above), since ffmpeg's own `libx265`/`hevc_nvenc` default to the different (also valid, but non-matching) `hev1` tag otherwise, which risks the exact same kind of splice mismatch this whole fix exists to avoid. `_nvenc_available()` itself was left unchanged (still only ever checks for `h264_nvenc`) rather than adding a second cached capability check for `hevc_nvenc` - a machine with the former but not the latter just costs one wasted NVENC attempt before falling through to the CPU encoder, the same safety net an unavailable/broken `h264_nvenc` already relies on; not worth the churn against the dozen existing tests that monkeypatch `_NVENC_AVAILABLE` directly as a plain bool. Every other existing caller (`map_video.py`, `gsensor_video.py`, `stitch.py`) doesn't pass `video_codec` at all, so they're all unaffected - `"h264"` remains the default exactly as before this existed.

**`parking_transition.py`.** `probe_video_properties()` now returns `(width, height, frame_rate, codec)` - a 4-tuple, up from 3 - reading `codec_name` in the same ffprobe call (no extra subprocess) on the success path, normalized against a new `_RECOGNIZED_CODECS = ("h264", "hevc")` tuple (anything else becomes `None`, same "fall back to the H.264 default" treatment as a codec that couldn't be read at all). `_probe_video_properties_from_boxes()` (the ffprobe-fallback helper, already touched twice this session) now also returns `info.codec` from the box reader - and, importantly, an unreadable/unrecognized codec there is *not* treated as fatal the way a bad width/height/frame_count already is, since a placeholder can still be produced (just H.264-default) even without codec info, whereas it can't be produced at all without real dimensions. `render_parking_transition_video()`/`_render_from_clip()` both gained a `codec: str = "h264"` parameter, threaded straight through to `encode_with_nvenc_fallback(..., video_codec=codec)`. `ParkingTransitionCache.video_for()` now unpacks all four probe values, defaults a `None` codec to `"h264"`, and folds codec into the render-cache key (`(width, height, frame_rate, codec)`, up from three fields) - two Parking recordings at the same resolution/frame rate but different codecs now correctly get two separate cached placeholders rather than one wrongly shared between them.

**Tests.** `test_mp4_box_reader.py`: new `_stsd()` fixture helper and a `codec_fourcc` kwarg on `_video_trak()`; four new tests covering H.264 detection, HEVC detection, an unrecognized fourcc, and a missing `stsd` box entirely. `test_parking_transition.py`: `_make_video()` gained a `codec` kwarg (`"libx265"` tagged `hvc1` for HEVC fixtures); every existing 3-tuple unpack of `probe_video_properties()` updated to 4-tuple; new tests covering codec detection via both ffprobe and the box-reader fallback, `render_parking_transition_video()` actually encoding the requested codec (verified by re-probing its own output), `ParkingTransitionCache` producing genuinely separate cached placeholders for same-resolution-different-codec sources - and, most importantly, `test_parking_transition_cache_video_for_hevc_splice_decodes_cleanly`, which builds real HEVC "before"/"after" clips, gets a real codec-matched placeholder from a real `ParkingTransitionCache`, splices all three with the real `concatenate_media()`, and then actually *decodes* the result with `ffmpeg -f null -`, asserting zero stderr output - the first test in this codebase that verifies bitstream-level playability rather than just metadata, which is exactly the class of bug every other assertion in this file would have missed. `test_trip_export.py` gained the same kind of test one layer up, at the full `export_trip()` level: `test_export_trip_hevc_camera_front_video_decodes_cleanly_after_parking_placeholder` builds a 3-recording trip entirely in HEVC, runs a real export with a mid-trip Parking recording, and decode-checks the real `front.mp4` output. All 154 tests across the six touched/related files pass (0 failures, 5 skipped for needing real `capsys`), verified via the hand-rolled sandbox runner - run in per-file/per-chunk batches this time since the suite's own runtime (real HEVC encodes are slower than the H.264 fixtures used everywhere else) started exceeding the sandbox's 45-second per-command limit.

Not yet confirmed against Christer's own real archive - but unlike the previous two attempts, this one was verified against an actual reproduction of the real bitstream corruption (both in an isolated minimal fixture and at the full `export_trip()` level) before being reported as fixed, specifically because the first two attempts turned out to be real-but-insufficient fixes for a different, deeper problem.

## Find the real, deeper root cause (SPS/PPS parameter sets) and remove the parking-placeholder feature entirely (2026-07-27)

The codec-matching fix above (commit `34c2833`) was real and necessary, but Christer reported the corruption **still happening** after a fresh export with it applied and every previous export wiped - confirmed with a screenshot of severe visual corruption in his media player, and his own description: "Both media player and vlc hangs a couple of seconds then the rest of the video looks like this at the timestamp 144115." This meant a real, complete fix from the previous entry still wasn't sufficient - so, rather than guess a third time, the investigation again started from direct evidence, this time gathered step by step with Christer running isolated Python snippets against his own real files (not synthetic fixtures) and reporting the exact output back.

That evidence established, in order: (1) ffprobe still fails outright on the real source file itself, with a *different* error than before ("contradictionary STSC and STCO") - a known, longstanding ffmpeg/BlackVue Parking-mode-container compatibility quirk, not per-file corruption (other players open these files fine); (2) `read_mp4_info()`'s own box reader correctly detects `codec='hevc'` on the real file despite ffprobe's failure; (3) `probe_video_properties()` and `render_parking_transition_video()` correctly produce a genuinely valid, standalone HEVC placeholder file from that; but (4) splicing that real placeholder together with the real neighboring camera segments via the real `concatenate_media()` and decode-checking the result **still reproduces corruption** - with new error signatures this time ("No ref lists in the SPS", "Zero refs for a frame with P or B slices", non-monotonic DTS) rather than the "Invalid NAL unit size" the codec-mismatch fix had already eliminated.

**Root cause, the real one this time:** this was never just a codec-*name* mismatch (already fixed correctly) - it's a deeper MP4/HEVC structural limitation. `hvc1`-tagged tracks (the tagging BlackVue's own cameras use, and the tagging the codec-matching fix deliberately replicated) declare a track's SPS/PPS/VPS parameter sets **once, at the container level**, in the `hvcC` box - not per-sample, not per-segment. Two files are only splice-compatible via a raw stream copy (`concatenate_media()`'s `-c copy`, never a re-encode) if their raw bitstream data was produced against the *same* declared parameter sets - which in practice means the *same encoder session*. Real BlackVue camera segments splice together cleanly because they all originate from one continuous hardware-encoder session with a fixed firmware configuration; a placeholder rendered by `bv-export`'s own `libx265`/`hevc_nvenc` encoder is a **separate** encoder session, with its own parameter sets, even when the codec name, resolution, frame rate, and `hvc1` tag all match exactly. `ffmpeg`'s concat demuxer performs zero validation of this, so the mux itself always "succeeds" with no error - the failure only surfaces at actual decode time, exactly matching every symptom Christer had reported across all three attempts at this bug.

Explained this to Christer directly (not as a foregone conclusion - laid out what a full fix would require: decode-and-re-encode the *entire* front/rear video whenever a placeholder is spliced in, not just the placeholder itself, since any boundary between "our encoder's output" and "the camera's untouched original" is unsafe for stream copy regardless of which side of the splice you look from). He initially chose the correct-but-expensive option ("re-encode front/rear whenever a placeholder is used"), then reversed once he'd weighed the actual cost against the benefit: "I changed my mind again, we don't want time consuming stuff if it not gives us something great back. Just skip it alltogether." He also asked directly whether the same risk applies to his own Kling-AI-generated "no parking" clips (the bundled random-pool feature) - confirmed yes, identically: any independently-encoded content, regardless of source, faces the same SPS/PPS incompatibility when stream-copy-spliced against real camera footage.

**Final decision (confirmed via two rounds of `AskUserQuestion`):** `include_parking=False` (the default, unchanged) now drops **every** Parking-mode recording from `front.mp4`/`rear.mp4`/`audio.aac` - leading, trailing, or mid-trip alike - with **no synthetic placeholder substituted anywhere**. This unifies what had been two different behaviors (leading/trailing recordings always kept as-is; only mid-trip recordings replaced with a transition clip) into one simple rule, matching Christer's own reasoning for the leading/trailing case from earlier this session: Parking mode typically takes a couple of minutes to activate, so a trip's real ending is very likely already captured before a trailing Parking recording begins, and only a few seconds might be missed exiting Parking mode at the start. `include_parking=True` is unaffected - raw, unmodified camera footage has no splicing-incompatible synthetic content involved and was never the source of any of this. Since there is no longer any legitimate use for synthetically rendering and splicing placeholder content into camera footage, Christer also chose (over "leave it dormant") to **remove the entire placeholder-rendering feature from the codebase**, rather than carry forward now-permanently-unreachable code.

**Removed entirely:** `src/blackvue/export/parking_transition.py` (the whole module - `ParkingTransitionCache`, `render_parking_transition_video()`/`_render_from_clip()`, `probe_video_properties()`, the procedural "PARKING FOOTAGE SKIPPED" frame renderer, `RANDOM_PARKING_TRANSITION_POOL`, `DEFAULT_PARKING_TRANSITION_CLIPS`) and its test file `tests/blackvue/export/test_parking_transition.py`; the six bundled Kling-generated `no_parking_1.mp4`-`no_parking_6.mp4` clips from `src/blackvue/export/assets/`; the CLI flags `--parking-transition-image`/`--parking-transition-clip`/`--parking-transition-random` (and the now-dead `--parking-transition-standard` procedural-frame concept, which was always the default and needed no flag of its own) from `bv_export.py`, along with their mutual-exclusion validation, per-trip random-pick wiring, and the now-unused `random` import. `media.py`'s `encode_with_nvenc_fallback()` lost the `video_codec` parameter and `_VIDEO_CODEC_ENCODERS` map added by the previous entry's fix - both existed solely to serve the now-deleted placeholder renderer, and reverting them removes genuinely dead code rather than leaving an unreachable HEVC-encode path behind (`mp4_box_reader.py`'s own codec-detection addition from that same fix was **kept**, since it's genuinely useful standalone diagnostic infrastructure - Christer used it directly, by hand, to help diagnose this very bug). `pyproject.toml`'s `blackvue.export` package-data glob dropped `assets/*.mp4` (no `.mp4` assets remain in that folder; `.png`/`.ttf`/`.txt` entries untouched).

**`trip_export.py`.** `_concatenate_asset()` simplified from a `0 < index < last_index` mid-trip check plus a `_parking_transition_source()` placeholder-lookup helper (itself removed, along with the now-unused `_SIBLING_VIDEO_ASSET` sibling-probe-fallback mapping) down to one uniform condition: `if recording.id.is_parking and not include_parking: continue` - skip the recording's contribution to this asset entirely, at any position, full stop. The `ParkingTransitionCache` instantiation/`tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` wiring in `export_trip()` (previously scoped around the three `_concatenate_asset()` calls, with its own try/finally cleanup) was removed along with the now-unused `tempfile` import. `export_trip()`'s signature dropped `parking_transition_image`/`parking_transition_clip`; `include_parking` itself is unchanged. Docstrings in both `trip_export.py` and `bv_export.py` rewritten to describe the new uniform behavior and to record, briefly, why the old placeholder approach was abandoned (for anyone reading the code later without this WORKING_CONTEXT.md entry in front of them).

**Tests.** `test_trip_export.py`: the mid-trip replace-with-placeholder test rewritten as `test_export_trip_drops_a_mid_trip_parking_recording_entirely` (asserts the real 6-second Parking segment is gone with nothing substituted, not shortened to a 3-second placeholder); the sibling-camera-fallback and HEVC-splice-decodes-cleanly tests removed outright (they tested mechanisms - sibling probing, codec-matched re-encoding of synthetic content - that no longer exist); the leading/trailing "left untouched" tests rewritten as "dropped" (`test_export_trip_drops_a_parking_recording_at_the_trip_start`/`_end`); the matching-silence-swap audio test rewritten as `test_export_trip_drops_a_skipped_parking_recordings_audio_too` (asserts the recording's audio is dropped too, nothing substituted); the three `parking_transition_image`/`clip`/priority-override tests removed outright. `_make_video()`'s `codec` parameter (added for the HEVC fixture the deleted test needed) reverted, no longer having any caller. `test_bv_export.py` (CLI layer): the entire block of `--parking-transition-*` flag/random-pool tests removed (`test_main_forwards_parking_transition_image/clip`, the three pairwise-rejection tests, the random-default/random-flag tests, `_parking_archive()`'s five dependent tests covering the plain-frame-default/random-pick/pool-membership/per-flag-priority/fresh-pick-per-trip behaviors) - the two `include_parking` flag tests themselves were kept, trimmed of their now-removed `parking_transition_*` assertions. The now-unused `DEFAULT_PARKING_TRANSITION_CLIPS`/`RANDOM_PARKING_TRANSITION_POOL` imports and the `bv_export_module.random` monkeypatches that went with them were removed.

Verified in stages rather than one long run, working around the sandbox's 45-second-per-command limit: `python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(...)"` against every touched file first to catch syntax errors immediately; then `test_mp4_box_reader.py` and `test_export_media.py` in full (26 tests, 0 failures); then all five new/rewritten parking-specific tests in `test_trip_export.py` individually (5/5 pass); then the *entire* `test_bv_export.py` module (104 remaining test functions after the removal, run in six batches of ~15-22 each to stay under the time limit) - 99 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped (real-`capsys`-only tests the sandbox's hand-rolled harness can't run, unrelated to this change); then the *entire* `test_trip_export.py` module the same way (70 test functions across five batches) - 65 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped (same `capsys` limitation). Zero failures across every test actually run.

Not yet shown to Christer - the fix (drop, don't synthesize) is a deliberate simplification he confirmed twice over (once for the mechanism, once for removing the now-dead code), but a real re-export against his own HEVC archive would still be worth doing to confirm `front.mp4`/`rear.mp4` decode cleanly end-to-end with no further surprises, now that no synthetic content is ever spliced into camera footage at all.

## Auto-detect and trim front/rear duration mismatches (this session, direct follow-up)

Christer ran a real export after the parking-placeholder removal above and reported a new symptom: "after the mid P file, the rear view footage is not in synch with the front camera anymore." Rather than guess, this followed the same discipline as the placeholder investigation - real evidence first. His `trip.log` showed all three assets (front.mp4/rear.mp4/audio.aac) concatenated from the same 15 recordings, ruling out an asymmetric-drop bug in the removal above. A diagnostic ffprobe script (front vs. rear duration for every recording ID in the trip) run against his real archive then isolated the actual cause: `20260726_145159_E` - an Event-triggered recording, unrelated to Parking mode entirely - had front=34.9s against rear=179.8s, a 144.9s gap that alone accounted for the reported 2:17 desync (net of the ~1s of ordinary jitter every other recording in the trip showed). Christer confirmed by hand: "The file was full size like 3 minutes, but length only 34 seconds. So i removed it from archive and redownloaded it. Now its 3 minutes." A corrupted/truncated download, not a bug in `bv-export` itself - but nothing in the pipeline had any way to notice or correct a mismatch like this from any cause, so Christer asked for a general defensive fix regardless of root cause: "Good idea to sync front and rear."

He first asked whether the shorter side could just be extended instead ("Cant you just extend the shorter clip a little or are we breaking everything then?") - explained this would carry the exact same risk just removed above: padding a file means splicing in content from a different encoder session (anything `bv-export` could generate to fill the gap), the same SPS/PPS parameter-set incompatibility that corrupted the Parking placeholder. Trimming the *longer* side instead is safe, because a plain stream-copy trim only ever removes real bytes from a file that's already one continuous, valid encoder session - no foreign content is introduced. Confirmed via two rounds of `AskUserQuestion`: **"warn and auto-trim"** the longer side down to match the shorter one, with a **5-second tolerance** (his own choice, given every ordinary recording in his real trip.log varied by under 1s on its own).

**`media.py`.** Added `trim_media(source, destination, duration_seconds)`: `ffmpeg -i source -t duration_seconds -c copy destination`, raising `MediaToolError` on failure (missing ffmpeg, or the underlying `ffmpeg` process itself failing) - same error-handling shape as `concatenate_media()`/`encode_with_nvenc_fallback()` in the same file.

**`trip_export.py`.** Added `FRONT_REAR_DURATION_TOLERANCE_SECONDS = 5.0` and `_align_front_rear_durations(trip, work_dir, warnings, log, *, include_parking, tolerance_seconds=...)`: for each recording with both a FRONT and REAR asset (skipping Parking recordings entirely when `include_parking` is False, since they're dropped regardless; skipping a recording missing either side, or one `probe()` can't read), probes both durations and, when they differ by more than the tolerance, calls `trim_media()` on the longer side into a scratch `work_dir`, recording the trimmed path in a `{(recording id, asset): trimmed path}` map and appending a warning describing the mismatch and which side was trimmed (to both `trip.log`, via `TripLog.warning()`, and the run's own `warnings` list/exit-code-relevant output). A `trim_media()` failure for one recording produces its own warning and is skipped, rather than aborting the whole export. `_concatenate_asset()` gained a `duration_overrides` keyword parameter: when building its `sources` list, it now checks the override map first for each `(recording id, asset)` pair and falls back to the recording's own real file only if no override exists - so a trimmed file transparently stands in for the real one during concatenation, with no other code needing to know alignment happened. `export_trip()`'s concatenation phase now opens a `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="bv_export_align_")` (the `tempfile` import, dropped by the placeholder-removal entry above, came back for this) around the existing `ThreadPoolExecutor` block, calls `_align_front_rear_durations()` first to build the overrides map, then passes it into the FRONT and REAR `_concatenate_asset()` calls (not AUDIO - this feature is video-only, matching the reported bug). The scratch directory's lifetime is scoped to just the concatenation phase, since no later phase reads the aligned files directly.

**Tests.** `test_export_media.py`: `test_trim_media_shortens_a_real_video_via_stream_copy` (a real 5s ffmpeg-generated video trimmed to under 3s, not mocked) and `test_trim_media_raises_when_the_source_does_not_exist`. `test_trip_export.py`: four unit tests calling `_align_front_rear_durations()` directly - a >5s mismatch trims the longer side and produces exactly one warning naming which side; a <5s mismatch (3.0s vs 3.2s) leaves both files and the warnings list untouched; a Parking recording is skipped without probing when `include_parking=False`; a recording missing one side is left alone without error - plus one end-to-end `test_export_trip_aligns_a_mismatched_front_rear_recording` confirming the full `export_trip()` wiring: a single recording with front=2s/rear=10s comes out of a real export with `front.mp4` at ~2s, `rear.mp4` trimmed to match, and exactly one warning in the result.

Verified in three batches (mp4_box_reader+export_media, trip_export, bv_export) to stay under the sandbox's 45-second-per-command limit, after first syntax-checking both touched source files: 28 passed / 0 failed (mp4_box_reader + export_media, includes the two new trim_media tests); 70 passed / 0 failed / 5 skipped (trip_export, `capsys`-only tests the sandbox's hand-rolled harness can't run, same pre-existing limitation as every prior verification pass this session); 99 passed / 0 failed / 5 skipped (bv_export). Zero failures across 197 tests actually run. `docs/man/bv-export.md` updated with a new "Front/rear duration alignment" subsection under Parking footage, and the `front.mp4`/`rear.mp4` output-table row now mentions the auto-trim behavior.

Not yet re-run against Christer's own archive - his specific triggering case is already fixed by the redownload, so this is purely a defensive addition for any future recurrence (a similarly corrupted download, or a camera-side front/rear frame-count divergence during Parking mode, which he raised as a plausible future cause).

## Drop the 5-second alignment tolerance - trim every recording exactly (this session, direct follow-up)

The tolerance above didn't survive first contact with a real export. Christer ran one and reported: "stitch file is 40:48, just like front, rear is 40:40, no trim is done." A `trip.log` he uploaded to show it turned out to predate the feature entirely (dated 2026-07-23, four days before the alignment code above was written and committed on 2026-07-27) - so it couldn't have shown a trim either way, and wasn't evidence about whether the shipped code works. But the *shape* of his report was the real signal regardless: an 8-second front/rear gap (and `stitch.mp4` following `front.mp4`'s longer length, since `stitch.py` composites whatever `front.mp4`/`rear.mp4` it's handed) with nothing in `trip.log` about a trim ever firing. The 5-second-tolerance design from the previous entry only compares each recording's own front/rear pair in isolation - it has no way to notice that many individually-small, individually-"within-tolerance" gaps can add up across a whole trip to something much larger than any one of them. A trip with, say, ten recordings each running 0.8s longer on the front side (never remotely close to the 5s skip threshold) would silently accumulate exactly this: 8 seconds of overall desync with `_align_front_rear_durations()` never once triggering.

Christer's fix, stated directly once this became clear: "Best is to trim every recording." Confirmed via `AskUserQuestion` on one remaining open question - since every recording now gets trimmed whenever its front/rear pair differs at all, should `trip.log` record every single trim regardless of size, or only ones large enough to be worth noticing? He chose **log every trim, any size** - no threshold, full visibility into what's being adjusted on every export.

**`trip_export.py`.** `FRONT_REAR_DURATION_TOLERANCE_SECONDS = 5.0` replaced with `FRONT_REAR_DURATION_EPSILON_SECONDS = 0.01` - no longer a "skip small real differences" tolerance at all, just a floating-point-noise guard so two recordings ffprobe reports as differing by a thousandth of a second (measurement noise, not a real gap) don't trigger a pointless trim-and-log cycle on every single recording of every export. `_align_front_rear_durations()`'s `tolerance_seconds` parameter renamed to `epsilon_seconds` to match, and its docstring rewritten to explain the accumulation gap directly rather than describing a deliberate skip window. The trim-and-warn message format bumped from one decimal place to two (`.1f` → `.2f`), since sub-second gaps are now the common case being logged, not just the dramatic multi-second ones from the corrupted-download case that originally motivated this feature.

**Tests.** `test_trip_export.py`: `test_align_front_rear_durations_leaves_pairs_within_tolerance_alone` (front=3.0s, rear=3.2s, previously asserted no trim under the 5s tolerance) replaced with two tests reflecting the new behavior - `test_align_front_rear_durations_trims_even_a_small_real_difference` (the same 3.0s/3.2s pair now *does* trim, asserting the override map and warning both show up for a gap far smaller than the old 5s threshold) and `test_align_front_rear_durations_ignores_sub_epsilon_float_noise` (two identically-generated 3.0s videos, confirming the epsilon guard still exists for genuine measurement noise rather than trimming on every recording of every trip regardless of whether front and rear actually match). The other four alignment tests (large-mismatch trim, Parking-skip, missing-one-side, and the end-to-end `export_trip()` integration test) needed no changes - none of them depended on the old tolerance's skip behavior. `docs/man/bv-export.md`'s "Front/rear duration alignment" section and the `front.mp4`/`rear.mp4` output-table row rewritten to describe always-trim-if-different instead of the 5-second threshold, with a short explanation of why the tolerance was dropped.

Verified the same way as the previous entry, in three batches to stay under the sandbox's per-command time limit: 28 passed / 0 failed (mp4_box_reader + export_media, unaffected by this change); 71 passed / 0 failed / 5 skipped (trip_export - one more passing test than before, from the tolerance test being replaced by two); 99 passed / 0 failed / 5 skipped (bv_export, unaffected). Zero failures across 198 tests actually run.

**Confirmed working against Christer's real archive.** He re-ran `bv-export --overwrite` for `test_trip_20260721_124108_20260721_124710` (a real 3-recording trip, not a synthetic fixture) and got back a fresh `trip.log` showing exactly the accumulation pattern this entry describes: three recordings, each with its own front/rear gap under a second (0.54s, 0.67s, 0.84s - every one of them front running long), every single one caught and trimmed. Before the fix, front totaled 543.00s (3 × 181.00s) against rear's 540.95s - a 2.05s gap that the previous 5-second-tolerance design would have missed entirely, since no individual recording came anywhere near 5s. After: front and rear both land at exactly 540.95s.

**Confirmed on the actual trip behind the original report.** He then re-ran `trip_20260726_142517_20260726_154431` itself - the real ~40-minute, 15-recording trip his original "stitch file is 40:48, rear is 40:40" report was about. The math lines up exactly: summing all 15 recordings' front durations from the fresh `trip.log` gives 2448.58s (40:48.58 - matching "40:48"); summing rear gives 2440.38s (40:40.38 - matching "40:40"). Every one of the 15 recordings shows its own front/rear gap between 0.07s and 0.97s, front always the longer side, every one caught and trimmed by the now-tolerance-free alignment check - none would have tripped the old 5-second threshold individually, yet together they accounted for the full 8.2-second gap he originally saw between `front.mp4` and `rear.mp4` (and, downstream, `stitch.mp4` and every stitch panel built from them). With every recording aligned, `front.mp4` now lands at 2440.38s, identical to `rear.mp4`. This closes the loop on the original bug report with the exact trip and exact numbers involved, not just a smaller stand-in.

## Investigate poor Thai->English --translate quality (this session, no code change)

Christer: "The translation from Thai to english is really bad, i checked with googletranslate and then i could ubderstand it." `--translate` uses argos-translate exclusively (`translate()` in `speech.py`), a deliberate offline/private-by-default choice from earlier in this project - no cloud calls, nothing leaves the machine. Before touching that design, checked whether the Thai quality gap was actually fixable within argos-translate itself: fetched the real package index directly (`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/argosopentech/argospm-index/main/index.json`, the same index `bv-lang install`/`get_available_packages()` reads from) and confirmed there is exactly one Thai<->English package published - version 1.9, a direct pair with no pivot-language routing involved (which would have been a separate, fixable source of quality loss). Whatever Christer already has installed via `bv-lang install th en` is almost certainly this same, only, latest version - there's no newer or better-quality package to switch to within argos-translate's own ecosystem.

Presented two real alternatives via `AskUserQuestion`: trying Meta's NLLB-200 model instead (offline via `ctranslate2` - the same inference engine `faster-whisper` already depends on in this project - purpose-built for lower-resource languages including Thai, generally rated well ahead of Argos's Marian-based models for exactly this kind of pair, at the cost of a new dependency and a multi-GB one-time model download), or reconsidering the online Google Translate option from earlier in this conversation now that there's no offline upgrade path left. Christer chose neither - **accept argos-translate's Thai quality as the current ceiling**, no code change. Noted here so this doesn't get re-investigated from scratch next time it comes up: the 1.9 package really is the best offline option available today, and the two upgrade paths (NLLB-200 offline, Google Translate online) are both still live options if he changes his mind later.

## Move the map's speed/timestamp text closer to the left edge (this session)

Christer, from a real narrow `--stitch-map` vertical panel at its default size: the timestamp's seconds weren't showing - his own read: "try to move as far left as possible." The text (`render_frame()` in `map_render.py`, drawn via `draw.multiline_text()`) was anchored at `x=margin`, the same `DEFAULT_MARGIN_PX` (24px) also used to frame the route/roads projection - fine on the default 640px-wide `map.mp4`, but on a much narrower vertical stitch panel a fixed 18px font rendering a 19-character `"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"` string easily runs past the right edge, and PIL draws off-canvas silently rather than clipping or wrapping - the tail of the line (the seconds) simply isn't part of the image.

Added `TEXT_MARGIN_PX = 10` (matching `GPS_BADGE_MARGIN_PX`'s own small-badge inset) as a separate constant from `DEFAULT_MARGIN_PX`, and pointed the timestamp/speed text's own x-coordinate at it instead of the shared `margin` parameter - the route/roads projection margin is untouched, so this only tightens the text's own left inset, buying back real width for the line on a narrow panel without changing how full-bleed the map background itself looks. Only the x-position changed; the y-position (bottom offset) still uses the shared `margin`, since Christer's report was specifically about the line running out horizontally, not vertical placement.

Tests added to `test_map_render.py`: one renders a frame with and without `timestamp_text` and confirms the leftmost pixel column where they differ is inside the old `DEFAULT_MARGIN_PX` (proving the text now starts left of where the previous shared-margin code would have put it, without pinning an exact pixel offset that font rendering/AA could make brittle across environments); a second, trivial one just asserts `TEXT_MARGIN_PX < DEFAULT_MARGIN_PX` so the two constants can never silently converge and undo the fix. Verified: the new `test_map_render` module in full (26 passed, 0 failed) plus the three other modules touched earlier this session to confirm no cross-module regressions (28 + 71/5 skipped + 99/5 skipped) - 224 tests run, zero failures.

Christer also flagged the GPS satellite badge (top-right corner) as visually oversized relative to its own background circle - but explicitly said he likes the effect ("gives a nice effect when signal part is outside of the circle"), so this is a note for the record, not something to fix.

## Analyze DR900S-2CH firmware for its web server API, build bv-live (this session)

Christer uploaded the camera's own firmware update package (`dr900s-2ch-v1.009-eng.zip`) and asked what calls could be made to its web server - `blackvue_live.cgi`, `blackvue_vod.cgi`, etc. This is reverse-engineering of his own hardware for interoperability, the same spirit as the rest of this project. Unpacked it layer by layer in the sandbox (SD-card layout -> `patch_DR900S.bin`, a gzip+tar'd full Linux rootfs for the camera's Hi3559 SoC) to reach the real web server: **Boa** (`/res/System/boa`), whose runtime config main_app writes to `/tmp/boa.conf` is fully readable as a string inside `main_app`'s own binary - `Port 80`, `DocumentRoot /res/System/www`, `AuthType None` (no authentication at all on any of this). All four CGI binaries (`blackvue_live.cgi`, `blackvue_livedata.cgi`, `blackvue_vod.cgi`, `upload.cgi`) were compiled with debug symbols intact, making `strings` unusually informative.

Findings reported to Christer: `blackvue_live.cgi` streams MJPEG (`?direction=R` for rear, front by default); `blackvue_vod.cgi` returns a plain-text file listing (`v:1.00` + `n:<path>,s:<bytes>` per line) with no query parameters, actual downloads being plain HTTP GETs against `/Record/<filename>` (a symlink straight in the doc root); `upload.cgi` accepts multipart POSTs for config/firmware upload; and `blackvue_livedata.cgi` streams live JSON telemetry as a never-ending `multipart/x-mixed-replace` sequence, alternating between `{"GPS":{"LATITUDE":..,"LONGITUDE":..}}` and `{"3G":{"FrontRear":..,"LeftRight":..,"UpperLower":..}}` objects - GPS and g-sensor only, nothing else, and no `valid`/fix-quality flag on the GPS object itself.

Christer then asked for a `bv-*`-style command to pull the camera's current GPS live and print it in Google Maps format plus a reverse-geocoded address (like `trip_info.txt` already does). Confirmed two design points via `AskUserQuestion`: command name (**`bv-live <id>`**, chosen over `bv-gps` to leave room for other live readings later) and the "Google Maps format" line (**both** a pasteable `lat,lon` coordinate pair and a clickable `https://www.google.com/maps?q=...` URL, one per line).

Discovered the project already has camera-network infrastructure from `bv-download`/`bv-config` to build on: `BlackVueClient` (`core/blackvue_client.py`, already has `vod()`/`config()`/`snapshot()`/`download()`), `core/connection.py`'s `connect(endpoints, timeout)` (tries each configured endpoint in order, returns the first that answers), and `core/camera_config.py`'s saved `CameraConfig`/`Endpoint` list from `bv-config`. `bv-live` reuses all of it rather than inventing a new connection path.

**`parser/livedata.py`** (new). `parse_gps_fix(text) -> (lat, lon) | None`: a plain regex search for `"GPS":{"LATITUDE":.., "LONGITUDE":..}` within a chunk of raw response text, deliberately not a full multipart parser - robust against the object landing anywhere in whatever a socket read happens to hand back, including split across two reads (returns `None` until the whole object is present in the accumulated buffer), and indifferent to the surrounding `--ptaboundary`/`Content-Type`/`Content-Length` framing.

**`domain/live_gps_fix.py`** (new). `LiveGpsFix(latitude, longitude)`, frozen dataclass, with a `has_fix` property that's `False` only for exactly `(0.0, 0.0)` - `blackvue_livedata.cgi`'s JSON has no explicit valid/invalid flag (confirmed from the CGI's own `strings` output), so `(0.0, 0.0)` (a real-world impossible reading for anywhere Christer's car would be) is the only practical signal that the camera currently has no fix, standing in for it rather than ever printing that as a real location.

**`core/blackvue_client.py`.** New `NoGpsDataError(RuntimeError)` and `BlackVueClient.live_gps() -> LiveGpsFix`. `blackvue_livedata.cgi` never closes its own connection (same never-ending `multipart/x-mixed-replace` shape as the MJPEG feed) - a plain `.read()` would hang forever, so `live_gps()` reads in bounded 4096-byte chunks into a growing buffer, re-parsing with `parse_gps_fix()` after each read and returning as soon as one full GPS object appears, up to a `LIVE_GPS_MAX_BYTES = 65536` cap before giving up with `NoGpsDataError` - a protocol-level failure (stream never yielded anything readable), kept distinct from `LiveGpsFix.has_fix` being `False` (a normal reading that just says "no fix right now").

**`cli/bv_live.py`** (new). `bv-live ID [--config-dir DIR] [--timeout SECONDS] [--no-address]` - loads the camera config, `connect()`s to the first live endpoint, calls `live_gps()`, and prints `Coordinates: lat,lon`, `Google Maps: https://www.google.com/maps?q=lat,lon`, and (unless `--no-address`) an `Address:` line via `export/geocoding.py`'s existing `reverse_geocode()` (the same Nominatim call `trip_info.txt` uses - not cached here, since a live position changes every call anyway and caching a moving point wouldn't help). A Nominatim failure degrades to `Address: unavailable (...)` rather than aborting the whole command, matching `reverse_geocode()`'s own "purely cosmetic, don't let it block real data" spirit. Exit codes: 0 OK, 1 config error (including "no endpoints configured", mirroring `bv-download`), 2 camera unreachable, 3 camera reachable but no GPS fix currently, 4 `blackvue_livedata.cgi` never yielded a readable GPS object. Registered as `bv-live = "blackvue.cli.bv_live:main"` in `pyproject.toml`.

**Tests.** `tests/blackvue/parser/test_livedata.py` (new): plain object, 3G-only chunk -> `None`, object cut off mid-way -> `None`, negative coordinates, multipart framing noise ignored, GPS object found after a 3G object. `tests/blackvue/core/test_blackvue_client.py`: four new tests reusing the file's existing `_fake_urlopen`/`_FakeResponse` fixtures - a normal reading, a reading split across multiple 4096-byte reads (padded past the chunk size to force it), a `(0.0, 0.0)` reading correctly returning `has_fix=False` rather than raising, and `NoGpsDataError` when the stream never yields a GPS object. `tests/blackvue/cli/test_bv_live.py` (new): `coordinate_pair()`/`google_maps_url()` formatting, `parse_args()` defaults/flags, and five `_run()`-level tests (mirroring `test_bv_export.py`'s `monkeypatch.setattr(module, name, fake)` pattern, since `test_bv_download.py` only has pure-function tests to follow) covering the happy path, `--no-address`, a Nominatim failure degrading gracefully, the no-fix exit code, the protocol-error exit code, and the no-endpoints-configured config error.

**Verification note.** This session's sandbox came up fresh with no installed project dependencies and no PyPI network access (`pip install -e .` and even `pip install pytest` both failed with a proxy 403 - an environment limitation, not a code problem), so the usual `pytest` runs this file has documented all session weren't possible here. Every new test was instead run by hand: a small script imports each test module directly (stubbing only `pytest.raises` and, for the CLI test, Python 3.10's missing `tomllib` - the project itself targets 3.11+, confirmed by `camera_config.py`'s own unconditional `import tomllib`) and calls every `test_*` function with real `monkeypatch`/`capsys`-equivalent fixtures built for this purpose. All 6 parser tests, all 8 client tests (4 new + 4 pre-existing, confirming no regression), and all 10 CLI tests passed. This is a real, if improvised, verification - not a skip - but it's not the same as a real `pytest` run against the project's actual configured environment, and `bv-live` itself has not been run against Christer's actual camera yet.

## Compare firmware v1.009 vs v1.015 for web API lockdown (this session, no code change)
