Explained it's closed-source, but that pulling the compiled Android APK and running the same `strings`-based static analysis already used repeatedly on the camera's own firmware was feasible in principle, with real caveats (app-store ToS reverse-engineering restrictions unlike analyzing your own owned hardware; downloading a third-party file needs explicit permission; unknown whether this sandbox has APK tooling) - recommended a phone packet capture instead as the cleaner option. Christer uploaded the actual APK bundle himself (`comb.blackvuec_4.27-42702...apkm`, an APKMirror multi-arch/DPI split bundle) rather than asking me to fetch one, which sidesteps the download-permission question entirely - I only read/extracted a file he provided directly.

**What was found:** unzipped the `.apkm` -> `base.apk` (107MB, has the actual code) -> its four `classes*.dex` files (~35MB total, Dalvik bytecode) -> ran `strings -n 4` and grepped for `.cgi`/`blackvue_`/endpoint-shaped paths, the same lightweight, read-only technique used on firmware - no execution of any app code, no decompiling beyond extracting the string pool.

Confirmed known endpoints: `/blackvue_live.cgi` (with `?direction=I` and `?direction=R` found literally - no literal `?direction=F` string anywhere, and a genuinely unexplained `?direction=O` value that isn't F/R/I), `/blackvue_vod.cgi`, `/upload.cgi`, `/BlackVue/Config/version.bin`. Camera's default AP IP `10.99.77.1` also appears, consistent with everything already known from firmware analysis.

Genuinely new, not previously known: `blackvue_config.cgi`, `blackvue_delete_file.cgi`, `blackvue_sim_info.cgi`, `blackvue_sos_info.cgi`/`sos_start.cgi`/`sos_stop.cgi`, `blackvue_status.cgi`, `format.cgi`, `upgrade2.cgi`. `blackvue_livedata.cgi` - the endpoint this project's own `bv-live`/telemetry code already uses - has **no literal reference anywhere** in the app's own code, which is odd given the app clearly shows live GPS/g-sensor data; `blackvue_status.cgi` is the most plausible alternative source, but unconfirmed without deeper decompiling than a strings pass gives.

Important corroboration: none of the four Elite-10-firmware-string-only entries (`snap.cgi`, `hss_live.cgi`, `gps.cgi`, `log.cgi`) appear anywhere in the real app's code either - a second independent signal (after the live scan's timeouts/502s) that these may not be real functioning endpoints, at least not as bare GETs.

**Fixed:** added three of the new app-sourced endpoints to `CANDIDATE_ENDPOINTS` - `blackvue_status.cgi`, `blackvue_sim_info.cgi`, `blackvue_sos_info.cgi` - placed last (newest, least confirmed group: found in the app, never tried against a real camera). Deliberately excluded `blackvue_delete_file.cgi`, `format.cgi`, `upgrade2.cgi` - destructive by name alone, exactly the category this script's own docstring already says never to probe even as a bare GET. `blackvue_config.cgi` also excluded for now (ambiguous - could plausibly be a "set config" write endpoint given the sibling `delete_file.cgi`/`format.cgi` in the same cluster; not clearly safe enough to add without more certainty).

**Verification:** `ast.parse()`, then a direct Python check confirming all three new paths are present in `CANDIDATE_ENDPOINTS` and all three excluded ones are absent. Full end-to-end run against a local synthetic server (one 200 on `blackvue_status.cgi`, 404s elsewhere) confirmed the three new entries print correctly in both the detailed section and the summary table, in the expected trailing position, with tallies updated to 13 total endpoints.

## Second real Elite 10 scan: core beyond-video functions confirmed live, second-tier endpoints all 502 (this session, no code change)

Christer ran the scan again against his Elite 10, now including the three app-sourced entries added above. Result: **every endpoint beyond-video actually depends on came back a clean 200/Valid** - `blackvue_vod.cgi` (downloads), both `blackvue_live.cgi` directions (live view), `blackvue_livedata.cgi` (GPS/g-sensor), `Config/config.ini` (RecordTime/settings). This is now the first real-hardware confirmation of beyond-video's core CGI dependencies on a second camera model, not just the DR900S-2CH - matching the first Elite 10 scan from earlier this session.

**New pattern worth recording:** all three newly-added endpoints (`blackvue_status.cgi`, `blackvue_sim_info.cgi`, `blackvue_sos_info.cgi`) came back `HTTP 502` - the exact same failure mode `blackvue_gps.cgi`/`blackvue_log.cgi` already showed in the first scan. Five different endpoints, five different features (status, SIM info, SOS, alternate GPS, event log), uniform 502 across all of them. `blackvue_snap.cgi`/`blackvue_hss_live.cgi` still timed out rather than erroring, as before.

The uniformity is the interesting part: this isn't "these particular five don't exist" (they're all `Found` - the path is real, something answers). It reads more like "an unauthenticated bare GET isn't the right way to call anything past the core six" - the real BlackVue app likely needs a different HTTP method, extra headers, or some session/state setup (WiFi handshake, an app-level "connect" step) this script's plain GETs never establish. Recorded as a hypothesis, not confirmed - nothing here proves it, but the consistency across five unrelated features makes "these specific five endpoints are each individually broken" a less likely explanation than "this whole tier needs something the scan script doesn't provide."

Practical takeaway for beyond-video itself: none of this second tier is anything the project currently uses or needs - `bv-download`/`bv-gps`/`bv-live` only ever touch the six core endpoints, all of which are now doubly confirmed working on Elite 10. This is purely exploratory data for possible future features (SOS status, SIM/LTE info), not a regression or blocker for anything that exists today.

## Git history rewrite: scrubbed camera's ap_ssid unique ID from a pushed commit (this session, no source change)

After the redaction fix above landed in the working tree, realized the original unredacted value (`BlackVueElite10-F8CF08`) was still sitting in git history - specifically in the diff of commit `32b58f1`, which was already pushed to `origin/main` on GitHub. Fixing the current file doesn't erase it from history; anyone could still `git show 32b58f1` and see it, or find it via GitHub's own history browser.

Flagged this to Christer explicitly rather than silently leaving it or unilaterally rewriting a pushed branch. He chose to rewrite history and force-push.

**What was done:** confirmed the exposure was recent and shallow - only the last 3 commits (`32b58f1`, `6bf7cae`, and the local unpushed redaction commit) needed new SHAs, out of 235 total. Made a local safety tag (`backup-before-history-rewrite`) pointing at the old history, then rebuilt those 3 commits from `32b58f1`'s parent: checked out at `32b58f1`, patched the offending line directly in that commit via `git commit --amend`, cherry-picked `6bf7cae` (unrelated content, applied clean), then cherry-picked the local redaction commit (its `WORKING_CONTEXT.md` hunk had become a no-op since the content already matched, so only its `README.md` change actually applied - git handled this automatically, no manual conflict resolution needed). Verified `git log --all -p | grep F8CF08` returns nothing reachable from the rewritten `main`, and that the rewritten commits' file contents are byte-identical to before (`git diff <old-tip> <new-tip> --stat` empty) - only the commit SHAs changed, nothing else.

**Could not push from here:** this sandbox has no network path to `github.com` (proxy returns 403 on `git ls-remote`), so the actual `git push --force-with-lease origin main` has to happen from Christer's own machine - gave him the exact command plus the caveats (GitHub can keep the old commit resolvable by direct SHA for a while after a force-push due to server-side GC lag; no other forks/clones of this personal repo to worry about).

**Note for future reference:** the mounted repo folder (`C:\My_git\beyond-video`) is Christer's real working directory, not a sandboxed copy - `git checkout` to an old commit or a temp branch during a rewrite like this changes the actual files on his machine mid-operation. Fine here since the end state was `git reset --hard` back onto `main` before finishing, but worth remembering for any future history surgery.

## bv-download --host/--target: config-free quick download

Christer's reasoning: most people who come across beyond-video probably just want to download recordings off their camera, not adopt the whole toolkit (bv-config's interactive wizard, the archive-directory convention, trip export, transcription, etc.). Asked whether `bv-download` should grow a `--host` option alongside a target-directory option to support that, and said I could change his suggested `--targetdir` name if I wanted to.

Agreed it's worth doing, and picked `--target` over his suggested `--targetdir` - `bv-export` already has a `--target DIR` flag with the exact same meaning ("directory to write into"), so matching that name keeps the two commands consistent rather than introducing a second word for the same concept.

**Design:** `id` (the existing positional, camera system id from `bv-config`) is now optional (`nargs="?"`). Added `--host HOST` and `--target DIR`. Exactly one of `ID` or `--host` is required; `--host` and `--target` must be given together. Validated in `parse_args()` with `parser.error()`, matching the existing `--files`-requires-`--dry-run` pattern (four checks: id-or-host required, host/id mutually exclusive, host requires target, target requires host).

In `_run()`, replaced the single config-loading block with a branch: `--host` builds `endpoints = [Endpoint(name="host", address=args.host)]` and uses `args.target` as the destination directly, skipping `bv-config`'s file lookup entirely; the `id` path is unchanged (loads the `.cfg`, uses its `endpoints`/`target`/`name`). Both branches feed the same `endpoints`/`destination`/`display_name` into the rest of the function - `connect()`, the confirm prompt, `--mode`/`--from`/`--until`/`--dry-run`/`--files`/`--trace` all work identically either way. The only real difference: `--host` only ever tries the one address given, where a `bv-config` camera can list several endpoints (e.g. home WiFi then a cellular fallback) tried in order.

**Verification:** no pytest in this sandbox (same `tomllib`/Python-3.10 constraint noted earlier - `camera_config.py` imports the 3.11+ stdlib module unconditionally) and no network to install a backport, so verified by stubbing a minimal `tomllib` module in `sys.modules` and running the new `parse_args()` cases directly: id-alone still works, no-id-and-no-host errors, id+host together errors, host-without-target errors, target-without-host errors, host+target together is accepted, and the existing `--files`/`--dry-run` behavior is untouched. Also ran `--help` to confirm the generated usage/options text reads sensibly. Added the same cases as real tests in `tests/blackvue/cli/test_bv_download.py` for when pytest is available.

Documented in `docs/man/bv-download.md` (new SYNOPSIS form, ARGUMENTS/OPTIONS rows, an example) and `docs/CLI.md` (noted `bv-download` is the one command in the camera-ID group that also accepts a config-free alternative).

**Follow-up, same session:** Christer asked whether `--host` mode should skip writing `record_time.txt` too. Agreed - that snapshot is bookkeeping for `bv-export`'s own `--max-gap` default, tied to the rest of the toolkit's archive conventions, not something a bare "just grab the videos" download should leave behind. Gated the existing `_capture_record_time()` call in `_run()` behind `args.host is None`, so `--host` runs skip both the extra `/Config/config.ini` fetch and the `.record_time.txt` file entirely. If the same directory is later downloaded into via a real `bv-config` id, the snapshot gets written on that first run same as always - nothing is permanently lost, just deferred. Updated `docs/man/bv-download.md`'s description accordingly (RecordTime paragraph now scoped to `ID`-based runs explicitly).

## Elite 10: no GPS/g-sensor files, and why (this session, no beyond-video code change)

Christer used the new `--host`/`--target` flags to grab recordings straight off his Elite 10 for the first time, and noticed something the toolkit had never actually confirmed: only `.mp4` files came back, no `.gps`/`.3gf` sidecars, unlike every DR900S-2CH archive. Investigated with him step by step, always checking real evidence over guessing:

1. **`blackvue_vod.cgi` itself.** Re-pasted the scan output for the Elite 10's recording listing: every line is `n:/Record/<timestamp>_[EN]F.mp4,s:1000000` / `..._[EN]R.mp4,s:1000000` - front/rear video only, no `.gps`/`.3gf`/`.thm` entries visible. Two caveats worth recording: the scan script's own preview is capped at 2048 bytes (a deliberate safety limit for continuously-streaming endpoints), so that alone couldn't rule out sidecar entries further down; but `BlackVueClient.vod()` (the method the real `bv-download` run actually used) does a plain uncapped `response.read()` with no such limit (`src/blackvue/core/blackvue_client.py`), so his real download producing only `.mp4` files is the authoritative signal, not an artifact of the scan tool's truncation. Also noted every entry's reported size is an identical, suspiciously round `s:1000000` regardless of the recording - clearly not a real byte count, more likely a placeholder this firmware's `vod.cgi` never bothered to compute. Decided to ignore that field rather than speculate further about it.

2. **The MP4 container itself** - Christer's idea, and a good one: some dashcams embed telemetry as an in-file track instead of separate sidecar files. `ffprobe` on a real Elite 10 recording reported `Found duplicated MOOV Atom. Skipped it` - i.e. the file has two top-level `moov` boxes and ffprobe silently discarded one, which meant its stream list (`vide`+`soun` only) couldn't be trusted as complete. Wrote `inspect_mp4_boxes.py` (a standalone, read-only, stdlib-only script - not part of beyond-video itself, sitting untracked at the repo root, same box-walking technique as `src/blackvue/generate/mp4_box_reader.py`) to walk every top-level box directly and list every track in every `moov` found, rather than trusting whichever one ffprobe happened to keep. Self-tested against synthetic MP4s built in the sandbox before trusting it against Christer's real file (one with a genuine extra track type, one with a `free` box containing planted text including a fake `$GPRMC` sentence, to confirm both the track-listing and string-detection logic actually work).

   Real result: the file is literally two complete, independently-parseable movies concatenated back to back - `ftyp+free+moov+mdat` (~230MB, matching ffprobe's reported 61s/~30Mbps almost exactly) immediately followed by a second, much smaller one (~8.8MB `mdat`). Both `moov`s have only `vide`+`soun` tracks, nothing else - **confirms Christer's memory** ("2 channels, one a low-quality fast-view stream") but rules out an embedded telemetry track as the explanation, since neither movie has one.

3. **The `free` boxes.** ~492KB each, between `ftyp` and `moov` - suspiciously large for what's normally a few KB of padding a parser is required to skip, and exactly the kind of place a vendor might stash private data for that reason. Extended `inspect_mp4_boxes.py` with a strings-style scan (same "extract, look for readable text" discipline used throughout this project's firmware analysis) of any non-zero `free` box. Found a JSON header: `cprt {"model":"ELITE 10","ver":1.008,"rev":"650","isp_front_ver":"1.3","isp_rear_ver":"1.3","lang":"English","direct":0,"psn":"<device serial, redacted>","temp":67,"GPS":1}` - a self-descriptive session header, not telemetry: `"GPS":1` is a capability/enabled flag, not coordinates. No NMEA sentences ($GPRMC etc.) or other GPS/g-sensor-shaped text anywhere in either `free` box. **Privacy note, same discipline as the earlier `ap_ssid` redaction:** `psn` (`EL10K1P1E03139`) is a real product serial number - flagged to Christer as something to keep out of any public sharing of this analysis, same category as the camera's unique ID redacted earlier this session.

   One incidental confirmation: the second `free` box's embedded filename read `20260802_162130_NFS.mp4` (note the extra `S`) versus the first's plain `NF.mp4` - the low-quality proxy stream is internally named with an `S` (sub/secondary) suffix even though both get merged into one physical file under the primary `NF` name on the SD card. Further corroborates point 2 above.

   Caveat given to Christer plainly: this rules out readable NMEA-style GPS *text* anywhere in the file, but the DR900S-2CH's own `.3gf` g-sensor format is binary, not text - so a strings scan alone can't fully rule out binary-encoded telemetry hiding in the ~450KB of non-printable `free`-box bytes. Judged unlikely given everything else found looks like ordinary compressed/calibration junk, but explicitly not proven either way.

**Working conclusion, not yet fully confirmed:** across three independent checks (vod.cgi listing, both `moov`s' tracks, `free`-box contents) nothing points to a downloadable GPS/g-sensor log existing for Elite 10 recordings - most likely this model is live-only for telemetry, via `blackvue_livedata.cgi` (already confirmed working), rather than persisting an offline log the way the DR900S-2CH does.

**Open question Christer raised next:** maybe the `.gps`/`.3gf` files DO still exist on the camera's filesystem under the same `/Record/<timestamp>_<kind>.gps` naming convention `RecordingId.parse()` already documents (`src/blackvue/archive/recording_id.py`), just omitted from `vod.cgi`'s own listing rather than genuinely absent - a listing gap, not a data gap. Worth checking directly since `BlackVueClient._get()` isn't restricted to whatever `vod.cgi` happens to list - any predictable path can be fetched directly. Two ways suggested to Christer to settle it: (a) a direct guessed `GET`/`curl` for `/Record/<timestamp>_N.gps` and `/Record/<timestamp>_N.3gf` alongside the recording already downloaded; (b) the Elite 10's own FTP server (port 21, serving `/mnt/sd` directly per the firmware's `inetd.conf` - see the "Find the CGI API in a different, newer BlackVue model's firmware" entry above) browsed directly, which would show the real filesystem contents regardless of what `vod.cgi` chooses to report. Neither has been tried yet - unresolved as of this entry.

**Resolved: it's a listing gap, not a data gap.** Christer tried option (a) directly against his Elite 10 and both guessed paths came back real: `/Record/<timestamp>_N.gps` (17,340 bytes) and `/Record/<timestamp>_N.3gf` (5,940 bytes), both HTTP 200 with real content. The `.gps` file is genuine `[epoch_ms]$SENTENCE` NMEA text in exactly the format `gps_reader.py`'s own docstring documents - saved to disk and grepped for `RMC`, it contains a full, well-formed stream of real `$GPRMC` sentences (12 fields, matching `_parse_rmc()`'s exact expected shape) at roughly 1Hz, date field reading the actual capture date. **Parses with the existing `gps_reader.py` completely unmodified** - no format differences from the DR900S-2CH at all, so the earlier worry about a possible `GN`-prefixed talker ID (multi-GNSS receivers sometimes emit `$GNRMC` instead of `$GPRMC`) turned out to be unfounded; this camera's `$GPRMC` sentences use the same plain `GP` prefix. (The `.3gf` binary format is unconfirmed the same way, since binary content can't be eyeballed the way NMEA text can, but there's no reason to expect a different convention given everything else matches.)

**Fixed:** since a camera's own listing can no longer be trusted as the sole source of truth for these two extensions, `bv-download` now opportunistically probes for them directly instead of only trusting whichever entries `blackvue_vod.cgi` happens to report.

- `BlackVueClient.probe(path) -> bool` (`src/blackvue/core/blackvue_client.py`): a plain GET, returning True on success and False on any `HTTPError` (typically 404). Deliberately a GET, not a HEAD - HEAD support against this camera's embedded web server was never actually confirmed (everything tested against it this session used GET), where a plain GET already has. Network-level failures (unreachable, timeout) are not caught and propagate, since those mean something's actually wrong, not just "this file doesn't exist here."
- `BlackVueCamera.probe_missing_sidecars(recording)` (`src/blackvue/core/blackvue_camera.py`): for each of `.gps`/`.3gf`, skips straight past it if the recording's listing already has an entry with that suffix (the normal case on every model confirmed so far except the Elite 10 - zero extra network calls for that case), otherwise probes `/Record/<recording.id><suffix>` and appends a synthetic `VodEntry` if found. Mutates `recording.entries` in place and returns the new entries found, so a caller can report on it.
- Wired into `bv_download.py`'s `_run()`: called once per recording after building the filtered `recordings` list (post `--from`/`--until`/`--timestamp` filtering, so this only ever probes recordings actually in scope for the run, not the camera's entire history), with a `--verbose` line when something new is found. From there the existing entry flows through the same selection (`--mode`/context-based)/download/`--dry-run --files` machinery unchanged - no special-casing needed anywhere else, since a probed `.gps`/`.3gf` entry is just an ordinary non-video `VodEntry` like any other.

Deliberately general, not Elite-10-specific: any camera with the same listing-gap behavior benefits the same way, and this is a genuine no-op (no extra requests, no behavior change at all) for cameras that already list everything, which is every model confirmed working before this session.

**Verification:** no pytest in this sandbox (same constraint noted throughout this session), so manually exercised via a stubbed `tomllib` module - `probe()` returning True/False/propagating correctly for success/HTTPError/URLError, and `probe_missing_sidecars()` finding+appending, being a true no-op (zero probe calls) when already listed, and only probing the specific extensions actually missing. Added the same cases as real tests in `tests/blackvue/core/test_blackvue_client.py` and `tests/blackvue/core/test_blackvue_camera.py` for when pytest is available. Documented in `docs/man/bv-download.md`'s DESCRIPTION.

**Correction to the earlier firmware-strings entry, prompted by Christer noticing the live scan's own `v:3.00` line:** the "Find the CGI API in a different, newer BlackVue model's firmware" entry above guessed, from `strings` output alone, that the three version banners found in the `pta_ELITE10_FASTBOOT` blob (`v:1.00`/`v:2.00`/`v:3.00`) belonged to `vod.cgi`/`log.cgi`/`hss_live.cgi` respectively - i.e. that `vod.cgi` itself was still `v:1.00`, same as the DR900S-2CH. Every real scan against the actual camera this session (both earlier ones, and Christer's re-check just now) shows `blackvue_vod.cgi` itself reporting `v:3.00`, not `v:1.00`. The firmware build matches (the `.mp4` `free`-box JSON header found earlier this session reads `"ver":1.008,"rev":"650"`, the same `b1.008` the analyzed firmware zip's filename carries), so this isn't a firmware-version mismatch - the earlier guess was simply an imprecise attribution, three format strings matched to three endpoint names without a way to confirm which string belongs to which binary from `strings` output alone. Live, directly-observed behavior is the reliable data point here, not the firmware-strings guess - noting the correction rather than leaving it standing uncorrected.

Christer's actual question: does the `v:3.00` protocol version tell us why `.gps`/`.3gf` aren't listed - i.e. did BlackVue deliberately drop them from a newer listing format? Plausible and consistent with everything else found (the placeholder `s:1000000` sizes, the Novatek/aarch64 platform being a materially different generation), but not something that can be confirmed one way or the other - there's no second Elite 10 vod.cgi version to diff against, and nothing in the firmware strings suggests a query parameter to request a different version explicitly (only `path=`/`del=` are confirmed real). Doesn't change anything practically either way: `parse_vod_entries()` (`src/blackvue/parser/vod.py`) already unconditionally skips any line starting with `v:` regardless of the number, and the `probe_missing_sidecars()` fix added this session works around the gap directly by checking the filesystem rather than depending on understanding why the listing is incomplete.

## bv-generate audio extraction failed on Elite 10: ADTS muxer rejects MP3 source

Christer pasted a `bv-generate` failure on two Elite 10 recordings: `ffmpeg` errored with `adts muxer supports only codec aac for type audio` / `Could not write header (incorrect codec parameters ?): Invalid argument` / `Conversion failed!`, and `bv-generate` reported `ffmpeg failed for <file>: ...` for each. Every downstream feature that depends on extracted audio - transcription, diarization, translation - was broken for this camera.

**Root cause:** `extract_audio()` (`src/blackvue/generate/media.py`) always ran `ffmpeg -vn -acodec copy` into a destination path ending `.aac`. The `.aac` extension makes ffmpeg pick the ADTS muxer, which can only hold raw AAC bitstream - so `-acodec copy` only works when the source audio is already AAC. The pasted ffprobe output showed the Elite 10's audio track is `mp3 (mp3float)`, not AAC; stream-copying MP3 into an ADTS container fails outright. This never surfaced on the DR900S-2CH because that camera's audio is (evidently) already AAC.

Confirmed the fix has to live inside `extract_audio()` itself rather than at any call site: all three callers (`_do_extract_audio`, the translate-fallback path, and the transcribe-fallback path in `bv_generate.py`, lines ~403/650/901) independently build a `<recording.id>.aac` destination and just call `extract_audio(source, destination)` - identical shape every time, no codec awareness at any of them.

**Fixed:** added `probe_audio_codec(path) -> str | None` to `media.py` - a lightweight `ffprobe -select_streams a:0 -show_entries stream=codec_name` call, returning the codec name or `None` if there's no audio stream (mirrors `MediaToolError` handling already used by `probe()` in the same file). `extract_audio()` now probes the source first: stream-copies (`-acodec copy`, unchanged, free) only when the source is already `"aac"`; otherwise transcodes (`-acodec aac`) instead. This keeps the fast/lossless path for every camera confirmed so far except the Elite 10, and fixes the Elite 10 (and any other future MP3-or-otherwise-non-AAC camera) by paying a small one-time transcode cost instead of failing outright. The extracted audio is only ever consumed for speech-to-text, where the small quality cost of a transcode isn't a practical concern.

**Verification:** no pytest in this sandbox (same `tomllib`/Python-3.10 constraint noted throughout this project), so verified two ways: (1) stubbed `tomllib`, monkeypatched `subprocess.run` directly, and confirmed `probe_audio_codec()` returns the codec name / `None` / raises `MediaToolError` correctly, and `extract_audio()` picks `-acodec copy` only when the probed codec is `"aac"` and `-acodec aac` for `"mp3"` and `None`; (2) a genuine end-to-end repro with real `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` - synthesized an MP4 with `-c:a mp3` (this sandbox has ffmpeg 4.4.2 installed), confirmed `probe_audio_codec()` correctly reports `"mp3"` on it, ran it through the new `extract_audio()`, and confirmed the output is a genuinely playable AAC file (`probe_audio_codec()` on the destination reports `"aac"`) - the exact failure Christer hit, reproduced and fixed with no mocking at all. Added the same cases (both mocked-branch tests and the real end-to-end repro, skipped via `shutil.which` if ffmpeg/ffprobe aren't installed) to `tests/blackvue/generate/test_media.py`.

No docs changes - `extract_audio()` is an internal implementation detail of `bv-generate`'s audio pipeline, not something the man page documents at this level.

## RecordTime snapshot backfill gap: earlier recordings left uncovered after a later batch

Christer hit this directly: downloaded a batch starting at `20260802_162130_N` (got a `.record_time.txt` for it, as expected), then later downloaded an earlier recording, `20260802_161928_N` - and got `Warning: archive contains no configuration snapshot. Using fallback RecordTime of 300 seconds.` for it, despite the archive already having a snapshot.

**Root cause:** `_capture_record_time()` (`src/blackvue/cli/bv_download.py`) anchors each snapshot to `recordings[0].id` - the earliest recording *in that run* - which is correct provenance (changing RecordTime on the camera reformats the SD card, so everything still on it shares one value). But the function only ever wrote a new file when the fetched RecordTime *value* differed from the most recently written snapshot. Christer's second run fetched the same RecordTime as before, so the write was skipped as a no-op - even though its anchor (`161928`) was chronologically earlier than the existing snapshot's anchor (`162130`).

That gap then surfaced in `Archive.configuration()` (`src/blackvue/archive/archive.py`): it walks snapshots in order and only accepts one whose `recording_id <= recording.id` - i.e. coverage is forward-only from a snapshot's own anchor, never retroactive. With only the `162130`-anchored snapshot on disk, a lookup for `161928` (which sorts *before* it) never matches any candidate, so it falls through to `Configuration.fallback()` and the 300s warning - even though the real value (180s in this example) was known and unchanged.

**Fixed:** `_capture_record_time()` now writes a new snapshot when *either* condition holds: the value changed (original behavior, unchanged), or this run's anchor recording isn't already covered by an existing snapshot - i.e. it's earlier than the earliest snapshot currently on disk. Determined by comparing the new anchor's `recording_id` against `existing[0]`'s (recording IDs are fixed-width `YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_K` strings, so plain string comparison is chronological comparison - same property `RecordingId`'s `order=True` dataclass relies on elsewhere). The existing "don't grow the archive with a redundant file every run" behavior is preserved for the ordinary case (anchor already covered, value unchanged -> no-op); only the previously-missed backfill case now writes. Added a distinct `--verbose` message ("extended RecordTime=Xs coverage back to <recording_id> ...") for this case so it doesn't read like a value actually changed.

**Verification:** no pytest in this sandbox (same constraint as every other entry this project has hit), so manually exercised via a stubbed `tomllib` module: confirmed the exact backfill scenario now writes a second, earlier-anchored snapshot with the correct value even though RecordTime was unchanged; confirmed the ordinary no-op case (later run, already covered, unchanged value) still writes nothing; confirmed the original "value actually changed" case still always writes; confirmed the verbose message says "extended" for the backfill case; and, most importantly, ran `Archive.configuration()` end-to-end against the resulting two-snapshot archive and confirmed it now resolves `161928`'s RecordTime correctly (180s) instead of falling back to 300s - the exact repro of what Christer saw. Added the same cases as real tests in `tests/blackvue/cli/test_bv_download.py` for when pytest is available. Updated `docs/man/bv-download.md`'s RecordTime paragraph to describe the "already covered" condition and the forward-only, non-retroactive nature of snapshot coverage.

## bv-generate reused a stale, empty .aac left over from the ADTS/MP3 bug

Immediately after the ADTS/MP3 codec fix above, Christer re-ran `bv-generate --timestamp 20260802 --transcribe --srt` on the same three Elite 10 recordings and hit a new error: `language detection failed for <id>.aac: [Errno 541478725] End of file` (a libsndfile error masquerading as an errno, from the `soundfile`/Whisper stack trying to open a file with nothing in it).

**Root cause, confirmed by direct repro:** ffmpeg opens (truncates) its output file *before* it can fail to write into it. Reproduced directly in this sandbox: running the old buggy `-acodec copy` command against an MP3-audio source left a genuine 0-byte `.aac` on disk even though the whole command errored out and exited non-zero. Those three recordings had exactly that leftover from before today's codec fix. `bv-generate` has three places that trust "the `.aac` already exists" as "already extracted, safe to reuse" without checking it actually has content: the language-detection source selection and the transcription audio source in `_do_transcribe_with_optional_translate`, and the cached-audio reuse in `_do_translate_only` (all in `src/blackvue/cli/bv_generate.py`). The first of those is exactly what Christer's error came from - `recording.file(Asset.AUDIO)` returned the empty `.aac` (tracked by `ArchiveReader` from a prior scan), so `detect_language()` got handed 0 bytes instead of falling back to the video.

**Fixed, two layers:**

1. **Prevention** - `extract_audio()` (`src/blackvue/generate/media.py`) now removes its destination file if the ffmpeg subprocess fails (`destination.unlink(missing_ok=True)` in the `CalledProcessError` handler), so a failed extraction - this bug or any other future ffmpeg failure - never again leaves a poisoned artifact that looks like a completed one.
2. **Self-healing for what's already out there** - added `_has_usable_audio(path)` to `bv_generate.py` (checks `path.stat().st_size > 0`, `False` on any `OSError`) and applied it at all three "trust an existing `.aac`" sites instead of a bare existence check. An empty cached file is now treated the same as "not extracted yet" and gets re-extracted automatically on the next run - no manual cleanup needed, and the same self-healing discipline `load_or_compute_duration()` already applies to `.duration.txt` (see that entry earlier in this file). This matters because layer 1 alone doesn't help archives that already have a poisoned file sitting in them from before today's fix.

Practical result for Christer: no manual deletion of the three broken `.aac` files needed - just re-running the same `bv-generate --transcribe --srt` command lets it self-heal, since the empty cached files are now recognized as unusable and get regenerated (correctly, via the now-fixed `extract_audio()`) automatically.

**Verification:** no pytest in this sandbox (same constraint as every entry above), so manually exercised via a stubbed `tomllib` module: confirmed `extract_audio()` removes a partial destination on ffmpeg failure (both mocked and, more importantly, a genuine end-to-end repro - built a real MP3-audio MP4, ran the *old* buggy stream-copy command directly to produce a real 0-byte poisoned file exactly like Christer hit, then ran the *fixed* `extract_audio()` over that same poisoned path and confirmed it produces a valid playable AAC file); confirmed all three `bv-generate` reuse sites fall back to re-extracting when the cached `.aac` is empty, reproducing Christer's exact language-detection failure path and confirming it now resolves; and confirmed the pre-existing "reuse a genuinely non-empty cached `.aac`" behavior is unchanged (no regression - `extract_audio()` is still never called when there's real content to reuse). Added the same cases as real tests in `tests/blackvue/generate/test_media.py` and `tests/blackvue/cli/test_bv_generate.py` for when pytest is available.

No docs changes - this is entirely an internal robustness fix to `bv-generate`'s existing caching behavior, not a change to its command-line surface.

## --srt/--lrc ignored --translate: subtitles stayed in the original spoken language

Christer ran `bv-generate --timestamp 20260802 --transcribe --srt --translate eng x:/files/test` and got an `.srt` still in Russian (the recording's spoken language) instead of English, even though `--translate eng` was given right there on the command line.

**Root cause:** `format_srt()`/`format_lrc()` (`src/blackvue/generate/subtitles.py`) were always called with the untranslated `transcript.segments` in both places that write subtitles - `_do_transcribe_with_optional_translate()`'s own SRT/LRC block and `_do_translate_only()`'s (both in `src/blackvue/cli/bv_generate.py`). `--translate` only ever fed the whole-text `translate()`/`_translate_diarized()` call that produces `.translation.txt` - nothing translated the per-segment text `format_srt()`/`format_lrc()` actually read. This directly contradicts `docs/man/bv-generate.md`'s own example ("Transcribe and translate to Swedish, with subtitles" - `bv-generate --translate sv --srt`), which promises translated subtitles.

**Fixed:** added `_translate_segments(segments, *, source_language, target_language)` to `bv_generate.py` - the per-segment analogue of `translate()` (whole text) and the existing `_translate_diarized()` (line-by-line "[SPEAKER_XX] text"). It translates each `SpeechSegment.text` individually via `translate()` while keeping `.start`/`.end` untouched, so cue timing survives exactly. Diarization speaker labels are unaffected either way - `format_srt()`/`format_lrc()` add them separately via `speaker_for()`, which only ever looks at a segment's own `start`/`end` midpoint against `turns`, never its text - confirmed by reading `speaker_for()` before relying on this.

Wired into both write sites:
- `_do_transcribe_with_optional_translate()`: when `--translate` was given and either `--srt` or `--lrc` needs writing, translates the segments once (shared between both files) before writing them, independent of whether `translation.txt` itself needs a rewrite. Without `--translate`, behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged - original spoken-language segments, `translate()` never called.
- `_do_translate_only()` (the `--translate`-without-`--transcribe` path): this function only ever runs with `--translate` given, so its SRT/LRC always use translated segments - no "no translation requested" branch needed here. Also fixes a related bug this function's own comment flagged from an earlier session: previously, if `translation.txt` was already up to date (so `need_translation_write` was False) but `--srt`/`--lrc` were freshly requested, `translate()` was never called at all and the subtitles came out in the original language - exactly Christer's bug, just reachable a second way. Now `translate()` is called whenever SRT/LRC need it, regardless of `translation.txt`'s own state.

Both sites fail closed on a translation error (e.g. missing argos-translate language pack): the error is printed once, `had_error`/return is set, and no `.srt`/`.lrc` is written - deliberately not falling back to writing an untranslated file that would look like a success while quietly giving the wrong language again.

**Verification:** no pytest in this sandbox (same constraint as every entry above), so built a small harness that stubs `tomllib` and a minimal `pytest` (just `pytest.raises`/`pytest.mark.skipif`, both used elsewhere in this test file) and runs every test function in `tests/blackvue/cli/test_bv_generate.py` directly with hand-rolled `tmp_path`/`monkeypatch` fixtures - not just the new cases, the *whole file*, 59/59 passing, to catch any regression in the existing SRT/LRC/translate machinery this touched. Found and fixed one real regression this surfaced: `test_translate_only_srt_lrc_still_generated_when_translation_already_exists` had asserted the *old, buggy* behavior (translate() never called, untranslated SRT/LRC) as correct - its own comment even describes Christer's exact scenario. Updated it to assert the corrected behavior (translate() is called, SRT/LRC come out translated, translation.txt itself is left alone since it was already up to date). Added new tests: `_translate_segments()` in isolation (translates each text, preserves timing, empty input); the exact Christer repro (Russian transcript + English target -> English SRT, plain transcript.txt unaffected); the "no --translate" regression (original language unchanged, translate() never called); a translation-failure case (no SRT written, error reported); and the `_do_translate_only` equivalent. Updated `docs/man/bv-generate.md`'s `--srt`/`--lrc` option descriptions to state the translated-language behavior explicitly.

## Second g-sensor test recording reconfirms Y=lateral/Z=longitudinal; reverts task #291/292's override

Christer uploaded `20260802_103545_M.3gf` (18000 bytes = 1800 records, 180.5s duration), labeling two real-world events directly: "16 seconds in heavy acceleration, 127 seconds in turn left in roundabout for 540 degrees." This is the exact follow-up recording task #291/292 flagged as pending - "Christer has a follow-up recording planned with hard acceleration, braking, and turns specifically to get more data than the first pass had; this mapping should be revisited once that comes in, in either direction" - so it was analyzed as the deciding test it was meant to be, not just another data point.

**Analysis:** parsed the raw `.3gf` directly with the same `>Ihhh` struct format `gsensor_reader.py` uses, computed a baseline (mean/stdev) from a quiet window (t=0-8s: X mean=119.38 stdev=2.71, Y mean=-12.65 stdev=1.67, Z mean=29.68 stdev=2.87), then measured each labeled event's peak deviation from baseline in units of that axis's own baseline stdev - an objective way to identify which axis actually responded, rather than eyeballing raw numbers.

- **Event 1 (16s, heavy acceleration):** raw Z spiked (first response at t=16.04s, lasting ~6.8s, max Z=106, peak deviation 26.6x baseline stdev) - clearly dominant. X and Y showed much smaller, noise-level deviations (~10-16x).
- **Event 2 (127s, 540-degree left turn in a roundabout):** raw Y dipped (first response at t=100.20s, lasting through t=153.38s, min Y=-84, peak deviation 41.6x baseline stdev, trough straddling t=127s as expected for a multi-second roundabout maneuver) - clearly dominant. X and Z again much smaller.
- Raw X showed no sustained response to either event, in either recording, across both test passes now on record.

This independently reconfirms the original task #283/284 finding (Y=lateral/turning, Z=longitudinal/acceleration-braking, X=no sustained response), which task #291/292 had overridden to X=lateral/Y=longitudinal at Christer's own explicit request ("Actually swap which raw channel means what"), with that override documented at the time as "a knowing, twice-confirmed override of this session's own empirical finding, not a correction of it." Presented the numbers directly and asked whether to revert now that the planned follow-up landed in favor of the original evidence; Christer confirmed: "yes, but in the gsensor overlay i want lateral movement to show at an imagined x axis and the accelaration as y" - i.e. revert which *raw field* feeds lateral/longitudinal, but keep the dot-gauge's own *screen-space* convention (lateral on the gauge's horizontal axis, longitudinal/acceleration on its vertical axis) exactly as it already was. Checked `gsensor_render.py`'s `_project()` before touching anything: the gauge has always mapped the first element of its `(lateral, longitudinal)` position tuple to horizontal screen position and the second to vertical (flipped for pixel-y-grows-downward) - that convention doesn't depend on which raw channel is currently plugged into "lateral," so satisfying Christer's request only required changing *which raw fields* `baseline_for_samples()`/`scale_for_samples()`/`render_gsensor_video()`'s position calc read, not any part of the projection/rendering code itself.

**Reverted:**
- `gsensor_render.py`: `baseline_for_samples()`/`scale_for_samples()` now read raw Y (lateral) and raw Z (longitudinal) instead of raw X/Y. Module docstring rewritten to describe both test recordings and the interim override in between, rather than presenting the override as the current unresolved state.
- `gsensor_video.py`: `render_gsensor_video()`'s per-frame position calculation now uses the interpolated raw Y/Z fields instead of X/Y (raw X is now the unused one, previously raw Z was). Module docstring updated to match.
- `gsensor_graph_render.py`: `LEGEND_LABELS` wording reverted to `(("X", "Up/down"), ("Y", "Left/right"), ("Z", "Acc/brake"))` - the tuple's fixed X/Y/Z *order* (zipped positionally against the fixed X/Y/Z colors) was never touched, only the wording each entry carries. This module's own `baseline_for_samples()`/`axis_scales_for_samples()` were *not* changed - the strip chart always plots all three raw fields independently regardless of which is "lateral," so only the legend's explanatory text needed to change, not any data path.
- `docs/man/bv-export.md`'s `--gsensor-video` row updated to describe the Y/Z mapping and both test recordings, in place of the X/Y override description.

**Verification:** no pytest in this sandbox (same constraint as every entry above). Built a small import-based harness (`run_gsensor_tests.py`) that discovers every `test_*` function across `test_gsensor_render.py`, `test_gsensor_video.py`, and `test_gsensor_graph_render.py`, hand-supplies `tmp_path`/`monkeypatch` fixtures where a test's signature asks for them, and reports pass/fail per test - ran the full 80 tests across all three files (not just the ones touched) to catch any regression. Updated tests before running: `test_gsensor_render.py`'s `_sample()` helper now assigns its `lateral`/`longitudinal` args to raw Y/Z (X becomes the filler arg), and the "ignore unused raw field" regression test now varies X instead of Z; `test_gsensor_video.py`'s `_sample()` helper likewise, plus fixed four raw-tuple assertions in the low-level interpolation tests that had hard-coded the old X/Y/900-default ordering; `test_gsensor_graph_render.py`'s `LEGEND_LABELS` assertion and several explanatory comments (legend-width test, two-rows-when-Z-hidden test) updated to match the new wording. All 80/80 passed on the first run after these updates. Also grepped the rest of `src/` for any other reader of `baseline_for_samples`/`scale_for_samples`/raw sample fields tied to this mapping (`trip_export.py`, `export/__init__.py`, `blackvue/live/`) - nothing else depends on which raw field means what, so no other files needed changes.

No further docs changes needed beyond `bv-export.md` above - `--stitch-gsensor`/`--stitch-graph`'s own option descriptions don't name specific raw fields.

## gsensor.mp4/map.mp4 drift out of sync with the real video on multi-recording trips

Christer: "My problem is that gsensor data is not in sync with the video." Traced this to a fundamental mismatch between two different trip-timeline models that `trip_export.py`/`map_video.py` had always conflated.

**Root cause:** `_merge_gsensor()` positioned each recording's g-sensor samples within the trip by `recording.id.timestamp - trip_start` - i.e. by the *nominal wall-clock gap* between recording IDs (`YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_K` filenames). `render_map_video()`'s GPS positioning did the equivalent thing via a single `video_start + elapsed` anchor. But the actual video (`_concatenate_asset()`) is built by literally gluing each included recording's own (possibly front/rear-trimmed) video file back-to-back, with zero wall-clock awareness - a recording's real position in the concatenated video is simply "wherever the earlier recordings' own actual durations happen to add up to." These two models only agree when every consecutive recording pair has exactly zero gap/overlap *and* no front/rear trim ever fired - which is close to never in practice. Confirmed with real numbers from Christer's own Aug 2 trip (`trip_20260802_103513_20260802_103846`): recording `20260802_103545_M` (a Manual-mode recording, which BlackVue cameras prebuffer - the video can contain several seconds of footage from *before* its own ID timestamp) actually starts 6 seconds before the prior recording `20260802_103513_N`'s own ID-timestamp span even ends, an overlap the nominal-ID-gap model has no way to represent; separately, the prior recording's own real video duration (36.73s) differed from its nominal 32s ID-gap by ~4.7s even before any prebuffer effect, confirming the drift isn't prebuffer-specific - any gap, overlap, or front/rear trim causes it.

Christer confirmed (via `AskUserQuestion`) this should be fixed for both `gsensor.mp4`/`trip.3gf` and `map.mp4`'s GPS marker/`--stitch-map` panel together, not just g-sensor - the same wall-clock-vs-real-video-position mismatch affects both.

**Fixed**, all in `src/blackvue/export/`:
- `trip_export.py`: new `_recording_video_offsets(trip, *, include_parking, duration_overrides=None)` walks `trip.recordings` in order, probes each included recording's real video duration (front if present else rear, resolving `_align_front_rear_durations()`'s trimmed-path override when given), and accumulates a real cumulative video-position offset per `RecordingId`. New `_video_position_breakpoints(trip, video_offsets)` reshapes that into sorted `(video_position_seconds, wallclock_id_timestamp)` pairs.
- `_merge_gsensor()` now takes an optional `video_offsets` dict; when a recording's id is present, its samples are rebased by the real video offset instead of the old `id.timestamp - trip_start` wall-clock gap. Falls back to the old behavior when `video_offsets` is None (preserves exact prior behavior for any other caller).
- `map_video.py`: new `_wallclock_for_elapsed(elapsed_seconds, breakpoints, fallback_start)` converts a video-elapsed-seconds position into the real wall-clock instant it corresponds to, by finding which recording's breakpoint span `elapsed_seconds` falls in and adding the remainder to that recording's own `wallclock_id_timestamp` - wall-clock time advances 1:1 with video-elapsed time *within* a recording's own span, so only the *which recording, and what's its own start* part needed fixing. Falls back to `fallback_start + elapsed_seconds` (the old single-anchor behavior) when `breakpoints` is empty (e.g. a GPS/g-sensor-only trip with no video to align against at all). `render_map_video()` gained a `recording_breakpoints` parameter threaded into the frame loop's timestamp calculation in place of the old plain `start + timedelta(seconds=elapsed)`.
- `stitch.py`: `map_recording_breakpoints` threaded through all three layers between the public API and the actual render call - `stitch_cameras()` -> `_stack()` -> `_render_map_panel()` -> `render_map_video(recording_breakpoints=...)` - so `--stitch-map`'s panel gets the identical fix, not just standalone `map.mp4`.
- `export_trip()`: computes `video_offsets`/`recording_breakpoints` once, right after `_align_front_rear_durations()` inside its existing `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory` block (needs the trimmed-file paths that tempdir holds) but before the block closes - the resulting offsets/breakpoints are plain data, safe to keep using after the tempdir is cleaned up. Passed into both `_merge_gsensor()` and every `_render_map_variant()`/`stitch_cameras()` call site (`map.mp4`, `map_zoom_*.mp4`, and the `--stitch-map` panel).

**Verification:** no pytest in this sandbox (same constraint as every entry above). Built a small import-based harness (`run_tests.py`) supporting `tmp_path`/`monkeypatch`/`capsys` fixture stand-ins and a `pytest.raises` stub, since none of `pytest`, `blackvue`, or this project's own venv are importable in this Linux sandbox (confirmed - the repo's `.venv` is a Windows venv with a `Scripts/` layout, not usable here). Ran:
- `test_map_video.py`: all 52 tests pass, including 6 new ones - direct unit tests of `_wallclock_for_elapsed()` (no-breakpoints fallback, contiguous-recordings-matches-old-behavior, a wall-clock-gap case where real video position diverges from nominal ID gap, the real overlapping-Manual-recording repro from Christer's own trip, and an edge case extrapolating before the first breakpoint) plus one `render_map_video()` integration test confirming `recording_breakpoints` overrides the single `video_start` anchor for frame positioning.
- `test_trip_export.py`: all 86 tests pass, including 8 new ones for `_recording_video_offsets()`/`_video_position_breakpoints()`/`_merge_gsensor()`'s new offset-based path, plus one pre-existing test (`test_export_trip_writes_everything_available`) updated - its old assertion hard-coded the wall-clock-gap-based sample offset (`timedelta(milliseconds=60000)`), which is exactly the bug being fixed; rewritten to assert the new, correct video-position-based offset instead.
- `test_stitch.py`: ran 92 of 141 tests directly (all pass), including one new test confirming `map_recording_breakpoints` threads correctly from `stitch_cameras()` through to `_render_map_panel()`. Skipped a handful of pre-existing tests unrelated to this change that hang in this specific sandbox regardless of any code here - real NVDEC hardware-decode-fallback tests (no GPU in this sandbox, so probing hangs) and a couple of debug-timing tests that run the full double-render pipeline twice at native resolution.

Not yet done: `docs/man/bv-export.md` doesn't need wording changes (no CLI flag changed, no user-facing behavior description changed - the fix makes existing behavior accurate rather than changing what's described), so none made.

## bv-download: extend sidecar probing to thumbnails - blackvue_vod.cgi never lists non-video files

Christer: "I am stupid, blackvue_vod.cgi have always only contained a listing of video files and nothing else. We have then got gps and gsensor files by knowing they should be there. We shouldn't forget the thumbnail files to."

This corrects the framing task #347/348/350's own sidecar-probing work used: `_PROBEABLE_SIDECAR_SUFFIXES`'s comment (and `docs/man/bv-download.md`) described `.gps`/`.3gf` omission as an Elite-10-specific quirk, implying "most models list everything including thumbnails." Christer's own report - and the fact `.gps`/`.3gf` probing was already firing on Kirby, a non-Elite-10 camera, per the `bv-download --verbose` output earlier in this session - says otherwise: `blackvue_vod.cgi`'s own listing has, across every camera he's actually run this against, only ever contained video files. Thumbnails were never given the same opportunistic-probe treatment `.gps`/`.3gf` got, so they were silently never downloaded whenever a camera's listing omitted them - which per this corrected understanding is apparently always, not an edge case.

**Fixed**, `src/blackvue/core/blackvue_camera.py`:
- `_PROBEABLE_SIDECAR_SUFFIXES`'s comment rewritten to describe the general finding (blackvue_vod.cgi = video-only listing, confirmed across multiple models) rather than framing it as Elite-10-specific.
- New `_THUMBNAIL_SUFFIX = ".thm"` and `_DIRECTION_LETTERS = ("F", "R", "I")` constants, and a new `_probe_missing_thumbnails()` method called from `probe_missing_sidecars()` after the existing `.gps`/`.3gf` loop. Thumbnails can't share that loop's flat suffix table: `.gps`/`.3gf` are one-per-recording (`{recording.id}{suffix}`), but thumbnails are one-per-camera-direction (`{recording.id}{F|R|I}.thm`, matching `Asset.FRONT_THUMBNAIL`/etc.'s existing `"F.thm"`/`"R.thm"`/`"I.thm"` suffixes in `archive_reader.py`). The new method computes which directions the recording actually has video for (`entry.is_video and entry.path.stem.endswith(letter)`) and which of those already have a listed thumbnail, then probes only the difference - so a recording with no rear camera never gets a spurious rear-thumbnail probe, and a camera that *does* list thumbnails costs nothing extra, same no-op guarantee the existing `.gps`/`.3gf` probing already had.
- `bv_download.py`'s comment above its `probe_missing_sidecars()` call site updated to match (mentions `.thm` now, drops the Elite-10-specific framing).
- `docs/man/bv-download.md`'s description of this behavior rewritten the same way.

**Verification:** no pytest in this sandbox (same constraint as every entry above), ran via the `run_tests.py` harness. `test_blackvue_camera.py`: all 11 tests pass, including 5 new ones (adds thumbnails for every direction with video; only probes directions that actually have video, not a phantom rear/interior; skips a thumbnail already listed; skips one the camera doesn't serve; probes an interior thumbnail too, not just front/rear) - and 3 pre-existing tests updated, since they now also trigger a thumbnail probe call as a side effect of having a video entry in their fixture (`test_probe_missing_sidecars_skips_extensions_the_camera_does_not_serve`'s and `test_probe_missing_sidecars_only_probes_extensions_actually_missing`'s `probe_calls` assertions extended to include the new `.thm` call; `test_probe_missing_sidecars_is_a_no_op_when_already_listed`'s fixture given an already-listed thumbnail entry too, to keep it a genuine full no-op rather than incidentally exercising the new thumbnail-probe code path). Confirmed via grep that `bv_download.py`'s own CLI-level tests don't exercise `probe_missing_sidecars` at all (no `probe`/`BlackVueCamera` references in `test_bv_download.py`), so no other test file needed changes.

## bv-export: self-heal missing per-recording audio instead of requiring a separate bv-generate --extract-audio pass first

Christer asked: "Shouldn't we always extract audio if present?" - questioning why `bv-export` only ever concatenated a trip's `audio.aac` from recordings that already had their own `<recording>.aac` sitting in the archive (produced by a prior, separate `bv-generate --extract-audio` run), rather than just extracting it itself. After talking through a few shapes (always-on flag in `bv-generate`, move extraction to `bv-download`, keep the flag but skip cleanly), Christer proposed the one actually used: "Or should it be extracted by bv-export?" - yes, confirmed with a plain "yes".

**Design:** `bv-export` now self-heals a missing `<recording>.aac` the same way it already self-heals two other things - `--stitch-gsensor`'s on-demand `gsensor.mp4` render (task #232) and `load_or_compute_duration()`'s `.duration.txt` (task #151/156). No new CLI flag: extraction just happens, scoped to the trip(s) actually being exported (same scoping task #156 settled on for duration), before that trip's own `audio.aac` concatenation starts.

**Implemented**, `src/blackvue/export/trip_export.py`:
- New `_ensure_recording_audio(trip, warnings, log, *, debug=False)`, called from `export_trip()` right after the `log.membership` loop and before concatenation starts (must finish before the front/rear/audio `ThreadPoolExecutor` block, since its audio worker reads `recording.assets` synchronously the moment it starts).
- For each recording in the trip missing `Asset.AUDIO` and not Parking (`recording.id.is_parking` - matches `bv-generate`'s own `_do_extract_audio()`, unconditionally, independent of `--include-parking`): finds its source video via `select_source()`, checks `probe_audio_codec()` first, and only calls `extract_audio()` if a real audio stream was detected. Writes `<recording>.aac` next to the source video in the archive and mutates `recording.assets[Asset.AUDIO]` in place, so the very next `_concatenate_asset(trip, Asset.AUDIO, ...)` call picks it up exactly like a pre-existing file - no separate wiring needed there. A `MediaToolError` from `extract_audio()` itself is caught, appended to `warnings`, logged via `log.warning()`, and that one recording is left out of the trip's audio - same "leave it out" behavior every other missing/corrupted asset already gets.
- The `probe_audio_codec()` pre-check turned out to matter more than expected: caught via reasoning through the existing test suite before running it, not by a failing run. Every fixture video in `test_trip_export.py` is created via `_make_video()` (`ffmpeg testsrc`, no embedded audio track at all), and an unconditional `extract_audio()` call would have made ffmpeg fail "naturally" (per `extract_audio()`'s own documented behavior of not pre-checking) on every single one of them - `probe_audio_codec()` returning `None` (no audio stream, not an error) is treated as "silently skip, nothing to warn about", reserving the warning path for a genuine extraction failure on a recording that does have an audio stream.

**Verification:** no pytest in this sandbox (same constraint as every entry above), ran via `run_tests.py`. Added a `_make_video_with_audio()` test helper (`ffmpeg testsrc` + `sine` audio, `-c:a aac`, verified directly against a raw `ffprobe` call before adding it to the suite) alongside the existing `_make_video()` (video-only) and `_make_audio()` (audio-only) helpers. New tests for `_ensure_recording_audio()`: extracts real audio from a video that has it and mutates `recording.assets`; skips silently (no warning) for a video with no audio stream at all; skips a Parking recording even though its video has real audio; skips a recording that already has `Asset.AUDIO` (no redundant extraction call, checked via monkeypatch); warns without crashing when `extract_audio()` itself raises `MediaToolError` for a recording that does have a detected audio stream; prints the `bv-export: {id}: extracted ... (self-healed, missing from archive)` debug line only when `debug=True`, silent otherwise. Plus one integration test through `export_trip()` itself, confirming a recording with no prior `.aac` ends up contributing to the trip's own `audio.aac` with zero warnings. All 7 new unit tests plus the integration test pass; full `test_trip_export.py` regression (94 tests total) passes with zero modifications needed to any pre-existing test - confirming the no-audio-stream skip doesn't introduce spurious warnings anywhere in the existing suite.

`docs/man/bv-export.md` updated: added a paragraph under the trip-assembly description noting audio no longer needs a prior `bv-generate --extract-audio` pass, framed as the same self-healing convention as `--duration-heal-archive`/`--stitch-gsensor`.
