## v0.2.0 CI failure: two "missing dependency" tests broke against the real CI environment

First real CI run against the v0.2.0 release commit failed two tests in `tests/blackvue/generate/test_speech.py`: `test_get_whisper_model_reports_missing_faster_whisper_cleanly` and `test_load_waveform_via_ffmpeg_reports_missing_torch_cleanly`.

**Root cause:** both tests were written to rely on faster-whisper/torch genuinely not being installed in whatever environment ran them - true in this project's dev sandbox (no outbound network to install the [speech] extra), but false in real GitHub Actions CI, which runs `pip install -e ".[speech,translate,web]"` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) - and torch comes along transitively via `pyannote.audio`. With both packages actually present: `_get_whisper_model()`'s `WhisperModel(model_size, ...)` ran for real against the test's clearly-fake model name and raised faster-whisper's own `ValueError` ("Invalid model size...") instead of the clean `MediaToolError` the test expected; `_load_waveform_via_ffmpeg()`'s `import torch` succeeded and the function ran all the way to a real ffmpeg decode attempt against the test's nonexistent source file, instead of hitting the clean `MediaToolError` at the torch-import check.

**Fixed:** both tests now force the relevant import to fail via `monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "faster_whisper", None)` / `monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "torch", None)` - standard Python import behavior (`sys.modules[name] is None` makes `import name` raise `ImportError` unconditionally) rather than depending on ambient environment state. This verifies the same thing either way: whether or not the real package happens to be installed.

**Verification:** couldn't run real pytest in this sandbox (no network to install it), so hand-simulated both test bodies directly against the real `speech.py` code with the sys.modules override - both raised the expected `MediaToolError` with the expected message content. `python -m py_compile` confirmed no syntax errors in the edited test file.

## bv-web job runner: bv-config and bv-gps triggerable from the browser (increment 1)

Christer, after scoping the cost of wiring the full pipeline into bv-web: "so first a job runner and then bv-config and bv-gps" - then walked through the design before building (interactive vs. Y/N prompts, poll vs. websocket, permission granularity) and gave the go-ahead ("ok, go for it").

**Design decisions made along the way, each with Christer's input:** bv-config's wizard is free-text prompts with defaults, not Y/N questions - corrected before it shaped a flawed UI design. Output delivery is polling (`<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="2">`), not a websocket - interactive Q&A maps naturally to an ordinary POST/render cycle, non-interactive output is fine with a couple seconds of latency for a personal/family-scale app, and a websocket would be the first departure from bv-web's own "no client-side app" architecture. Permissions stay a single `require_owner` gate (already scaffolded, previously unused) rather than a granular per-command permission matrix - only worth building if there's a real semi-trusted third party, which there currently isn't.

**Job execution model:** new `web/jobs.py` (`JobStatus`, `Job`, `JobRunner`) runs each triggered command's own already-tested `_run()` function directly in a background `threading.Thread`, in-process - deliberately not a subprocess. A subprocess's stdout can't reliably distinguish "waiting for input" from "more output still coming" (`input()`'s own prompt text has no trailing newline), which would need fragile scraping heuristics; calling the real Python function directly means the job runner controls exactly when `ask()`/`say()` fire. It also avoids a thread-safety hazard a subprocess+global-`sys.stdout`-redirect approach would have, since each job's own `ask`/`say` closures only ever touch that job's own `Job.output` list.

`bv_config.py`'s `prompt()`/`edit_endpoints()`/`run_wizard()`/`_run()` and `bv_gps.py`'s `_run()` all gained injectable `ask`/`say`/`warn` keyword-only parameters (default: real `input`/`print`/stderr-`print` - real terminal use is completely unaffected). `Job.snapshot()` returns a lock-guarded `(status, output, prompt)` triple so a reader never sees a torn read (e.g. status already `waiting_for_input` but the old prompt still showing). `Job._answer_queue` (a `queue.Queue`) is what `ask()` blocks on until the browser POSTs an answer via `Job.submit_answer()`. Jobs live in an in-memory `dict` on `JobRunner` - the same restart-loses-state trade-off `SessionStore` already accepts.

**Wired into `web/app.py`:** `app.state.job_runner = JobRunner()`, plus six new routes - `GET`/`POST /jobs/bv-config`, `GET`/`POST /jobs/bv-gps`, `GET /jobs/{job_id}`, `POST /jobs/{job_id}/answer` - all gated by the existing `require_owner` dependency. `start_bv_config()` deliberately only takes the camera id (not every CLI flag) - matches the "curated subset" scope of this first increment. Three new templates (`job_new_bv_config.html`, `job_new_bv_gps.html`, `job_detail.html`); `base.html` gained owner-only nav links and CSS for the status badge/output transcript/answer form.

**Caught along the way:** `JobStatus(str, Enum)`'s own `__str__` renders as `"JobStatus.RUNNING"` in a Jinja `{{ status }}`, not the plain `"running"` the template's `{% if %}` checks and CSS classes need - fixed by passing `job_status.value` explicitly from `app.py`'s `job_detail` route rather than the raw enum. Python's default-argument binding also bit a first verification attempt: `def prompt(question, default="", *, ask=input)` binds the real `input` builtin at function-definition time, so monkeypatching `builtins.input` afterward has zero effect - must always pass `ask=` explicitly instead, which is exactly why the injectable parameter exists in the first place.

**Verification:** no fastapi/pytest available in this sandbox, so `app.py`'s routes were checked via `ast.parse()` rather than run for real. Everything else got genuine test coverage since none of it depends on fastapi: new `tests/blackvue/cli/test_bv_config.py` (13 tests - no test file existed for bv-config at all before this; covers `prompt()`/`edit_endpoints()`/`run_wizard()`/`_run()`, including the endpoint-review/remove/append loop and both retry paths) and new `tests/blackvue/web/test_jobs.py` (19 tests - `Job`/`JobStatus`'s state-machine methods directly, `JobRunner._spawn()`/`_make_ask()`'s thread/queue plumbing with a fake command, and `start_bv_config()`/`start_bv_gps()`'s real wiring with the target module's `_run()` monkeypatched out so no test touches a real camera or the real `~/.config/beyond-video`). The existing `tests/blackvue/cli/test_bv_gps.py` (18 tests) re-run in full to confirm the `say`/`warn` injection refactor didn't change its default (real-terminal) behavior - all still pass. All three files run via a hand-written fake-pytest harness (`monkeypatch`/`tmp_path`/`capsys` fixture substitutes), since no real pytest is installed in this sandbox.

### Follow-up: bv-gps job trigger loses --host, jobs gain a Cancel button

Christer, right after trying the job runner out: "I think it should only work with camera id, not with the test options of --host, we probably need a kill switch for jobs." Two separate fixes.

**bv-gps job trigger, camera id only:** `JobRunner.start_bv_gps()` dropped its `host` parameter entirely - it now only accepts `id_`/`no_address`/`username`. `bv-gps`'s own CLI keeps `--host` (a real terminal feature for probing a bare IP that hasn't been set up with bv-config yet, same use case as `scan_blackvue_endpoints.py`'s output) - only the browser-facing job trigger loses it, since that's a "test/scan an arbitrary address" escape hatch that shouldn't be reachable from a form anyone with owner access can submit. `job_new_bv_gps.html` lost its host field; `app.py`'s `new_bv_gps_submit` route lost its `host` form parameter.

**Kill switch, scoped by design discussion:** asked Christer what "kill switch" should actually mean - a per-job Cancel button, a global switch that disables triggering new jobs entirely, or both. He chose per-job Cancel. Python can't force-kill a thread, so this is honest about what it can and can't guarantee rather than pretending otherwise: new `JobStatus.CANCELLED` (counts as finished) plus `Job.cancel()`/`JobRunner.cancel()`. A job currently `waiting_for_input` is unblocked immediately - `cancel()` pushes a sentinel onto the job's own answer queue, its `ask()` recognizes the sentinel and raises a new `_JobCancelled` exception, which unwinds the wizard right away, same as any other exception escaping `_run()`. A job that's `running` with no prompt open (e.g. `bv-gps` blocked inside a socket call) can't be interrupted mid-call - `cancel()` instead flips the status to `CANCELLED` immediately so the browser stops trusting the job's output, while the background thread may keep running invisibly until whatever it's blocked on returns or times out on its own; `JobRunner._spawn()`'s completion handler now checks for an already-`CANCELLED` status before recording a success/failure result, so a thread that does eventually finish on its own doesn't clobber the cancellation the browser already saw.

New `POST /jobs/{job_id}/cancel` route (owner-only, same no-op-if-already-finished treatment as the existing `/answer` route). `job_detail.html` gets a "Cancel job" button whenever a job isn't finished; `base.html` gets a `.status-badge.cancelled` style and `.cancel-button` CSS.

**Verification:** `tests/blackvue/web/test_jobs.py` grew from 19 to 27 tests - `Job.cancel()`'s three cases (running, waiting-for-input, already-finished/already-cancelled) tested directly, plus `JobRunner.cancel()` exercised against a real background thread for both the waiting-for-input unblock path and the running-with-no-prompt path (including confirming a late-finishing thread doesn't overwrite the CANCELLED status). The two `start_bv_gps` host-related tests were replaced with id-only equivalents. `app.py`/`jobs.py` re-checked with `ast.parse()` (still no fastapi in this sandbox).

### Follow-up: camera pick-list instead of typing an id by hand

Christer: "i know most people will have only 1 config id, but we should support more, can it scan the config folder for config files to get a list or something." The job-trigger forms (bv-config, bv-gps) had only ever offered a bare text field for the camera id - fine for the common one-camera case, but meant retyping/remembering an id by hand for anyone with more than one.

**New `list_camera_ids(config_dir)` in `core/camera_config.py`**: returns every camera system id with a config file in `config_dir`, sorted alphabetically - filenames only (`*.cfg` stems via `Path.glob`), deliberately not loading/parsing each one, so a single corrupt config can't break the whole listing. Empty list if `config_dir` doesn't exist yet (e.g. before bv-config has ever been run). Every real `bv-*` command still requires an explicit id argument, same as before - this is purely for UIs that want to offer a pick-list.

**`app.py`'s new `_camera_options()`** scans the same `default_config_dir()` the job runner itself already hardcodes (`start_bv_config()`/`start_bv_gps()` neither take a `--config-dir` override), then loads each id's config just for a friendly label - `"<name> (<id>)"`, or just the id if name and id are the same. A config that fails to load falls back to showing its bare id rather than disappearing from the list or crashing the page.

**Forms updated differently based on what each command actually needs:** `job_new_bv_config.html` gets a `<datalist>` alongside its existing free-text id input (list="camera-ids") plus a small hint line listing existing cameras - bv-config can still create a brand-new id, so the field had to stay free text; the datalist is a suggestion, not a constraint. `job_new_bv_gps.html` instead switched from a text input to a real `<select>`, since bv-gps only ever works against an already-configured id (never a new one) - if no cameras exist yet, the page shows a message pointing at bv-config instead of an empty/useless dropdown. `base.html` gained matching `select` styling (previously only text/password inputs were styled) and a `.hint` class for the small existing-cameras line.

**Verification:** new tests in `tests/blackvue/core/test_camera_config.py` (sorted listing, ignores non-`.cfg` files, ignores a directory that happens to be named `*.cfg`, empty when the dir is missing/empty, doesn't raise on a corrupt config) - all pass against a real TOML-parsing stub built for this verification pass (the sandbox has no real `tomllib`/`tomli` available, Python 3.10 and no network - previous sessions' fake stub always returned `{}}`, which happened to not matter for tests that never called `load_camera_config()` for real content, but would have silently passed a broken round-trip test; this session's stub actually parses the project's own simple TOML subset). `_camera_options()`'s logic (label building, corrupt-config fallback, empty-dir case) verified directly against real `save_camera_config()`-written files. Both templates rendered directly through real Jinja2 (available in this sandbox) across all four cases (with/without existing cameras, both templates) and inspected by hand. `app.py` re-checked with `ast.parse()`.

### Follow-up: grouped form fields (Required/Defaults/Optional) + help tooltips

Christer: "i would like to split up options in 2 or 3 groups. Required, Defaults (maybe not an own group) and Optional. We also need some help on each command and a help balloon for each option." Asked where this should apply (bv-web's browser forms, vs. each CLI's own terminal --help output) and which command(s), since "help balloon" is a UI/browser term with no real terminal equivalent - confirmed: the bv-web job-trigger forms, starting with bv-config/bv-gps (the only two wired in so far), with the eventual goal of covering every command once/if the rest of the pipeline gets wired into bv-web too.

**Grouping**: both `job_new_bv_config.html` and `job_new_bv_gps.html` now wrap their fields in `.option-group` sections with a `<h3>Required</h3>` / `<h3>Defaults</h3>` / `<h3>Optional</h3>` heading - not every command needs all three (bv-config's job form only has a `Required` group today, since `--config-dir` stays deliberately unexposed - see the camera-pick-list follow-up above for why). To actually make the "Defaults" group mean something for bv-gps rather than being empty, its own `--timeout` flag (a real bv-gps CLI option, previously never exposed through the job form) got wired through: `JobRunner.start_bv_gps()` gained a `timeout: int` parameter, `app.py`'s `new_bv_gps_submit` route gained `timeout: int = Form(5, ge=1)` (validated at the FastAPI layer so a bad value 422s cleanly rather than reaching `bv_gps.parse_args()`'s own `type=int` and crashing the app), and the form gained a "Connection timeout (seconds)" number input defaulting to 5.

**Help tooltips ("help balloons")**: implemented as a pure-CSS tooltip (`.help-tip` - a small circular "?" next to each field label; `.tooltip-text` - the hidden balloon, shown via `:hover`/`:focus` so it's keyboard-accessible too) - no JavaScript, consistent with bv-web's existing "no client-side app" approach used everywhere else (polling instead of websockets, `<meta refresh>` instead of JS). Each field's tooltip explains what that specific option does; a `.command-help` box at the top of each form explains what the command as a whole does (bv-config's wizard flow, bv-gps's live-fetch-and-print behavior).

**Design intentionally left generic rather than building a schema system**: fields/groups/tooltip text are hardcoded directly in each template rather than introduced as a generic option-metadata abstraction (e.g. a shared Python data structure driving both the CLI's argparse `help=` strings and the web form) - with only two commands and a handful of fields in bv-web today, that abstraction would be speculative. If/when bv-export's 47-flag surface gets wired in, the grouping/tooltip *pattern* established here (three `.option-group` sections, one `.help-tip` per field) is meant to scale to that without a page redesign - but the actual data-driven refactor is worth doing at that point, not before.

**Verification**: both templates rendered directly through real Jinja2 across all four cases (with/without existing cameras) and inspected by hand - no stray `{%`/`{{` left unrendered, correct group/tooltip structure. `tests/blackvue/web/test_jobs.py` updated for `start_bv_gps()`'s new required `timeout` parameter (2 existing tests) plus one new test confirming a non-default timeout value reaches `bv_gps.parse_args()` correctly - 28/28 passing (up from 27). `app.py`/`jobs.py` re-checked with `ast.parse()`.

## bv-web archive browser: browse bv-download's raw archive, with thumbnails

Christer: "More stuff. Today we already have view trips, later maybe we should allow for view archive videos to." Asked what "archive videos" meant, since bv-web only knows about `bv-export`'s processed trip output today - "The raw archive, with thumbnails to easier find a video in the archive. nothing fancy." Also confirmed access level: same as trip browsing (`require_login`, any logged-in user), not owner-only.

**What "raw archive" means here, and why it's a different data source than trips**: `bv-download` writes a flat, unstructured directory per camera - `YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_K{F|R|I}.ext` files (video/GPS/g-sensor/thumbnail sidecars), no subfolders, no trip grouping. That directory is `CameraConfig.target` - not the same thing as `bv-export --target`/`app.state.target` (the trips directory `trips.py` already reads). A camera id names a *source* archive; a trip id names *processed* output produced from one or more archives. Conflating the two would have meant either browsing the wrong directory or reusing `trips.py`'s trip-folder assumptions somewhere they don't apply.

**New `web/archive_browser.py`** is deliberately thin, mirroring how thin `trips.py` already is relative to what it wraps: it reuses `blackvue.archive.Archive`/`ArchiveReader` - the exact same reader `bv-ls`/`bv-export` already use to enumerate recordings - rather than writing any new archive-scanning logic. `ArchiveRecording` wraps a `camera_id` + the real `Recording` with browsing-friendly properties (`id`, `timestamp`, `kind_label` mapping N/E/M/P/A to Normal/Event/Manual/Parking/Unknown, `size_label`, `videos`/`sidecars` as (label, filename) pairs, `thumbnail_direction`, `known_filenames`, `file_path()`/`thumbnail_path()`). `scan_archive()` mirrors `scan_trips()`'s missing-directory convention (a camera that's never been downloaded from yet is zero recordings, not an error - guards with `.is_dir()` first since `ArchiveReader.read()`'s `os.scandir()` raises `FileNotFoundError` otherwise), sorted newest-first via `RecordingId`'s own `order=True` dataclass comparison. `find_recording()` is a single-item lookup (there's no cheaper way than a full scan, same trade-off `scan_archive()` itself already accepts) and `group_by_day()` buckets an already-sorted list via `itertools.groupby` for the day-grouped grid template.

**Thumbnails are real files already on disk, not generated**: `bv-download` already downloads `.thm` sidecars unconditionally (the sidecar-probing feature from a previous session), so no ffmpeg-based thumbnail generation exists or was needed anywhere. `thumbnail_direction` prefers front, then rear, then interior, and is `None` when a recording has no thumbnail at all (older archives, or a camera/firmware that never served `.thm` files) - the list template shows a plain "No thumbnail" placeholder in that case rather than a broken image.

**Wired into `app.py`**: five new routes - `GET /archive` (camera picker, reusing the existing `_camera_options()` pick-list from the job-trigger forms), `GET /archive/{camera_id}` (day-grouped thumbnail grid), `GET /archive/{camera_id}/{recording_id}` (detail page with video playback + download links), `GET /archive/{camera_id}/{recording_id}/thumbnail/{direction}`, `GET /archive/{camera_id}/{recording_id}/files/{filename}` - all gated by `require_login`, not `require_owner`, matching Christer's answer. New `_find_camera_archive(camera_id)` helper resolves a camera id to its archive directory via `load_camera_config()`, and `_find_archive_recording()` builds on it plus `find_recording()`. Both `camera_id` and `recording_id` path segments get the same untrusted-URL-segment guard `_find_trip()` already uses for `trip_id` (reject `/`, `\`, and `.`/`..` before ever touching the filesystem), and the file-serving/thumbnail routes check requested filenames against `ArchiveRecording.known_filenames` before resolving a path - same allow-list pattern as `trips.py`'s `trip_file` route.

**Three new templates** (`archive_camera_list.html`, `archive_recording_list.html`, `archive_recording_detail.html`) plus a `.thumb-grid`/`.thumb-card`/`.thumb-image`/`.thumb-placeholder`/`.thumb-meta`/`.day-heading` CSS block in `base.html`, and a "Browse archive" nav link visible to every logged-in user (not inside the owner-only block that already gates the job-trigger links). No caching, same as `trips.py` - every request rescans the archive directory fresh.

**Verification**: new `tests/blackvue/web/test_archive_browser.py` (18 tests) builds small fake archives on disk using the real `ArchiveReader` filename convention rather than mocking `Archive` - covers empty/missing archives, kind-letter label mapping, newest-first sorting, `videos`/`sidecars`/`thumbnail_direction`/`thumbnail_path`/`known_filenames`/`file_path`/`size_label`, `find_recording()`'s found/not-found/missing-archive cases, and `group_by_day()`'s grouping and empty-input cases - all 18 pass via the hand-written fake-pytest harness (no real pytest in this sandbox). All three new templates rendered directly through real Jinja2 (populated cases and empty-state cases for each) and inspected by hand - no stray `{%`/`{{` left unrendered, correct nav/CSS output. `app.py`/`archive_browser.py` re-checked with `ast.parse()` (still no fastapi in this sandbox, consistent with every other bv-web route-level change this project has made).

### Follow-up: mode + lexical time-range filters for the archive browser

Christer: "Since there are so many video files in an archive, we might need a filter for MODE selection and our fantastic lexical timestamp range." A long archive's day-grouped thumbnail grid can still be a lot to scroll through even grouped by day, so the archive browser's list page gained a filter bar.

**Reused the project's existing lexical time filter rather than inventing a new one**: `lexicaltimeparser.py`'s `LexicalTimeParser`/`TimeInterval` is already what `bv-ls`/`bv-export`/`bv-download`/`bv-generate` all filter recordings with on the CLI side - a prefix like `2026`, `20260715`, or `20260715_14` expands to an inclusive lexical range (`--timestamp` for an exact prefix match, or `--from`/`--until` for a range; the two forms can't be combined, enforced by `LexicalTimeParser.parse()` itself raising `ValueError`). `archive_browser.py` now imports `TimeInterval` and reuses it as-is - `ArchiveRecording.id` (e.g. `"20260715_140212_N"`) is exactly the string form `TimeInterval.__contains__` already knows how to match (it strips the trailing `_K` suffix itself).

**New in `archive_browser.py`**: `kind_options()` returns the canonical N/E/M/P/A `(letter, label)` pairs the filter bar's checkboxes are built from (reusing the existing `_KIND_LABELS` mapping). `filter_recordings(recordings, *, modes=None, time_interval=None)` applies both filters over an already-`scan_archive()`'d list - `modes=None` (not an empty set) means "no mode filter, show every kind," matching how an unchecked-by-default checkbox row should read; an explicit empty set would mean "match nothing," which is a real but different case, covered by its own test.

**Wired into `app.py`**: `GET /archive/{camera_id}` gained four query params - `mode` (repeatable, `Query(default=[])`), `timestamp`, `from` (aliased from Python's reserved `from_`), `until`. An empty `mode` selection becomes `modes=None` before calling `filter_recordings()` (not `modes=set()`) - the "nothing checked = no filter" convention from `filter_recordings()`'s own docstring. A `LexicalTimeParser.parse()` `ValueError` (e.g. `--timestamp` combined with `--from`) doesn't 500 the page or silently drop the filter - it's caught, shown as an inline error message, and the full unfiltered list renders underneath so the owner can see what to fix, mirroring how a bad CLI flag combination would just print an error rather than doing something unexpected.

**`archive_recording_list.html`** gained a `<form method="get">` filter bar above the thumbnail grid - mode checkboxes (pre-checked to match the current query string) plus three text inputs (Exact/From/Until) with a `.help-tip` explaining the lexical prefix format, an Apply button, and a "Clear filters" link shown only when a filter is actually active. Deliberately `GET`, not `POST` - the resulting URL (`?mode=E&from=20260701`) is bookmarkable/shareable and survives a page reload, consistent with bv-web's "no client-side app" approach used everywhere else. The empty-state message now distinguishes "no recordings match these filters" from "no recordings in this archive yet" depending on whether a filter is active. New `.filter-bar`/`.filter-row`/`.filter-label`/`.filter-modes`/`.filter-checkbox`/`.filter-fields`/`.filter-actions` CSS in `base.html`.

**Verification**: `tests/blackvue/web/test_archive_browser.py` grew from 18 to 26 tests - `kind_options()`'s canonical ordering, `filter_recordings()` with no filters/a single mode/multiple modes/an explicit empty mode set (matches nothing, as documented)/a lexical range/an exact prefix/mode+time combined. All 26 pass via the same hand-written fake-pytest harness. `archive_recording_list.html` re-rendered through real Jinja2 across four new cases (results with no filter, filtered-to-empty with the "Clear filters" link, empty archive with no filter and no "Clear filters" link, and the error-message case) and inspected by hand. `app.py`/`archive_browser.py` re-checked with `ast.parse()` (still no fastapi in this sandbox).

### Follow-up: bv-config job page's auto-refresh was wiping the answer field mid-type

Christer, trying the bv-config job form via the browser: "In bv-config when i try to fill name, it gets deleted." Confirmed he meant the browser job form, not the terminal.

**Root cause**: `job_detail.html`'s `<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="2">` was gated on `{% if not is_finished %}` - which is true for `waiting_for_input` just as much as `running`. So while the job was paused waiting for an answer (e.g. bv-config's "Name" prompt), the page kept reloading every 2 seconds regardless, wiping out whatever partial text was sitting in the answer `<input>` before the owner could finish typing it and hit Answer.

**Fix**: changed the condition to `{% if status == "running" %}` - the meta refresh only fires while a job is actively running with no open prompt (the case that genuinely needs polling for new output). Once a job reaches `waiting_for_input`, polling stops entirely; the page only reloads again once the owner submits the answer form (`POST /jobs/{job_id}/answer`, which redirects back to `GET /jobs/{job_id}` - a fresh, deliberate reload, not a timed one). If the job goes back to `running` after that (or asks another question), refresh resumes/stops accordingly on the next render.

**Verification**: rendered `job_detail.html` through real Jinja2 for all three states - confirmed no `http-equiv="refresh"` in the `waiting_for_input` output (and the answer `<input>` present), confirmed it *is* present for `running`, and confirmed it's absent for a finished (`succeeded`) job too (already correct before this fix, re-checked as a regression guard). No existing test file renders `job_detail.html` at the pytest level (verification for this template has always been direct Jinja2 rendering + inspection, same as this session's other template checks) - not a Python-testable behavior on its own since it's pure template conditionals with no accompanying app.py logic change.

### Follow-up: archive browser was slow to load thumbnails, and video playback hung

Christer, about the archive browser: "It slow before loading thumbnails, and when i click on a thumbnail i get a player, that hangs or are very slow to load."

**Root cause**: `find_recording()` resolved a single recording id by calling `scan_archive()` - a full read of the *entire* archive directory - and then linear-searching the result for a match. That's fine once per page load (the day-grouped grid page does exactly that), but `find_recording()` itself is called far more often than once per page: once per thumbnail `<img>` on the grid page (each thumbnail is its own HTTP request to `/archive/{camera_id}/{recording_id}/thumbnail/{direction}`), and once per HTTP range request a video player makes while seeking/buffering on the detail page (`/archive/{camera_id}/{recording_id}/files/{filename}`, and video players routinely make dozens of range requests per playback session). A full `scan_archive()` calls `os.scandir()` + `stat()` on every single file across the whole archive - so an N-recording page with N thumbnails was O(N^2) (N full archive scans just to render N images), and every seek/buffer during playback re-scanned the entire archive from scratch, which is exactly what felt like a hang.

**Fix**: added `ArchiveReader.read_recording(recording_id)` to `archive/archive_reader.py` - a targeted lookup that globs only for files whose name starts with the requested recording's own 17-character id prefix (`archive_path.glob(f"{recording_id.value}*")`), rather than `os.scandir()`-ing and `stat()`-ing every file in the archive. It reuses `_detect_asset()`/`ASSETS` (the same suffix-to-Asset classification `read()` itself uses) and builds a `Recording` the same way, so it stays in lockstep with any future asset type the reader learns about - no logic duplicated, just a narrower scan. `ArchiveReader` is now exported from `archive/__init__.py` (it previously wasn't - only `Archive` was, since nothing outside the archive package needed the reader directly before this). `web/archive_browser.py`'s `find_recording()` now calls `ArchiveReader(archive_path).read_recording(parsed_id)` instead of scanning+searching via `scan_archive()`. `scan_archive()` itself is untouched - the day-grouped grid page still does one full read per page load, which is fine (that's the actually-necessary "list everything" case, not a per-recording lookup).

**Measured improvement**: a synthetic 400-recording archive (6 files each, matching a realistic front+rear+thumbnails+GPS+g-sensor set) went from ~14.7ms/call to ~0.9ms/call for `find_recording()` - roughly 15x at N=400, and the gap widens linearly with archive size since the old path was O(N) per call and the new one is ~O(1) (bounded by how many files share one recording's own prefix, not by archive size).

**Verification**: new tests appended to `tests/blackvue/archive/test_archive_reader.py` (found/not-found/missing-directory/ignores-other-recordings/matches-read()'s-own-result/correct-total-size - 6 new tests, all pass) confirm `read_recording()` behaves identically to filtering `read()`'s full result, just without the full scan. `tests/blackvue/web/test_archive_browser.py`'s existing `find_recording()` tests (found/not-found/missing-archive) still pass unchanged against the new implementation - a pure behavior-preserving swap underneath. `app.py`/`archive_browser.py`/`archive_reader.py`/`archive/__init__.py` re-checked with `ast.parse()` (still no fastapi/pytest in this sandbox; the two pre-existing test files that need `pytest`/`capsys` fixtures the hand-written harness doesn't provide - `test_configuration.py`, one test in `test_archive.py` - are pre-existing sandbox limitations unrelated to this change).

### Follow-up: playback slowness was actually event-loop blocking from the archive scan bug, not (mainly) network latency; removed GPS/G-sensor download links

Christer, after the thumbnail/video perf fix: "Now the thumbnails was fast, when i start to play its slow trips too (on my pc), before when i run it on the NAS it was quick for trips. When i clicl on the 3gf or gps file they get downloaded by the browser, whats the thought about that?" - two separate items.

**Playback slowness - first (wrong) theory, then the real cause**: initially guessed pure network latency (bv-web on the PC, archive/trips folders still on the NAS over the network) since `trips.py` was never touched this session yet trip playback slowed down too. Christer confirmed the PC/NAS split, which fit that theory - but after pushing the `find_recording()` perf fix, he reported trip playback got fast again too, on the same PC, over the same network path. That ruled out network latency as the (main) explanation, since nothing about the network changed - only the archive-scanning code did.

The real mechanism: every route in `app.py`, including `trip_file` and the archive routes, is declared `async def`. Starlette only offloads *synchronous* (`def`) route handlers to a thread pool; an `async def` handler's own body runs directly on the single-threaded asyncio event loop uvicorn serves every concurrent request through. The old `find_recording()` did a fully synchronous `os.scandir()` + `.stat()` scan of the whole archive (`Archive.__init__()`/`ArchiveReader.read()`, no `anyio`/thread-pool offload anywhere in that path) inside that `async def` handler - so for however long that scan took, it blocked the *entire* event loop, stalling every other in-flight request on the server, including an unrelated trip's `FileResponse` range requests (which are themselves async-safe/non-blocking - Starlette's `FileResponse` reads file chunks via `anyio.open_file()` off-thread - but still have to wait their turn on the same blocked loop). One recording's thumbnail grid or a video player's dozens of range requests were enough sync-blocking time to make *everything* on `bv-web` feel slow, not just the archive browser itself. Once `read_recording()` made that per-request work ~O(1) instead of O(archive size), the blocking window shrank to a few milliseconds, and trip playback - never touched by any of this session's code - got fast again as a side effect.

**Residual risk, not yet acted on**: `scan_archive()` (used once per `/archive/{camera_id}` list-page load, for the day-grouped grid) is still a fully synchronous full-archive scan with no thread-pool offload. That's intentionally not O(N^2) like the old bug was, but on a very large archive - especially over Christer's NAS network path, where each `stat()` costs real round-trip time - a single list-page load could still block the event loop for a noticeable stretch and transiently stall other users'/trips' concurrent requests. Wrapping that call (and the equivalent one in `_find_trip`/`_find_archive_recording` if they ever grow real I/O cost) in `anyio.to_thread.run_sync()` would remove this class of bug entirely rather than just shrinking it - not done here since nothing currently reported this as a problem, but worth keeping in mind if a large archive ever makes list-page loads themselves feel slow to other concurrent users.

`docs/DEPLOY.md` still documents running `bv-web` on the NAS itself as the intended production setup - that remains true and worth doing eventually for the network-latency-on-individual-reads factor (a real, separate, smaller effect from the event-loop-blocking bug above), just not the explanation for what Christer actually observed here.

### Follow-up: a flaky sidecar probe was silently blocking bv-download's partial-video resume

Christer: "something is broken in bv-download it doesnt fix partial downloaded videos any more."

**Root cause**: `_run()`'s per-recording loop in `cli/bv_download.py` calls `camera.probe_missing_sidecars(recording)` (the opportunistic .gps/.3gf/.thm check - see the sidecar-probing feature above) immediately before `camera.download(recording, ...)` - and `camera.download()` is the one place with the actual partial-file resume logic (`BlackVueClient.download()`: compares local file size to a HEAD'd remote size, and does a `Range: bytes=<local_size>-` request to resume a short local file, untouched by anything this session). The `except OSError: continue` wrapped around the probe call (added for the skip-and-continue-on-one-bad-recording behavior from an earlier session, see the `--trace`/timeout-handling entry above) meant that if the probe itself hit a transient `OSError` - a dropped WiFi frame, a timeout - the whole recording was skipped via `continue`, **before `camera.download()` ever ran**. A recording with a genuinely partial video already on disk from an interrupted earlier run would just sit there unrepaired for as many runs as its sidecar probe kept failing, with only a "couldn't check for sidecar files... skipping this recording" message as a clue - nothing indicating the video itself was never even attempted.

**Fix**: the probe's `except OSError` block no longer `continue`s. It now just treats the probe as having found nothing (`found = []`), prints a softer message ("continuing without it" instead of "skipping this recording"), and falls through to the download step regardless - `camera.download()` (and its resume logic) now always gets a chance to run for every recording in the batch, whether or not the sidecar probe that ran just before it succeeded. `failed_ids` (which drives the batch's exit code and end-of-run summary) is no longer appended to on a probe failure either, since the recording's actual download may still succeed - only a genuine download failure counts as a batch failure now.

**Verification**: `tests/blackvue/cli/test_bv_download.py`'s `test_run_skips_a_recording_whose_sidecar_probe_fails` - which had asserted the buggy behavior as if it were correct (`camera.downloaded_ids` missing the recording whose probe failed, `exit_code == EXIT_PARTIAL_FAILURE`) - renamed to `test_run_still_downloads_a_recording_whose_sidecar_probe_fails` and rewritten to assert the fixed behavior (both recordings downloaded, `exit_code == EXIT_OK`, the probe-failure message still printed for visibility). All 47 tests in the file still pass, run via a hand-built fixture harness (no real pytest/tomllib in this Python 3.10 sandbox - stubbed both as bare-minimum `sys.modules` entries just for import purposes, since none of this file's tests actually exercise real TOML parsing or `pytest.raises` outside a couple of unrelated argument-parsing tests). `ast.parse()` on `bv_download.py` (still no fastapi in this sandbox, unrelated to this file but kept for consistency with every other syntax-only check this project does).

**Correction**: the above "trips got fast again too" observation, and the event-loop-blocking explanation for it, turned out to be wrong - or at least premature. Christer tested more carefully: the one trip that played fast right after the archive fix was one he'd already played before (during earlier testing), and a different, not-yet-played trip was slow again. That means the "trip got fast" data point was very likely just Windows SMB client-side caching (or NAS-side RAM caching) of a file already read once, not anything the archive-scanning fix touched - `trips.py` was never modified this session, and there's no code path connecting the archive routes' event loop time to how fast an unrelated trip's *first* read from the NAS streams in. The event-loop-blocking analysis above is still correct and still real for the archive routes themselves (that part was independently verified via the benchmark and the fix's own test coverage) - it just isn't the explanation for trip playback speed, which this session's changes never touched either way. The likely, boring explanation for "first play of any given trip is slow, replays are fast" is the original one: `bv-web` on the PC reads a cold file from the NAS over the network (real, unavoidable per-file latency/throughput cost), and once read once, it's cached somewhere in the read path (Windows/SMB client, the NAS's own cache, or OS page cache) so a repeat read of that *same* file is fast. Nothing here points to a bug in this project's code - moving `bv-web` back onto the NAS (per `docs/DEPLOY.md`) would remove the network hop for every read, cold or not, which is the only real fix available if the cold-read cost itself is a problem worth solving.

**GPS/G-sensor sidecar links removed from the archive detail page**: clicking a `.gps`/`.3gf` link triggered a browser download instead of viewing anything, because Python's `mimetypes` module has no mapping for those non-standard extensions, so Starlette's `FileResponse` falls back to `application/octet-stream` - browsers treat that as "download," not "display." Asked what behavior was wanted (keep downloading / view `.gps` inline as text, since it's plain NMEA text unlike the genuinely-binary `.3gf` / leave as-is); Christer's answer was simpler than any of those: "I don't want to see them att all." Removed the `{% for label, filename in recording.sidecars %}` loop from `archive_recording_detail.html` entirely - the video links (`recording.videos`) are untouched. Left `ArchiveRecording.sidecars`/`has_gps`/`has_gsensor` in `archive_browser.py` as-is (still real, tested properties on the model - `test_sidecars_lists_gps_and_gsensor_when_present` still covers `sidecars` - just no longer rendered anywhere); the GPS/g-sensor files themselves are untouched on disk and still downloadable directly by filename if someone knows the URL, since `known_filenames`/`file_path()` weren't changed.

**Verification**: `archive_recording_detail.html` re-rendered through real Jinja2 with a fake recording carrying both video and sidecar entries - confirmed no `.gps`/`.3gf`/"GPS log"/"G-sensor log" text anywhere in the output, and both video links still present. No Python logic changed (template-only edit), so no new test file needed; existing `tests/blackvue/web/test_archive_browser.py` (26 tests, including `test_sidecars_lists_gps_and_gsensor_when_present`) still passes unchanged since the `sidecars` property itself wasn't touched.

### Follow-up: `git pull` fails on the NAS's existing checkout - `docs/DEPLOY.md`'s update instructions were stale

Christer tried updating his NAS's existing `bv-web` container to pick up this session's fixes, following `docs/DEPLOY.md`'s "Updating later" section as written (`git pull`). It failed: `git pull` reported "You have divergent branches and need to specify how to reconcile them" after a `(forced update)` fetch.

**Root cause**: this repo's git history has been force-rewritten more than once in the past (see the real-IP scrub and the ap_ssid-ID scrub entries earlier in this file, plus the No_Parking-clips purge) - each rewrite replaces `origin/main`'s commit history outright rather than adding commits on top of it. Any existing clone made before a given rewrite (Christer's NAS checkout, in this case) shares old commits with the new history only up to the rewrite point, then diverges completely - there's nothing for `git pull`'s merge/rebase to reconcile, since the "old" and "new" versions of every commit after that point are unrelated objects with different hashes. `docs/DEPLOY.md`'s "Updating later" section had never been updated to account for this - it was written before any of the history rewrites happened, and nobody had hit the resulting failure on a real deployment until now.

**Fix**: `docs/DEPLOY.md`'s "Updating later" section now uses `git fetch origin` + `git reset --hard origin/main` instead of `git pull`, with a paragraph explaining why (history rewrites, divergent branches, `reset --hard` just points the local branch at `origin/main` directly rather than trying to merge unrelated histories). Confirmed this doesn't touch `data/` (gitignored, `reset --hard` only affects git-tracked files) - accounts/config/archive/trips all survive exactly as the old "Updating later" text already claimed.

**Not independently verified against a real NAS** (no access to Christer's NAS from this sandbox) - the fix is git behavior that doesn't need bv-web-specific verification, and matches the same `git fetch && git reset --hard origin/main` pattern already used (and explained) elsewhere in this same doc's step 2/step 7 commentary, which was apparently never carried over to the "Updating later" section when it was originally written.

### Follow-up: `docker-compose build bv-web` sent an 88.56GB build context - Synology's `#recycle` folder

After the git-update fix above, Christer rebuilt `bv-web` for real and hit exactly the "hanging" symptom reported earlier in this session - except this time the build actually did finish (`Successfully built`/`Successfully tagged`/`Recreating beyond-video-web ... done`), just after printing `Sending build context to Docker daemon 88.56GB` and then staying silent for minutes. Docker prints nothing while gathering/tar-ing the build context, so a context that size explains the apparent hang and the earlier `top`/`df -h` observations (dockerd at ~93% CPU, nothing else obviously running) perfectly - it wasn't stuck, it was tar-ing tens of gigabytes.

**Root cause**: `du -sh /volume1/beyond-video/*` found it - `#recycle` alone was 83G. That's DSM's own Recycle Bin for the `beyond-video` shared folder (same family of hidden-at-the-shared-folder-root housekeeping directory as `@eaDir`, which step 2 of this doc already warned about for `git clone` - files "deleted" through DSM land here instead of actually being removed, and it isn't visible in File Station by default). `.dockerignore` already excluded `data/` (where the real archive/trips content lives), but had no entry for `#recycle` or `@eaDir`, so Docker's build-context walker picked up all 83G+ of it every single build.

**Fix**: added `\#recycle/` and `@eaDir/` to `.dockerignore`. The backslash matters: `.dockerignore` follows the same convention as `.gitignore` where a line starting with `#` is a comment, not a pattern - a bare `#recycle` line would have been silently ignored rather than actually excluding the folder, so it has to be escaped as `\#recycle`.

**Not yet independently confirmed to have fixed the context size** - the fix is based on directly reading the `du -sh` output Christer ran and pasted, which unambiguously shows `#recycle` as the dominant contributor at 83G out of the reported 88.56G context; the next `docker-compose build bv-web` on his NAS should show a dramatically smaller "Sending build context" line if this is right. Also flagged to Christer, not yet acted on: the same `du` output showed several stray 0-byte files/directories sitting directly in `/volume1/beyond-video/` with names matching Docker image layer hashes from the build log (e.g. `07e73fe84973`, `d2e817ebc210`) plus word-fragment names (`Runni`, `Running`, `Using`, `debconf:`) - almost certainly created by pasting terminal/build output into an active shell at some point, where stray words got shell-interpreted. Harmless (0 bytes, and `.dockerignore` doesn't need to exclude them since they cost nothing in the build context) but worth a manual cleanup for tidiness; not fixed here since it's unrelated to the actual problem and only Christer can safely identify/remove them via his own shell.

Separately worth Christer's own judgment call, not performed here: DSM's Recycle Bin for that shared folder can be emptied from File Station (right-click the shared folder -> Recycle Bin, or Control Panel -> Shared Folder settings) to reclaim the real 83G of disk space those "deleted" files are still occupying, if he doesn't need them - not something to do blindly from a terminal `rm -rf`, since the whole point of DSM's Recycle Bin is to let him review what's actually in there first.

### Follow-up: bv-web's Docker container couldn't see any camera at all - `default_config_dir()` had no persisted `$HOME`

Once `bv-web` was actually running on the NAS (build context fixed above, container up and confirmed clean in `docker-compose logs`), Christer asked "why is my archive empty seen from docker" after confirming (via `docker-compose config`) that `bv-cli`'s `/data/archive` mount correctly points at his real archive folder.

**Root cause**: `bv-web`'s own `docker-compose.yml` service had no volume for camera `.cfg` files at all - only `./data/trips` (read-only) and `./data/config` (bv-web's own `web-users.cfg`, an unrelated file). Both the camera pick-list (`app.py`'s `_camera_options()`) and the archive browser's camera-to-archive-path resolution (`_find_camera_archive()`) call `core/camera_config.py`'s `default_config_dir()` with no override - which resolves to `Path.home() / ".config" / "beyond-video"`. Inside a Docker container running as root with no `USER` directive (confirmed via `Dockerfile` - none set), that's `/root/.config/beyond-video`: a fresh, empty directory baked into the image, never mounted to anything persisted, and completely disconnected from `/volume1/beyond-video/data/camera-config` - the real folder `bv-cli`'s own `docker-compose run --rm bv-cli bv-config Kirby --config-dir /data/config` invocations actually write `Kirby.cfg` into. So `bv-web`'s container had zero visibility into any camera ever configured: an empty pick-list on the job-trigger forms, and every archive-browser camera id 404ing - "archive empty" was really "no camera found at all," one level up from what it looked like.

Same root cause also silently affects the in-process job runner: `jobs.py`'s `start_bv_config()`/`start_bv_gps()` deliberately don't take a `--config-dir` override either ("curated subset, not every CLI flag" - see their own docstrings), so triggering "bv-config" from bv-web's own browser UI would have written a new camera's config into that same disconnected `/root/.config/beyond-video` - invisible to `bv-cli`, and lost on the next container rebuild.

**Fix**: `default_config_dir()` now checks a `BEYOND_VIDEO_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable first, falling back to `~/.config/beyond-video` if unset - every CLI's own `--config-dir` flag still defaults to calling this same function, so nothing about native/bare-metal use changes. `docker-compose.yml`'s `bv-web` service gained `environment: - BEYOND_VIDEO_CONFIG_DIR=/data/camera-config` plus a new `./data/camera-config:/data/camera-config` volume (read-write, since the in-browser bv-config job can create/edit a camera, not just read one `bv-cli` already wrote) - the *same* host folder `bv-cli`'s own camera-config mount already points at, so a camera set up either way is visible to both containers. `Dockerfile` now also `mkdir -p`s `/data/camera-config` alongside the existing `/data/trips`/`/data/config`, matching the "missing directory reads as empty, not an error" convention this app uses everywhere else if that volume ever isn't mounted for some reason.

Chose an environment variable over adding a `--config-dir` flag to `bv-web serve` (and threading it through `create_app()`/`JobRunner`) specifically to preserve the "curated subset, not every CLI flag" design principle already established for this job runner three separate times (`_camera_options()`, `start_bv_config()`, `start_bv_gps()` docstrings all say some version of this) - the fix needed to reach all three call sites without adding new plumbing to any of them, and they all already share the one low-level function this touches.

Confirmed via `docker-compose config` (Christer pasted the real merged output) that his `docker-compose.override.yml` only overrides `bv-cli`'s archive path (`/volume1/Dashcam/files`), not camera-config - so the base `docker-compose.yml` fix here needs no matching change in his personal override file.

**Verification**: `core/camera_config.py`/`web/app.py`/`web/jobs.py`/`cli/bv_config.py`/`cli/bv_gps.py` re-checked with `ast.parse()`. Three new tests in `tests/blackvue/core/test_camera_config.py` (`test_default_config_dir_uses_env_var_override_when_set`, `test_default_config_dir_falls_back_to_home_when_unset`, `test_default_config_dir_falls_back_to_home_when_empty` - an empty string is treated as unset, not as `Path("")`'s own surprising "current directory" meaning) pass via a hand-built fixture harness supporting `monkeypatch.setenv`/`delenv` (no real pytest in this Python 3.10 sandbox). The file's three pre-existing failures (`test_load_defaults_id_and_name_from_filename`, `test_load_missing_target_is_an_error`, `test_save_and_load_round_trip`) are the same sandbox-only TOML-stub limitation noted in earlier sessions, unrelated to this change - confirmed unchanged before/after. **Not yet confirmed against Christer's real NAS** - waiting on him to `git pull` + rebuild + check the camera pick-list/archive browser actually populate now.

After rebuilding `bv-web` with the `default_config_dir()` fix above, Christer's camera pick-list worked, but every camera's `/archive/{camera_id}` page said "No recordings found in this camera's archive yet." - even for a camera `bv-download` had already filled with real files. Fixed by navigating to the bare `/` URL to drop the stale `next` value; no code changed for this part (Christer didn't ask for the 404 page itself to be made friendlier, so that's still raw JSON today - a candidate follow-up, not done).

The actual archive-browser bug: `app.py`'s `_find_camera_archive()` resolves a camera id to `CameraConfig.target` (e.g. `/data/archive/Kirby`), and `scan_archive()` reads recordings straight from that path - a completely separate lookup from `default_config_dir()`/`BEYOND_VIDEO_CONFIG_DIR` above, which only covers finding the camera's `.cfg` file, not the recordings the config file points at. `docker-compose.yml`'s `bv-web` service had never had a `/data/archive` volume at all - only `bv-cli` did (added back when this project was pipeline-only, before the archive-browser feature existed) - so once `bv-web` could see the camera's config, it still couldn't see any of the files that config pointed at.

Also caught and fixed proactively: Christer's own `docker-compose.override.yml` (confirmed via an earlier `docker-compose config` paste) only redirects `bv-cli`'s archive mount to his real path (`/volume1/Dashcam/files`), not `bv-web`'s - without extending that override too, `bv-web`'s new archive mount would've silently pointed at the empty default `./data/archive` placeholder instead of his real files, reproducing the exact same "No recordings found" symptom one layer down. `docs/DEPLOY.md`'s override example now shows both services; `docs/WEB_ARCHITECTURE.md` gained a matching paragraph (its own opening line previously claimed `bv-web` "doesn't touch the source archive at all," also stale since the archive-browser feature shipped - corrected there too).

**Verification**: `docker-compose.yml` isn't machine-checkable from this sandbox (no live Docker Compose parser available), so this was reviewed by re-reading the merged structure by eye against the existing `bv-cli` block's own working pattern, and cross-checked against `app.py`'s `_find_camera_archive()`/`scan_archive()` call chain to confirm the container path (`/data/archive`) matches what `bv-config`'s wizard already tells users to answer for **Target (download path)** (`docs/DEPLOY.md` step 6, unchanged). **Not yet confirmed against Christer's real NAS** - waiting on him to update his `docker-compose.override.yml` with the new `bv-web` block, `git pull`, rebuild, and check the archive browser actually lists recordings now.

Separately, once the archive itself was visible: Christer's own `.cfg` had `target = "/volume1/Dashcam/files"` (the real host path) instead of the container path `/data/archive` - a leftover from before this Docker deployment existed (likely set by an earlier native/non-containerized `bv-config` run), never updated when he moved to `docker-compose`. `_find_camera_archive()` uses `CameraConfig.target` verbatim with no translation, so `scan_archive()` was pointed at a path that simply doesn't exist inside either container, silently returning zero recordings - fixed by hand-editing the `.cfg`'s `target` line directly (`sed`, on the NAS, no code change) rather than re-running the wizard, since only that one field was wrong.

### Follow-up: archive detail page - raw HEVC footage doesn't play inline in the browser, plus a filter bug

Two more issues surfaced once the archive was actually browsable with real data:

**Video playback on the recording detail page**: Christer reported "not showing anything" when trying to play a recording from `/archive/{camera_id}/{recording_id}`. Root cause (not yet independently confirmed against his exact browser/OS, but strongly consistent with earlier notes in this file that his camera's own archive is HEVC/H.265): the archive browser's `<video>` tag (`archive_recording_detail.html`) serves the raw camera file completely untouched via `FileResponse` - unlike the trip player, which only ever plays `bv-export`'s own output, and `bv-export`'s concatenation pipeline (`export/media.py`'s `encode_with_nvenc_fallback()`) always re-encodes to H.264 regardless of the source codec. Most desktop browsers (Chrome/Edge in particular) can't decode HEVC inline in a `<video>` element even though the file itself is perfectly valid - it just renders as a blank player with no error message, which matches what was reported. Suggested Christer confirm by downloading the file directly (the existing per-file link already on that page) and opening it in a local player like VLC - if that plays fine, it confirms this is a browser-codec limitation, not a server bug. No code changed for this - in-browser transcoding-on-demand for raw archive playback would be a real feature to design, not something to build speculatively; offered but not started, pending Christer's steer.

**A camera showing a thumbnail but no video for one recording**: explained as most likely two separate downloads (thumbnail vs. video file) where only the smaller/faster thumbnail completed, or - for a genuinely old recording - the BlackVue camera's own loop recording having already overwritten/deleted that video from the SD card before `bv-download` ever got to it, in which case there is nothing left on the camera for a re-run to recover. No code change - explanation only, pending confirmation of whether the specific recording in question is old enough for the second explanation to apply.

**Real bug found and fixed**: Christer reported the archive filter's "Exact" field still triggering `LexicalTimeParser`'s "--timestamp cannot be combined with --from or --until" error even though he'd never touched the "From"/"Until" fields. Root cause: an HTML GET form always submits every named field's value, even ones left blank, as an empty string (`from=&until=`) rather than omitting the parameter - so `app.py`'s `archive_recording_list()` route received `from_=""`/`until_=""` (not `None`) from FastAPI's `Query(default=None, ...)`, since the query param was *present* (just empty), not absent. `LexicalTimeParser.parse()` checks `is not None` (not truthiness) to detect a `--timestamp`/`--from` conflict - by design, since a CLI caller's unset argparse flag is a genuine `None` - so it read the empty string the same as a real value and raised, even though the user only meant to filter by "Exact". A CLI user can never hit this; only the web form's own request shape triggers it. Fixed by normalizing `timestamp`/`from_`/`until` to `None` via `x or None` immediately on entry to the route, before any use. Added `test_empty_string_from_and_until_count_as_combined_not_unset` to `tests/blackvue/test_lexicaltimeparser.py`, documenting the trap directly against `LexicalTimeParser` (confirmed raising, matching the reported bug) - a true HTTP-level regression test of `app.py`'s own route isn't possible in this sandbox since `fastapi` isn't installed here (confirmed via `python3 -c "import fastapi"` failing), so the fix itself is verified by code review plus this trap-level test, not an end-to-end one; worth Christer confirming on the real NAS that entering only "Exact" no longer errors.

## Speed up trip video playback on the NAS (Christer: "time to work")

Investigated `trip_file()`'s per-request cost, the thing flagged as a candidate cause the last time playback slowness came up (see "Fix O(N) archive rescan per thumbnail/video-range request" earlier). Correcting an inaccuracy in that earlier note: `_find_trip()` was never doing a full `scan_trips(target)` sweep across every trip folder on each request - it already called `scan_trip(target / trip_id)`, a targeted single-folder read, the same shape of fix the archive browser needed. The real cost is different: `scan_trip()` itself does about nine `stat()`/`open()` calls against the trip's own folder (`trip.log` existence + read, up to three video filenames, a `map_zoom_*.mp4` glob, map/gsensor/gpx/srt/lrc checks) - cheap in isolation, but `trip_file()` re-runs every one of those on *every single HTTP range request*, and a video player issues many of those per second while seeking or buffering. On a Synology bind-mounted volume in particular, where syscalls carry more overhead than a plain local disk, that repeated per-chunk cost is plausible as real, felt playback lag - distinct from (and possibly compounding) the earlier SMB-cache-based slowness diagnosis for Christer's PC-side playback.

Added `TripCache` to `web/trips.py`: a small per-`trip_id` cache with a short TTL (default 2 seconds) wrapping `scan_trip()`. A burst of range requests for the same trip within that window reuses one real scan instead of repeating it; the TTL keeps `create_app()`'s own documented promise intact - a trip `bv-export` finishes writing while `bv-web` is already running still shows up within a couple of seconds, not "needs a restart." Misses (a bad/typo'd trip id, or a trip mid-creation before `trip.log` exists) are deliberately *not* cached, so they're re-checked on the very next request rather than held as "not found" for the TTL. Wired into `app.py`: `app.state.trip_cache = TripCache()` created once in `create_app()`, `_find_trip()` now takes the cache as an explicit parameter and calls `cache.get(target, trip_id)` instead of `scan_trip()` directly, and both call sites (`trip_detail()`, `trip_file()`) pass `app.state.trip_cache` through. Deliberately scoped to this single-trip lookup only - `scan_trips()` (the trip list, loaded once per page view rather than once per range request) is untouched and still scans fresh every time, preserving that page's own existing freshness guarantee.

`docs/WEB_ARCHITECTURE.md` updated: the "Trip detail" bullet now explains `TripCache` and why it's scoped where it is, and the archive-browser section's old "Like `trips.py`, there's no caching" line is corrected - that comparison predates this fix and was about avoiding a full-archive scan per request (a different problem, already solved differently there), not about caching in general.

**Verification**: `ast.parse()` on `app.py`/`trips.py`. Three new tests in `tests/blackvue/web/test_trips.py` (`test_trip_cache_reuses_result_within_ttl`, `test_trip_cache_rescans_once_ttl_expires`, `test_trip_cache_does_not_cache_a_miss`), using a `monkeypatch.setattr(trips_module.time, "monotonic", fake_clock)` fake clock rather than a real `time.sleep()`, so TTL expiry is deterministic and instant rather than flaky/slow. All 15 tests in the file pass (12 pre-existing + 3 new) via the same hand-built fixture harness used throughout this sandbox session (no real pytest installed). **Confirmed on Christer's real NAS**: "it is very snappy on the Nas now."
