## Open issue (not yet investigated): Parking-mode recordings won't play in the archive browser

Christer: "bv-web can't play parking videos, probably because it's a timelapse video." Noted here for follow-up, not investigated or fixed yet. Playback relies entirely on Starlette's built-in Range support on the plain `FileResponse` the `/archive/{camera_id}/{recording_id}/files/{filename}` route returns (see app.py's own docstring: "range-request support comes for free from Starlette's own FileResponse") - there's no transcoding or format-checking anywhere in that path, so if the browser's `<video>` tag can't make sense of a file, it just silently fails to play with no error surfaced anywhere in bv-web itself.

Christer's own theory (reduced frame-rate timelapse encoding) is plausible but there's a second, already-documented candidate worth checking first: Parking-mode files have already been found to have non-standard MP4 structure severe enough to break `ffprobe` outright (see "Investigate 'all parking files' ffprobe failure" and the box-reader fallback work earlier in this file, plus the Parking-mode corrupted-header case mentioned under "Current Goal" at the top) - `mp4_box_reader.py`'s pure-Python fallback was built specifically because `ffprobe` couldn't read some Parking files' headers at all. A browser's native `<video>` decoder could plausibly choke on the exact same malformed/non-faststart header structure, independent of the actual frame rate or codec - worth checking with `ffprobe`/`mp4_box_reader.py` against one of Christer's actual unplayable Parking files before assuming timelapse frame rate is the cause, since a real header problem would need a different fix (e.g. remuxing) than a frame-rate one would.

## Open issue (not yet investigated): --prefix doesn't show anywhere in bv-web's Trips list

Christer: "Prefix not show in bv-web trips." Noted here for follow-up, not fixed yet - traced the cause, though, so this one already has a clear answer, just not a decided fix.

`bv-export`'s web form does expose `--prefix` (`job_new_bv_export.html`: "Trip folder name prefix... Prepend PREFIX_ to each trip's folder name, e.g. Holiday -> Holiday_trip_20260715_133458_..."), and it does land in the folder name on disk. But `trips.py`'s `TripAssets.label` is deliberately *not* read from the folder name - it's parsed straight out of `trip.log`'s own header line instead, specifically because (per that module's own comment) "the folder name may carry an extra --prefix... that isn't part of the trip's own label." `trip_list.html` only ever renders `trip.label` (never `trip.id`, which is the raw folder name and *does* include the prefix - see `TripAssets.id`'s docstring), and `trip_detail.html`'s heading is `trip.label` too. So the prefix isn't a bug in the sense of being dropped or lost - it's on disk, in the URL path (`trip.id` is used for both the trips-list link and every `/trips/{id}/...` route), just never rendered as visible text anywhere.

Whether that's actually wrong depends on what the prefix is *for* - if it exists to disambiguate trips at a glance (e.g. multiple cameras exporting into the same shared `data/trips` folder), hiding it from the list defeats that purpose and the fix would be showing it (either back it into the label instead of stripping it, or show `trip.id`/the folder name as a secondary line in `trip_list.html`). If it's purely a filesystem/organizational convenience, the current behavior might be intentional and this is a non-issue. Worth asking Christer why he uses `--prefix` before picking a fix.

## Map zoom follows video shape instead of rendering square; front/rear trim downgraded to info

Two small requests from Christer, both implemented directly rather than just logged: "Map zoom layout shouldn't be square, it should match the videos height or width depending on layout" and "front/rear duration differs shouldn't be a warning, just an info." Follow-up on the first: "If layout is left then it should match video height and if bottom it should match the video width. jus as the other map."

**Map zoom aspect ratio.** `map_zoom_METERSm.mp4` (`--map-zoom`) always rendered at `render_map_video()`'s square default (640x640), regardless of the trip's own camera aspect ratio or `--stitch-layout`. `--stitch-map`'s embedded panel already solved this exact problem for its own use case - `_map_panel_dimensions()` sizes a map panel to fill one dimension exactly (height for a `left`/`right` side, width for `top`/`down`) and derive the other from the trip's real-world GPS bounding-box aspect ratio, clamped to a sane fraction of the composite. Rather than invent a second sizing rule, added `map_zoom_dimensions(video_path, fixes)` to `stitch.py`, which probes the trip's own front (or rear) video for its real pixel dimensions via the existing `_video_dimensions()` helper, picks a side the exact same way `--stitch-map`'s rearview-mirror layout already auto-picks one (`_default_rearview_mirror_map_side()` - `left` for a north-south/portrait trip, `down` for east-west, the same geometry check `pick_stitch_layout()` itself uses), and feeds both into `_map_panel_dimensions()`. Falls back to the video's own raw width/height if there's no GPS bounding box to derive an aspect ratio from (e.g. a trip with no valid fixes). No new CLI flag - this reuses geometry the trip already implies, the same way `--stitch-layout auto` does, so there was nothing for Christer to configure.

Wired into `trip_export.py`: `_render_map_variant()` (the shared helper behind both `map.mp4` and `map_zoom_*.mp4`) gained optional `width`/`height` params, passed through to `render_map_video()` only when given. The `map.mp4` call site still passes neither - it's deliberately staying square, Christer's request was specifically about "Map zoom." The map-zoom call site now probes `front_video or rear_video` (the same "whichever camera exists" pattern already used elsewhere in `export_trip()` for duration probing) through `map_zoom_dimensions()` inside a `try/except MediaToolError`; a probe failure falls back to the old square default and adds a real warning (a genuine problem, not the routine case) rather than failing the whole export.

**Front/rear duration-mismatch downgrade.** `_align_front_rear_durations()` has two distinct warning sites: one when a trim runs to completion (routine, expected, happens on nearly every real export - see "Remove tolerance, trim every recording exactly" earlier in this file for why this fires so often), and one when alignment can't be resolved at all (a genuine unresolved problem). Christer's complaint was about the first one showing up as a warning in the CLI output for something that isn't actually wrong. Changed the success-path message to go through `log.step()` only (still written to `trip.log`, so the information isn't lost) instead of also being appended to `ExportResult.warnings` - it no longer surfaces as a CLI warning or counts toward the export's warning total. The failure-path message was left untouched as a real warning; that distinction is called out explicitly in a code comment quoting Christer's own wording.

**Fix**: `map_zoom_dimensions()` added to `stitch.py`; `_render_map_variant()`, the map-zoom render call site, and `_align_front_rear_durations()`'s success path updated in `trip_export.py`; `docs/man/bv-export.md` updated in two places - the Map section now explains `map.mp4` stays square while `map_zoom_METERSm.mp4` matches the video's own shape, and the Front/rear duration alignment section no longer calls the per-trim message "the run's own warning output."

**Verification**: `ast.parse()`-clean on `stitch.py`, `trip_export.py`, and both touched test files. Added 4 new unit tests for `map_zoom_dimensions()` in `test_stitch.py` (north-south matches video height, east-west matches video width, no-GPS falls back to raw video size, unprobeable video raises). In `test_trip_export.py`: renamed and updated the three existing `_align_front_rear_durations()` unit tests plus the end-to-end `test_export_trip_aligns_a_mismatched_front_rear_recording` integration test to assert the trim message now lands only in `trip.log` (via a new `_StepLog` test double for the unit tests, and by reading the real `trip.log` file for the integration test) and `warnings` is empty; added two new integration tests (`test_export_trip_map_zoom_matches_video_height_for_north_south_trip`, `test_export_trip_map_zoom_matches_video_width_for_east_west_trip`) that build real 64x64 test videos with north-south/east-west GPS fixtures, monkeypatch `render_map_video` to capture its call kwargs, and confirm `map_zoom_50m.mp4` receives the expected non-square `width`/`height` while `map.mp4` receives neither kwarg at all. No `pytest` available in this sandbox (Python 3.10, no `tomllib`) - as with the rest of this session, verified via `ast.parse()` and careful manual review rather than an actual test run; ready for CI.

## Parking-mode playback fix (in progress): built a diagnostic script, waiting on real box-table data from Christer

Follow-up on "Open issue: Parking-mode recordings won't play in the archive browser" above. Christer picked "attempt a real repair" over the safer/quicker "show a download link instead" fallback when asked which way to take this.

Real repair needs real data first - this codebase has already been burned twice in this exact area (the `frame_count==0` and `avg_frame_rate="0/0"` placeholder regressions, both earlier in this file) by shipping a fix against synthetic fixtures alone and finding out it didn't match Christer's actual hardware output. Rather than repeat that, built `scripts/dump_parking_container.py` first - a read-only, stdlib-only diagnostic (same style/spirit as the existing `scripts/check_mp4_recoverability.py`) that walks a real Parking `.mp4`'s `moov` box and reports, per track: `stsc`'s entry count and last entry's `first_chunk`, `stco`/`co64`'s chunk count, `stsz`'s sample count, `stts`'s entry count and total sample count - and flags directly whether `stsc`'s last `first_chunk` exceeds `stco`'s chunk count, which is ffmpeg's own literal "contradictionary STSC and STCO" check (confirmed via web search of FFmpeg's own `mov.c` patch history: `sc->stsc_data[sc->stsc_count - 1].first > sc->chunk_count`).

This targets a specific, promising theory already sitting undocumented in this codebase: `mp4_box_reader.py`'s own module docstring says Parking-mode's ffprobe failures happen because "the firmware sometimes still writes an empty/broken audio 'trak' that trips ffmpeg's stricter container validation, even though the video track itself is intact" - i.e. the *video* track (and its frame data in `mdat`) may be completely fine; it's an unused, broken audio index tripping the same strict validation that blocks both ffprobe and (theorized) the browser's own `<video>` decoder. If a real file confirms this, the fix is narrow and safe: strip or repair just the audio track's index in `moov`, leave `mdat` and the video track's own tables completely untouched - Parking recordings are already silent timelapses (`bv-generate --extract-audio` already skips them, "no audio track worth extracting"), so losing an already-broken, meaningless audio track costs nothing. If the real numbers show the *video* track's own tables are the broken ones instead, the fix is a different and harder problem (real sample-accurate table reconstruction), so this needs checking before design goes any further.

**Verification.** Built a synthetic MP4 by hand (raw `struct.pack` box construction, not reusing any test helper) with a clean, self-consistent video `trak` (`stsc` entry `first_chunk=1`, `stco` `chunk_count=3`) and a deliberately broken audio `trak` (`stsc` last entry `first_chunk=99`, `stco` `chunk_count=2` - `99 > 2`, the exact contradiction shape). Ran `dump_parking_container.py` against it: correctly identified both tracks' `handler_type` (`'vide'`/`'soun'`), printed matching table counts for the clean video track with no contradiction flagged, and printed the `==> CONTRADICTION` line naming the exact `99`/`2` mismatch only for the audio track. `ast.parse()`-clean.

**Not yet done - blocked on Christer.** Asked him (outside this note, in chat) to run `python scripts/dump_parking_container.py <path-to-a-real-_PF.mp4-or-_PR.mp4>` against one of his own real Parking recordings and paste back the output - it's table sizes/counts only, no video content, safe to share. Once that confirms (or disproves) the broken-audio-track theory with real numbers, the actual repair function, its tests, and the archive-browser wiring can be built and verified against those real numbers rather than guessed blind.

## Parking-mode playback fix (completed): confirmed real numbers, built and wired the repair

Direct continuation of the entry above. Christer ran `scripts/dump_parking_container.py` against one of his own real `_PF.mp4` files and reported back:

```
--- #1 track ---
  handler_type: 'vide'
  stsc: entry_count=647  last_entry.first_chunk=647
  stco: chunk_count=647
  stsz: sample_count=647
  stts: entry_count=1  total_sample_count=647
--- #2 track ---
  handler_type: 'soun'
  stsc: entry_count=1  last_entry.first_chunk=0
  stco: chunk_count=0
  stsz: sample_count=0
  stts: entry_count=1  total_sample_count=0
```

This confirmed the theory cleanly: the video track (647 samples, agreeing across every table) is completely intact. The audio track is an empty stub - zero samples, zero chunks - but still carries one stray `stsc` entry pointing at chunk `0`, which is what trips ffmpeg's/browsers' strict validation (`first_chunk=0` isn't `> chunk_count=0` in the naive sense, but `stsc` describing *any* chunk when `stco` declares zero of them is itself the contradiction - ffmpeg's own check, per its `mov.c` patch history researched in the entry above). Built a synthetic MP4 with these exact numbers and ran the real `ffprobe` binary (available in this sandbox) against it directly: it failed with the identical `"contradictionary STSC and STCO"` / `"error reading header"` error Christer's real file produces - the synthetic fixture reproduces the real bug precisely, not just approximately.

**`generate/mp4_repair.py`** (new module, sibling to `mp4_box_reader.py`). `repair_parking_container(source, destination) -> bool` drops any audio (`'soun'`) `trak` whose `stco`/`co64` reports zero chunks - the one specific, now-confirmed pattern - from a copy of `moov`, writing the result to `destination`. Deliberately narrow: an audio track with real samples that's broken some *other* way, or a broken video track, is left completely untouched and the function returns `False` (writes nothing) rather than guessing at a problem it hasn't been shown real data for. `mdat` (the actual frame data, potentially gigabytes) is never read into memory, edited, or moved - only `moov` (a few KB to tens of KB) is rewritten, and everything else is copied through byte for byte. Handles both possible file layouts correctly: if every `mdat` already sits before `moov` (shrinking `moov` can't move anything that matters), it just shrinks; if `moov` precedes `mdat` (shrinking would shift `mdat`'s absolute position and silently invalidate the kept video track's own `stco` offsets), it pads the new, smaller `moov` back out to its original total size with a trailing `free` box instead - a box type the MP4 spec defines as always-ignorable filler, the standard safe way to pad - so nothing after it ever moves. `load_or_repair_parking_video(source, cache_dir) -> Path` wraps this in the same load-if-cached-else-compute-and-cache pattern `media.load_or_compute_duration()`/`geocoding.load_or_reverse_geocode()` already use, keyed by the source's resolved path plus its mtime/size (so a re-download never serves a stale repair, and two different cameras' archives never collide in the shared cache) - returns the cached repaired path once built, or `source` itself unchanged if `repair_parking_container()` found nothing to fix.

**`web/app.py`**. The `/archive/{camera_id}/{recording_id}/files/{filename}` route now calls `load_or_repair_parking_video()` for a Parking (`P`) recording's own video files only (never its GPS/g-sensor sidecars, never another kind's video) before handing the resolved path to `FileResponse` - cached under `default_config_dir() / ".parking_repair_cache"` (bv-web's own writable scratch space, not the archive itself - the same reasoning that moved the geocode cache out of `/data/archive` when that mount turned out to be read-only in some deployments; see "Fix geocode cache dir" earlier in this file). Fully transparent to the frontend: the `<video>` tag's `src` is unchanged, so no template edits were needed.

**Verification.** `tests/blackvue/generate/test_mp4_repair.py`: six tests, all run against the real `ffprobe` binary (no mocking - matching this whole test suite's established style for anything touching the actual media tools), covering both file layouts (`moov` before/after `mdat` - the padding and shrinking paths respectively), confirming `mdat`'s own bytes and absolute offset survive a repair byte-for-byte identical, confirming the repaired file reports exactly one (video) stream via a real `ffprobe -show_entries stream=codec_type` call, and confirming the narrow-scope guarantee: a *non-empty* but still internally broken audio track, and a file with no droppable track at all, are both left completely untouched (`repair_parking_container()` returns `False`, writes nothing). All 6 pass via a hand-rolled runner (no `pytest` in this sandbox). `ast.parse()`-clean on `mp4_repair.py`, `app.py`, and the test file. Additionally hand-verified `load_or_repair_parking_video()` directly against the same file built from Christer's real numbers: `repair_parking_container()` returns `True`, and its output is byte-for-byte identical to a manually-constructed reference file built independently by hand for cross-checking.

## Open issue (not yet investigated): adjustable playback speed for Parking recordings

Christer, right after the Parking playback fix above: "i would like to be able to add an playback speed for parking files between 0.10 and 5." Noted here for follow-up, not investigated or implemented yet - almost certainly motivated by Parking recordings being 1fps timelapses (see the earlier "Parking mode (P) is a 1fps timelapse" note in this file): played back at 1x their footage covers real time much faster than it looks, and a fast/slow control would make that easier to actually watch.

`archive_recording_detail.html`'s `<video>` tag (the only place a Parking recording's own video plays) is currently a bare `<video controls preload="metadata" src="...">`, and - confirmed via a grep of every template in `web/templates/` - there is currently no `<script>` tag anywhere in bv-web at all. That's a real, deliberate project convention (see `docs/WEB_ARCHITECTURE.md`'s own description of `bv-web` as server-rendered with "no client-side app to build/deploy" - even the job-output page polls via a plain meta-refresh rather than JS/websockets). A 0.10-5x range slider isn't something native `<video controls>` exposes on its own (some browsers' built-in menu offers a small fixed set of speeds, typically capped well under 5x and not going below ~0.25x) - getting Christer's actual requested range would need a real `<input type="range">` bound to the video element's own `playbackRate` property via a small inline `<script>`. That would be the first JavaScript in this entire project's web app, worth flagging as a real design decision (not just an implementation detail) rather than adding quietly - whether to keep the "no JS" line intact by scoping this some other way (e.g. a fixed set of speed buttons that just reload the page with a `?speed=` query param and reissue `playbackRate` via a tiny per-request inline script, still JS but not a persistent app-wide script) versus accepting a first small `<script>` block, is worth deciding explicitly before implementing, not assumed.

Scope question for whenever this is picked up: Christer said "for parking files" specifically - worth confirming whether that means the control should only appear for Parking (`P`) recordings (`recording.kind_label == "Parking"`, matching this issue's own motivation) or he'd want it generally useful for any recording once it exists, before building it one way or the other.

## bv-export web job not producing stitch.mp4: real job runs tested, no code bug found (follow-up on the earlier open issue)

Direct continuation of "Open issue: bv-export via the web UI isn't producing stitch.mp4" above, which only did a quick static code read. This time ran the actual web-triggered pipeline for real - `JobRunner.start_bv_export()` (the literal code `app.py`'s `/jobs/bv-export` POST route calls) against a real, on-disk synthetic archive, with a real (unmocked) `bv_export._run()` underneath, exactly the path a browser-triggered job takes end to end. `test_jobs.py`'s own module docstring notes every existing test in that file mocks `_run()` out - so this specific "does the whole thing actually work" question had never been exercised anywhere in the test suite before.

Four scenarios, all run for real (real ffmpeg, real archive scan, real trip detection, real `stitch_cameras()` call), all correctly produced `stitch.mp4`:

1. A fresh front+rear trip, clean target directory, `stitch=True` - `stitch.mp4` written, no errors.
2. The same archive exported twice in a row (`stitch=False` then `stitch=True`) - correctly produced `stitch.mp4` on the second run (into a *new* trip folder, not the first run's - see the unrelated finding below).
3. The exact trip folder pre-created with stale placeholder content (`front.mp4` containing junk bytes, simulating "already exported once, before `--stitch` was added"), run non-interactively (`overwrite=False`, no tty - the same "keep in place, don't wipe" path a web job always takes, see the earlier wipe-vs-keep work) with `stitch=True` - `front.mp4`/`rear.mp4` were freely regenerated with real content and `stitch.mp4` was added, confirming a non-interactive "update in place" run doesn't skip requested-but-previously-absent outputs.
4. A front-only trip (no rear video at all) with `stitch=True` - `stitch_cameras()`'s own documented single-camera fallback (a plain copy, ignoring layout) fired correctly and `stitch.mp4` was still written.

No bug found in any of these. The full chain - `job_new_bv_export.html`'s checkbox -> `app.py`'s `stitch: bool = Form(False)` -> `jobs.py`'s `argv.append("--stitch")` -> `bv_export.py`'s real `parse_args()`/`_run()` -> `export_trip()`'s `if stitch_layout is not None:` gate -> `stitch_cameras()` - works correctly end to end in every shape tried.

**Unrelated finding, noted but not chased further:** scenario 2's second run landed in `trip_20260720_100000_20260720_100001`, not the first run's `..._100000` folder - a one-second difference in the trip's own computed end-timestamp between two exports of the *identical* unchanged source archive. Not investigated (out of scope for this specific bug report, and not something Christer has reported noticing), but worth keeping in mind if trip-folder-naming stability ever comes up as its own issue - plausibly floating-point jitter in ffprobe's reported duration for a very short (1s) synthetic test clip specifically, may not reproduce on real multi-minute dashcam footage at all.

**Still not resolved - needs something from Christer.** Since the code path itself now has real, passing coverage across every shape a broken run could plausibly take, the two remaining explanations from the original note are the most likely ones left: the `--stitch` checkbox wasn't actually ticked (it's an easy one to miss - unchecked by default, in the "Defaults" section, well down an unusually long form with no visual emphasis over any other checkbox), or the job's own real output/warnings (visible on the job detail page, or in `trip.log` inside the resulting trip folder) would show something this session's synthetic archives never triggered. Asked Christer (in chat, not here) to confirm whether the box was checked and, if so, to paste the job's own output.

## bv-export stitch.mp4 "bug" resolved: checkbox label wording, not a code issue

Follow-up on the investigation above. Christer: "I cant find stitch as an option on bw-web" - I suspected a stale Docker deployment (checkbox missing entirely) and suggested rebuilding. He corrected that: "No its there, \"Render combined stitch.mp4 (front + rear composed together)\" feels a little confusing ib parenteses" - the checkbox was there all along; he just didn't recognize the label as the stitch option, and found the parenthetical confusing.

Reading the old label again with that in mind, the confusion is real: "combined" and "(front + rear composed together)" say the same thing twice, in different words, which makes the parenthetical read like it's qualifying or contradicting the main clause rather than just restating it.

**Fix.** `job_new_bv_export.html`'s stitch checkbox label changed from `Render combined stitch.mp4 (front + rear composed together)` to `Render stitch.mp4 (front and rear cameras combined into one video)` - drops the redundant "combined", and the parenthetical now does the one job of explaining what stitch.mp4 actually is, without repeating itself.

No code bug ever existed in the stitch pipeline itself - the four real end-to-end job runs in the entry above stand as-is. This was purely a labeling/discoverability issue.

## bv-export --include-parking silently dropping Parking-mode PF/PR.mp4: same container quirk, export-side fix

Christer, from a real `bv-export --include-parking --stitch ...` run:

```
bv-export: trip_20230728_105305_20230728_112131: warning: front.mp4: 20230728_105305_PF.mp4 could not be read and was left out (ffprobe failed for 20230728_105305_PF.mp4: [mov,mp4,m4a,3gp,3g2,mj2 @ ...] stream 1, contradictionary STSC and STCO
[mov,mp4,m4a,3gp,3g2,mj2 @ ...] error reading header
x:\files\2023\20230728_105305_PF.mp4: Invalid data found when processing input) - likely an incomplete recording (e.g. the camera lost power mid-write)
```

Same error message and same root cause as the earlier "Parking-mode playback fix" entry above (an empty, unused audio track that still trips ffmpeg's strict container validation) - but this time hitting `_concatenate_asset()`'s own `check_readable()` step in the CLI export pipeline, not bv-web's archive-browser route. `mp4_repair.py`'s own docstring already says as much: "every Parking-mode (P) recording fails ffprobe/ffmpeg outright" - a systemic quirk, not sporadic corruption - so `--include-parking` was silently defeating itself: every Parking recording it was supposed to include got immediately treated as unreadable and dropped with a warning, indistinguishable from genuine corruption (see "Skip unreadable/corrupted sources during concat instead of failing entire asset" above, whose own good-faith error handling is exactly what was swallowing this).

**Fix.** New `_repair_parking_sources(trip)` in `trip_export.py`: walks every Parking-mode recording's FRONT/REAR (never AUDIO - a `.aac` extraction, not an MP4 container, and Parking recordings have no real audio anyway) and runs each through the same `load_or_repair_parking_video()` already wired into bv-web's archive browser, sharing the same `default_config_dir() / ".parking_repair_cache"` cache dir - a recording repaired once for browser playback doesn't need repairing again for an export, and vice versa. Returns a `{(recording id, asset): repaired path}` map in exactly the shape `_align_front_rear_durations()`/`_concatenate_asset()` already expect (`duration_overrides`), so it slots into `export_trip()`'s existing override-chaining pipeline ahead of `_trim_prebuffers()`/`_align_front_rear_durations()`, rather than needing a parallel mechanism: `duration_overrides = {**parking_repair_overrides, **prebuffer_overrides, **alignment_overrides}`. This matters because `_align_front_rear_durations()` also probes each recording's own raw file directly (not just `_concatenate_asset()`) - without the repaired path reaching it first via `source_overrides`, it would keep silently "leaving the pair alone" (its own documented behavior for a file ffprobe can't read) rather than actually aligning a Parking pair's durations.

**Verification.** New tests in `test_trip_export.py`: `test_repair_parking_sources_returns_repaired_paths_for_broken_containers` (built from a *real* ffmpeg-encoded video with a broken empty-audio trak spliced into its real `moov` - real ffmpeg output puts `moov` after `mdat`, confirmed directly in this sandbox, so splicing in the extra trak never moves `mdat` or invalidates the real video trak's own `stco` offsets - reproduces the actual end-to-end bug rather than just the container-validation half of it), `test_repair_parking_sources_skips_non_parking_recordings`, and `test_concatenate_asset_uses_repaired_parking_source_instead_of_dropping_it` (confirms the repaired path actually gets concatenated into `front.mp4` with zero warnings, not just that `check_readable()` stops rejecting it). All pass via the hand-rolled runner (no `pytest` in this sandbox), along with the full existing `test_trip_export.py` suite (102/109 runnable - 7 skipped for needing a real `capsys` fixture this runner doesn't provide, pre-existing and unrelated) and all 6 `test_mp4_repair.py` tests, confirming no regression. `ast.parse()`-clean on `trip_export.py` and the test file.

Not yet re-confirmed against Christer's own real archive/command line - only against synthetic fixtures built from the exact real error message and the already-confirmed real box-table numbers.

## Open issue (not yet investigated): rotate the map(s) to the car's heading instead of fixed north-up

Christer: "Could we let the maps(booth of them) rotate as the car turns, instead of having north at the top" - i.e. "track-up" orientation (the vehicle's own heading always points "up" on screen, the way most phone turn-by-turn apps default) instead of the current fixed "north-up" orientation, for both `--map` (the full-trip overview, `map.mp4`) and `--map-zoom` (the zoomed follow-camera map, `map_zoom_XXXm.mp4`). Noted here for follow-up, not investigated or implemented yet.

Currently, in `map_render.py`'s `render_frame()`, only the position marker itself is rotated to match GPS course over ground (`_arrow_points()`/`_paste_marker_image()`) - the route line, roads, and areas are all drawn with a fixed, unrotated lat/lon-to-pixel projection (north always up), every frame. Real track-up rotation would mean rotating that whole projected geometry - route, roads, areas, and the marker together - around the frame's own center by the negative of the current heading, every single frame, not just changing which way the marker arrow points. `map_video.py`'s `render_map_video()` already re-renders each frame independently (especially in `zoom_meters` follow-camera mode, where a fresh bounding box is already computed per frame), so per-frame rotation is architecturally where this would need to plug in, but it's a real rendering change, not a flag flip.

Worth deciding explicitly before implementing: Christer said "both" of them, but the two map variants are different in why you'd rotate them at all. `--map-zoom`'s zoomed, scrolling follow-camera view is exactly the case track-up conventionally applies to (phone nav apps do this specifically for a close-in, moving view). `--map`'s full-trip overview is framed once to fit the *entire* route (`bounding_box_for_fixes()`) and stays static otherwise - rotating that as the car turns would either need to re-fit/re-center the bbox every frame too (a bigger change, and arguably fighting the "overview" point of that map at all) or would rotate a fixed frame around a car that's often nowhere near its center, which could read as more confusing than the current fixed north-up. Worth confirming with Christer whether he wants true track-up on both, or primarily means `--map-zoom` (where "booth of them" may just reflect that `--map`/`--map-zoom` are usually both enabled together, not a considered opinion that the full overview should rotate too).

## Trip folder name / trip_info.txt claiming a wider span than the exported video actually covers

Christer: "When create trip with bv-export with a parking video first, the name of the trip includes the start of the parking video, but in the glitch.mp4 the parking is not included unless we specify --include-parking."

Root cause: `Trip.start_timestamp`/`end_timestamp` (and therefore `Trip.label`, used both by `folder_name_for_trip()` and `write_trip_info()`) are always derived from the trip's *first and last recordings, period* - Parking or not. But `_concatenate_asset()` leaves a Parking-mode recording out of `front.mp4`/`rear.mp4` entirely unless `--include-parking` is given (the default is off). So a trip starting with a Parking recording got a folder name (and a trip_info.txt "Started:" line) claiming that earlier start time, while the actual exported video started later, at the first real driving recording - name and content disagreed.

**Fix.** New `_content_timestamps(trip, include_parking)` in `trip_export.py`: returns `trip.start_timestamp`/`end_timestamp` unchanged when `include_parking=True` (nothing to fix - every recording really is in the video), but the first/last *non*-Parking recording's own boundary when `include_parking=False`, falling back to the full boundary only if the trip is Parking-only (no video either way, so no narrower boundary means anything). `folder_name_for_trip()` gained an `include_parking: bool = True` keyword (default preserves every existing caller's behavior unless they opt in) and now builds its label from `_content_timestamps()` instead of `trip.label` directly; `bv_export.py`'s own call site now passes its real `include_parking`. `export_trip()`'s `write_trip_info()` call now passes the same content-aware start/end (and derives `duration` from them too, instead of `trip.duration`) rather than `trip.start_timestamp`/`end_timestamp`.

Deliberately scoped to just these two consumers. `Trip.label` itself (bv-ls's `--trips` listing) and `trip.gpx`'s own name (`write_gpx(..., name=trip.label)`) are untouched - both describe the trip as *detected*, and `trip.gpx`'s actual content already covers every recording's GPS data regardless of `include_parking` (GPS/g-sensor were never gated behind that flag, only video/audio was), so its full-boundary name was already consistent with what's inside it. Only the two places that specifically describe *what's in front.mp4/rear.mp4* needed to change.

**Verification.** Six new tests in `test_trip_export.py`: `folder_name_for_trip()`'s default (`include_parking=True`, unchanged) vs. `include_parking=False` skipping a leading and a trailing Parking recording respectively, using the last non-Parking recording's real duration when known, and falling back to the full boundary for an all-Parking trip; plus one full `export_trip()` end-to-end test confirming trip_info.txt's "Started:" line matches the real exported `front.mp4` (1s, driving-only) rather than the excluded Parking recording's earlier start. All 108 runnable tests in the file pass (up from 102 - 6 new, all others unaffected), plus the full existing suite, via the hand-rolled runner (no `pytest` in this sandbox). `ast.parse()`-clean on `trip_export.py`, `bv_export.py`, and the test file.

## `--include-parking` export "hangs" - map phase O(frames x total fixes) route-redraw cost

Christer, on a real `--include-parking --map --map-zoom 60 --stitch-map zoom ...` export: "Looks like including a parking file take very very long time, or it hangs." The export eventually finished; the real numbers he pasted back made the shape of the problem obvious: `map phase took 946.5s`, wildly disproportionate to `gsensor.mp4: 131.2s` and the entire `--stitch` encode (map/graph/gsensor overlay plus front+rear NVDEC decode combined): `189.3s`. Map rendering alone took nearly 5x longer than everything else in the pipeline put together.

My first hypothesis was a re-emergent version of the O(n^2) interpolation hang already fixed once for both `map_video.py`'s own position lookup (`_advance_fix_index()`/`_interpolate_position_from_index()`) and `gsensor_video.py`'s sample lookup (`_advance_search_index()`/`_interpolate_from_index()`) - both call sites I checked were still correctly using their forward-only cursors. A synthetic repro built around that hypothesis (a Parking recording with a 50-minute real span behind a short video file, plus a short driving recording, real map/gsensor/stitch rendering) finished in ~12s, not reproducing anything - a dead end I only got past by asking Christer for the actual timing breakdown rather than continuing to guess blind.

Root cause, once the numbers pointed at the map phase specifically: `render_map_video()`'s per-frame loop builds `route_so_far` - the list of every real GPS fix reached so far - correctly in O(fixes + frames) amortized (each fix only gets appended once, via a forward-only index same as the position lookup). But every frame then passed the *entire* `route_so_far` accumulated up to that point straight to `render_frame()`, which re-projects (`proj(lat, lon)`) and redraws (`draw.line(...)`) every single point of it from scratch - `map_render.py`'s `render_frame()`, lines ~539-553. That's O(frames x total fixes so far) for the route line alone, unlike roads and areas, which already got exactly this same "filter to what's actually on screen" treatment for `--map-zoom` mode (see `index_roads()`/`roads_within_bbox()`, `index_features()`/`features_within_bbox()`) - the route polyline was the one piece of per-frame drawing that never got it.

This cost was always present in `--map-zoom` mode, even without Parking footage - a whole trip's worth of fixes redrawn every frame, nearly all of it permanently off-canvas once the follow-camera view has moved on. `--include-parking` made it dramatically worse in practice because the merged GPS fix stream always includes every Parking-mode recording's own fixes regardless of `--include-parking` (that flag only gates video/audio inclusion, per the trip-folder-naming entry above; GPS/g-sensor were never gated behind it) - a car parked in one spot for tens of minutes can log hundreds to thousands of near-identical fixes, every one of which used to get re-projected and redrawn on every remaining frame of the render.

**Fix.** New `MAX_ZOOM_ROUTE_TRAIL_FIXES = 300` constant in `map_video.py` (~5 minutes of trailing route at the typical ~1Hz fix rate - generous relative to any reasonable `--map-zoom` radius, small and constant regardless of the trip's own total fix count). `render_map_video()`'s per-frame loop now slices `route_so_far` down to its own trailing `MAX_ZOOM_ROUTE_TRAIL_FIXES` entries before handing it to `render_frame()`, but *only* when `zoom_meters is not None` (i.e. `--map-zoom` mode). Static `--map` (whole-trip overview) mode is deliberately left untouched: showing the entire route is the entire point of that view, so capping it there would be a correctness regression, not a speed one - it keeps its own (smaller, since it doesn't also re-render roads/areas or a fresh bbox per frame) unaddressed version of the same architectural cost as a known, separate, lower-priority item.

**Verification.** Two new tests in `test_map_video.py`: `test_render_map_video_caps_route_trail_when_zoomed` (350 synthetic fixes, well past the 300-fix cap, confirms every frame passed to the mocked `render_frame()` gets at most `MAX_ZOOM_ROUTE_TRAIL_FIXES + 1` route points once the cap is biting) and `test_render_map_video_does_not_cap_route_trail_when_not_zoomed` (same fix count, static mode, confirms the full accumulated route is still passed uncapped). All 54 tests in `test_map_video.py` pass via the hand-rolled runner (no `pytest` in this sandbox). `test_stitch.py`'s own suite (real ffmpeg encodes) was not re-run in full - it consistently exceeds this sandbox's tool timeout even unmodified - but this fix is entirely internal to `render_map_video()`'s per-frame loop with no change to its public signature or callers, so stitch.py's own map-panel tests (which only assert on output video existence/dimensions, not internal route-point counts) aren't expected to be affected.

## Frame-holding for stationary Parking spans - the other half of the 946.5s map phase

Direct follow-up on the route-trail-cap fix above. Christer, after seeing that fix land: "Somehow the parking videos timelapse complicated stuff for the video file, sound was good but the overall time of the video was over 1 hour and the fps on stitch is 6.84, this explains the long time it took."

This corrected a load-bearing assumption the earlier investigation (and this project's own prior comments, e.g. `trip_builder.py`'s "1fps timelapse" note) had been carrying: that a Parking recording's own video file plays back in a few minutes while representing a much longer real parked span. Christer's own real numbers say otherwise for this recording - the container's own `avg_frame_rate` (6.84fps, a real, ffprobe-reported value, not a detection bug) times its own real >1 hour duration means the concatenated video genuinely spans that long once the Parking segment is included with `--include-parking`. That matters independently of the route-trail cost already fixed: `render_map_video()`'s `frame_count = total_seconds * fps` (5fps by default) means a genuinely 1-hour-plus video needs roughly 18,000 map frames rendered for that one recording's span alone - unavoidable *if* every one of those frames actually needs a fresh, unique render. Nearly all of them don't: a parked car's map view barely changes frame to frame, yet every single one used to trigger a full background/roads/areas/route/marker redraw regardless.

**Fix.** Split what used to be one `map_render.render_frame()` call into two: `render_frame_visual()` (background, roads, areas, the route line, and the position marker - the expensive, position-dependent part) and `compose_frame_overlay()` (just the timestamp/speed text and the live-GPS badge - cheap, and meaningful to redraw every frame regardless of whether the visual underneath changed, so the on-screen clock never visibly freezes even during a long held span). `render_frame()` itself is now a thin wrapper combining the two, unchanged for every existing caller (this project's own tests, `blackvue.live.map_stream`'s live map). `render_map_video()`'s per-frame loop now builds a small signature per frame (`frame_bbox`, position rounded to `STATIONARY_VISUAL_ROUND_DECIMALS` (5, ~1.1m), heading, `show_marker`, and the route's own rounded tip point) and reuses the last `render_frame_visual()` result whenever a frame's signature matches the previous one, instead of calling it fresh - `compose_frame_overlay()` still runs on every single frame either way. The route's rounded *tip point* (not `len(route_points)`) is what makes this actually fire during a real Parking span: `route_so_far` keeps growing by one entry every time a new (but, for a parked car, coordinate-identical) fix arrives, which would otherwise invalidate the cache on nearly every frame even though the drawn line hasn't visually changed at all.

**Verification.** New tests in `test_map_render.py` (`render_frame()` still equals `render_frame_visual()` + `compose_frame_overlay()` combined; the visual alone omits text/badge; `compose_frame_overlay()` copies rather than mutates its input, matching the caching's own requirement that the same cached object gets reused safely across many frames; two different `timestamp_text` values on the same visual produce different output, confirming the clock stays live) and in `test_map_video.py` (`test_render_map_video_reuses_the_cached_visual_during_a_stationary_span`: 20 fixes all at the same coordinate collapse to a single `render_frame_visual()` call across 39 output frames while `compose_frame_overlay()` still runs all 39 times; `test_render_map_video_does_not_reuse_the_visual_while_moving`: a genuinely moving trip calls both exactly once per frame, confirming the cache never fires when it shouldn't). All pre-existing `render_map_video()` tests that used to mock the single `render_frame()` were updated to mock `render_frame_visual()`/`compose_frame_overlay()` at whichever layer they actually care about instead. Full `test_map_video.py` (56/56), `test_map_render.py` (30/30), and `test_map_stream.py` (18/18, confirming `render_frame()`'s unchanged combined behavior didn't regress bv-live's own map) pass via the hand-rolled runner. `test_stitch.py` was not re-run in full for the same sandbox-timeout reason as the entry above.

## The video was never really over an hour - front.mp4's own duration metadata was corrupted by concatenation

Direct follow-up on both entries above, and it overturns the premise they were built on. Christer, after the frame-holding fix landed: "Video still over 1 hour and very slow" - render time and playback length both, and "The funny thing is that the rear video is correct."

That one line reframed the whole investigation: this was never a single genuinely-long recording. Working through it with Christer's own real numbers, in order: his exported `front.mp4` reported 01:01:22, `rear.mp4` reported 00:03:50 (a real, current export - not the earlier 946.5s report reused); the single Parking recording in that trip's archive folder had matching `_PF.mp4`/`_PR.mp4` files of comparable size (80MB/61MB, not a 16x split); `scripts/dump_parking_container.py` against both real files showed identical, internally consistent video tracks (1530 samples each) with the same known broken-empty-audio-track pattern this project already has a fix for (`mp4_repair.py`, see "Parking-mode playback fix" earlier in this file); repairing both with that existing fix and probing the results directly showed them **identical** - 1530 frames, 1000/33 (~30.3fps, a normal real-time rate, not a timelapse at all), 50.457s, both sides. The Parking recording itself was never the problem. Probing Christer's actual exported `front.mp4`/`rear.mp4` directly nailed it down: `nb_frames` matched almost exactly (6822 vs 6829 - the same real footage) but `avg_frame_rate` didn't (47375/25573 ≈ 1.85fps for front, 3414500/115109 ≈ 29.66fps for rear) - the same number of real frames, but front's container metadata claimed a ~16x lower frame rate, which is exactly what turns real ~230s footage into a reported 3682s. `-c copy` concatenation doesn't harmonize timescales across inputs that don't share one - plausibly the Parking recording's own repaired container (`mp4_repair.py` rewrites `moov` from scratch) carrying a different timescale than the camera's normal recording pipeline - so the real packets and real frame count survive concatenation fine, but the container-level *summary* duration/frame-rate ffprobe reports for the assembled file can describe something that never happened, on the front side only.

This means the entry above ("the other half of the 946.5s map phase") was solving a real cost (redundant re-rendering of stationary frames, which is still worth having fixed) for a premise that was itself wrong: the trip was never genuinely over an hour long, and the earlier "6.84fps, not a detection bug" conclusion doesn't hold up against these real numbers either - both entries' route-trail-cap and frame-holding work stay valid and worth keeping (real stationary spans do occur, and redundant re-rendering is real waste whenever they do), they just weren't the primary cause of *this* report.

**Fix.** `_recording_video_offsets()` in `trip_export.py` already probed every recording's own individual (possibly front/rear-trimmed) source file to build per-recording start offsets - it just threw away the running total once the last recording's offset was recorded. Changed its return type from `dict[RecordingId, float]` to `tuple[dict[RecordingId, float], float | None]`, exposing that same running sum as the trip's own real total video duration (`None` only if no recording's video could be probed at all). `export_trip()`'s `video_duration_seconds` - which feeds `map.mp4`/`map_zoom_*.mp4`'s own `frame_count` math, the `--stitch` map/graph panel durations, and `trip.srt`/`trip.lrc` padding - now prefers that summed value over `probe(front.mp4 or rear.mp4).duration_seconds` (the old approach, and the one that was silently wrong here), falling back to the old probe-the-concatenated-file behavior only in the (structurally rare) case the summed approach found nothing to probe at all.

**Verification.** Extended `_recording_video_offsets()`'s four existing unit tests in `test_trip_export.py` with assertions on the new total return value (real per-source sum; correctly reflects a trimmed-duration override; correctly excludes an excluded Parking recording; correctly falls back when a recording has no video). New integration test `test_export_trip_video_duration_uses_summed_sources_not_corrupted_concat_probe`: monkeypatches `probe()` to return a 16x-inflated duration specifically for the concatenated `front.mp4` path (reproducing the real corruption's shape) while every individual source still probes correctly, then confirms `render_map_video()` receives the real ~1s `video_duration_seconds`, not the corrupted ~16s one. Full `test_trip_export.py` (109 passed, 7 skipped - same skip count as before, unrelated to this change), `test_map_video.py` (56/56), and `test_map_render.py` (30/30) pass via the hand-rolled runner; `test_map_stream.py` (18/18) confirms `blackvue.live.map_stream` - which builds its own duration independently and never touches `trip_export.py` - is unaffected. `test_stitch.py` was not re-run in full for the same sandbox-timeout reason as both entries above; this fix only changes what value `trip_export.py` computes and passes into `stitch_cameras()`'s existing `map_video_duration_seconds`/`graph_video_duration_seconds` parameters, not `stitch.py` itself.

## Root cause of the corrupted front.mp4: mixed audio-stream counts across a `-c copy` concat

Direct follow-up on the entry above. Christer, once told that fix only corrected this project's own internal math and not the actual exported file: "front still 1.85 fps" - the real `front.mp4` on disk was still broken, which meant real playback (and any future `--stitch` run built from it) was still affected, not just this codebase's own frame_count arithmetic.

Tracked it down with Christer running real commands against his own archive. `scripts/dump_parking_container.py` had already shown a real front Parking file (`20230728_105305_PF.mp4`) carries **two** tracks - `vide` and `soun` - confirming BlackVue's FRONT camera files embed their own audio internally; REAR files (confirmed via the same tooling on `_PR.mp4`, and by every other place in this codebase that reads audio, always preferring FRONT) never do. `generate/mp4_repair.py`'s existing fix for the Parking-recording container bug (documented earlier in this file) works by *dropping* that broken empty audio track entirely from a Parking recording's repaired file - correct and necessary for that file to be readable at all, but it leaves the repaired file **video-only** while every *other* FRONT recording in the same trip still carries two streams (video+audio). `time_base` probes nailed the mechanism precisely: the repaired Parking file alone reports `time_base=1/1000` (correct), the very next (Event) recording in the trip reports `time_base=1/1000` too (correct, and *matching* - ruling out a simple two-file timescale mismatch) - but the real, already-concatenated `front.mp4` itself reports `time_base=1/16000`, a value belonging to neither input and suspiciously matching a common *audio* sample rate. ffmpeg's `-f concat -c copy` demuxer requires every segment to share the same stream layout; mixing a 1-stream (video-only, repaired Parking) segment in among 2-stream (video+audio) FRONT segments doesn't error out, it silently mis-muxes - real frame data and frame count survive (`nb_frames` matched rear's almost exactly, 6822 vs 6829, confirmed in the prior entry), but the video stream's own container-level timing metadata comes out describing something that never happened. REAR is unaffected because it's video-only throughout - no per-segment stream-count inconsistency ever exists on that side, which is exactly why Christer's own "the rear video is correct" observation held.

**Fix.** `concatenate_media()` (`export/media.py`) gained a `video_only: bool = False` parameter - when True, appends `-an` to the ffmpeg command, so the output never carries audio at all regardless of what any individual source has, sidestepping the whole class of bug by never letting inconsistent per-segment audio reach the concat demuxer. New `mux_audio_track(video_source, audio_source, destination)` in the same module remuxes a video-only file with a separate audio file as a plain stream copy (`-map 0:v:0 -map 1:a:0 -c copy`) - no re-encode of either. `_concatenate_asset()` (`trip_export.py`) gained a matching `video_only` parameter threaded straight through to `concatenate_media()`. `export_trip()`'s FRONT `executor.submit()` call now passes `video_only=True`, so `front.mp4` is always built video-only first; once both `front_video` and `audio` (the trip's already-independently-built `audio.aac` - the same file already muxed into `stitch.mp4`, see "Mux trip audio into stitch.mp4" earlier in this file) are ready, `mux_audio_track()` remuxes `audio.aac` back into `front.mp4`, written to a throwaway temp file and swapped into place only on success (a mux failure leaves the already-good video-only `front.mp4` in place with a warning, rather than losing it - same "don't take good footage down with a secondary failure" spirit as this file's own corrupted-source-skip fix). `front.mp4`'s audio now always comes from the same reliable, already-extracted `audio.aac` pipeline stitch.mp4 already trusted, rather than depending on raw per-recording embedded audio surviving a `-c copy` concat intact - REAR is untouched (already video-only, never affected).

Checked before implementing: `stitch.mp4`'s own audio is completely independent of `front.mp4`'s embedded track (it already comes from `audio.aac` via its own `-map`/`-c:a copy`, confirmed in `stitch.py`), so this change doesn't touch stitch.mp4's audio at all. bv-web's trip-detail page, though, falls back to playing `front.mp4` directly via a bare `<video>` element whenever `stitch.mp4` doesn't exist (`web/trips.py`'s `VIDEO_FILENAMES = ("stitch.mp4", "front.mp4", "rear.mp4")`) - that page has no separate audio source, so it depends entirely on `front.mp4` carrying real embedded audio, which is exactly why this fix remuxes `audio.aac` back in rather than just leaving `front.mp4` silent.

**Verification.** New tests in `test_export_media.py`: `test_concatenate_media_strips_audio_when_video_only` (two real video+audio sources concatenated with `video_only=True` produce an audio-free output, confirmed via `probe_audio_codec() is None`), `test_concatenate_media_keeps_audio_by_default` (confirms the default preserves every other existing caller's behavior), `test_mux_audio_track_combines_a_video_only_file_with_a_separate_audio_file`, and two `MediaToolError`-on-missing-source tests mirroring this module's existing `trim_media`/`trim_media_head` test style. New integration test in `test_trip_export.py`, `test_export_trip_front_mp4_keeps_audio_despite_a_video_only_source`: a two-recording trip where one FRONT source is video+audio and the other is video-only (standing in for a repaired Parking file), run through the real `export_trip()` end to end, confirms the real exported `front.mp4` ends up with a real audio stream (`_has_audio_stream()`) despite one of its two sources carrying none. Fixed one pre-existing test (`test_export_trip_concatenates_front_rear_audio_independently`) whose monkeypatched fake `concatenate_media()` needed to accept the new `video_only` keyword. Full `test_export_media.py` (28/28) and `test_trip_export.py` (110 passed, 7 skipped) pass via the hand-rolled runner (no `pytest` in this sandbox); `test_map_video.py` (56/56) confirmed unaffected. `test_stitch.py` was not re-run in full for the same sandbox-timeout reason as every other entry in this file's own Parking/map investigation - this fix doesn't touch `stitch.py` at all (confirmed above that stitch.mp4's audio path is independent).

Not yet re-confirmed against Christer's own real archive/command line - only against the synthetic fixtures above, built directly from the real numbers and mechanism his own commands revealed.

## Fix cross-drive temp file swap breaking the audio remux on Windows

Direct follow-up on the entry above. First real-world run after that fix, Christer: "front file still the same + bv-export: The system cannot move the file to a different disk drive: C:\Users\christer\AppData\Local\Temp\bv_export_mux_d3mymymi\front_with_audio.mp4". The video-only-concat fix itself was fine, but the remux step never got a chance to run: `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` was called with no `dir=` argument, so it defaulted to the OS temp location - `C:\Users\...\AppData\Local\Temp` on Windows, which sits on the `C:` system drive. Christer's real exports land on `Z:\data\trips\...`, a different drive/network share. The final step, `muxed.replace(front_video)`, is `Path.replace()` -> `os.replace()`, and on Windows that's implemented via `MoveFileExW` without `MOVEFILE_COPY_ALLOWED` - it can rename within a volume but refuses to move across volumes, raising exactly the "cannot move the file to a different disk drive" error Christer saw. The sandbox's own synthetic test never caught this because everything in that environment - source, destination, and OS temp dir - lives on the same single filesystem.

**Fix.** One-line change in `export_trip()` (`trip_export.py`): `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=".bv_export_mux_", dir=front_video.parent)` - the temp directory is now created inside the export destination folder itself (same drive as `front_video`), not the OS default temp location. The final `muxed.replace(front_video)` is then always a same-volume rename, which Windows allows unconditionally. Everything else about the mux-then-swap design (temp file first, swap only on success, leave the good video-only file in place on failure) is unchanged.

**Verification.** `ast.parse()`-clean. Full `test_trip_export.py` still 110/110 passed, 7 skipped, via the hand-rolled sandbox runner - unchanged from before, since the sandbox's single-filesystem layout can't exercise the cross-drive path either way; this is a real-environment-only bug class. Not yet re-confirmed against Christer's real archive - next run against `z:\data\trips\...` should show `front.mp4` gaining real audio without the drive error.

## `-an` on the concat output wasn't enough - normalize every source's own file first

Direct follow-up. With the drive-move bug fixed, Christer re-ran a full `--wipe` export - fresh files, no stale cache - and reported: "1.85" / "same with wipe". Real diagnostics on the freshly-rebuilt `front.mp4` (`r_frame_rate=1000/33`, `avg_frame_rate=47375/25573`, `time_base=1/16000`, `nb_frames=6822`, `duration=3682.512000`) turned out to be **bit-for-bit identical** to the very first corrupted front.mp4 probed at the start of this whole investigation, before any of these fixes existed. `codec_type` on the file showed only `video` (confirming the earlier `-an` really did keep front.mp4 audio-free at the output level, and this run wasn't a stale-cache artifact - `_concatenate_asset()`/`concatenate_media()` unconditionally rebuild front.mp4 from scratch on every `export_trip()` call regardless of `--wipe`, so this genuinely was a fresh concat). So the fix from the previous two entries provably ran, and provably made no difference to the corruption itself.

That meant the earlier root-cause theory needed revisiting: `video_only=True` only added `-an` to the *final* concat command - an output-side restriction. It never changed what any individual source file loofoked like on disk; a normal FRONT recording handed to the concat demuxer was still a real 2-stream (video+audio) file, right alongside the repaired Parking recording's genuine 1-stream file (it "looked" the same to the demuxer either way `-an` was set on the output). `-an` tells the muxer not to *write* audio to the output; it doesn't stop the concat demuxer from having to reconcile a mid-list stream-layout change while *reading*. Comparing against REAR - which has never had this corruption, ever, at any point in this investigation - the one thing REAR's sources have always shared, that FRONT's never did until now, is that every single REAR source file is video-only from the start. FRONT's sources were still a real mix even after `-an`.

Re-derived from the numbers: 6822 real frames at a real ~30fps implies a real duration in the ~227-230s range - matching REAR's own real, correct 230.218s almost exactly (`3682.512 / 230.218 \u2248 16.0` once adjusted for the frame-count difference between the two sides). A precise 16x inflation, not a vague "roughly too long," is a strong sign this is a specific timescale/timestamp-handling defect triggered specifically by concatenating segments whose own stream layouts differ, not corruption from "any FRONT concat" in general - a synthetic repro attempt in this project's own sandbox (three lavfi-generated segments, one video-only sandwiched between two video+audio ones, run through both the old `-an`-only command and a fully-mixed no-`-an` command) came back with correct durations/frame counts either way, confirming this sandbox's ffmpeg build doesn't reproduce whatever real behavior Christer's does - this fix is reasoned from the evidence and from documented ffmpeg concat-demuxer fragility around per-segment stream-layout consistency, not from a local reproduction of the exact bug.

**Fix.** `concatenate_media()` (`export/media.py`), when `video_only=True`, no longer just appends `-an` to the final command - it first strips audio from *every source individually* into its own throwaway temp copy (`ffmpeg -an -c copy`, one file at a time, via new `_strip_audio_stream_copy()`), and builds the concat list from those normalized copies instead of the originals. Every file the concat demuxer ever opens is now genuinely, identically single-stream (exactly the shape REAR's sources have always had), rather than asking the demuxer to reconcile a real layout difference mid-list. `-an` is still kept on the final command too, redundant now but harmless, and cheap insurance. The per-source temp copies live in their own `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` (not written into `destination`'s own folder - these are read-only inputs to the later concat step, never renamed into place, so the earlier cross-drive rename concern from the previous entry doesn't apply here).

**Verification.** New test `test_concatenate_media_video_only_normalizes_each_source_before_concat` (`test_export_media.py`, 29/29 total): three sources - video+audio, video-only, video+audio, in that order (mirroring a repaired Parking recording sitting mid-trip among ordinary FRONT recordings) - concatenated with `video_only=True`, asserts the output is audio-free *and* its total duration lands in the correct ~3s range (not corrupted), rather than just checking "no audio track" the way the original test did. Can't assert this reproduces Christer's exact real-world corruption (this sandbox's ffmpeg doesn't exhibit it either way, confirmed above), so this is a sanity/regression test for the normalization logic itself, not a proof the real bug is fixed. `ast.parse()`-clean. `test_trip_export.py` still 110/110 passed, 7 skipped - unaffected, since it never asserts on real ffmpeg-produced duration values for this specific mixed-layout case. Not yet re-confirmed against Christer's real archive - this is the third attempt at the same underlying bug, so the next real-world result matters more than usual here.

## front.mp4 is fixed - now harden the audio-remux swap against a transient Windows lock

Christer, on the next real export: "Its not done yet, but front video is ok now." - confirmation the per-source normalization fix above actually resolved the real corruption. Same run then hit a new failure: "bv-export: Access is denied: z:\\...\\.bv_export_mux_.../front_with_audio.mp4". Different error than the earlier cross-drive one (`ERROR_NOT_SAME_DEVICE` vs. plain Windows `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED`) - the temp dir already lives on the same volume as `destination` (previous entry's fix), so this isn't a drive-crossing problem. `Path.replace()`/`os.replace()` briefly failing with "access denied" right after a large media file is written is a known real-world Windows pattern - most often real-time antivirus scanning the file the instant ffmpeg closes its handle, sometimes a network share's own locking semantics - and it's usually gone within a second or two. The real bug here wasn't the lock itself (nothing can fully prevent a third-party process from doing this) but that `muxed.replace(front_video)` was called with no error handling at all, unlike every other step in this same block - a transient lock crashed the *entire* export instead of degrading the way a failed `mux_audio_track()` call already does (leave the good video-only front.mp4 in place, warn, move on).

**Fix.** New `_replace_with_retry(source, destination, attempts=5, delay_seconds=0.5)` in `trip_export.py`: retries `Path.replace()` a few times with a short delay before giving up, then falls back to a plain overwrite copy (`shutil.copyfile` + delete source - a different Windows API path than `MoveFileExW`, which sometimes succeeds where a rename doesn't), and only then re-raises the original error. `export_trip()`'s call site now wraps `_replace_with_retry()` in its own `try`/`except OSError`, appending a warning and leaving `front_video` untouched on failure - the same "don't take good footage down with a secondary failure" pattern the `mux_audio_track()` `MediaToolError` branch right next to it already uses, just extended to cover the swap step too.

**Verification.** Four new unit tests in `test_trip_export.py` (114/114 total, up from 110) directly exercise `_replace_with_retry()`'s own decision logic via a monkeypatched `Path.replace()`/`shutil.copyfile` (a real transient Windows lock isn't reproducible on demand in this sandbox): succeeds immediately when nothing's locked, retries past a `PermissionError` that clears after a couple of attempts, falls back to the copy path when `replace()` never succeeds, and re-raises the original error (leaving both source and destination untouched) if the copy fallback also fails. `pytest` had to be added as an explicit import to this test file for `pytest.raises` - it had never been imported directly before (every previous test in the file only used `tmp_path`/`monkeypatch`, whose stand-ins the hand-rolled sandbox runner injects without needing the module itself). `ast.parse()`-clean. Not yet re-confirmed against Christer's real archive - this addresses a failure *after* the export he just confirmed the real video-only-concat fix on, so the underlying front.mp4 corruption itself is already verified fixed; this entry only hardens the swap step around it.

## Real confirmation, plus one more lock-related edge case

Christer, on his next real run: "some lock on file, could delete, so i changed prefix instead. it was good now" - confirming both real fixes above actually worked (front.mp4's real corruption, and the retry/fallback swap), worked around a leftover locked temp folder by hand this once, and the export completed. The lock he hit was most likely a stale `.bv_export_mux_*`/`bv_export_strip_*` temp directory left over from an earlier failed attempt (from before the retry/fallback fix existed) that a `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()`'s own automatic cleanup couldn't fully delete - `TemporaryDirectory.__exit__` raises if `shutil.rmtree()` can't remove everything inside it, which would crash the export on the way *out* of this code even after `_replace_with_retry()` had already recovered the actual swap successfully.

**Fix.** Added `ignore_cleanup_errors=True` to both `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` calls in this pipeline that can be left holding a locked file: `trip_export.py`'s front.mp4 mux temp dir, and `media.py`'s `concatenate_media(video_only=True)` per-source audio-stripping temp dir. A directory tempfile can't fully tear down is a stale leftover on disk, not lost footage - same "don't let a secondary failure take good output down with it" reasoning as `_replace_with_retry()` itself. (`ignore_cleanup_errors` needs Python 3.10+; this project requires 3.13, so no compatibility concern.) Deliberately scoped to just these two temp dirs - the ones this real report actually implicates - rather than every `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` call in the export pipeline (stitch.py, map_video.py, gsensor_video.py, gsensor_graph_video.py also have their own); those can get the same treatment if they ever show the same symptom.

**Verification.** `ast.parse()`-clean on both files. `test_trip_export.py` (114/114) and `test_export_media.py` (29/29) both unaffected, since `ignore_cleanup_errors` only changes behavior on a cleanup failure neither test suite triggers. This entry closes out the front.mp4 corruption investigation - Christer's own words, "it was good now" - real-world confirmed on his own archive, not just synthetic sandbox tests.

## Two follow-on Parking gaps: audio drifting out of sync, subtitles vanishing entirely

Front.mp4's own corruption fixed and confirmed, Christer reported two more real symptoms from the same underlying cause - a mid-trip Parking recording's real video duration not matching how the rest of the pipeline accounted for it: "audio it not in sync width front, its synching with the parking file" and "No stitch of subtitle, may be because parking files doesnt have any."

**Audio.** `_ensure_recording_audio()` deliberately never extracts audio for a Parking recording (already documented in that function - Parking's own audio track is broken/empty, and this predates the front.mp4 work entirely). `_concatenate_asset(trip, Asset.AUDIO, ...)` then just leaves any recording with no `Asset.AUDIO` out of audio.aac's own timeline - correct for audio.aac in isolation, but front.mp4's video (fixed in the previous two entries) keeps every included recording's *real* duration, Parking included. Muxed together, audio.aac ends up shorter than the video by exactly the skipped recording's own length, and everything muxed on afterward - `mux_audio_track()` for front.mp4, and stitch.py's own audio mux into stitch.mp4, since both draw from the same audio.aac - plays back against audio recorded for an entirely different moment in the trip.

**Fix.** New `_pad_missing_audio_with_silence()` (`trip_export.py`), run right after `_recording_video_offsets()`/`_video_position_breakpoints()` are computed and before the front/rear/audio concat executor starts (same "must finish before the audio worker reads recording.assets" timing `_ensure_recording_audio()` already established). For any recording present in the video timeline (`video_offsets`) but missing `Asset.AUDIO`, generates a silent `.aac` of exactly that recording's own real duration (derived from the gap between consecutive `video_offsets` entries - the same numbers `_concatenate_asset()` itself built the video from, not a reprobe) and assigns it into `recording.assets[Asset.AUDIO]` in place, so the AUDIO `_concatenate_asset()` call picks it up with zero changes of its own. New `generate_silence()` (`export/media.py`) does the actual `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i anullsrc=... -c:a aac` work; new `probe_audio_format()` (`generate/media.py`) probes an existing real `.aac`'s own sample rate/channel layout so the synthesized silence matches it exactly - ffmpeg's concat demuxer doesn't harmonize mismatched audio parameters across a `-c copy` list any more than it does for video (the whole subject of the last three entries), so a hardcoded default here would just trade one class of corruption for another. A trip with no real audio anywhere is a no-op (no reference format to match, and nothing downstream would use the silence for anyway).

**Subtitles.** `_merge_subtitle_segments()` (`subtitles.py`) rebased every recording's SRT/LRC cues by `recording.id.timestamp - trip_start` - wall-clock gap from the trip's first recording - never updated to the video-position scheme `_merge_gsensor()` already moved to back in the sync-fix entry earlier in this file (task #369-370). A Parking recording's wall-clock span is commonly far longer than the real video seconds it contributes (the entire premise of `_recording_video_offsets()`'s own docstring), so every cue for a recording *after* a mid-trip Parking recording landed offset by the Parking segment's wall-clock duration instead of its much shorter real video duration - often placing them well past the video's actual end, indistinguishable from no subtitles at all during playback.

**Fix.** `_merge_subtitle_segments()`/`merge_srt()`/`merge_lrc()` (`subtitles.py`) gained an optional `video_offsets` parameter, applied exactly the way `_merge_gsensor()` already does: a recording present in it is rebased by its own real video position; one absent from it (or when `video_offsets` isn't given at all) falls back to the old ID-timestamp-gap behavior. `trip_export.py`'s two call sites now pass the same `video_offsets` already computed for `_merge_gsensor()`/map rendering.

**Verification.** New tests in `test_export_media.py` (`generate_silence` - exact duration, matching/defaulted sample rate and channels, missing-ffmpeg error) and `tests/blackvue/generate/test_media.py` (`probe_audio_format` - codec-name-style mocked tests mirroring `probe_audio_codec`'s own). New integration test in `test_trip_export.py`, `test_export_trip_audio_stays_in_sync_when_a_middle_recording_has_no_audio`: three recordings (video+audio, video-only standing in for Parking, video+audio), confirms the exported front.mp4's *audio stream's own* duration (not the container's overall duration, which a shorter audio track hiding inside a longer video wouldn't change) lands within 0.5s of the video's - before the fix this would be off by close to a full recording's length. New tests in `test_subtitles.py`: `video_offsets` overriding a 3600s ID-timestamp gap down to the real 60s video position, and falling back to the ID-gap behavior for a recording absent from `video_offsets`. Full suite: `test_export_media.py` (33/33), `test_subtitles.py` (12/12), `test_trip_export.py` (115/115, 7 skipped) via the hand-rolled sandbox runner; `tests/blackvue/generate/test_media.py` needed a one-off dotted-module import (`importlib.import_module('tests.blackvue.generate.test_media')`) rather than the runner's usual `spec_from_file_location`, since that file's own `from .test_mp4_box_reader import ...` relative import needs real package context - a pre-existing constraint on that file, not something this change introduced. Not yet re-confirmed against Christer's real archive.

## Surface --prefix in bv-web's Trips list/detail pages

`bv-export --prefix Holiday` names a trip's output folder `Holiday_trip_20260715_..._20260715_...` (see `folder_name_for_trip()`, `export/trip_export.py`), but `web/trips.py`'s `TripAssets.label` deliberately reads the trip's own label straight from `trip.log`'s header line rather than the folder name, specifically so a `--prefix` doesn't leak into it (see the module's own `_TRIP_LABEL_RE` comment, in place since the trip-list feature was first built). The net effect: neither the Trips list nor a trip's detail page ever showed a `--prefix` anywhere - the only place it was visible at all was the raw folder name on disk, which nobody browsing bv-web day to day sees.

**Fix.** New `TripAssets.prefix` property (`web/trips.py`) recovers the prefix by diffing the folder name against the already-known label: `folder_name_for_trip()` only ever builds a folder name as either `label` or `f"{prefix}_{label}"`, so stripping the trailing `"_{label}"` off `folder.name` returns the exact prefix, or `None` when there wasn't one (including the case where `label` itself already fell back to `folder.name` because `trip.log` was unparseable - nothing real to diff there). `trip_list.html` and `trip_detail.html` both render it as a small `.badge` next to the trip's label, the same badge style already used for the Extras column and the account-bar role/theme controls, so no new CSS was needed.

**Verification.** Three new tests in `test_trips.py`: prefix correctly recovered for a real `Holiday_trip_...` folder, `None` for a plain unprefixed folder, and `None` for the label-fallback edge case. Full suite: `test_trips.py` 18/18 (up from 15) via the hand-rolled sandbox runner. Both edited templates re-parsed cleanly with a real `jinja2.Environment`. Not yet seen in Christer's own browser.

## Progressive disclosure for the bv-export web form

Christer, describing how bv-web should differ from the CLI rather than mirror it: "Instead of exposing all the advanced controls immediately, I'd make the UI progressive. Initially the user sees perhaps 8-10 controls. Then: Advanced stitching, Advanced map, Advanced g-sensor... checking 'Create stitched video' can reveal the stitch options automatically... The CLI has no choice but to expose every option up front, but the web UI can be much more conversational... they don't have to look the same. They just have to drive the same backend."

`job_new_bv_export.html` had grown to ~46 form fields, every one of `bv-export`'s own flags laid out flat across "Required"/"Time range"/"Defaults"/"Optional" `.option-group` divs - full CLI parity, but no CLI-vs-web distinction at all in how it's presented.

**Fix.** Reorganized into a small always-visible core (camera, timestamp/from/until, trip folder prefix, and the three headline checkboxes - Create stitched video, Include map, Include Parking-mode recordings - plus overwrite/dry-run/debug, 11 fields total) and four native `<details>`/`<summary>` sections that hold everything else, grouped by what they tune: Advanced trip detection (gap/parking-duration knobs), Advanced map (marker image, follow-camera radius), Advanced g-sensor (the two standalone overlay-video renders + Z-axis toggle), and Advanced stitching (every `stitch_*` field - layout, mirror inset x5, resolution/bitrate/scale/caps, the stitch-only map/g-sensor/subtitle panels). `<details>` gives free click-to-expand/collapse with no JS required for that part; new CSS in `base.html` (`.option-group > summary`) makes a collapsed section look identical to today's plain `.option-group h3` headers, just with a small rotating disclosure triangle. A small inline `<script>` in `job_new_bv_export.html` wires the two triggers Christer named explicitly: checking "Create stitched video" force-opens Advanced stitching, checking "Include map" force-opens Advanced map - deliberately one-directional (unchecking never force-closes), so a manually-opened section or values a user already typed into it are never fought or hidden again. Every field keeps its original `name`/`id` and default value untouched - this is a pure re-layout, app.py's `new_bv_export_submit()` route and `JobRunner.start_bv_export()` needed zero changes.
