**`generate/speech.py`.** `_load_npu_whisper_pipeline(model_dir)` constructs `openvino_genai.WhisperPipeline(str(model_dir), "NPU")` - the device string is the one documented difference from a CPU/GPU OpenVINO GenAI setup. `_get_npu_whisper_pipeline(model_dir)` caches it per model_dir in a new `_NPU_PIPELINE_CACHE` dict (same shape as `_WHISPER_MODEL_CACHE`/`_DIARIZATION_PIPELINE_CACHE` above it), wrapping a missing `openvino-genai` install or any other load failure in a `MediaToolError` with actionable guidance. `_decode_for_npu(source)` reuses `_load_waveform_via_ffmpeg()`'s own approach (shell out to ffmpeg directly rather than depend on a Python audio-decode library with its own native-DLL story - see that function's docstring) but returns a plain numpy `float32` array instead of a torch tensor wrapped in pyannote's `{'waveform', 'sample_rate'}` dict, since `WhisperPipeline.generate()` takes a raw sample array directly. `_whisper_language_token(language)` normalizes a plain code like `"en"` into the `"<|en|>"`-style token the pipeline's `language=` argument expects. `_npu_whisper_transcribe(model_dir, source, *, language)` ties these together and converts the result's `.chunks` (each with `.start_ts`/`.end_ts`/`.text`) into the same `SpeechSegment` tuples the faster-whisper path produces. `transcribe()` gained an `npu_model_dir: Path | None = None` parameter; when given, it bypasses `_whisper_transcribe()` (faster-whisper) entirely and calls the NPU path instead - and raises `MediaToolError` up front if `language` wasn't also given, since this backend has no auto-detect support (mirrors Whisper's own auto-detect only working from a real audio decode, which the NPU path's fixed `language=` requirement deliberately avoids depending on).

**CLI (`bv_generate.py`).** New `--npu-model-dir PATH` flag. `parse_args()` gained a validation check: `--npu-model-dir` without `--language` is a `parser.error()`, not a runtime failure partway through OpenVINO GenAI - matching this file's existing `--diarize requires --transcribe or --translate` / `--srt/--lrc require ...` validation style. `args.npu_model_dir` threaded through both of `transcribe()`'s call sites (`_do_translate_only`, `_do_transcribe_with_optional_translate`). `_do_transcribe_with_optional_translate`'s own `detect_language()` call (used when `--language` is omitted) is untouched by name, but a comment notes why it's never actually reached in NPU mode: `parse_args()`'s validation already guarantees `args.language` is set whenever `args.npu_model_dir` is, so `transcript_language` is never `None` on that path.

**Not verified against real Intel NPU hardware.** There is no Intel NPU in this project's dev/CI/sandbox environment - the implementation is built from OpenVINO GenAI's own published API (device string `"NPU"` swapped in for `"CPU"`/`"GPU"`, no other documented call changes) rather than confirmed by actually running it. Every relevant docstring/doc-page says this explicitly. Christer: worth trying `--transcribe --language en --npu-model-dir <converted-model>` on your Core Ultra desktop and reporting back if the real API doesn't match what's called here (the shape of `WhisperPipeline.generate()`'s return value - `.chunks` with `.start_ts`/`.end_ts`/`.text` - is the part most likely to be off, since it was the hardest part to pin down from documentation alone; see below).

**Setup dependency.** New `npu` optional-dependency group in `pyproject.toml` (`openvino-genai>=2025.1`), kept separate from the existing `speech` group rather than folded in - it's a large, Intel-specific dependency nobody without the right NPU has a reason to install, and `speech` already works standalone without it.

**Docs.** `docs/man/bv-generate.md`: synopsis line, `--npu-model-dir`/updated `--language`/`--model-size` rows in the options table, a new "Intel NPU transcription" section with the one-time `optimum-cli export openvino --trust-remote-code --model openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo --weight-format int4 --disable-stateful <dir>` model-conversion command (`--disable-stateful` specifically required for NPU's KV-cache decoder, not CPU/GPU) and a note about pre-converted models being available on Hugging Face as an alternative, plus a new usage example.

**Tests.** `test_speech.py`: fakes `openvino_genai` via `sys.modules` the same way `_install_fake_faster_whisper`/`_install_fake_pyannote_audio` already fake their own optional dependencies. Covers: `_load_npu_whisper_pipeline()` passes `"NPU"` as the device; `_get_npu_whisper_pipeline()` reports a missing `openvino-genai` cleanly, wraps other load failures with the model dir in the message, and caches by model dir; `_decode_for_npu()` decodes real audio via real ffmpeg (mirroring `test_load_waveform_via_ffmpeg_decodes_real_audio`) and reports a missing numpy cleanly; `_whisper_language_token()` wraps a plain code and passes through an already-wrapped one; `_npu_whisper_transcribe()` converts fake `.chunks` into the right `SpeechSegment`s and passes the right `generate()` kwargs, and wraps a `generate()` failure in `MediaToolError`; `transcribe(..., npu_model_dir=...)` raises without `language`, and bypasses `_whisper_transcribe()` entirely (asserted via a refuse-if-called stub) when the NPU path is used. `test_bv_generate.py`: `--npu-model-dir` defaults to `None`, requires `--language` (`SystemExit` without it), parses correctly with it; and `npu_model_dir` is confirmed to actually reach the `transcribe()` call inside `_do_transcribe_with_optional_translate`. Along the way, two small gaps in this project's own hand-rolled test harness (`FakeMonkeypatch` in `/tmp/run_one.py`/`/tmp/run_selected.py`, not part of the repo) were fixed to unblock these and several pre-existing tests that depend on them: `monkeypatch.setitem`/`delitem` support (several existing `test_speech.py` tests already called this; it just silently didn't exist) and `monkeypatch.setattr()`'s 2-positional-argument dotted-string form (`monkeypatch.setattr("builtins.input", fn)`), which several pre-existing `test_bv_generate.py` tests also depend on - both were previously-undiagnosed pre-existing failures, not caused by this feature, now fixed as a side effect of needing them for these tests.

**Verification.** Full harness runs, no regressions: `test_speech.py` 28/28 (16 pre-existing + 12 new), `test_bv_generate.py` 63/63 (all previously-failing tests from the two harness gaps above now pass too), `test_bv_export.py` 112/113 (1 pre-existing unrelated SRT-timing failure, unaffected by any of this).

Follow-up from Christer's own first real-hardware test: the NPU path did run (OpenVINO's `Core().available_devices` confirmed `NPU` present and visible), but was still running after a long wait with no NPU utilization showing in Task Manager - inconclusive on whether that's compile-time overhead, a Task Manager reporting gap (known to be unreliable for NPU workloads), or the NPU genuinely being slower than CPU/GPU faster-whisper for this workload (plausible: Core Ultra-class NPUs are tens of TOPS, well below what CTranslate2's mature CPU/GPU paths already achieve - NPUs are generally pitched for power efficiency and freeing up CPU/GPU for concurrent work, not raw single-job speed). Christer moved on without a conclusive timing comparison; treat the NPU path's practical usefulness on his hardware as unresolved, not confirmed-bad.

**Second follow-up: a real conversion-format bug, found and fixed.** Christer tried `--npu-model-dir` again on a real recording and got a hard failure loading the model: `Stateful models without 'beam_idx' input are not supported in StatefulToStateless transformation`, from deep inside OpenVINO's NPU plugin (`stateful_to_stateless.cpp`). Web research (Intel's own release notes/docs snippets) found the root cause: this project's original setup instructions - `optimum-cli export openvino ... --disable-stateful` - were correct for OpenVINO versions before 2025.1, but current (2025.1+) OpenVINO GenAI installs (which is what `pip install openvino-genai` gets you as of this writing) handle stateful Whisper models on NPU natively and no longer want a pre-stripped stateless export; the NPU plugin's own `StatefulToStateless` pass expects to find the state structure itself (specifically a `beam_idx` input) and chokes when handed a model that `--disable-stateful` already removed it from. A GitHub issue for `openvinotoolkit/openvino.genai` (#1965, "Whisper turbo v3 model hanging when trying to run on NPU") shows another user hitting NPU trouble with the exact same model+flag combination, consistent with this.

**Fix.** Dropped `--disable-stateful` from every conversion command in `_load_npu_whisper_pipeline()`'s docstring (`speech.py`) and `docs/man/bv-generate.md`'s setup section, with an explanation of the version history so a future reader isn't tempted to re-add it. Added a new Troubleshooting subsection to the docs quoting the exact error text (for grep-ability) and a secondary tip from the same research: if `WhisperPipeline` hangs even with a correct stateful export, check the NPU driver version (Intel recommends 32.0.100.3104+).

**Still unverified.** Christer hasn't yet re-converted without `--disable-stateful` and re-run `--transcribe` against real audio, so a full working end-to-end NPU transcription still hasn't been confirmed - this fix addresses a real, confirmed load-time failure, but "does it actually transcribe correctly once it loads" remains open. No code changes were needed beyond the docstring/docs correction - the bug was entirely in the setup instructions, not in `_load_npu_whisper_pipeline()`'s actual `WhisperPipeline(str(model_dir), "NPU")` call, which was always going to work fine against a correctly-converted model.

## Fix faster-whisper's repetition-loop hallucination on dashcam audio

While testing the NPU work above, Christer tried the default `--model-size small` path on a real recording and got this back: "I didn't fly much, I just went straight up. Parking mode off. He said it's for people laying outside there. With a dildo up his back flashing lights. I can't turn right. He said it's for people laying outside there." - repeated nine times in a row. This is faster-whisper's well-known repetition-loop hallucination failure mode, not a model-size problem: dashcam audio has a lot of non-speech noise (road/wind/engine), and two of faster-whisper's own defaults - `vad_filter=False` (no voice-activity filtering, so noise gets transcribed as if it were speech) and `condition_on_previous_text=True` (each segment's transcription is conditioned on the previous segment's text) - combine into exactly this symptom: one noisy stretch comes out garbled, and the model then latches onto that garbled phrase and repeats it into every subsequent segment instead of recovering.

**Fix.** `_whisper_transcribe()` (`speech.py`) now calls `kwargs.setdefault("vad_filter", True)` and `kwargs.setdefault("condition_on_previous_text", False)` before calling `model.transcribe()` - `setdefault` rather than an unconditional override, so an explicit kwarg from a future caller still wins. This applies to both `detect_language()` and `transcribe()`, since both go through `_whisper_transcribe()`. Not touched: the NPU path (`_npu_whisper_transcribe()`) - that's a different library (OpenVINO GenAI) with its own API, out of scope for this specific fix, and not something this project has had a chance to test for the same failure mode yet.

**Tests.** Two new tests in `test_speech.py`: `_FakeWhisperModel.transcribe()` was widened from a narrow `(self, source, language=None)` signature to `**kwargs`, capturing what it received (`self.received_kwargs`) so `test_whisper_transcribe_defaults_to_vad_filter_and_no_condition_on_previous_text` can assert both new defaults are actually passed through, and `test_whisper_transcribe_lets_an_explicit_kwarg_override_the_defaults` confirms `setdefault()`'s override behavior by passing both kwargs explicitly with the opposite values and checking they survive unmodified.

**Verification.** Full harness runs: `test_speech.py` 30/30 (28 previous + 2 new), `test_bv_generate.py` 63/63 unaffected (its own fakes fully replace `transcribe()`, so they never exercise `_whisper_transcribe()`'s new defaults directly). `docs/man/bv-generate.md` updated with a one-line note under the transcription-tuning options table. Not yet re-confirmed by Christer against the same recording that produced the original garbled output - worth him re-running `--transcribe --model-size small --overwrite` on it to see whether the repetition loop is actually gone now.

## Fix cuBLAS DLL search-path gap in faster-whisper's CUDA path

While still testing the two fixes above, Christer's `--model-size medium --language en` run (default faster-whisper path, no NPU flag involved) hit a fresh error: "transcription failed for 20230728_111831_E.aac: Library cublas64_12.dll is not found or cannot be loaded". This is the same *symptom* as the cuBLAS lazy-load bug already fixed in task #117 (CTranslate2 only initializes its real CUDA/cuBLAS runtime on first `.transcribe()` inference, not at `WhisperModel(...)` construction, so a CUDA model can pass `_load_whisper_model()`'s own construction-time CUDA-then-CPU-fallback probe and still fail here) - but this time the existing CPU-retry fallback didn't save him from it, and Christer independently ran `pip install nvidia-cublas-cu12 nvidia-cudnn-cu12` and got "Requirement already satisfied" for both, correctly diagnosing "Its a path problem."

**Root cause.** Since Python 3.8, Windows no longer implicitly searches `PATH` for a loaded native extension's own dependent DLLs - `os.add_dll_directory()` must be called explicitly to register any extra search directory. pip-installed `nvidia-cublas-cu12`/`nvidia-cudnn-cu12` place their real `.dll` files under `site-packages/nvidia/<component>/bin/`, but installing them via pip does nothing to register that path anywhere - so the DLL is genuinely present on disk (hence "Requirement already satisfied"), but nothing ever told Windows where to look for it. This also explains why the existing CPU-retry fallback didn't help: the hypothesis here is that CTranslate2's combined Windows GPU+CPU binary references cuBLAS symbols in a shared code path regardless of the `device=` parameter used, so forcing `device="cpu"` alone doesn't route around a missing-DLL-search-path problem the way it routes around a missing-GPU problem.

**Fix.** Added `_register_nvidia_dll_directories()` to `speech.py`: on Windows only (`os.name == "nt"` and `hasattr(os, "add_dll_directory")`; no-ops instantly elsewhere), tries `import nvidia` and, if present, globs `nvidia/*/bin` under each of its namespace-package path entries, calling `os.add_dll_directory()` on every directory found. No-ops entirely if `nvidia` isn't installed (e.g. a CPU-only machine), and short-circuits after its first real call via a module-level `_NVIDIA_DLL_DIRECTORIES_REGISTERED` flag - safe to call unconditionally. Called at the top of both `_load_whisper_model()` and `_load_cpu_whisper_model()`, before their respective `from faster_whisper import WhisperModel` imports, so the search directories are registered before CTranslate2's native extension ever loads - deliberately called from both the CUDA and the forced-CPU path, given the shared-binary hypothesis above.

**Tests.** Five new tests in `test_speech.py`: non-Windows no-op, missing-`add_dll_directory`-attribute no-op (exercised for real on this Linux sandbox rather than faked), `nvidia`-not-installed no-op, a real registration test (fake `nvidia` module with `__path__` pointing at a `tmp_path` tree containing `cublas/bin/` and `cudnn/bin/` plus a component with no `bin/` at all, confirming only the real `bin/` dirs get registered and the missing one is silently skipped), and a short-circuit-after-first-call test. The registration test patches `speech_module.os` itself (a fake object with `name="nt"` and a fake `add_dll_directory`) rather than the real `os` module - patching the real `os.name` to `"nt"` broke `pathlib.Path()` on this Linux sandbox (`NotImplementedError: cannot instantiate 'WindowsPath' on your system`, since pathlib picks its flavor from the real `os` module), so only `speech.py`'s own `os` reference is swapped, leaving the real `os` (and therefore `Path()`) untouched.

**Verification.** Full harness runs: `test_speech.py` 35/35 (30 previous + 5 new), `test_bv_generate.py` 63/63 unaffected. **Not yet confirmed on Christer's real machine** - he hasn't re-run his `--model-size medium --language en` command since this fix was written, so whether it actually resolves the real `cublas64_12.dll` error remains open.

**Follow-up: `add_dll_directory()` alone didn't fix it.** Christer re-ran the exact same command against this fix and got the identical error, verbatim: "transcription failed for 20230728_111831_E.aac: Library cublas64_12.dll is not found or cannot be loaded" - no change at all. Python's own docs claim `os.add_dll_directory()`'s registered directories also apply to "correspondingly loaded DLLs, transitively," which should have covered this, but empirically it didn't on his machine. Plausible explanation (not confirmed): CTranslate2's Windows binary may resolve cuBLAS through a delay-load stub or a nested `LoadLibrary` call from one of its own dependencies (e.g. a CUDA runtime DLL loading cuBLAS itself) that doesn't request the "extended"/safe-search flags `add_dll_directory` relies on - a known real-world gotcha with that API, distinct from the plain `PATH`-based search order which every DLL-loading code path honors regardless of which flags it uses.

**Fix, take two.** `_register_nvidia_dll_directories()` now *also* prepends every discovered `nvidia/*/bin` directory to the `PATH` environment variable (`os.environ["PATH"]`), in addition to (not instead of) the `os.add_dll_directory()` calls from the first attempt - belt and suspenders, since `PATH` is the mechanism this project's own upstream already documents for Windows (faster-whisper's README's pip-install section documents `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` for Linux; Purfview's `whisper-standalone-win` project, which bundles the same NVIDIA libraries for Windows, explicitly says to "place the libraries in a directory included in the PATH"). The `os.name != "nt"` early-return is now the only short-circuit gate; the previous `hasattr(os, "add_dll_directory")` check moved to guard just that one mechanism, so `PATH`-prepending still happens even in the hypothetical case that API is unavailable.

**Tests.** The registration test's fake Windows `os` stand-in gained `pathsep`/`environ` attributes and now asserts both bin dirs land in the (fake) `PATH`, with the original value preserved after them. The missing-`add_dll_directory` no-op test now also forces `nvidia` absent via `sys.modules`, since that code path no longer short-circuits before ever trying to import it.

**Verification.** Full harness runs: `test_speech.py` 35/35, `test_bv_generate.py` 63/63, no regressions. **Still not confirmed on Christer's real machine** - this is a second attempt at the same underlying problem, shipped without being able to reproduce the failure in this sandbox (no Windows/NVIDIA hardware here) - worth him re-running the same `--model-size medium --language en` command again once he's pulled this fix.

**Confirmed fixed.** Christer re-ran it: "It worked great, even the small model took 10 seconds and the large took 16." So the `PATH`-prepend mechanism (not `add_dll_directory` alone) was the piece that actually mattered for CTranslate2's Windows binary - worth remembering if a similar DLL-not-found report comes up for a different NVIDIA library down the line. He's sticking with `--model-size large` for accuracy given both sizes are fast enough on his hardware (GPU/CUDA now genuinely in use, not the CPU fallback - CPU-only int8 inference on a `large` model would not be anywhere near 16 seconds for a real recording).

## Fix intro.mp4's 20x render-time regression (map phase 16s -> 335s)

Christer, running the exact same `--map-intro --stitch --stitch-map` command twice in a row with only `--prefix` changed: "map phase time went from 16 seconds to 335 seconds, when I asked you for more details in intro video. I expected a little more time, bit not 20 times more. Could we just get the overview intro map and then overlay the zoomed in flyby, then we don't need to render every step of The big map. Or do you have a better solution." His own pasted `--debug` timing lines showed the damage precisely: `map phase` 16.4s -> 331.2s, `stitch: map panel render` 11.0s -> 298.2s, `bv-export: map intro phase` 18.6s -> 45.9s. The "details" he'd asked for earlier were `--map-intro`'s wide establishing-shot OSM fetch (task #577) and the caption bar (task #575/576) - this fix targets the fetch-widening side, which turned out to have a much bigger blast radius than intended.

**Two independent root causes, found by reading the actual code paths rather than guessing.**

1. **The widened road/area pool was shared with every other map render, not just the intro.** `_load_trip_roads()` (`trip_export.py`) widens its OSM fetch bounding box up to `zoom_start_multiplier`x per axis (~64x area at the default 8x) when `include_intro_bbox=True`, specifically so the intro's wide opening frame has real map data instead of rendering mostly blank. But the *same* widened `roads`/`areas` tuple it returned was then reused, unmodified, by map.mp4 (`--map`), the `--stitch-map` panel, and `--map-zoom` - none of which ever needs anything beyond the trip's own tight bbox. `roads_within_bbox()` (`osm_roads.py`) is an O(n) linear rectangle-overlap scan, run on *every single frame* of every one of those renders - so a 64x bigger pool meant every map-related render on the whole export paid the intro's own widened-fetch cost, not just the intro itself. This alone explains why `stitch: map panel render` (which has nothing to do with the intro) also blew up 11.0s -> 298.2s.

2. **`render_intro_flyover()` itself redrew everything from scratch on every one of its own frames.** Called `roads_within_bbox()` + `render_frame_visual()` fresh per frame (`frame_count` times - small at the 5-second default, but scales with `fps`, which the `--stitch` path sets to the real probed video frame rate), even though every frame is just a tighter crop of the same shot.

**Fix, Part A - stop sharing the widened pool.** `_load_trip_roads()` (`trip_export.py`) now returns a 5-tuple - `(bbox, roads, areas, intro_roads, intro_areas)` - instead of 3. `roads`/`areas` stay narrowed to the trip's own tight bbox (via `roads_within_bbox(index_roads(...), bbox)`) regardless of whether the fetch itself was widened; `intro_roads`/`intro_areas` carry the full widened set, used only by the two `render_intro_flyover()` call sites in `trip_export.py` (standalone `--map-intro` and the stitch-sized intro path). map.mp4, `--stitch-map`, and `--map-zoom` now only ever see the tight set, same as before `--map-intro` existed.

**Fix, Part B - Ken-Burns single-raster rewrite of `render_intro_flyover()` itself (`map_video.py`).** Every `frame_bbox` in the flyover's zoom is, by construction, a smaller concentric sub-rectangle of `start_bbox` (`_lerp_bbox()`/`_scale_bbox_from_center()` both center on the same point) - so a single high-resolution raster rendered once at `start_bbox` already contains everything any later, tighter frame needs to show. The function now renders that one raster via `render_frame_visual()` (called exactly once, not once per frame) and produces every output frame via `raster.resize((width, height), resample=Image.LANCZOS, box=crop_box)`, where `crop_box` is `bbox_pixel_rect()` - a new helper added to `map_render.py` right after `_project()`, the inverse operation: given a nested target bbox and the raster's own reference bbox, it returns the pixel rectangle the target occupies within the raster. This is what Christer asked for ("get the overview intro map and then overlay the zoomed in flyby") implemented as a proper Ken-Burns crop-zoom (one raster, panned/scaled) rather than a literal second composited video layer, since a crop of one raster reproduces the existing smooth eased zoom exactly, just without paying to redraw it every frame.

The raster itself is oversampled up to `zoom_start_multiplier`x linearly (so the tightest/last frame's crop still has enough source pixels to avoid visible upscaling), capped by a new `INTRO_MAX_RASTER_DIMENSION = 4096` constant so a large output size (e.g. sized to match a full stitch.mp4) can't blow up the one-time raster's memory/render cost unboundedly.

**Known, documented side effect - not yet confirmed either way with Christer.** The position marker used to be redrawn at a constant on-screen size every frame; it's now baked into the single raster, so it visibly grows as the camera zooms in instead of staying a fixed pixel size throughout. Arguably more cinematically correct for a "camera flying toward a fixed point" shot, but a real behavior change worth watching for in his next render.

**Tests.** `test_trip_export.py`: the two existing `_load_trip_roads()` tests updated to unpack/assert against the new 5-tuple (`intro_roads`/`intro_areas` equal the full fetched set; `roads`/`areas` narrowed to the tight bbox when the fetch was widened), plus the two edge-case tests (empty-fixes, no-widening) updated the same way. `test_map_video.py`: rewrote all ten `render_intro_flyover()` tests that assumed the old per-frame-redraw architecture, since `render_frame_visual()` is now called exactly once instead of once per frame - captured bboxes/positions/routes/show_marker are now asserted as single values instead of per-frame lists, and the "starts wide, ends tight" and "eases rather than moving at a constant rate" tests were rewritten to inspect the *crop rectangle* (`raster.resize()`'s `box` kwarg, tracked via a `_FakeFrameImage.resize()` stub added for this) rather than a bbox `render_frame_visual()` was called with per frame, using the new `bbox_pixel_rect()` helper (imported from `map_render.py`) to compute the expected crop for a given target bbox the same way the real code does.

**Verification.** Full harness run: `test_map_render.py` 44/44, `test_map_video.py` 85/85, `test_trip_export.py` 130/130 (7 skipped, pre-existing/unrelated) - 259 passed, 0 failed. All three touched source files (`trip_export.py`, `map_render.py`, `map_video.py`) also confirmed to import cleanly. `test_stitch.py` (which imports `stitch.py`, itself unmodified by this fix beyond a stale comment reference) was not run end-to-end in this pass - it drives real ffmpeg encodes and consistently exceeds this sandbox's command timeout regardless of what it's testing, unrelated to this change; `stitch.py` doesn't call `render_intro_flyover()` or `_load_trip_roads()` directly, so the blast radius here should be limited to `trip_export.py`'s own two call sites, but that's reasoning from the code, not a real end-to-end run. **Not yet run against real hardware/data at all** - no real GPS/OSM data is available in this sandbox, so the actual render-time numbers (hoped-for: map phase and stitch map panel render back near their original ~16s/~11s, with the intro phase itself possibly even faster than before task #577 ever widened the fetch) are unconfirmed. Worth Christer re-running the exact command from his report (`bv-export ... --stitch --stitch-map ... --map-intro ...`) to confirm the timings recovered and that the marker's now-growing size doesn't bother him.

## GPU-aware --model-size default + --cpu flag for bv-generate

Christer, after confirming the cuBLAS DLL fix above ("It worked great, even the small model took 10 seconds and the large took 16."): "can we compare transcribe small model on cpu with large model on gpu? I would like medium or large model default if you have a gpu." Asked via `AskUserQuestion` which size to default to on a GPU machine; Christer picked "large" - consistent with his own follow-up in the previous entry ("He's sticking with `--model-size large` for accuracy given both sizes are fast enough on his hardware").

**Design.** Two related pieces: a cheap way to know whether this machine can actually run faster-whisper on a CUDA GPU, and a way to force CPU explicitly even when a GPU is available (needed for the small/CPU vs large/GPU comparison itself - without it, there'd be no way to ask for the small model without also getting CPU by starving it of the GPU some other way).

**`gpu_available()` (new, `speech.py`).** Queries `ctranslate2.get_cuda_device_count() > 0` - CTranslate2 is the library faster-whisper itself is built on, so this asks the same library that will actually do the inference, rather than partially constructing a `WhisperModel` just to find out (wasteful) or shelling out to `nvidia-smi` (an extra external dependency, and not what CTranslate2 itself checks). Calls `_register_nvidia_dll_directories()` first - the same Windows DLL-search-path fix from the previous entry - so the device-count check itself benefits from it too, not just real transcription. Cached in a new module-level `_GPU_AVAILABLE: bool | None` flag (mirrors `_NVIDIA_DLL_DIRECTORIES_REGISTERED`'s own pattern) so repeat calls within one process don't re-import/re-query. Returns `False` on any failure (no NVIDIA GPU, driver too old, ctranslate2 not installed, ...) rather than raising - this only ever picks a friendlier default, never something that should block startup.

**`force_cpu` (new parameter, threaded through `speech.py`'s whole Whisper call chain).** `_get_whisper_model(model_size, *, force_cpu=False)` now caches under a distinct `f"{model_size}:cpu"` key when `force_cpu=True`, loading via the existing `_load_cpu_whisper_model()` instead of `_load_whisper_model()`'s CUDA-then-CPU-fallback - so a forced-CPU load never collides with (or overwrites) an auto-detected GPU/CPU load for the same `model_size`, letting both coexist in one process (exactly what the small/CPU-vs-large/GPU comparison needs, run back to back). `_whisper_transcribe()`'s existing cuBLAS-lazy-failure CPU-retry (from the earlier fix) now only fires `if not force_cpu` - a caller that already asked for CPU explicitly has nothing further to fall back to, so that failure propagates directly instead of retrying pointlessly. `detect_language()` and `transcribe()` both gained `force_cpu: bool = False`, passed straight through; `transcribe()`'s docstring notes it's ignored when `npu_model_dir` is given (that backend has no CPU/GPU choice of its own).

**CLI (`bv_generate.py`).** `--model-size` changed from a static `default="small"` to `default=None`, resolved once at the end of `parse_args()`: `args.model_size = "large" if gpu_available() else "small"` - but only when a Whisper transcribe/translate action is actually requested and `--npu-model-dir` isn't given (which doesn't use `model_size` at all), so `--extract-audio`/`--get-duration`-only invocations never pay for the `ctranslate2` import. An explicit `--model-size` always short-circuits this - `gpu_available()` is never even called if the user said what they wanted. New `--cpu` `store_true` flag, threaded as `force_cpu=args.cpu` into all three `transcribe()`/`detect_language()` call sites (`_do_translate_only`, both calls inside `_do_transcribe_with_optional_translate`).

**Tests.** `test_speech.py`: new `_install_fake_ctranslate2()` helper (mirrors `_install_fake_faster_whisper()`) backs five `gpu_available()` tests - true/false on device count, false when ctranslate2 isn't installed, false when the device-count call itself raises, and a caching test confirming a second call doesn't re-query. Three more cover `_get_whisper_model()`'s distinct cache-key behavior (force_cpu reads/writes a separate `:cpu`-suffixed key) and its use of `_load_cpu_whisper_model()` instead of the CUDA-then-CPU auto-detect path, plus one confirming `_whisper_transcribe(force_cpu=True)` re-raises a failure directly instead of retrying. `test_bv_generate.py`: new tests for `--cpu` parsing (defaults `False`, settable), and `--model-size`'s dynamic default resolution - explicit value always wins (asserted by making a mocked `gpu_available()` raise if called at all), defaults to `large`/`small` based on a mocked `gpu_available()` for both `--transcribe` and `--translate`, and is skipped entirely (again asserted via a raising mock) for `--extract-audio`-only and `--npu-model-dir` invocations. All of the pre-existing `transcribe`/`detect_language` fakes across both test files (there were many - `_fake_transcribe_factory`, several inline lambdas/defs) needed a `force_cpu=False` parameter added to their signatures too, since the real call sites now always pass that keyword; caught by running the full harness after the implementation, not by inspection.

**Verification.** Full harness runs: `test_speech.py` 43/43 (35 previous + 8 new), `test_bv_generate.py` 71/71 (63 previous + 8 new), `test_jobs.py` (bv-web's job runner, which shells out to `bv_generate.parse_args()` with an explicit `--model-size` from its own form data) 51/52 - the one failure is a pre-existing, unrelated `bv_export` argparse-error assertion untouched by this change. Docs (`docs/man/bv-generate.md`): synopsis line, updated `--model-size` row, new `--cpu` row, and a new example showing the small/CPU-vs-large/GPU comparison command pair.

**Not yet run against real hardware.** No GPU, no NVIDIA drivers, and no real dashcam audio exist in this sandbox, so the actual comparison Christer asked for hasn't been run by me - only implemented and unit-tested. To run it himself:

```
bv-generate --transcribe --model-size small --cpu --overwrite <path>
bv-generate --transcribe --overwrite <path>
```

(the second line now defaults to `--model-size large` on his GPU machine, per his own choice above) - worth him comparing timing and transcript quality between the two and reporting back.

## Fix: bv-web's bv-generate form bypassed the GPU-aware --model-size default

Christer: "bv-generate in bv-web does not show default model large for gpu server." The GPU-aware default from the entry above only ever kicks in when `--model-size` is *omitted* from argv (`bv_generate.py`'s `parse_args()` only resolves `args.model_size` when it's still `None`) - but `job_new_bv_generate.html`'s Whisper-model-size `<select>` always had `small` marked `selected`, and every HTML `<select>` always submits *some* value, never a blank one, unless an option itself has `value=""`. So `jobs.py`'s `start_bv_generate()` always received an explicit `model_size` string from the web form and always appended `--model-size <value>` to argv (`if model_size: argv += [...]`), permanently short-circuiting the CLI's own dynamic default for every web-triggered job - the GPU-aware default only ever worked from the raw command line, never through bv-web.

**Fix.** Added a new first `<option value="" selected>Auto (large on GPU, small otherwise)</option>` to the `<select>` in `job_new_bv_generate.html`, and removed `selected` from `small` (now just a normal explicit choice, same as `tiny`/`base`/`medium`/`large-v3`). `app.py`'s route handler already normalizes several other optional text fields from `""` to `None` right after receiving them (`translate`, `language`, `hf_token`, ...) with a shared comment explaining why (`"" == "not given at all"` for these forms); `model_size` is now normalized the same way (`model_size.strip() or None`), and its `Form(...)` default changed from `Form("small")` to `Form("")` to match. `jobs.py`'s `start_bv_generate()` already guarded the `--model-size` append with `if model_size:` (true even before this fix, just never reachable with a falsy value from the web form) - only its type hint changed, from `model_size: str` to `model_size: str | None`, to match the other already-optional parameters in the same signature. No change was needed to `bv_generate.py` itself - `parse_args()`'s dynamic-default block already does exactly the right thing once it actually sees a `None`.

**Tests.** `test_jobs.py`: `_generate_kwargs()`'s shared default changed from `model_size="small"` to `model_size=None`, matching the new real-world default and incidentally exercising the "Auto" path in every existing test that doesn't override it. Two new tests, `test_start_bv_generate_auto_model_size_applies_gpu_aware_default` and `..._falls_back_to_small_without_gpu`, monkeypatch `bv_generate_module.gpu_available` directly (rather than depending on whether this sandbox happens to have a GPU) and confirm `model_size=None` reaches `parse_args()` as a real `None` (not an empty string, which would resolve the same way but isn't what the fix actually produces) and comes back out the other end as `"large"`/`"small"` respectively - i.e. that a web-triggered job now gets the exact same GPU-aware default the CLI already had.

**Verification.** Full harness runs: `test_bv_generate.py` 71/71 unaffected (no changes to `bv_generate.py` itself), `test_jobs.py` 53/54 (51 previous + 2 new; the one failure is the same pre-existing, unrelated `bv_export` argparse-error assertion noted in the entry above), `test_archive_browser.py` 38/38, `test_trips.py` 22/22. `test_users.py` couldn't be run in this pass at all - `AttributeError: module 'tomllib' has no attribute 'TOMLDecodeError'` in `load_users_config()`, an environment/stdlib-version mismatch in this sandbox unrelated to this change (untouched by this fix; not investigated further here). No route-level test exists for `POST /jobs/bv-generate` in this codebase (only `JobRunner.start_bv_generate()` itself is tested directly), so `app.py`'s `Form("")` default change has no dedicated test of its own, consistent with how the rest of that route is already tested.

## Merge scene-scribe into beyond-video: --describe-scene + bv-scribe

Christer had kept `scene-scribe` (a standalone Qwen2.5-VL/Qwen3-VL dashcam scene-description/OCR prototype) deliberately outside this repo - "keep it outside of beyond video for now, if its good enough we might merge it in later" (see `scene_scribe.py`'s own docstring). During a real-footage OCR review session, two concrete failure modes surfaced: a real license plate came back confidently misread (`ETR734` reported as-is; the actual plate was `FTR78P` - not flagged "not legible", just wrong), and "Palm Jumeirah" (a Dubai landmark) showed up as on-screen text on a Stockholm-area trip, more than once across separate runs - a training-prior hallucination on "tunnel exit onto elevated highway" imagery, unrelated to anything actually in frame. Christer decided that was the trigger to merge it in now, specifically so the confidence-handling work happens in the real codebase rather than the prototype, and asked for two surfaces sharing one implementation: `bv-generate --describe-scene` (fixed sensible defaults, runs alongside other generation actions) and a new standalone `bv-scribe` command (the full tuning surface, batch/`--trip-summary` mode) - confirmed he wanted `bv-scribe` to use the same `LexicalTimeParser`-based recording selection every other `bv-*` command already uses, rather than scene-scribe's original raw file/folder path arguments. Also confirmed: GPU-preferred with a `--cpu` fallback (not GPU-only), matching the precedent already set for Whisper (`gpu_available()`/`--cpu` in `speech.py`).

**New module: `generate/scene.py`.** Ported from `scene_scribe.py` (prompts, patch-factor-by-model-family logic, the main describe/OCR pass, the detect-then-zoom sign/plate sub-pipeline, the text-only `--trip-summary` synthesis pass), refactored from a CLI script into a library module: `SceneOptions` dataclass replaces `argparse.Namespace` as the shared settings carrier threaded through every helper; model loading goes through a `_get_scene_model()` cache keyed by `(model name, cpu)` - same shape as `speech.py`'s `_get_whisper_model()` - so repeated `describe_scene()` calls within one process (bv-scribe's batch mode) only pay the load cost once; `vision_gpu_available()` mirrors `speech.py`'s `gpu_available()` but checks plain `torch.cuda.is_available()` rather than ctranslate2, kept as a separate cached flag since the two libraries could in principle disagree. Public API: `describe_scene(video_path, **options) -> str`, `summarize_trip(segments, **options) -> str`, `extract_description_section()`.

**Plate confidence check (new, `zoom_plate_confidence_check`, on by default).** Directly targets the real `ETR734`/`FTR78P` finding: every plate crop the zoom pipeline detects is now read twice - once with the normal (greedy) decoding, once with sampling forced on regardless of the caller's own `do_sample` setting (`_run_single_image_prompt(..., force_sample=True)`) - and the two reads are compared (`_normalize_plate_text()`: case/whitespace-insensitive). If they agree, the read is reported as-is; if they disagree, it's reported as `[unverified - two independent reads disagreed: 'X' vs 'Y']` instead of picking one. This operationalizes a heuristic the original prototype's own `--do-sample` help text already named ("trust text that reads the same across runs") but never actually applied - previously that heuristic required a human to notice instability across separate manual runs. Verified against a synthetic repro of the real finding (fake `_run_single_image_prompt` returning `ETR734` on the greedy call and `FTR78P` on the forced-sample call): confirmed the disagreement is caught and flagged, confirmed agreement produces no note, and confirmed non-plate signs never trigger the extra call at all (label-gated on `"plate" in det["label"].lower()`).

**Disclaimer footer (new, `DISCLAIMER` constant, unconditional).** Targets the "Palm Jumeirah" finding - no reliable *prompt-side* fix was found for this class of error (the module docstring documents why: a stricter "don't infer from general knowledge" prompt was tried in the original prototype and reverted, since it fixed one hallucinated tunnel name but caused a worse regression elsewhere - a long invented wall of fake administrative text on a different clip, plus loss of a previously-correct shop-sign read). Every `describe_scene()` output now ends with a fixed disclaimer naming both failure modes explicitly and stating that every read - especially plates/signs/place names - should be treated as unverified until checked against the source video, rather than trying to prompt the hallucination away.

**Asset type + suffix.** New `Asset.SCENE_DESCRIPTION = ("Scene",)` in `archive/asset.py`; `.scene.txt` registered in `ArchiveReader.ASSETS`.

**`bv-generate --describe-scene`.** New flag + `--scene-model` (default `Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct`, resolved once in `parse_args()` like the other action flags), added to the "at least one action" validation alongside `--extract-audio`/`--get-duration`/`--transcribe`/`--translate`. New `_do_describe_scene()` follows the same `_should_write_for`/dry-run/overwrite shape as `_do_get_duration()` - but deliberately does **not** skip Parking-mode recordings the way the audio actions do, since Parking recordings are still video (just no audio) and a vision model has real content to look at. Reuses `select_source()` for front/rear video selection and `args.cpu` for `force_cpu`, same as the transcription path.

**New `bv-scribe` CLI.** Mirrors `bv-generate`'s selection (`--from`/`--until`/`--timestamp` via `LexicalTimeParser`, `Archive`) and general-flag conventions (`--overwrite`/`--dry-run`/`-v`, injectable `say`/`warn` for bv-web's job runner to pick up later), but exposes the full `scene.py` tuning surface scene-scribe's real-footage testing converged on (frame sampling, resolution, crop, generation tuning, the zoom sub-pipeline's own flags, `--zoom-debug-dir`) rather than bv-generate's fixed defaults. Adds `--trip-summary` (needs 2+ described recordings in the selection; writes `trip_summary.txt` to the archive root) and `--trip-summary-max-new-tokens`. `_scene_kwargs()` is the single place mapping parsed CLI args to `SceneOptions` fields, used by both the per-recording `describe_scene()` calls and the `summarize_trip()` call.

**`pyproject.toml`.** New `bv-scribe = "blackvue.cli.bv_scribe:main"` script entry. New `scene` optional-dependency group (`transformers>=4.49.0`, `accelerate`, `qwen-vl-utils[decord]==0.0.8` - mirrors `scene_scribe.py`'s own `requirements.txt`) with a comment noting torch needs installing separately first for the right CUDA build, same as the original prototype's README instructed.

**Hardening beyond the direct port.** `describe_scene()`'s exception handling originally did a bare `import torch` inside its `except Exception` block to check for `torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError` - hardened to a nested try/except so an environment where torch somehow isn't importable at that point doesn't mask the real exception being handled with a new, unrelated `ImportError` (torch is already guaranteed loaded by `_get_scene_model()` earlier in real usage, so this is defense-in-depth, not something expected to fire in practice - caught while writing a fake-model test for the disclaimer-footer behavior, since the original fake `processor()` output didn't support `**`-unpacking the way a real HF `BatchFeature` does, which is what first surfaced needing to look closely at that code path).

**Tests.** `test_scene.py` (new): pure-function coverage (`is_qwen3_vl`/patch-factor selection, `build_prompt`, `extract_description_section`, `_normalize_plate_text`, `_parse_grounding_boxes` including markdown-fenced and truncated-JSON recovery, `vision_gpu_available` false when torch import fails), `SceneOptions` defaults, `describe_scene()`'s `opts=`/`**overrides` mutual-exclusion, and three real-execution tests against a faked `_LoadedSceneModel`/`_run_single_image_prompt`/`_extract_full_res_frames`: the plate-disagreement-flags-as-unverified regression test (the core one - directly reproduces the real `ETR734`/`FTR78P` finding), a plate-agreement-produces-no-note test, and a non-plate-sign-skips-the-extra-call test. Plus a `describe_scene()` disclaimer-presence test against a fully faked model/processor/generate chain. `test_bv_generate.py`: new tests for `--describe-scene` parse_args validation/`--scene-model` override, and `_do_describe_scene()` - Parking-mode NOT skipped (contrast with audio actions), no-source-is-an-error, dry-run writes nothing, `MediaToolError` propagates as `had_error=True`. `test_bv_scribe.py` (new): `parse_args()` defaults and flag parsing, and `_run()` against a fake `Archive` - writes one `.scene.txt` per recording, skips an existing file without `--overwrite`, dry-run writes nothing, no-recordings-in-range message, `MediaToolError` becomes `EXIT_HAD_ERRORS`, `--trip-summary` needs 2+ recordings and skips with a message otherwise, and a full two-recording trip-summary synthesis writing `trip_summary.txt`.

**Verification.** No `pytest` available in this sandbox (network-isolated, can't install it) - same limitation noted in earlier entries (e.g. task #323). Verified instead by direct execution: every pure function called and asserted against by hand (`PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c ...`), the plate-confidence-check regression scenario run for real against the faked model chain (confirmed the exact `ETR734 vs FTR78P` disagreement gets flagged, confirmed agreement doesn't, confirmed non-plate signs skip the extra call), `describe_scene()`'s disclaimer-footer path and its `opts`/`overrides` conflict both run for real, and `bv_scribe._run()`'s four core behaviors (write-per-recording, skip-existing, trip-summary-needs-2+, trip-summary-synthesizes-and-writes-file) all run for real against a fake `Archive`/`describe_scene`/`summarize_trip`. `ast.parse()` swept clean across every file in `src/` (one pre-existing, unrelated BOM-encoding error in `parser/vod.py`, untouched by this change) and all of `tests/`. **Not run against a real GPU, real Qwen model weights, or real dashcam footage** - no GPU and no network access to download model weights exist in this sandbox, so the actual vision-model inference path (as opposed to everything around it) is unconfirmed end-to-end. Worth Christer running `bv-scribe` or `bv-generate --describe-scene` for real once the `scene` extra + torch are installed, and specifically re-checking a recording with a known plate to see whether the confidence check either confirms a correct read cleanly or catches a bad one - and reporting back either way, plus whether "Palm Jumeirah" or similar hallucinations still show up despite the disclaimer (which only flags the risk, doesn't prevent it).

## --camera and --raw for the scene-description feature, bv-export scene merge

Follow-up to the scene-description merge above. Christer asked for three more things, worked out via back-and-forth: a way to point `bv-scribe` at non-BlackVue video ("can i have both?" - re: raw file/folder mode vs archive mode - discussed pros/cons, he picked a `--raw` flag over auto-detection, since auto-detecting risks silently misclassifying a partially-downloaded/oddly-named BlackVue folder as "raw" and losing the overlay-text crop), a way to choose which camera(s) get described ("will bv-scribe use our lexical parser" confirmed yes; then "can i have both?" for camera selection led to a `--camera {front,rear,both}` flag, confirmed as opt-in/default-`front` - "we follow our standard" - consistent with every other extra-inference-pass feature in this codebase defaulting off), and automatic trip-level merging of the per-recording scene files in `bv-export` ("dont touch bv-export except for merge of scene" - explicitly ruled out a new `--camera` flag or invoking `summarize_trip()` there, just the merge).

**`Asset.SCENE_DESCRIPTION_REAR` (new, `archive/asset.py`).** `SCENE_DESCRIPTION` relabeled from `("Scene",)` to `("Front", "Scene")` and a new `SCENE_DESCRIPTION_REAR = ("Rear", "Scene")` added alongside it - same grouped-label shape as `TRANSCRIPT`/`TRANSCRIPT_DIARIZED` ("Plain"/"Diar" under a shared "Transcript" `bv-ls` header group). `.rear.scene.txt` registered in `ArchiveReader.ASSETS` *before* the plain `.scene.txt` entry - `_detect_asset()` does an ordered `endswith()` scan, and `.rear.scene.txt` also ends with `.scene.txt`, so the more specific suffix has to come first (same reasoning already documented there for the diarized-before-plain transcript/translation ordering).

**`--camera {front,rear,both}` (new, `bv-generate --describe-scene` and `bv-scribe`, archive mode only).** `front` (default) is byte-for-byte the old behavior: front video, or rear as fallback if there's no front, written to `<recording>.scene.txt` with no camera suffix. `rear` processes *only* the rear video, with the same full `--task`/description+OCR treatment as `front` (not OCR-only) - a deliberate choice to look at the rear camera specifically gets full treatment, not just plates - written to `<recording>.rear.scene.txt`; errors if the recording has no rear video at all. `both` runs the normal front pass *plus* a cheap OCR-only bonus pass on the rear video (`task` forced to `"ocr"` regardless of `--task`), also written to `<recording>.rear.scene.txt` - a full rear-camera description would mostly just restate the front one's, so only plates/signs are worth the extra inference call - skipped with an info-level note (not an error) when the recording has no *distinct* rear video, i.e. front didn't exist and rear was already used as front's own fallback source, since a second pass on the identical file would just duplicate work under a different name.

`bv-generate`'s `_do_describe_scene()` was split into a small shared per-pass helper (`_run_describe_scene_pass()` - one `describe_scene()` call + write, given a `task` override or `None` for the default) and a dispatcher that looks up `recording.file(Asset.FRONT)`/`recording.file(Asset.REAR)` once and calls the pass helper for whichever camera(s) `--camera` selects. `bv-scribe`'s equivalent (`_run_scene_pass()` + `_describe_recording()`) follows the same shape but threads the full `SceneOptions` tuning surface instead of bv-generate's fixed `{model, force_cpu}`, and additionally returns the description text for whichever pass is the "canonical" one for `--trip-summary` purposes (front's, or rear's when `--camera rear` has no front pass at all) - reusing an existing, unwritten-to file's content when `_should_write()` says skip, same as the pre-existing trip-summary-reuse behavior.

**`--raw` (new, `bv-scribe` only).** Points `PATH` at a single raw video file or a directory of them (non-recursive, sorted by name, recognized extensions `.mp4`/`.mov`/`.avi`/`.mkv`/`.m4v`/`.webm`) instead of a BlackVue archive - no `Archive`/`LexicalTimeParser` recording selection at all, since raw footage has none of BlackVue's filename/sidecar structure to select on. `--from`/`--until`/`--timestamp` and `--camera` both exit with `EXIT_ARGS_ERROR` if given alongside `--raw` (meaningless without an archive/front-rear structure) rather than silently ignored. `--crop-top`/`--crop-bottom` changed from fixed `0.0378`/`0.0344` defaults to `None`, resolved once at the end of `parse_args()` to `0.0` under `--raw` (BlackVue's burned-in overlay text won't exist on non-BlackVue footage) or the old tuned values otherwise - an explicit `--crop-top`/`--crop-bottom` always wins regardless of `--raw`, since the resolution only fires when the parsed value is still `None`. Output is `<video-stem>.scene.txt` next to each source video, matching archive mode's `.scene.txt` suffix. `--trip-summary` still works in `--raw` mode, using each video's filename stem as its label and writing `trip_summary.txt` into the directory (or the single video's own parent directory, for a single-file `PATH`).

**bv-export scene merge (new, `TEXT_ASSETS` in `trip_export.py`).** Two entries added to the existing `TEXT_ASSETS` tuple - `(Asset.SCENE_DESCRIPTION, "scene.txt")` and `(Asset.SCENE_DESCRIPTION_REAR, "scene.rear.txt")` - reusing the exact same generic mechanism already used for `transcript.txt`/`translation.txt` (`merge_text_assets()`: per-recording text concatenated in trip order under a `# <recording_id>` header, `None` if no recording in the trip has the asset) and the same loop in `export_trip()` that already consumes `TEXT_ASSETS` generically. No new flag, no new function, no dependency - plain text concatenation, matching the `trip.srt`/`trip.lrc` "merge automatically if present, skip silently if absent" precedent Christer pointed at. `bv-export` itself is otherwise untouched, per his explicit instruction.

**Docs.** `docs/man/bv-generate.md`: new `--camera` row + synopsis update. `docs/man/bv-scribe.md`: new `--raw`/`--camera` synopsis entries, a new "RAW VIDEO MODE" section, updated `PATH`/`--crop-top`/`--crop-bottom` descriptions, two new examples. `docs/man/bv-export.md`: new `OUTPUT` table rows for `scene.txt`/`scene.rear.txt` - and, noticing the gap while there, also added the previously-undocumented `transcript.txt`/`transcript.diarized.txt`/`translation.txt`/`translation.diarized.txt` rows, which were already real `TEXT_ASSETS` behavior but had never been written down. `docs/CLI.md`: a parenthetical on the shared timestamp-selection section noting `bv-scribe --raw` as the one exception.

**Tests.** `test_bv_generate.py`: `_base_args()` gained a `camera="front"` default (existing calls to `_do_describe_scene()` would otherwise hit `AttributeError: camera` now that the dispatcher reads it); new tests for `--camera` parse_args (default/choices/invalid-value) and `_do_describe_scene()`'s four camera-dispatch paths (front-unchanged, rear-only-full-task, rear-errors-without-rear-video, both-writes-both-with-ocr-bonus, both-skips-bonus-without-distinct-rear). `test_bv_scribe.py`: new tests for `--camera`/`--raw` parse_args (defaults, crop-default resolution under `--raw`, explicit-crop-overrides-raw-default) and `_run()`'s camera dispatch (rear-only, both, rear-errors) plus `--raw` behavior (single file, directory with non-video files ignored and sorted, rejects `--timestamp`/`--camera`, `--trip-summary` writes to the directory). `test_trip_export.py`: a `TEXT_ASSETS`-contains-the-new-entries sanity test plus direct `merge_text_assets()` tests against fake `Recording`/`AssetFile` fixtures (multi-recording front merge, rear-only-on-one-recording merge, no-scene-data returns `None`) - lighter-weight than the existing full `export_trip()` integration test for transcripts, since `TEXT_ASSETS`'s consuming loop in `export_trip()` is already exercised generically by that test and doesn't need re-proving per asset type.

**Verification.** No `pytest` in this sandbox (network-isolated, confirmed again this session - `pip install pytest` fails with the same proxy 403 as prior entries), and `trip_export.py`'s own import chain additionally needs `tomllib` (stdlib 3.11+; this sandbox has 3.10) via `camera_config.py` - worked around for `test_trip_export.py` specifically with a throwaway `tomllib` stub module on `PYTHONPATH` providing just enough surface (`load()`, `TOMLDecodeError`) for the import chain to complete, since nothing in the new tests actually exercises `camera_config.py`. Built a small pytest-fixture shim (`tmp_path`/`monkeypatch`/`capsys`, plus a `pytest.raises`-only stub for `pytest` itself) to run every new/modified test function for real against the actual test files rather than only hand-rolled verification scripts - all of `_do_describe_scene()`'s camera-dispatch edge cases (front/rear/both, rear-with-no-rear-video, both-with-no-distinct-rear) confirmed via direct execution before the formal tests existed, then the formal tests themselves run through the shim: `test_bv_generate.py` full module 80 passed/8 failed (all 8 failures are shim limitations unrelated to this change - `capsys` not capturing stderr, `monkeypatch.setattr("dotted.string", value)` form not supported by the minimal shim - none touch `describe_scene`/`--camera` code), `test_bv_scribe.py` full module 23/23, `test_trip_export.py`'s 3 new tests 3/3. `ast.parse()` clean across all touched files.

## bv-search: text + GPS proximity search command

Christer: "I would like to have search utility, maybe bv-search or bv-find with standard lexical time parser, that can search for text in scribe/transcribe/translate files and also for close (specified by option for a search area of X meters) by gps coordinates or geografix name, and in combination to, and probably more stuff in the future." The `AskUserQuestion` tool failed repeatedly this session (`AbortError: Tool permission stream closed before response received`, three times running the same clarifying questions) - Christer noticed the hang and said "Are you hanging, no output for 7 minutes. use the name bv-search," an explicit instruction to stop retrying the broken tool and proceed. Design decisions below were made as stated defaults rather than confirmed interactively, given that constraint - flagged here in case any need revisiting.

**Design.** `bv-search` follows the same archive-mode-only, `LexicalTimeParser`-based recording selection every other `bv-*` command uses (`--from`/`--until`/`--timestamp`) - no raw-file mode, unlike `bv-scribe --raw`, since text/GPS search only makes sense against an archive's own generated sidecar files. Two independent search criteria, combinable: `--text PATTERN` (transcript/translation/scene-description content, restrictable to one category via `--asset`) and `--near LAT,LON`/`--place NAME` (GPS proximity within `--radius` meters, `--place` forward-geocoded via Nominatim). When both are given, a recording only matches if it satisfies both - AND, not OR - since "traffic near this intersection" is a more useful query than "traffic anywhere, or anything near this intersection." Kept deliberately minimal/modular (a small library module plus a thin CLI dispatcher) given Christer's own "probably more stuff in the future," so another criterion can be added later as one more function plus one more flag rather than a restructuring.

**`forward_geocode()`/`load_or_forward_geocode()` (new, `export/geocoding.py`).** The inverse of the existing `reverse_geocode()`/`load_or_reverse_geocode()` pair (already used by `bv-export`'s `trip_info.txt`) - same Nominatim service, same throttle/`USER_AGENT`/timeout/`MediaToolError`-on-failure conventions, but hitting the `/search` endpoint with a free-text query instead of `/reverse` with a coordinate, taking the single best-ranked match (`limit=1`) since `bv-search` wants one search point, not a disambiguation list. Cache key (`_forward_cache_key()`) differs from the coordinate-based `_cache_key()` it sits alongside: a free-text query can contain arbitrary characters/length, so it's normalized (casefolded, whitespace-collapsed) and SHA-1 hashed into a `geocode_place_<hash>.json` filename rather than used directly. A genuine "no result" (empty Nominatim response) is cached as `None`, same as the reverse direction; a request/parse failure raises `MediaToolError` and writes nothing, so a transient network blip gets retried next time rather than permanently remembered as "no result."

**`search.py` (new top-level module, not a package - mirrors `lexicaltimeparser.py`'s own precedent for a small standalone library module).** `TEXT_SEARCH_ASSETS`: a dict mapping `--asset`'s four choices (`transcript`/`translation`/`scene`/`all`) to tuples of `Asset` enum members - diarized transcript/translation and the rear-camera scene description are grouped in with their plain/front counterparts (not left out), so a default `all` run doesn't silently miss half of what `--diarize` or `--camera` produced just because it's a different `Asset` type under the hood. `search_text(recording, pattern, *, assets, case_sensitive, regex)`: builds a `test(line) -> bool` closure once (regex via `re.compile`, raising `MediaToolError` on `re.error`; plain mode is case-insensitive substring by default, matching `grep`'s own default), then iterates the given assets, silently skipping ones the recording doesn't have - same "not every recording has every asset" shape `bv-ls` already treats as normal. `search_near(recording, lat, lon, radius_meters)`: iterates the recording's `.gps` file via the existing `read_gps()`, skips fixes where `not fix.valid` or position is `None` (same NMEA-mode-indicator validity `gps_reader.py` already established), returns the single closest fix within radius as a `GeoMatch`, or `None` if the recording has no GPS data at all or nothing qualifies. Haversine distance duplicated (not imported) from `trip_stats.py`'s own module-private copy, with a comment following that module's own precedent for why - a genuinely separate concern, worth the small duplication over a cross-module import.

**`cli/bv_search.py` (new CLI entry point).** Validates at least one of `--text`/`--near`/`--place` is given before doing anything else. `--near`/`--place` are an argparse mutually-exclusive group; `--near` parses `LAT,LON` as one comma-separated token (a custom `type=` function) rather than two separate flags, so it composes cleanly with the rest of the flag set. `--place`'s `load_or_forward_geocode` import is deferred to inside the `if args.place is not None:` branch rather than module scope - importing any submodule of `blackvue.export` (even just `geocoding.py`) forces Python to run `export/__init__.py` first, which eagerly imports the entire heavy export/stitch/map-rendering toolkit (`trip_export.py`, `stitch.py`, `map_video.py`, ...) - wasteful for a lightweight, mostly-read-only search command, and specifically what surfaced a `ModuleNotFoundError: tomllib` failure in this Python-3.10 sandbox (an unrelated, pre-existing sandbox-vs-`requires-python=">=3.13"` mismatch already documented in earlier entries) when `bv_search.py` first tried a module-scope import. Same deferred-import pattern `speech.py`/`scene.py` already use for `torch`/`ctranslate2`. `_run()` filters recordings by the parsed interval, then per recording runs `search_text()`/`search_near()` in sequence with early `continue`s for the AND-combine semantics, printing the recording id plus every matching text line and/or the closest GPS match for every recording that survives both filters; reports "no matches" if nothing did, tracks per-recording `MediaToolError`s as `EXIT_HAD_ERRORS` without stopping the run (same shape every other `bv-*` command's per-recording error handling already uses).

**`pyproject.toml`.** New `bv-search = "blackvue.cli.bv_search:main"` script entry - no new optional-dependency group needed, since `search.py`/`bv_search.py` only use stdlib plus modules already covered by the base install (the `--place` geocoding path reuses `geocoding.py`'s existing, already-unconditional Nominatim/urllib code).

**Docs.** `docs/man/bv-search.md` (new): full synopsis/description/options/examples following the established man-page format. `docs/CLI.md`: added `bv-search` to both the "operates directly on an archive directory" list and the shared-timestamp-selection command list, plus one example line.

**Tests.** `tests/blackvue/test_search.py` (new, 12 tests): `TEXT_SEARCH_ASSETS["all"]` composition, `search_text()` case-insensitive/case-sensitive/regex/invalid-regex/asset-restriction/skip-missing-asset/unreadable-file behavior, `search_near()` closest-fix-within-radius/nothing-in-radius/invalid-fixes-skipped/no-gps-at-all (GPS tests monkeypatch `read_gps` directly rather than writing real NMEA sentences, mirroring `test_osm_roads.py`'s own fake-fixture style for GPS-consuming tests). `tests/blackvue/export/test_geocoding.py` (new, 8 tests, first test file this module has ever had): `forward_geocode()` success/no-match/network-failure/malformed-JSON/malformed-payload, `load_or_forward_geocode()` fetch-and-cache/cache-hit-avoids-second-request/normalizes-query-for-cache-hits/caches-genuine-no-result - monkeypatches `geocoding_module.urlopen` the same way `test_osm_roads.py` already does for its own Nominatim-adjacent (Overpass) fetch tests. `tests/blackvue/cli/test_bv_search.py` (new, 14 tests): `parse_args()` defaults/path-default/`--near` parsing/malformed-`--near`/`--near`-`--place` mutual exclusion, and `_run()`'s no-criteria-is-an-error, no-recordings-in-range, text-match-reporting, text-no-match, `--asset` restriction, `--near` GPS match reporting, the AND-combine test (one recording matches text but is geographically far away and is correctly excluded; another matches both and is included), and both `--place` paths (geocodes-then-searches with a faked `load_or_forward_geocode`, and reports `EXIT_HAD_ERRORS` when geocoding finds nothing).

**Verification.** No `pytest` in this sandbox (same network-isolated/proxy-403 limitation as every prior entry). Before writing the formal test files, `bv_search.py`'s `_run()` was exercised directly end-to-end against a real temp archive with real recording/GPS/text files (not faked): `--text` matching, `--asset scene` restriction, `--near` proximity matching against a real synthesized `$GPRMC` `.gps` file, the AND-combine behavior, the "no matches" message, and the no-criteria `EXIT_ARGS_ERROR` path - all confirmed correct before any test file existed. Then built a small pytest-fixture-and-assertion shim (`monkeypatch`/`tmp_path`/`capsys`/`pytest.raises`/`pytest.approx`, plus a `tomllib` stub on `PYTHONPATH` for the same pre-existing sandbox-vs-3.13 mismatch documented in the previous entry) and ran the three new formal test files through it for real, rather than relying only on the hand-rolled verification: `test_search.py` 12/12, `test_geocoding.py` 8/8, `test_bv_search.py` 14/14 - all 34 new tests passing. `ast.parse()` clean across `search.py`, `cli/bv_search.py`, and the modified `export/geocoding.py`.

## bv-search follow-up: --place line-geometry matching for long roads

Right after the entry above, Christer asked: "wil gps search be any good if i enter a road name, roads can be very long." He was right to check - `forward_geocode()` only ever kept `payload[0]["lat"]`/`["lon"]`, Nominatim's *single* best-match point, which for a road is just one point somewhere along it (often near the middle, or one endpoint of whichever OSM way segment matched best). A normal `--radius` around that one point would only cover a small stretch of a multi-kilometer road, silently missing recordings near the rest of it. Presented the gap plus three options (add real line-geometry matching, document the limitation instead, or skip it for now); Christer picked adding line-geometry matching.

**`GeocodeResult` (new, `export/geocoding.py`, replaces the old plain `tuple[float, float] | None` return type of `forward_geocode()`/`load_or_forward_geocode()`).** Frozen dataclass: `point: tuple[float, float]` (always populated - Nominatim's own lat/lon, exactly what the old return value was) plus `lines: tuple[tuple[tuple[float, float], ...], ...] = ()` (0+ polylines, each a tuple of (lat, lon) vertices - populated only when Nominatim's match is a road or area, not a point-like address/POI). `forward_geocode()` now requests `polygon_geojson=1` alongside the existing `format`/`q`/`limit` params, so a road/area match's actual OSM geometry comes back in the response's `geojson` field. New `_geojson_to_lines()` normalizes whatever GeoJSON type comes back: `LineString`/`MultiLineString` (roads) map directly to one or more lines; `Polygon`/`MultiPolygon` (areas - parks, water, administrative boundaries) use only each ring's *exterior* boundary, not holes, since this only needs a proximity-to-boundary check, not full point-in-polygon containment; a plain `Point` match (most addresses/POIs) or any missing/unrecognized geometry falls back to `lines=()`, meaning "just use `point`" downstream - a normal, common outcome, not a failure. `load_or_forward_geocode()`'s on-disk cache format changed to match (`{"point": [...], "lines": [[...], ...]}` instead of the old `{"coordinates": [...]}`) - no migration needed, since no real cache files existed yet from this feature's first commit just prior.

**Point-to-segment distance math (new, `search.py`).** `_project_local_meters()`: flat-Earth (equirectangular) projection of (lat, lon) into local x/y meters around a reference latitude - accurate enough at the few-hundred-meter-to-few-kilometer scale `--radius` operates at, the same order of approximation `_haversine_distance_meters()` already makes (a perfect sphere, not the real ellipsoid). `_point_to_segment_distance_meters()`: standard 2D point-to-segment projection (clamped `t` in `[0, 1]`) done in that local projection, rather than a closed-form great-circle point-to-segment formula, which would be substantially more involved for no real accuracy benefit at this scale. `_min_distance_to_lines_meters()`: the shortest distance from a GPS fix to *any* segment across *any* of the given lines (not just to the nearest vertex - a road's own vertices can be sparsely spaced on long straight stretches, so vertex-only distance would still undershoot); a degenerate single-vertex "line" (Nominatim can return one for a very short way) falls back to plain point distance.

**`search_near()` (modified, `search.py`).** New optional `lines` keyword-only parameter. When given (non-empty), every GPS fix's distance is computed via `_min_distance_to_lines_meters()` against the line geometry instead of `_haversine_distance_meters()` against the plain `lat`/`lon` point - `lat`/`lon` themselves are effectively unused in that case (the line geometry is authoritative), kept as required positional params so `--near`'s existing plain-point call sites don't change. `GeoMatch`'s own shape (closest fix + its distance) is unchanged either way - callers don't need to know which distance method produced a match.

**`bv_search.py` (modified).** `--place`'s resolution now unpacks a `GeocodeResult` instead of a plain tuple: `target = result.point`, `target_lines = result.lines`, both threaded into every `search_near()` call (`--near`'s `args.near` path leaves `target_lines` as `()`, unaffected). The confirmation line printed after a successful `--place` lookup now notes when line geometry was found and used (`"<name>" -> lat,lon (road/area geometry, N segment(s) - searching along the whole shape, not just this point)`), so it's visible at a glance whether a query resolved to a road/area (whole-shape search) or a plain point (single-point-plus-radius search, same as `--near`).

**Docs.** `docs/man/bv-search.md`: new paragraph under "GPS proximity search" explaining the road/area line-geometry behavior and why it matters for long roads specifically, plus the confirmation-line format.

**Tests.** `tests/blackvue/export/test_geocoding.py`: `forward_geocode()` tests updated to assert against `GeocodeResult` instead of a bare tuple, plus new tests for `polygon_geojson=1` being requested, `LineString`/`MultiLineString`/`Polygon` geometry extraction (including the exterior-ring-only behavior for a polygon with a hole), and `Point` geometry correctly producing no extra lines; `load_or_forward_geocode()` gained a round-trip-through-cache test for line geometry specifically. `tests/blackvue/test_search.py`: new tests for `_point_to_segment_distance_meters()` (on-segment near-zero, off-segment endpoint-clamping), `_min_distance_to_lines_meters()` (picks the closest segment across multiple lines, handles a degenerate single-vertex line), and an end-to-end `search_near()` test that directly demonstrates the fix - a GPS fix ~5km from a road's single representative point is missed with plain point/radius search but found once the road's own line geometry is passed in. `tests/blackvue/cli/test_bv_search.py`: existing `--place` test's fake `load_or_forward_geocode` now returns a `GeocodeResult`; new test confirms `_run()` finds a recording near the far end of a road via `--place` when the road resolves with line geometry, and that the output reports "segment" so the behavior is visible to the user.

**Verification.** Same no-`pytest`-in-sandbox situation as every prior entry; ran all three modified/extended test files through the same pytest-fixture shim used in the previous entry: `test_search.py` 17/17 (12 previous + 5 new), `test_geocoding.py` 14/14 (8 previous + 6 new), `test_bv_search.py` 15/15 (14 previous + 1 new) - 46/46 total, zero failures. `ast.parse()` clean across `search.py`, `cli/bv_search.py`, and `export/geocoding.py`.

## Camera-id resolution for bv-ls/bv-generate/bv-export/bv-scribe/bv-search, plus an Output config field for bv-export

Christer noted a bv-search timing result ("bv-search searching through this year 7.5 months only took 33 seconds, thats fair") and approved: "yes build it" - two combined asks from the discussion just prior. First: `bv-ls`, `bv-generate`, `bv-export`, `bv-scribe`, and `bv-search` all took a plain archive-directory `PATH`, unlike `bv-config`/`bv-download`/`bv-gps`/`bv-live`, which already take a camera system id and resolve it themselves - an inconsistency worth closing, so every archive-reading command accepts either form. Second: `bv-export --target` is required on every run with no way to default it, even though most cameras only ever export to one place - an optional `Output` field on the camera config, defaulted from there when `--target` is omitted, removes the need to repeat it by hand every time.

**`resolve_archive_path()` (new, `core/camera_config.py`).** `resolve_archive_path(path_or_id, config_dir) -> tuple[Path, CameraConfig | None]` - the one shared resolver all five CLIs now call. `_looks_like_path()` (new, private) is checked first: if the given string starts with `./`/`.\`, is `.`/`..`, is absolute, or contains a path separator, it's always treated as a literal directory (`config=None` returned) - the same escape hatch git itself uses to disambiguate `./file` from a branch name, so `./Kirby` always means a literal directory even when a camera id `Kirby` also exists. Otherwise, `load_camera_config()` is tried for that id under `config_dir`; a real camera config resolves to its `target` directory plus the loaded `CameraConfig`. A bare name that isn't a configured camera id falls back to being used as a literal path too (also `config=None`) - matching prior behavior for anyone not using camera configs at all, rather than turning "typo'd a camera id" into a hard error. A camera config that exists but fails to parse propagates its `CameraConfigError` rather than silently falling back, since that's a real misconfiguration worth surfacing.

**`CameraConfig.output` (new field, `core/camera_config.py`).** `output: Path | None = None`, TOML-serialized only when set (omitted from the file entirely otherwise, matching how optional fields already behave in this format). Threaded through `save_camera_config()`/`load_camera_config()`'s existing TOML round-trip.

**`cli/bv_config.py` (modified).** `run_wizard()` gained a third prompt, "Output (bv-export destination, optional)", between Target and Endpoints, defaulting to the existing saved value when editing a config (blank when creating one or when never set) - leaving it blank preserves the exact prior behavior of requiring `--target` explicitly on every `bv-export` run.

**`cli/bv_ls.py`, `cli/bv_generate.py`, `cli/bv_scribe.py`, `cli/bv_search.py` (modified).** Each gained a `--config-dir DIR` argument (default: `default_config_dir()`, same default `bv-config` itself uses) and now resolves `PATH` via `resolve_archive_path(args.path, args.config_dir)` instead of a bare `Path(args.path)`. `bv-scribe`'s `--raw` mode is deliberately excluded - `_run_raw()`'s own separate raw-path handling was left untouched, since raw mode operates on video files/directories directly, not a camera's archive.

**`cli/bv_export.py` (modified, most involved).** Same `resolve_archive_path()` wiring for `PATH`, plus `--target`'s own resolution logic: if `--target` is given explicitly, it always wins (even over a configured `Output`, and even when both a camera id and `Output` are present) - explicit always overrides configured, no silent divergence. If `--target` is omitted, an `Output` in the resolved camera's config is used automatically. If neither is available, the original error is raised, but with a new detail worth noting: the message mentions `bv-config` specifically when a camera *was* resolved but has no `Output` set (a pointer toward the fix), while a plain literal-path invocation with no matching camera gets the original, unchanged message (no confusing mention of a config command that isn't relevant to that usage).

**Docs.** `docs/CLI.md`: replaced the old "these five commands take a plain path" sentence with two new paragraphs covering camera-id resolution (including the escape-hatch rules and per-command `--config-dir` flag) and `bv-export`'s Output-based `--target` default. `docs/man/bv-config.md`: DESCRIPTION and the numbered wizard-question list updated for the new Output field and its cross-references. `docs/man/bv-ls.md`, `bv-generate.md`, `bv-scribe.md`, `bv-search.md`: SYNOPSIS gained `[--config-dir DIR]`, the `PATH` ARGUMENTS row describes camera-id resolution, and a `--config-dir DIR` OPTIONS row was added under "Selection" (`bv-scribe.md`'s row notes it's not used with `--raw`). `docs/man/bv-export.md`: SYNOPSIS's `--target DIR` became optional (`[--target DIR]`), the "Required" OPTIONS subsection renamed to "Required (usually)" with `--target DIR`'s row explaining the Output-field default and override behavior, plus a new `--config-dir DIR` row.
