**Tests.** `tests/blackvue/core/test_camera_config.py`: round-trip/omitted-when-unset tests for the new `output` field, plus a dedicated block of `resolve_archive_path()` tests - resolves a known camera id, falls back to literal for an unknown bare name, treats every path-shaped form (`./Kirby`, `.\Kirby`, `.`, `..`, an absolute path, a path containing a separator) as literal via `@pytest.mark.parametrize`, propagates a broken camera config's `CameraConfigError` rather than swallowing it, and exposes the resolved config's `output` field. `tests/blackvue/cli/test_bv_config.py`: five existing scripted-wizard tests updated for the new prompt; two new tests for setting Output and for it defaulting from an existing config. `tests/blackvue/cli/test_bv_ls.py`, `test_bv_generate.py`, `test_bv_scribe.py`, `test_bv_search.py`: one new end-to-end test each, saving a real camera config then invoking `main(["Kirby", "--config-dir", ...])` and confirming the resolved target directory's contents show up in output. `tests/blackvue/cli/test_bv_export.py`: four new tests using real ffmpeg-generated fixtures - Output-based `--target` default, the `bv-config`-mentioning vs plain "target required" error message depending on whether a camera resolved, and explicit `--target` overriding a configured Output (confirming the configured directory is never touched in that case).

**Sandbox test-harness fixes along the way (`/tmp/run_tests.py`, `/tmp/shim/tomllib.py`), unrelated to this feature's own logic but required to get a truthful pass/fail signal:** added `pytest.mark.parametrize` support; added `MonkeyPatch.setenv()`/`.delenv()` and fixed `.undo()` for both dict-like and attribute-like targets; rewrote `Capsys` to actually capture stdout/stderr via `io.StringIO()` + `contextlib.redirect_stdout`/`redirect_stderr` - it had previously been a no-op stub always returning empty strings, silently invalidating every capsys-based assertion in the *entire* existing test suite, not just this feature's new tests (found while adding new capsys-dependent tests; worth knowing for any future work that trusted an old "all tests passing" claim involving `capsys`); fixed a resulting ordering bug where the runner's own PASS/FAIL print landed inside the still-active redirected buffer; widened per-test exception handling from `except Exception` to also catch `SystemExit`/other `BaseException`s so one test's uncaught `SystemExit` (from an `argparse` error) fails just that test instead of killing the whole file's run; and turned `/tmp/shim/tomllib.py` from an always-raises stub into an actual minimal TOML parser matching this project's own emitted TOML shape.

**Verification.** Same no-`pytest`-in-sandbox situation as every prior entry; ran every modified/extended test file through the (now-fixed) pytest shim: `test_camera_config.py` 47/47, `test_bv_config.py` 15/15, `test_bv_ls.py`/`test_bv_generate.py`/`test_bv_scribe.py`/`test_bv_search.py` all green for the new tests (a handful of pre-existing, unrelated failures in `test_bv_generate.py`/`test_bv_export.py` around `monkeypatch.setattr("builtins.input", ...)` with a dotted-string target, plus one pre-existing unrelated failure each in `test_bv_ls.py`/`test_bv_export.py`, are a shim limitation and pre-existing test-logic issue respectively - left as-is, out of scope), `test_bv_export.py` 119/123 (4 new tests all passing; the 4 failures are the same pre-existing unrelated ones). `ast.parse()` clean across every touched source file.

## bv-config: suggest a default Target directory for a brand-new camera

Follow-up to the entry above, same day. Asked "What about bv-config" - after two rounds of `AskUserQuestion` narrowing down what that meant (first pass covered whether *other* commands' `--target` flags should gain camera-id resolution, which wasn't it; second pass landed on it), Christer confirmed he meant: bv-config's own **Target** prompt should suggest a default value for a brand-new camera, instead of requiring a full path typed from scratch every time (editing an existing camera was never in question - it already defaults to the saved value).

**`default_target_dir()` (new, `core/camera_config.py`).** `default_target_dir(id_: str) -> Path` returns `~/beyond-video/archive/<id>` - deliberately nested by id (unlike `default_config_dir()`, whose own `<id>.cfg` filename is already namespaced, so the directory itself doesn't need to be), so two cameras' suggested defaults never collide if both are accepted as-is. Purely a suggestion: the wizard's own `[default]` value, always overridable by typing a different path, and this function never creates the directory itself - only `bv-download` actually writes files there, and it already creates its destination as needed.

**`cli/bv_config.py` (modified).** `run_wizard()`'s `default_target` local changed from `str(existing.target) if existing else ""` to `str(existing.target) if existing else str(default_target_dir(id_))` - editing an existing camera is completely unaffected (still shows its saved `target`), only the brand-new-camera case changes, from an empty default (bracket omitted, must type the full path) to a suggested one (bracket shown, Enter accepts it).

**A side effect worth noting, not a regression:** the wizard's existing "Target must not be empty" reprompt guard (`while True: target = prompt(...); if target: break`) is now effectively unreachable through normal use for a brand-new camera, since the suggested default is always a non-empty string and `prompt()`'s `answer or default` logic means a blank Enter can no longer produce an empty `target` anymore in that case. Left the guard in place (still defensive, and still reachable if `default_target_dir()` itself were ever broken) rather than removing it - see the test note below for how it's still exercised.

**Docs.** `docs/man/bv-config.md`: wizard question 2 now notes the pre-filled suggestion and its `~/beyond-video/archive/<ID>` shape.

**Tests.** `tests/blackvue/core/test_camera_config.py`: two new tests for `default_target_dir()` - nests correctly under `Path.home()`, and differs between two different camera ids (the collision-avoidance point). `tests/blackvue/cli/test_bv_config.py`: every scripted-`ask` test that builds a *new* config had its `"Target (download path): "` key updated to include the new suggested-default bracket (via a shared `_MYCAR_TARGET_PROMPT` constant computed from the real `default_target_dir("mycar")`, so the test doesn't hardcode a path that would differ per machine); added `test_run_wizard_target_defaults_to_a_suggested_archive_dir_for_a_new_camera` (blank Enter -> `config.target == default_target_dir("mycar")`); `test_run_wizard_reprompts_on_an_empty_target` rewritten to monkeypatch `default_target_dir` itself to return `""` (a bare string, not a `Path` - `Path("")` stringifies to `"."`, not `""`, so a genuinely empty local `default_target` can only be produced this way now), the one remaining way to reach the "must not be empty" guard now that a real suggestion is always non-empty - keeps that guard's test meaningful rather than leaving it as untested dead code. Tests editing an *existing* config were untouched, since that path's own defaulting behavior didn't change.

**Verification.** Ran both modified test files through the pytest shim: `test_camera_config.py` 49/49 (47 previous + 2 new), `test_bv_config.py` 16/16 (15 previous + 1 new). `ast.parse()` clean on `camera_config.py` and `bv_config.py`. Confirmed no other test file in the repo references the old blank `"Target (download path): "` prompt text (`grep -rn` across `tests/`/`src/`).

## CameraConfig field rename: target -> archive, output -> target

Follow-up to the two entries above, same session. Christer: "That was not what i meant. target gets confusing since it was used for bv.download, i was taking about the target for bv-exports. How we should name them and default it should be a parallel folder." - the prior "suggest a default Target directory" entry had built the wrong feature (bv-config's own download-path default), when he actually meant the bv-export-destination field's default. After a first pass renaming that field's wizard label to "Trips" (matching the project's own `data/archive`/`data/trips` docker-compose convention), a further instruction arrived mid-session: "First of all change target to archive in bv-config and all *.cfg files, then add target for use with trips and other" - superseding the "Trips" label with a full field rename instead: the download-directory field (previously `target`) becomes `archive`, and the bv-export-destination field (previously `output`, briefly relabeled "Trips") becomes `target` - so it now shares its name exactly with `bv-export`'s own `--target` CLI flag, since that field *is* that flag's default value.

**`CameraConfig` (`core/camera_config.py`).** Fields renamed: `target: Path` (required, the download directory) -> `archive: Path`; `output: Path | None = None` (bv-export destination) -> `target: Path | None = None`.

**`default_archive_dir()` (renamed from `default_target_dir()`, same behavior).** `~/beyond-video/archive/<id>` - the brand-new-camera suggestion for the Archive prompt, unchanged from the previous entry apart from the name.

**`default_target_dir()` (reused name, new meaning and signature - previously the function above, now a different function entirely).** `default_target_dir(archive: Path) -> Path` suggests a Target (bv-export destination) parallel to whatever Archive was just answered - swaps the last path component literally named "archive" (case-insensitive) for "trips" (`.../archive/Kirby` -> `.../trips/Kirby`, `/data/archive` -> `/data/trips`, matching the project's own docker-compose/`docs/DEPLOY.md` sibling convention), falling back to `archive.parent / "trips"` when no component is literally named "archive". Computed in `run_wizard()` only after the Archive question is answered (not up front), so the suggestion is always parallel to wherever Archive actually ended up, not just its own default.

**Backward compatibility (`load_camera_config()`).** A config's key names are read either way: `archive`/`target` (current) or `target`/`output` (pre-rename) - disambiguated by which key is actually present (an `archive` key means current names; no `archive` but a `target` key means pre-rename names, where that `target` was the download dir and `output`, if present, was the export destination). Added proactively, not requested explicitly: Christer's real deployed camera configs live outside this repo (on his NAS/PC), so a hard break on the old key names would have silently broken every one of them. `save_camera_config()` always writes the current key names, so an old config self-upgrades to `archive =`/`target =` the next time it's saved (e.g. running `bv-config` on it again) - no separate migration step needed.

**`cli/bv_config.py`.** Wizard prompts renamed: "Target (download path)" -> "Archive (download path)"; "Output (bv-export destination, optional)" (briefly "Trips (bv-export destination, optional)") -> "Target (bv-export destination, optional)". `run_wizard()`'s local variable names and `CameraConfig(...)` construction updated to match.

**`cli/bv_export.py`, `bv_download.py`, `bv_live.py`, `web/app.py`.** Every `config.target` (meaning the download directory) became `config.archive`; `bv-export`'s own `config.output` became `config.target` - now the same name as its own `--target` CLI flag, which is the point (the field *is* that flag's default value). `web/app.py`'s `_find_camera_archive()` docstring rewritten to disambiguate `CameraConfig.archive` (a camera's raw recordings) from `CameraConfig.target` (bv-export's default destination) from bv-web's own separate `app.state.target`/`--target` (the trips directory `trips.py` browses) - three different "target"-adjacent concepts that don't collide in code, only in the word itself, now that two of the three have been renamed.

**Docs.** `docs/man/bv-config.md`: DESCRIPTION and numbered wizard list rewritten for Archive/Target, plus a new "Naming note" paragraph explaining the historical rename and that old `.cfg` files keep working via the backward-compat loader. `docs/man/bv-export.md`: `--target`/`--config-dir` rows reworded for "Target directory" instead of "Output". `docs/CLI.md`: "configured `archive` directory" (was `target`); the `bv-export`/Target-default paragraph reworded for the new field name. `docs/DEPLOY.md`: three spots changed from "Target (download path)"/`target =` to "Archive (download path)"/`archive =`. `docs/WEB_ARCHITECTURE.md`: three spots referencing `CameraConfig.target` (the download dir) updated to `CameraConfig.archive`.

**Tests.** `tests/blackvue/core/test_camera_config.py`: renamed the two `default_target_dir()` tests to `default_archive_dir()`; added four new tests for the reused `default_target_dir()` name's new parallel-folder-swap behavior; every `CameraConfig(...)`/TOML fixture updated from `target=`/`output=` to `archive=`/`target=`; added three new backward-compatibility tests (loading a pre-rename `target =`/`output =` config, and confirming a re-save upgrades it to `archive =`/`target =` with no `output` key left behind). `tests/blackvue/cli/test_bv_config.py`: every scripted-`ask` test rewritten for the new "Archive (download path)"/"Target (bv-export destination, optional)" prompt text (via new `_MYCAR_ARCHIVE_PROMPT`/`_target_prompt_for()` helpers computed from the real `default_archive_dir()`/`default_target_dir()`, so nothing hardcodes a path that would differ per machine), including a rewritten "leave Target unset" test (monkeypatches `default_target_dir` to return `""`, since the real function never does, mirroring the equivalent Archive-side technique from the previous entry). `test_bv_ls.py`, `test_bv_generate.py`, `test_bv_scribe.py`, `test_bv_search.py`, `test_bv_export.py`: every `CameraConfig(target=...)`/`CameraConfig(..., output=...)` call site updated to `archive=`/`target=`.

**Verification.** `ast.parse()` clean across every touched source and test file. Ran every touched test file through the sandbox's pytest shim: `test_camera_config.py` 56/56, `test_bv_config.py` 18/18, `test_bv_ls.py`/`test_bv_generate.py`/`test_bv_scribe.py`/`test_bv_search.py`/`test_bv_export.py` all green for every archive/target-related test (259 passed across the five files combined; the 11 failures present are the same pre-existing, unrelated shim limitations documented in earlier entries - `monkeypatch.setattr("dotted.string", value)`'s two-argument form and `pytest.raises(...).value` aren't supported by the minimal shim, plus one pre-existing asset-grouping-order test in `test_bv_ls.py` - none touch `CameraConfig`/archive/target code, confirmed by reading each failure's traceback).

## bv-search: start/finished timing lines + --trace progress dots

Christer, after finding a recording of an elk via `bv-search --near`: "Print start and stop time and duration for bv-search and maybe a dot now and then showing that the search is active" - a wide-range search over a big archive (the earlier entry recorded 33 seconds for 7.5 months of recordings) prints nothing while it runs, so there's no visible sign of progress or, afterward, of how long it actually took.

**Started/finished timing (`_run()`, `cli/bv_search.py`).** Right after the "give at least one criterion" argument check (so a pure usage error still fails fast with no timing noise), `_run()` prints `bv-search: started HH:MM:SS` and records `time.monotonic()`. The rest of the function's existing body is now wrapped in `try`/`finally`, so `bv-search: finished HH:MM:SS (N.Ns)` prints on every exit path - normal completion, "no recordings in range", a `--place` lookup failure, and a `LexicalTimeParser` argument error that occurs after the initial criteria check all now report a duration, not just the happy path. `datetime.now()` for the wall-clock `HH:MM:SS` (matching `trip_log.py`'s own `step()` formatting), `time.monotonic()` for the elapsed duration (immune to wall-clock adjustments, matching every other elapsed-time measurement already in this codebase, e.g. `trip_export.py`'s debug timing).

**`DotProgress`/`--trace` (new, `cli/bv_search.py`).** Deliberately mirrors `bv-download`'s own `DotProgress` class (`cli/bv_download.py`) - same shape, same "only a heartbeat, not a percentage" reasoning - just counting recordings searched (`tick()`, called once per recording in `_run()`'s main loop) instead of bytes downloaded. `TRACE_INTERVAL_RECORDINGS = 25` (a recording-count interval makes more sense here than a byte interval, given `bv-search` never downloads anything). Prints directly to real stdout via `print()`, not through the injected `say` callable - same choice `bv-download`'s `DotProgress` already made, since a raw `.` heartbeat isn't a structured message worth routing through `say`/`warn`'s injectable seams. `finish()` closes the line with a trailing newline, but only if at least one dot was ever printed (a short/`--trace`-without-many-recordings run doesn't print a stray blank line). Gated behind a new `--trace` flag, off by default - unlike the timing lines above, which always print.

**Tests.** `tests/blackvue/cli/test_bv_search.py`: `--trace` defaults to `False`/parses to `True`; `DotProgress` unit tests mirroring `test_bv_download.py`'s own five (`interval=5`, tests below-interval/one-dot/multiple-dots/finish-with-no-dots/finish-with-a-trailing-newline); `_run()` tests confirming started/finished lines bracket a normal run (and appear in the right order), still both appear when the time parser rejects `--timestamp abc` (an error path inside the `try`), and neither appears for the pure "no criteria given" usage error (returns before the `try` block). Two more confirm `--trace` produces the expected dot count against a small monkeypatched interval (`DotProgress(interval=2)` over 5 fake recordings -> 2 dots) and that omitting `--trace` produces none.

**Docs.** `docs/man/bv-search.md`: SYNOPSIS gained `[--trace]`; new paragraph in DESCRIPTION explaining both the timing lines and `--trace`'s heartbeat; new `--trace` row under General options.

**Verification.** `ast.parse()` clean on both touched files. `test_bv_search.py` 27/27 (16 previous + 11 new) through the sandbox's pytest shim.

## bv-search follow-up: --place resolution before the started/timed section

Christer, right after the timing/--trace feature above: "I would like the --place resolution be printed before the search begins." In the version just shipped, `--place`'s Nominatim lookup and confirmation line happened *inside* the timed block, after the `started` line - correct in terms of ordering relative to the recording-matching loop, but wrong in spirit: a `--place` lookup is a one-off setup step (and, on a cache miss, a real network round-trip), not "the search" itself.

**`_run()` (`cli/bv_search.py`).** The whole `--place` block (`load_or_forward_geocode()` call, its two error paths, and the `bv-search: '<name>' -> lat,lon` confirmation line) moved up to run immediately after archive-path resolution, before `started_at`/`started_monotonic` are captured and before the `bv-search: started HH:MM:SS` line prints. The `try`/`finally` wrapping "finished HH:MM:SS (N.Ns)" now starts right after the `started` line, covering only `LexicalTimeParser` parsing, the recording-selection filter, and the search loop itself - a `--place` lookup failure (not found, network/`MediaToolError`) now returns before `started`/`finished` ever print, matching the idea that a failed setup step never really became "a search run" at all. `LexicalTimeParser` parsing stayed inside the timed section, unchanged - only `--place` moved.

**Tests.** `tests/blackvue/cli/test_bv_search.py`: new `test_run_place_resolution_prints_before_the_started_line`, confirming the `--place` confirmation message's index in the collected `say`/`warn` messages comes before the `started` line's index. All prior tests (`test_run_place_geocodes_then_searches`, `test_run_place_with_road_geometry_matches_along_the_whole_road`, `test_run_place_reports_error_when_not_found`, the started/finished timing tests) still pass unchanged - they check message content via `any(...)`, not exact position, so the reorder didn't require touching them.

**Docs.** `docs/man/bv-search.md`: DESCRIPTION's timing paragraph reworded to explain `--place` resolves first, before the timed section begins.

**Verification.** `ast.parse()` clean. `test_bv_search.py` 28/28 (27 previous + 1 new) through the sandbox pytest shim.

## bv-search: blank line before each matching recording

Christer: "just add a newline before printing recordingid." `_run()`'s match-reporting block now calls `say("")` immediately before `say(str(recording.id))`, so each match starts with a blank separator line - readable when several recordings match in one run (and when `--trace` dots or the started/`--place` lines precede the first result).

**Tests.** `tests/blackvue/cli/test_bv_search.py`: new `test_run_text_match_is_preceded_by_a_blank_line`, confirming the message immediately before a matching recording id is an empty string.

**Verification.** `ast.parse()` clean. `test_bv_search.py` 29/29 (28 previous + 1 new) through the sandbox pytest shim.

## bv-web job runner: bv-scribe and bv-search triggerable from the browser (increment 3)

Christer: "Time to include bv-scribe and bv-search in bv-web, but you can use the camera id just like the others." - the two most recently added CLIs (scene description + text/GPS search) hadn't been wired into the job runner yet, unlike bv-config/bv-gps/bv-download/bv-generate/bv-export/bv-ls before them. "just like the others" meant: resolve a camera id to its archive via `_find_camera_archive()`, the same as every other job-trigger form, rather than exposing a raw path or `--config-dir`/`--raw` escape hatches.

**No CLI refactor needed, unlike every increment before this one.** Every earlier job-runner addition (bv-generate, bv-export, bv-download, bv-ls) first needed its own `_run()` (and, for bv-generate, several of its internal helpers) refactored to accept injectable `say`/`warn`/`ask` before it could be run in-process. `bv_scribe.py`'s and `bv_search.py`'s own `_run()`s already had `say=print, warn=_default_warn` keyword-only parameters from when they were originally built (tasks #608/#621 - both were designed test-first with the job-runner pattern already in mind, unlike the earlier CLIs which predate `bv-web` entirely) - confirmed by reading both files in full before starting, which turned what would have been two more refactor-and-reverify passes into a straight wiring job.

**`JobRunner.start_bv_scribe()`/`start_bv_search()` (new, `web/jobs.py`).** Same shape every other `start_bv_*()` method uses: build a real argv list from keyword parameters, call the target module's own `parse_args(argv)` so its existing validation is the single source of truth, spawn a background thread that calls `_run(args, say=job.append_output, warn=job.append_output)`. `start_bv_scribe()` takes 13 keywords (`camera_id`, `archive_path`, `from_`/`until`/`timestamp`, `task`, `camera`, `model`, `trip_summary`, `cpu`, `overwrite`, `dry_run`, `verbose`, `username`) - a **curated subset** of bv-scribe's own ~40 flags, deliberately not full parity (see below for why). `start_bv_search()` takes 14 keywords (`camera_id`, `archive_path`, `from_`/`until`/`timestamp`, `text`, `asset`, `regex`, `case_sensitive`, `near`, `place`, `radius`, `trace`, `username`) - **full parity** with bv-search's own CLI, since its flag surface is small. `near` is passed through as the raw `"LAT,LON"` text bv-search's own `--near` takes (its `type=_parse_coordinates` handles the split-and-float-parse inside `parse_args()`, same as a real terminal invocation).

**Curated subset vs. full parity, decided per-command again.** Asked directly (bv-scribe's flag surface is large enough that it wasn't obvious which precedent to follow - bv-generate/bv-export/bv-ls's "full parity, grouped by Required/Defaults/Optional", or bv-config/bv-gps/bv-download's "curated, no arbitrary-target escape hatches"), Christer's answer was "curated subset." bv-scribe's ~40 flags are mostly narrow fine-tuning knobs for its zoom-detection sub-pipeline (`--zoom-signs`/`--zoom-frames`/`--zoom-detect-width`/`--zoom-padding`/`--zoom-ocr-width`/`--zoom-debug-dir`/`--zoom-max-new-tokens`/`--zoom-detect-max-new-tokens`/`--zoom-repetition-penalty`/`--zoom-no-repeat-ngram-size`/`--zoom-plate-confidence-check`) plus generic sampling/frame-budget knobs (`--fps`/`--max-frames`/`--max-pixels`/`--resized-width`/`--resized-height`/`--crop-top`/`--crop-bottom`/`--max-new-tokens`/`--repetition-penalty`/`--no-repeat-ngram-size`/`--do-sample`/`--temperature`/`--top-p`/`--top-k`) - real command-line tuning knobs, but the kind of thing that would just clutter a web form with little upside for the common case. `job_new_bv_scribe.html` exposes: camera id (Required); `--from`/`--until`/`--timestamp` (Time range); `--task`/`--camera`/`--model` (Defaults); `--trip-summary`/`--cpu`/`--overwrite`/`--dry-run`/`--verbose` as plain checkboxes (Optional). Everything else keeps its own CLI default - there's no way to reach the zoom-tuning/sampling flags from the browser at all, only from the command line. bv-search, by contrast, gets full parity like bv-generate/bv-export/bv-ls: `job_new_bv_search.html` exposes every flag (`--text`/`--asset`/`--regex`/`--case-sensitive`, `--near`/`--place`/`--radius`, `--trace`) grouped the same Required/Time range/Text search/GPS proximity search/Optional way the other full-parity forms are.

**`/jobs/bv-scribe`, `/jobs/bv-search` routes (new, `app.py`).** Same GET-form/POST-submit pair every other job trigger uses, resolving `id` to an archive path via `_find_camera_archive()`. bv-search's POST route does one thing none of the curated-subset routes need: a plain pre-check (not `BvExportArgError`'s `parse_args()`-`SystemExit`-catching machinery - bv-search only has a handful of conditions, the same "plain pre-check" scale bv-ls's two numeric fields already used) that at least one of text/near/place was given, mirroring `bv_search._run()`'s own runtime check but surfaced as a form re-render with a friendly message instead of a job that starts and immediately fails; near/place are also checked mutually exclusive before ever building a job. A `--near` value is validated through `bv_search._parse_coordinates()` - the identical helper the CLI's own `--near` `type=` already uses - via a function-scoped `from ..cli.bv_search import _parse_coordinates` import inside the route, since `app.py` otherwise never imports a `cli.*` module directly at its own module scope (that's `jobs.py`'s job, always done lazily inside each `start_bv_*` method) - caught this myself before running anything, by checking that app.py had zero `from ..cli import ...` statements anywhere before adding the first one.

**Templates + nav.** `job_new_bv_scribe.html`/`job_new_bv_search.html` follow the established `option-group`/`field-label`/`help-tip`/`checkbox-row` conventions from `job_new_bv_generate.html` (rendered with a fake Jinja2 environment/request to confirm both templates - and both their error and empty-camera-list paths - render without exceptions before touching `base.html`). Two new nav tabs ("Describe scenes", "Search") added to `base.html`'s owner-only tab list, after "List recordings".

**Tests.** `tests/blackvue/web/test_jobs.py`: 13 new tests for `start_bv_scribe()`/`start_bv_search()`, mirroring the existing `_ls_kwargs()`/`test_start_bv_ls_*` shape - say/warn wiring, every curated flag reaching `parsed_args` for bv-scribe, text/asset/regex/case-sensitive/near/place/radius/trace all reaching `parsed_args` for bv-search, and a job-fails-on-nonzero-exit test for each. No route-level tests were added - `app.py`'s routes have never had `TestClient`-based tests in this project (confirmed: no `test_app.py` exists, and no other job-trigger route is tested that way either), so this follows the existing coverage pattern rather than introducing a new one.

**Verification.** `ast.parse()` clean on `jobs.py`, `app.py`, and the updated `test_jobs.py`. Both new templates render clean (including error and empty-camera-list paths) via a standalone Jinja2 environment, and `base.html`'s nav renders with both new tab links present. Full `test_jobs.py` run through the sandbox's pytest shim (a fake `tomllib` stub reused from earlier sessions, since this sandbox's Python 3.10 lacks the 3.11+ stdlib module `core/camera_config.py` imports - see many earlier entries for this standing limitation): 63 passed, 1 failed - the failure (`test_start_bv_export_raises_bv_export_arg_error_on_bad_value`) is a pre-existing, unrelated shim limitation (`pytest.raises(...).value` isn't supported by the minimal shim) already present before this session's changes, confirmed by checking it's untouched in the diff.

**Docs.** `docs/WEB_ARCHITECTURE.md`: the Jobs bullet, the "Job runner" section's opening paragraph and its `say`/`warn`-refactor paragraph, the camera-path-resolution sentence, the curated-vs-parity paragraph (new paragraph explaining bv-scribe's curated choice and bv-search's full parity), the job-routes list, and the `Structure` section's `jobs.py`/`templates/` entries all updated. `app.py`'s own module docstring updated to name bv-ls/bv-scribe/bv-search alongside the commands it already listed.

## bv-scribe web form correction: progressive disclosure, not a curated subset

Christer, right after the increment above shipped: "i must have misunderstood Curated subset, i wanted it hidden like in bv-export." The "curated subset" version had genuinely left bv-scribe's zoom-detection/sampling flags off the form entirely - CLI-only, no way to reach them from the browser at all. What he'd actually meant was `bv-export`'s own progressive-disclosure pattern (see "Progressive disclosure for the bv-export web form" above): every flag still gets a real field, just collapsed behind a `<details>`/`<summary>` section by default rather than omitted.

**`JobRunner.start_bv_scribe()` (`web/jobs.py`), rewritten to full parity.** Grew from 13 keywords to 38 - every one of bv-scribe's flags now gets its own parameter, the same "build argv, call the target module's own `parse_args()`" shape every other `start_bv_*()` uses. Every newly-added numeric field (`fps`, `max_frames`, `max_pixels`, `resized_width`, `resized_height`, `crop_top`, `crop_bottom`, `max_new_tokens`, `repetition_penalty`, `no_repeat_ngram_size`, `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`, `zoom_frames`, `zoom_detect_width`, `zoom_padding`, `zoom_ocr_width`, `zoom_max_new_tokens`, `zoom_detect_max_new_tokens`, `zoom_repetition_penalty`, `zoom_no_repeat_ngram_size`, `trip_summary_max_new_tokens`) follows the same `None`-means-omit-the-flag convention `start_bv_export()`'s own optional numeric fields already established, so bv-scribe's `parse_args()` remains the single source of truth for defaults/validation. `do_sample` is a plain bool (append `--do-sample` only when `True`, matching `--trip-summary`'s existing treatment); `zoom_signs`/`zoom_plate_confidence_check` default `True` and only append a `--no-...` flag when explicitly turned off - the exact "default-true-omits-the-negative-flag" pattern `start_bv_ls()`'s own `duration` parameter already uses. `--raw`/`--config-dir` stay excluded (an escape hatch for non-archive footage with no camera id, unrelated to this correction), and `--zoom-debug-dir` is deliberately still excluded too - it writes to an arbitrary server filesystem path, the same reason `bv-export`'s own `--target` was never a form field.

**`job_new_bv_scribe.html`, rewritten with three collapsible `<details>` sections.** Core (camera id, time range, task/camera/model, the plain on/off checkboxes) stays always-visible, ~11 fields, matching the "8-10 controls, everything else behind Advanced" shape Christer described for `bv-export`. "Advanced sampling & model" holds the frame-sampling/generation-tuning knobs; "Advanced zoom detection" holds the zoom sub-pipeline; "Advanced trip summary" holds just `--trip-summary-max-new-tokens` and auto-opens the moment "Also write a trip summary" is checked - the identical one-directional checkbox-opens-details script `job_new_bv_export.html` already uses (unchecking never force-closes a section, so nothing a user already typed gets hidden). Each numeric `<input>` shows the CLI's own default as its `placeholder`, matching `job_new_bv_export.html`'s own convention for optional numeric fields.

**`new_bv_scribe_submit()` route (`web/app.py`), rewritten to match.** Every advanced field arrives as an optional text `Form("")`, cleaned to `str | None` via the same `_clean()` helper `new_bv_export_submit()` already defined for its own large numeric-field surface, then passed straight through - `start_bv_scribe()` just `str()`s whatever isn't `None` into argv, so real parsing/range-checking happens exactly once, inside `bv_scribe.parse_args()` itself. `zoom_signs`/`zoom_plate_confidence_check` are collected as inverted `no_zoom_signs`/`no_zoom_plate_confidence_check` checkboxes (unchecked by default, `not no_zoom_signs` passed through) - the same inverted-checkbox shape `no_duration` already uses on the bv-ls/bv-export forms, simpler HTML than pre-checking a box to represent a default-True flag.

**Tests.** `tests/blackvue/web/test_jobs.py`: `_scribe_kwargs()` rewritten for the 38-parameter signature (every advanced field defaults to `None`/`True`/`False` matching bv-scribe's own CLI defaults). `test_start_bv_scribe_curated_flags_reach_parsed_args` renamed to `test_start_bv_scribe_core_flags_reach_parsed_args` (same assertions, new name matching what it actually tests now). Three new tests: `test_start_bv_scribe_advanced_sampling_flags_reach_parsed_args` (13 sampling/model fields), `test_start_bv_scribe_advanced_zoom_flags_reach_parsed_args` (10 zoom fields, including `zoom_signs=False`/`zoom_plate_confidence_check=False` producing the right `--no-...` flags), `test_start_bv_scribe_trip_summary_max_new_tokens_reaches_parsed_args`. `test_start_bv_scribe_defaults_reach_parsed_args` extended to also assert `args.fps == 1.0`/`args.zoom_signs is True`/`args.trip_summary_max_new_tokens == 768` - confirming the `None`-means-omit convention really does leave `parse_args()`'s own defaults untouched.

**Verification.** `ast.parse()` clean on `jobs.py`, `app.py`, `test_jobs.py`. `job_new_bv_scribe.html` re-rendered through a standalone `jinja2.Environment` (default context, error context, empty-camera-list context) with no exceptions, and its three `<details>`/`</details>` pairs confirmed balanced by line-numbered `grep` (an earlier naive substring count came back 6-vs-3 and looked like a bug at first - traced to `base.html`'s own CSS comments mentioning "`<details>`" as plain text, not malformed markup; the real tag count in the template itself is 3-and-3). Full `test_jobs.py` run through the sandbox's pytest shim: 66 passed, 1 failed - the same single pre-existing, unrelated `pytest.raises(...).value` shim limitation every other entry in this file already documents, confirmed untouched by this change.

**Docs.** `docs/WEB_ARCHITECTURE.md`'s curated-vs-parity paragraph rewritten to describe the actual final shape: bv-scribe gets full parity behind progressive disclosure (not a curated subset), bv-search stays flat full parity (its surface was always small enough not to need disclosure), and the correction itself is called out explicitly so a future reader doesn't wonder why the wording changed mid-document.

## bv-scribe/bv-search web forms: light-theme fix + bv-search recording-id links

Christer: "both bv-scribe och bvsearch needs help for light theme. Could the output from bv-search showingrecordingid be a link to the video?" Two separate fixes.

**Light theme.** Investigated by static CSS reading (this sandbox has no `playwright`/chromium, so no real browser render is possible here - same standing limitation as every earlier light-theme fix in this file). Found two real gaps, one per page:

`base.html`'s shared themed-input selector (`input[type="text"], input[type="password"], select`) never included `input[type="number"]` - so every number field on `job_new_bv_scribe.html`'s three Advanced sections (21 fields: fps, max_frames, temperature, the zoom-detection knobs, etc.) fell back to the browser's raw unstyled default box instead of `var(--input-bg)`/`var(--input-border)`. Fixed by adding `input[type="number"]` to that selector. `job_new_bv_search.html` has no number fields (all text/checkbox), so this alone didn't touch it - a follow-up question narrowed Christer's actual bv-search complaint down to "labels checkboxes."

That pointed at a second, bigger gap shared by both pages: unlike `trip_detail.html`/the archive browser pages (which wrap their content in `.content-panel`, a solid `var(--panel-bg)` surface), neither `job_new_bv_scribe.html` nor `job_new_bv_search.html` ever did - their `<form>`s (including every `.option-group`'s `<h3>`/labels/checkboxes) sat directly on the bare page background, relying only on the thin `.page-tint` wash (see base.html's own comment: that wash was tuned assuming "panels/tables/etc. still sit on their own solid `--panel-bg` regardless" - true everywhere else, but never true for these two forms). In light theme, over a busy section of the background photo, that's exactly the "labels/checkboxes hard to read" Christer described. Fixed by wrapping both forms' `<form>...</form>` in a `<div class="content-panel">`, the same treatment `trip_detail.html` already uses - no CSS changes needed, `.content-panel` already existed.

**bv-search recording-id links.** `cli/bv_search.py`'s `_run()` prints each match as a bare, unindented `say(str(recording.id))` line (format `YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_<kind>`, e.g. `20260810_120000_N` - see `domain/recording.py`'s `kind` property) sandwiched between a blank separator line and the match's own indented detail lines. `job_detail.html`'s `<pre class="job-output">` had one existing special case (`"> "`-prefixed lines get wrapped for echoed `ask()` input) and nothing else - every other line rendered as plain escaped text.

Added a second case, scoped tightly to bv-search jobs only so no other command's output is ever touched: a new `RECORDING_ID_RE = re.compile(r"^\d{8}_\d{6}_[A-Za-z]$")` in `app.py`, exposed to Jinja as a global `is_recording_id(line)` (same pattern `capitalize_first` already used as a filter). The `/jobs/{job_id}` route computes `camera_id` from `job.command` - `None` for every job type except bv-search, where `start_bv_search()` already sets `job.command = f"bv-search {camera_id}"` (no dedicated `Job.camera_id` field exists, and adding one felt like more churn than reading the one value already embedded in the command string bv-search's job type alone guarantees the shape of). `job_detail.html`'s output loop gained `{% elif camera_id and is_recording_id(line) %}<a href="/archive/{{ camera_id }}/{{ line }}">{{ line }}</a>` between the existing echo case and the plain-text fallback - `camera_id` being `None` for every other job type means a bv-ls listing or any other command's output that happens to contain a recording-id-shaped string never gets linked, only bv-search's own match lines do. Links render themed (`a { color: var(--link) }` is already global in base.html), so no separate light-theme concern here.

## bv-search zoom/crop: experimental geometry-based crop toward --near/--place matches

Christer, after a back-and-forth about what a previously-noted idea (task #642, "zoom/crop toward bv-search --near matches so distant subjects are visible") actually meant: "let's try your zoom crop thing, we can always delete it later. As a Max member i have both the time and credits to try it out." Scoped over three quick questions: render both a thumbnail and a clip (not one or the other), run automatically on every `--near`/`--place` match (no opt-in flag), and use a documented default field-of-view (136 degrees, confirmed both by web search and by Christer directly for his own DR900S-2CH) with a `--fov` override rather than asking him to supply it every time.

**The idea.** A `--near`/`--place` match only confirms the car's GPS track came within `--radius` of a target coordinate - the target itself might be a speck off to one side of the wide (136-degree) dashcam frame, easy to miss on playback. Rather than object detection, this uses geometry already on hand: at the matching GPS fix, the target's compass bearing from the car's own position is compared against the car's own heading (GPS course-over-ground) to get a relative bearing (how far left/right of straight-ahead), which maps onto the camera's horizontal FOV to pick a crop position; distance to the target picks how tight the crop is. Explicitly a heuristic, not a calibrated lens model - BlackVue doesn't publish per-model distortion data, so this assumes a simple rectilinear (pinhole) mapping rather than correcting for real fisheye-like barrel distortion, especially near the wide edges. Documented as such in the new module's own docstring and in `docs/man/bv-search.md`'s new "ZOOM/CROP" section, so a future reader doesn't mistake it for pixel-precise framing.

**New module: `blackvue/search_zoom.py`.** `_bearing_degrees()`/`_relative_bearing_degrees()` - standard great-circle forward-azimuth and signed-relative-bearing math (verified by hand: due east from the same point is bearing 90, due south is 180, etc.). `compute_crop_box()` returns `None` (rather than a box) when the crop can't be reasonably placed: no heading, speed under `MIN_SPEED_FOR_HEADING_KMH` (5 km/h - below that, NMEA course-over-ground is noise, not a real heading), or the target's relative bearing falls outside `fov_degrees/2` entirely (behind or to the side, out of shot no matter the crop). Crop width scales inversely with distance (`_REFERENCE_DISTANCE_METERS`/`_REFERENCE_CROP_FRACTION`, clamped to `_MIN_CROP_FRACTION`/`_MAX_CROP_FRACTION`) - closer targets need less zoom. `CropBox.width_fraction`/`height_fraction` are always kept equal, which is what preserves the source frame's own aspect ratio in the crop (not a separate calculation - a crop that's X% of both dimensions is automatically the same aspect ratio as the frame it's cut from). `render_zoom_thumbnail()`/`render_zoom_clip()` follow the exact same ffprobe/ffmpeg subprocess pattern already established in `generate/media.py`/`export/stitch.py`'s own private helpers (`_video_dimensions()` duplicated here rather than imported, matching this codebase's existing convention of small ffmpeg helpers staying module-private rather than shared - see `search.py`'s own `_EARTH_RADIUS_METERS` comment for the same reasoning) - crop via ffmpeg's `crop` filter, scaled back up to the source's own resolution so it reads as "zoomed in" rather than just smaller; the clip drops audio (`-an`) since this is a quick directional preview, not a polished export. `render_zoom_outputs()` renders both into `<recording-id>_zoom.jpg`/`<recording-id>_zoom.mp4`, right next to the recording's own front video.

**Wired into `cli/bv_search.py`.** New `--fov DEGREES` flag (default `search_zoom.DEFAULT_HORIZONTAL_FOV_DEGREES`). Inside `_run()`'s per-recording loop, right after `_report_geo_match()`: if the recording has no `Asset.FRONT`, say `zoom: skipped (no front video for this recording)`; otherwise call `compute_crop_box()` using the matching fix's own lat/lon/course/speed as the car's state and the search `target` tuple as the target coordinate - `None` back means say `zoom: skipped (target out of frame, or no reliable heading at this fix)`; otherwise call `render_zoom_outputs()` wrapped in `try/except MediaToolError` (`warn()` + `had_error = True` on failure, same pattern `--text`'s own per-recording `MediaToolError` handling already uses) so one recording's ffmpeg failure doesn't drop the match's own GPS/text reporting or abort the whole search - it just downgrades exit status to `EXIT_HAD_ERRORS` the same way any other per-recording error already does. Known limitation, not yet addressed: for a `--place` match that resolved to a road/area (line geometry, not a point), the crop still bears toward Nominatim's single representative point rather than the actual nearest point along the line the distance was measured to - a rougher approximation there than for a plain coordinate `--near` match.

**Tests.** `tests/blackvue/test_search_zoom.py` (new): bearing/relative-bearing math, every `compute_crop_box()` None-case (no heading, too slow, behind the car), left/right/straight-ahead crop positioning, width-fraction clamping and close-vs-far ordering, aspect-ratio preservation, FOV-override behavior, `_crop_filter()`'s pixel-bounds-clamping and even-dimension guarantees, and real-ffmpeg render tests (`render_zoom_thumbnail`/`render_zoom_clip`/`render_zoom_outputs`) using the same `lavfi testsrc` pattern `test_export_media.py` already established for exercising real ffmpeg rather than mocking `subprocess`. `tests/blackvue/cli/test_bv_search.py`: `--fov` default/override parsing, plus four new `_run()`-level tests covering the no-front-video skip, a real successful render (asserting the reported thumbnail/clip paths actually exist on disk), the out-of-frame skip, and the `MediaToolError`-keeps-the-match-but-downgrades-exit-status path.

**Verification.** This sandbox still has no real `pytest`, but does have a real `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` on `PATH` (confirmed the CI workflow installs it too), so every geometry function and every render function in `search_zoom.py`, plus all five new `bv_search.py`-level scenarios, were run directly as plain Python (not through a test framework) against real `ffmpeg`-generated `lavfi testsrc` videos and asserted by hand - all passed, including the exact distance/bearing numbers matching what the geometry functions themselves computed. `ast.parse()` clean on `search_zoom.py`, `cli/bv_search.py`, and both new/modified test files. Confirmed the existing `test_run_near_reports_geo_match`/`test_run_combines_text_and_near_with_and_semantics`/`test_run_place_geocodes_then_searches`/`test_run_place_with_road_geometry_matches_along_the_whole_road` tests (none of which register `Asset.FRONT` on their fake recordings) still pass unchanged - they now also emit a `zoom: skipped (no front video...)` line, which none of their assertions check for or are broken by.

**Not done, deliberately out of scope for this pass:** no `bv-web` wiring (the job-trigger form doesn't expose `--fov` or show the rendered thumbnail/clip anywhere) - this is a CLI-only experimental feature for now, Christer's own framing ("we can always delete it later") suggesting it should prove itself before investing in a web UI for it.

**Root cause.** bv-scribe's scene-description feature needs the `scene` optional-dependencies group (`transformers`, `accelerate`, `qwen-vl-utils[decord]`, from `pyproject.toml`). Task #653/#656 wired bv-scribe into bv-web's job runner - which, per `Dockerfile`'s own header comment, executes *inside the bv-web container itself*, not on Christer's PC. But `Dockerfile`'s `pip install` line was never updated to include `scene` when that wiring landed - it still only installed `.[web,speech,translate]`. Same gap in `Dockerfile.cli` (`.[speech,translate]`, missing `scene`), which matters too since that image's own header comment lists `bv-generate` (including `--describe-scene`) among the commands it runs.

**Fix.** `Dockerfile`: `.[web,speech,translate]` -> `.[web,speech,translate,scene]`. `Dockerfile.cli`: `.[speech,translate]` -> `.[speech,translate,scene]`. Updated both files' header comments to mention the scene/qwen-vl-utils addition, and `docs/DEPLOY.md`'s two toolchain-description passages (the "build is slow" note near step 4, and the three-ways-to-run-bv-generate/bv-export list near step 7) to mention bv-scribe and the scene extra alongside the existing speech/translate/torch mentions.

**Not re-verified end-to-end** - this sandbox has no network access to actually `pip install .[scene]` (qwen-vl-utils/transformers/accelerate aren't installed here), so the fix is a straightforward extras-list correction confirmed by reading `pyproject.toml`'s `scene` group and matching it against the exact `ModuleNotFoundError` Christer reported, not a live rebuild-and-test. Once pulled, Christer needs to `sudo docker-compose build bv-web` (and `bv-cli` if he wants `--describe-scene` there too) on the NAS to pick up the new extra - a plain restart won't do it, the image itself has to rebuild.

## Show the equivalent bv-* CLI command on every bv-web job page

Christer, while a large bv-scribe job ran on bv-web: "Is it possible for every bv-* command to print out how its called in bv-web, so i can replicate it in pwsh or bash later?"

**Design.** Every `JobRunner.start_bv_*()` method already builds a real `argv` list to call the target CLI's own `parse_args()` - that same argv (rebuilt with the camera id in place of the resolved server-side archive path, see below) becomes `Job.replicate_command`, a new field shown on `job_detail.html` in a small code box with a "Copy" button (`navigator.clipboard.writeText()`, falling back to a `window.prompt()` if unavailable - the same light-touch inline-`<script>` precedent `job_new_bv_export.html`'s own progressive-disclosure auto-reveal already established, not a break from "no JS" - that phrase in this doc's own job-runner section refers only to the polling/refresh mechanism, not every script in the app).

**The archive_path -> camera_id substitution.** `start_bv_ls()`/`start_bv_generate()`/`start_bv_export()`/`start_bv_scribe()`/`start_bv_search()` all build their real `argv[0]` from the *resolved* `archive_path` (e.g. `/data/archive/Kirby` inside the container) rather than the plain camera id - correct for actually running the job, useless for replicating it on a different machine, since that path is container-internal. The replicate command swaps in `camera_id` instead (`[camera_id, *argv[1:]]`) - the same id a terminal invocation would use directly, and the same one `bv-config` on any other machine (Christer's NAS+PC dual setup) would resolve fresh. `bv-config`/`bv-gps`/`bv-download` need no substitution - their own positional argument already *is* the camera id, not a resolved path.

**Quoting.** `_quote_for_replicate()` wraps a value in double quotes only when it's empty or contains whitespace (e.g. `--place "Slussen, Stockholm"`), escaping an embedded double quote with a backslash. Deliberately not `shlex.quote()` - its single-quote style is bash-only and would confuse someone pasting the same line into PowerShell. This is "good enough for the realistic values these arguments take," not a fully correct dual-shell quoting implementation - explicitly documented as such in both `Job.replicate_command`'s own docstring and `docs/WEB_ARCHITECTURE.md`.

**What's included.** Flags a job-trigger method always forces on regardless of the form (e.g. `bv-download`'s own `--yes`, added because its `confirm()` prompt has no safe way to reach this job runner's `ask()`) are included - the replicate command shows what actually ran, not a hypothetical minimal invocation.

**Implementation.** Added `_quote_for_replicate()`/`_replicate_command_line()` module-level helpers to `web/jobs.py`, a `replicate_command: str = ""` field to `Job`, and a `replicate_command` parameter (defaulting to `""` so the existing low-level `_new_job()` test call sites didn't need updating) threaded through all 8 `start_bv_*()` methods. `job_detail.html` renders the box only when `job.replicate_command` is truthy. `base.html` got matching `.replicate-command`/`.copy-button` CSS.

**Tests.** New `test_quote_for_replicate_*`/`test_replicate_command_line_*` unit tests, plus a `job.replicate_command` assertion added to each command's existing "wires say/warn into run" test and to the `--place`-with-a-space case (asserting the quoted form). All hand-verified against the real `JobRunner`/CLI `parse_args()` code (no pytest in this sandbox) by monkeypatching each target module's `_run()` directly and reading back `job.replicate_command` - caught two mistakes this way before they reached the committed test file: `--stitch-layout auto` is always appended (its own CLI default is a truthy string, not gated on `--stitch`), and `--asset` is built before `--place` in `start_bv_search()`'s own argv order, not after.

**Verification.** `job_detail.html`/`base.html` rendered end-to-end via a real `jinja2.Environment` with a fake `Request`/`Job`/`user`, both with and without a `replicate_command` set - confirmed the copy box only appears when there's something to show. `ast.parse()` clean on `jobs.py` and the test file.

## Document CUDA-index torch install for the scene extra (root cause of the bv-scribe "hung on video 1" report)

Christer reported a bv-scribe job via bv-web (model `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct`, 902 recordings) showing zero output for 20+ minutes - not even the first `[1/902] <recording_id>` label line bv-scribe normally prints before any model work starts.

**Diagnosis.** Walked through it live with Christer rather than guessing: confirmed the label line actually was printing (so the hang was inside `describe_scene()`, not before it), then confirmed `nvidia-smi` showed no python/torch process on his RTX 5090 despite the job "running." `python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available())"` in `beyond-video\.venv` (the exact venv both `bv-web` and `bv-scribe` use, confirmed via `where.exe bv-scribe`) printed `False` - torch was a CPU-only build. An 8B-parameter vision-language model on CPU can look completely hung for many minutes on just the first recording.

The apparent contradiction - Christer said running scene description directly via `python scene_scribe.py` (a separate standalone prototype script/project, `C:\My_git\scene-scribe`, predating bv-scribe - see task #604) was fast - turned out to be the actual clue, not a contradiction. `scene-scribe`'s own `README.md` documents installing `torch`/`torchvision` from PyTorch's CUDA 12.8 wheel index *before* anything else, specifically because Christer's GPU (RTX 5090, Blackwell/sm_120) isn't supported by older CUDA wheel builds - which silently fall back to CPU instead of erroring. `scene-scribe` has its own separate venv where that step was actually done; `beyond-video`'s `pyproject.toml`/README never documented it for the `scene` extra, so `pip install -e ".[scene]"` there pulled torch from PyPI's default index (CPU-only) into `beyond-video\.venv`. Same physical GPU, two venvs, only one configured correctly.

**Fix applied and confirmed working** (Christer reinstalled in `beyond-video\.venv` and re-ran the check - now prints `True`):
```
pip install torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128
pip install -e ".[scene]"
```

**Docs.** Added a "if you have an NVIDIA GPU" callout to `README.md`'s Install section with the same two-step command, a pointer to PyTorch's own "Get Started" page for the current `cuXXX` tag (this changes over time/by GPU generation), and an explicit note that CPU inference on an 8B model can look indistinguishable from "stuck" for many minutes. Expanded `docs/man/bv-scribe.md`'s existing (vague) "install torch separately, see PyTorch's Get Started page" line into the same concrete two-command block plus the same CPU-slowness warning, since `pyproject.toml`'s `scene` extra comment already points there for CUDA-build instructions.

**Not changed:** `pyproject.toml` itself - its existing comment above the `scene` group already said "install torch separately first per its own instructions (CUDA build selection - see docs/man/bv-scribe.md)," which now resolves to the concrete command. No code change needed, this was purely a documentation gap.

## Fix _interactive() false positive hanging bv-web jobs on input()

Christer's bv-scribe web job looked hung: job page stuck showing "Running" with zero output, and GPU memory never rose (confirmed via nvidia-smi) - even though the exact same command had just completed in 37 seconds run directly in pwsh, in the same venv, with CUDA torch already confirmed working (see "Document CUDA-index torch install for the scene extra"). So this wasn't a CUDA/model problem at all.

**Root cause.** `_should_write()` in both `bv_scribe.py` and `bv_generate.py` decides whether to (re)generate an already-existing output file. When not `--overwrite` and not `--dry-run`, it checks `_interactive()` (`sys.stdin.isatty() and sys.stdout.isatty()`) and, if true, calls Python's raw `input("... Overwrite? [y/N] ")` directly - not the `ask()` callable bv-web's job runner injects for exactly this kind of prompt elsewhere (bv-config's wizard). `sys.stdin`/`sys.stdout` are process-wide, not per-thread: Christer runs `bv-web serve z:/data/trips` directly in an interactive pwsh window rather than as a detached service, so the whole process has a real terminal attached, and `_interactive()` returned `True` even inside bv-web's background job thread. `input()` then blocked that thread forever, waiting for a keypress on the *server's own console* (which nobody was watching for this) - its prompt text was also written there, never into the job's output box. Zero web output, no error, job stuck "Running" indefinitely - exactly Christer's symptoms.

Confirmed via elimination, not guesswork: a `bv-ls` job against the same camera (`Kirby_2019`) via bv-web returned instantly with a normal listing, ruling out archive/config-path resolution. Reading `_run_scene_pass()`/`_describe_recording()` showed no other candidate before the model-loading call. `_scene_kwargs()` is pure dict-building. That left `_should_write()`'s `_interactive()`/`input()` branch as the only remaining place execution could silently stall - and it explained why this only started happening *after* Christer's successful direct-pwsh run: that run had already written the `.scene.txt`/`.rear.scene.txt` files for those recordings, so re-running the same job via bv-web hit the "file already exists" branch for the first time.

**Fix.** `_interactive()` in both files now also requires `threading.current_thread() is threading.main_thread()`. A genuine direct CLI invocation is always on the main thread, so its interactive-prompt behavior is unchanged. Every bv-web job (always a background `threading.Thread`, per `JobRunner._spawn()`) now always takes the safe branch instead: `warn()`-and-skip, which routes through `say`/`warn` into the job's own output box like everything else, and returns quickly instead of hanging.

**Not done:** did not thread a real `ask()` callable through `_should_write()` so bv-web could offer an interactive "overwrite?" prompt in the web UI itself (the way bv-config's wizard does) - out of scope for this fix, which is specifically about eliminating the hang. Skipping with a warning on an already-described recording is the correct default behavior anyway (`--overwrite` exists for the rare case someone wants to redo it).

**Tests.** Added `test_interactive_requires_the_main_thread` to both `test_bv_scribe.py` and `test_bv_generate.py` - monkeypatches `sys.stdin`/`sys.stdout` with a fake always-tty object, confirms `_interactive()` is `True` on the main thread and `False` when checked from inside a real `threading.Thread`. Manually verified in the sandbox (no pytest available) by importing both modules directly and running the same check inline - printed `main_thread=True background_thread=False` for both `bv_scribe` and `bv_generate`, confirming the fix works as intended. `ast.parse()` clean on all four changed files.
