## Make bv-scribe skip Parking recordings + survive per-file failures

Christer's 902-recording Kirby_2019 bv-scribe web job died partway through with `Error: Error reading \\192.168.140.63\Dashcam\files\2019\20190128_164930_PF.mp4...` - the `Error:` prefix is `JobRunner._spawn()`'s own wrapping, confirming the exception escaped all the way up and killed the entire job, not just that one recording. His response: Parking-mode recordings "shouldn't even be considered for bv-scribe," and separately, "we need some kind of log to see what files failed, or just list it in the end for now."

**Root cause of the unwrapped exception.** `describe_scene()` in `src/blackvue/generate/scene.py` only wrapped the model-inference calls (`processor(...)`, `model.generate(...)`) in `try/except Exception -> MediaToolError`. The earlier video-reading step - `_fetch_vision_inputs()` (which calls `qwen_vl_utils.process_vision_info()`, which reads/decodes the actual video via decord/ffmpeg) - sat *outside* that try block. A read failure there (a flaky network path, a corrupt file - exactly what a large Parking-mode timelapse over `\\192.168.140.63\Dashcam\...` risks) raised a raw, unwrapped exception straight out of `describe_scene()`. `_run_scene_pass()` in `bv_scribe.py` only ever caught `MediaToolError` from that call, so the raw exception propagated through `_describe_recording()`, `_run()`'s loop, and finally hit `JobRunner._spawn()`'s outer catch-all - which correctly does its job (report the error, don't crash the process) but has no way to know this was "one recording out of 902," not the whole run.

**Fix, three parts:**

1. **`scene.py`:** widened the `try/except Exception` in `describe_scene()` to also cover `_fetch_vision_inputs()`/`_crop_top_bottom()` - any failure reading/decoding the video now becomes a normal `MediaToolError` like every other `describe_scene()` failure, which callers already know how to handle per-recording.

2. **`bv_scribe.py`'s `_run()`:** Parking-mode recordings (`recording.id.is_parking`) are now filtered out of the selection entirely, before the loop even starts - a skip-count message is printed when any are excluded ("skipping N parking-mode recording(s) - not considered for scene description"). Deliberately different from `bv-generate --describe-scene`, which still documents running on Parking recordings ("they're still video, just no audio") - that design choice is untouched; this exclusion is `bv-scribe`-specific, per Christer's own words. `--raw` mode is unaffected (no recording-id-based filtering there at all - still the escape hatch if someone genuinely wants a parking clip described).

3. **`bv_scribe.py`'s `_run()` loop:** wrapped the per-recording `_describe_recording()` call in its own `try/except Exception`, matching the "skip unreadable/corrupted sources instead of failing the whole asset" precedent already established in `bv-export`'s concat step (task #304-307). A failing recording is now recorded into a `failures: list[tuple[str, str]]`, warned about immediately (`bv-scribe: [i/N] recording_id: FAILED - {exc}`), and the loop continues. At the end of the run, if `failures` is non-empty, a summary is printed: `bv-scribe: N recording(s) failed:` followed by one `  recording_id: message` line per failure - Christer's "just list it in the end for now" ask, no persistent log file, just visible in the job's/terminal's own output.

**Tests.** `test_run_skips_parking_recordings_entirely` (a Parking + a Normal recording in the fake archive - confirms only the Normal one gets described, the Parking one's `.scene.txt` never gets written, and the skip-count message appears). `test_run_survives_one_recordings_failure_and_reports_it` (first recording's fake `describe_scene()` raises `OSError`, second succeeds - confirms both were attempted, the second's `.scene.txt` was written, the first's wasn't, exit code is `EXIT_HAD_ERRORS`, and the failure summary contains both the count and the specific recording id + message). Manually run in the sandbox (no pytest available) by importing `bv_scribe` directly and driving `_run()` with fake `Archive`/`describe_scene` - both passed, plus the two pre-existing `_run()` tests re-verified unaffected. `ast.parse()` clean on both changed source files.

**Not done:** no persistent log file - Christer explicitly said the end-of-run listing is enough "for now." Revisit if a real need for a durable failure log across runs comes up later.

## Note: persistent command history + output logfile for bv-web jobs (future improvement)

Christer, right after restarting bv-web to clear stuck GPU memory (and, as a side effect, losing all record of what had been running): "I would like history file of the command that has been executed, think history in pwsh or bash. I would also want a logfile of all the output."

Current state: `JobRunner` (`web/jobs.py`) is fully in-memory - `self._jobs: dict[str, Job]` - by explicit original design (its own class docstring: "In-memory only... restart regardless of whether it's tracked here"), reasoned at the time as "a job mid-run when bv-web restarts is gone either way, since its background thread doesn't survive the restart regardless." That reasoning covers in-flight jobs correctly, but doesn't address *completed* jobs - today, once bv-web restarts, there is no way to see what commands were run previously (`Job.replicate_command`, from task #676) or what their output was (`Job.output`), even though those jobs finished cleanly before the restart.

Two related but distinct asks:
1. **Command history** - a persistent, append-only record of every `replicate_command` actually run via bv-web, with a timestamp, surviving restarts - the bv-web equivalent of a pwsh/bash history file.
2. **Output logfile** - the full `say()`/`warn()` transcript for each job, also written to disk, so a past run's output can be reviewed even after the in-memory `Job` is gone.

Natural pairing: a history file could just index into per-job log files (job id/command/timestamp -> log file path), rather than being two entirely separate mechanisms.

**Not implemented** - recorded per Christer's "More notes:" framing, not a build request yet.

Christer's own suggestion for where this should live: a folder parallel to `beyond-video` itself (a sibling directory, not inside the repo/package - e.g. `../log` next to `../beyond-video`), named `log` or similar. Would need a real default-path story matching how `default_config_dir()`/archive paths already work across his split NAS(Docker)+PC(native) setup - a sibling-of-the-repo path makes sense for a native install but needs an explicit Docker volume mount (same pattern as `/data/archive`, `/data/trips`) to mean anything inside a container, plus probably an env-var override for the same reasons `BEYOND_VIDEO_USERS_FILE`/`default_config_dir()` got one.

**Revised, after discussion:** a repo-parallel folder ties the location to wherever the git checkout happens to sit - fragile if the repo moves or is checked out twice. Better precedent: `default_config_dir()` already established `~/.config/beyond-video` as beyond-video's own app-data home, with `BEYOND_VIDEO_CONFIG_DIR` as an existing Docker-friendly override - reusing that convention needs zero new infrastructure. Christer's follow-up preference, though: the name `.config` reads oddly holding non-config data, and he'd rather logs live somewhere visible by default (not a dotfolder you have to un-hide to browse to).

**Settled on:**
- Logs/history: `~/beyond-video-data/logs/` (not dot-prefixed, easy to just browse to).
- **Also decided: relocate the existing config default from `~/.config/beyond-video/` to `~/beyond-video-data/.config/`** - i.e. one shared non-hidden top-level home (`~/beyond-video-data/`) with `.config` and `logs` as subfolders under it, instead of scattering app state across a dotfolder in $HOME plus (previously) a sibling-of-the-repo folder.

**Real migration implication, not yet resolved:** Christer already has live camera configs under the *current* default (`~/.config/beyond-video/*.cfg` on his PC) - `resolve_archive_path()`/every `bv-*` command depends on `default_config_dir()` finding them. Moving the default without a migration step would silently break every existing command for him (configs "missing" at the new default path) until he manually copies the files over, or a migration/fallback (check the new path first, fall back to the old one with a one-time warning, or auto-move on first run) gets built alongside the path change. Needs to be part of the implementation, not an afterthought.

**Still not implemented** - Christer explicitly asked not to touch/restart anything while his current bv-scribe run (892 recordings) is in progress. Build this once that run is done.

**Migration approach settled:** auto-move, not a permanent dual-path fallback. On first call to `default_config_dir()` under the new default: if the new location (`~/beyond-video-data/.config`) doesn't exist yet AND the old one (`~/.config/beyond-video`) does, rename the old folder to the new path (same home-directory tree, so a plain `Path.rename()` - no cross-device copy needed) and print a one-line notice so it's not a silent surprise. If the new location already exists, just use it. If neither exists, create the new one fresh (normal new-install case). No indefinite fallback-checking of the old path needed once the one-time move has happened - simpler than maintaining both paths forever.

**Log rotation:** the output-logfile half of this (per-job or running transcript logs under `~/beyond-video-data/logs/`) should rotate with compression rather than growing forever - standard pattern: Python's stdlib `logging.handlers.TimedRotatingFileHandler` (or `RotatingFileHandler` if sized-based is preferred over time-based) with rotated/old files gzipped, similar to how `logrotate` behaves on Linux (rotate on a schedule or size cap, keep N backups, compress everything but the currently-active file). Exact policy (daily vs. weekly vs. size-triggered, how many backups to keep) still open - reasonable stdlib default to start with, no new dependency needed.

**Who owns rotation - settled:** the job print function itself (i.e. whatever backs `say()`/`warn()`/the job's output-writing path), via stdlib `RotatingFileHandler`/`TimedRotatingFileHandler` - not external OS-level scheduling (cron/logrotate on the NAS, Task Scheduler on the PC). Reasoning: beyond-video runs both natively on Christer's PC and in Docker on the NAS, so an external-scheduling approach would mean building and maintaining two different platform-specific setups outside the app itself, undocumented/untested here, plus logrotate-style external rotation of a file a process is actively writing to normally needs a reopen-signal or copytruncate dance to avoid writing into a moved/renamed file - real coordination overhead for no benefit over just letting Python's own handler do it. Self-rotating in-process is cross-platform, zero new dependency, ships working with no separate setup step on either machine.

**Cadence - settled: monthly, not weekly.** bv-web usage here is sporadic manual job runs (bv-generate/export/scribe/search/etc. triggered by hand), not a high-traffic always-on service - weekly rotation would produce a lot of near-empty files. Monthly keeps the file count low, still bounds growth, and is easy to navigate by eye ("July log", "August log") when looking back for something. `TimedRotatingFileHandler(when="...")` doesn't have a native "monthly" unit (its largest built-in is `"W0"`-`"W6"` weekly) - monthly would need either `when="midnight"` with a custom rollover check for month-boundary, or a small subclass/cron-like day-of-month check. Worth remembering when implementing - not a plain one-line `when=` value like weekly would have been.

**Scope - settled: direct CLI calls too, not just bv-web jobs.** Christer confirmed the history/logfile feature should cover a command typed straight into pwsh (`bv-scribe Kirby_2019 ...`), not only runs triggered through bv-web's job forms. This answers the open question the `bv-history` note below raised. Real implication: `JobRunner` alone isn't a sufficient hook point anymore, since a direct CLI invocation never goes through it - the write-history/write-log call needs to sit somewhere both paths pass through. Natural candidate given the existing refactor pattern: every `bv-*` CLI already takes injectable `say`/`warn` callbacks (bv-web's `JobRunner` supplies its own; a direct terminal run falls back to plain `print()`-based ones) - hooking history/log recording into that shared say/warn-construction layer, or into each CLI's common `main()` entrypoint, would cover both invocation paths with one mechanism instead of two.

## Note: let bv-web viewers run bv-search (future improvement)

**Implemented - see "Let bv-web viewers run bv-search" further below.** Left in place for the design-discussion/reasoning trail (option (a) below is the one that shipped).

Christer wants bv-web's "viewer" role to have access to bv-search, not just "owner". Checked `app.py`: bv-search's routes (`GET`/`POST /jobs/bv-search`, plus the job-detail route it shares with every other job type) are currently gated behind `Depends(require_owner)` exactly like bv-generate/bv-export/bv-download/bv-scribe/bv-config/bv-gps/bv-ls - there's no partial-access tier today, `users.py`'s `ROLES = ("owner", "viewer")` is a strict two-way split (owner: full read/write incl. download/generate/export; viewer: read-only browsing).

bv-search is a read-only query over already-generated scene/OCR/transcript text plus GPS - it doesn't create, modify, or consume GPU/CPU the way the other job types do, so treating it like the others is arguably too strict. Two implementation shapes to weigh when this gets built: (a) a one-off carve-out - add a `require_viewer_or_owner` (or similar) dependency and apply it only to the bv-search routes, leaving every other job route on `require_owner` unchanged; (b) something more general, e.g. a per-job-type permission table, if more "read-only" job types show up later. (a) is the smaller change and matches the current codebase's very literal, explicit-per-route style (`require_owner` is already applied route-by-route, not blanket-mounted).

Not implemented - noted only, per Christer's "don't touch bv-web while my run is going" constraint.

## Note: bv-history command (future improvement)

**Implemented - see "Add bv-history command (CLI + bv-web)" further below.** Left in place for the design-discussion history/reasoning trail.

Christer originally wanted a `bv-history` command explicitly CLI-only, not surfaced in bv-web.

**Reversed:** asked whether there was a good reason to wire it into bv-web anyway. The one that landed: checking history from a phone/other machine with no terminal access is the whole point of bv-web existing, and CLI-only would block that. Weighed against it: bv-web already covers *some* of the same need via each job's replicate-able command line on its detail page (task #676) and the separate tail-view idea (task #687) for "what's running now" - so a bv-web bv-history page isn't purely additive, but "check what I ran while away from my PC" is a real, distinct use case those two don't cover (they're both about currently-tracked/in-memory jobs, not the persistent cross-restart history this feature is for). Christer agreed: wire it into bv-web too, not CLI-only. Likely shape: a read-only browse/filter page (own role-gating decision needed - probably owner-only like every other job/admin surface) sitting on top of the same shared history store the CLI `bv-history` reads, rather than two separate mechanisms. Read as a companion to the persistent command-history feature already noted above (tasks: persistent command-history file for bv-web jobs / persistent logfile of bv-web job output) - this would be the command that reads and displays that history, the way `history` works in pwsh/bash. Depends on the history file actually existing first (still just a design discussion - see the `~/beyond-video-data/` notes above), so this is a follow-on command, not a separate independent feature.

**Settled:** covers both bv-web-triggered and direct-CLI runs - see the "Scope - settled" note above. So `bv-history` should show the combined record of everything, regardless of which path started it.

**Design ideas discussed, some confirmed:** offered several shapes - default most-recent-first listing (timestamp, full command line incl. options, duration, source, status); `bv-history show <id>` to dump a past run's full logged output; a replicate/copy-command action (reusing `Job.replicate_command`, task #676); filtering by `--command`, `--camera`, `--since`/`--until` (reusing the existing `LexicalTimeParser`), `--failed-only`; `--limit N`; text search over past command lines/output. Explicitly proposed *not* building live-tail into `bv-history` - that's the separate quick-tail-view idea (task #687), and a direct CLI run's own terminal already shows its live output.

Christer confirmed the core motivating use case: **"find all the bv-ls i have done and the options"** - i.e. filter by command name (`--command bv-ls`) and see the exact flags/arguments used on each past invocation, not just that it ran. This means the history record must capture the *full* command line per entry (matches the "full command line" field already in the default-listing idea above - now confirmed essential, not just a nice-to-have). Timestamp + duration per entry confirmed as good defaults.

**Ordering - corrected:** I initially said most-recent-first, reasoning from `git log`/`journalctl` precedent - Christer pushed back, correctly: bash and pwsh `history` actually list **ascending** (oldest first, most recent at the bottom near the prompt), and `history 20` shows the last 20 entries while keeping that same chronological order. That's the better default here too - matches the tool `bv-history` is explicitly modeled after. So: ascending order by default, with a `--last N` (or bare count arg, mirroring bash's own `history 20` syntax) to limit to the most recent N entries, still shown oldest-to-newest within that slice.

**Default limit - "I am more like a tail guy":** Christer wants tail-style behavior by default, not just as an opt-in flag - i.e. `bv-history` with no args should already show only the most recent N entries (ascending order, truncated to the end), the same way plain `tail` defaults to the last 10 lines without needing `-n` typed every time. `--last N`/count-arg then overrides that default count rather than being required to get a limited view at all. Exact default N still open (bash's own `history` default is unbounded/config-driven, but a tail-like default of ~10-20 fits Christer's stated preference better).

Not implemented - noted only.

## Note: quick "tail" view for a running bv-web job (future improvement)

**Implemented - see "Quick tail view for running bv-web jobs" further below.** Went with option (a) from the discussion below (a lighter render of the existing job-detail page); (b), the separate jobs-overview page, is still not built. Left in place for the design-discussion/reasoning trail.

Christer wants a button (or similar) to peek at the tail end of a running job's output without the current full-page experience. Checked `job_detail.html`: today a running job's output is the *entire* captured output so far, auto-refreshing on a meta-refresh timer (with a "pause" state once the page is left idle) - there's no separate lightweight/tail-only view, and no jobs-overview/index page exists at all (each job type only has its own "new job" form; after submitting you're redirected straight to that one job's `/jobs/{job.id}` detail page). So there's currently no place to glance at "what's my job doing right now" without navigating to and loading that job's full detail page.

Worth deciding, when this gets built: whether "tail" means (a) a smaller/lighter endpoint on the existing job-detail page that only returns the last N lines (helps on very long-running jobs like a 900-recording bv-scribe batch, where the full output list is now huge and the whole page reloads on every auto-refresh tick), or (b) a genuinely separate quick-peek surface, e.g. a small tail widget reachable from the nav bar showing whatever job(s) are currently running, without a full page navigation at all. (a) is the smaller change and fixes a real, already-visible pain point (long job pages getting heavier every refresh); (b) is more ambitious and implies also building the jobs-overview page that doesn't exist yet.

Not implemented - noted only.

## Migrate default_config_dir() to ~/beyond-video-data/.config

First implemented piece of the beyond-video-data/ restructure discussed above, now that Christer's bv-scribe run finished and he gave the go-ahead ("do your thing, 1 step at a time"). `core/camera_config.py`'s `default_config_dir()` (no-override fallback) moved from `~/.config/beyond-video` to `~/beyond-video-data/.config`, matching the "settled" decision above.

One-time auto-migration, not a permanent dual-path fallback (also matches the earlier decision): if the new location doesn't exist yet but the old one does, `Path.rename()` moves the whole folder in one shot (same home-directory tree, no cross-device copy) and a one-line notice prints to stderr. If the rename itself fails (permissions, concurrent access), falls back to returning the old location rather than losing every camera config - not fatal, just retried on the next invocation. `BEYOND_VIDEO_CONFIG_DIR` env override is checked first, unchanged - Docker deployments (which always set it) never even reach the fallback/migration logic.

`web/users.py`'s `default_users_path()` (bv-web's accounts file) was hardcoding its own independent copy of the exact same `~/.config/beyond-video` fallback directory - found while implementing this, not something Christer explicitly asked about. Fixed by having it call `camera_config.default_config_dir()` directly instead of re-deriving the path by hand, so the one migration covers both camera configs and `web-users.cfg` for free (whichever runs first triggers the move). Confirmed this is safe for the Docker deployment: `docker-compose.yml` sets `BEYOND_VIDEO_CONFIG_DIR` and `BEYOND_VIDEO_USERS_FILE` to two *different* mounted paths on purpose (`/data/camera-config` vs `/data/config/web-users.cfg`) - each function's own env-var check still wins before this shared fallback is ever reached, so nothing there changes.

Updated: `docs/man/bv-config.md` (`--config-dir` default), `docs/DEPLOY.md` (accurate fallback path in the adduser section), `docs/WEB_ARCHITECTURE.md` (added a superseded-note after the original `default_config_dir()`-in-a-container writeup rather than rewriting it), `docker-compose.yml`'s own `BEYOND_VIDEO_USERS_FILE` comment.

Tests: `test_camera_config.py` and `test_users.py`'s existing env-var/fallback tests updated to monkeypatch `Path.home()` to a `tmp_path` (previously compared against the *real* home directory with zero filesystem side effects - now that the function touches disk, letting those tests run against the real machine would have been dangerous). Added new tests for: fresh install (new path returned, never auto-created), migration (old renamed into new, content preserved), both-exist (prefers new, leaves old alone), and the printed notice. `default_users_path()` got its own test confirming it shares the migration through `default_config_dir()`. All manually verified in the sandbox (no pytest available) via a standalone script exercising all four scenarios plus the env-override case - see commit for the script's assertions.

## Add ~/beyond-video-data/logs/ + rotating job output logfile

Second piece of the beyond-video-data/ restructure, per the earlier-settled design (monthly cadence, in-process ownership via a custom handler, gzip compression, direct-CLI calls covered too - see the notes above).

`core/camera_config.py` gained `default_logs_dir()`, a sibling of `default_config_dir()` with the same override-then-fallback shape: `BEYOND_VIDEO_LOGS_DIR` env var if set, otherwise `~/beyond-video-data/logs`. No migration needed here (unlike `default_config_dir()`) since persistent logging is a brand-new feature, not a relocated one.

New module `core/joblog.py`: `MonthlyRotatingFileHandler(logging.Handler)` writes to one active `beyond-video-YYYY-MM.log` file, comparing the current year-month against the currently-open file's own year-month on every `emit()` rather than fighting `TimedRotatingFileHandler`'s seconds-based rollover math (no native monthly unit exists there). On a month change it closes the old file, gzips it (`gzip.open` + `shutil.copyfileobj`, best-effort - a compression failure never breaks logging itself), prunes anything beyond `DEFAULT_BACKUP_MONTHS = 12`, and opens the new month's file. A process-wide singleton (`get_logger()`, guarded by a `threading.Lock` since bv-web's job runner writes from multiple background threads) backs `log_line(source, message)` - the one shared write path both invocation styles funnel through, never raising even if logging itself fails (disk full, permissions).

Two call sites feed it, matching the "direct CLI calls too, not just bv-web jobs" scope decision:
- Every one of the 8 `bv-*.py` CLIs' own `main()` now builds `say`/`warn` via `wrap_say(prog)`/`wrap_warn(prog, ...)` (`core/joblog.py`) before calling `_run()`, instead of relying on `_run()`'s own unwrapped `print`/stderr defaults. Each wrapper calls the original `say`/`warn` unchanged (purely additive, no behavior/formatting change to real terminal output) and mirrors the same line into `log_line()`. `bv-config`'s `ask` (the wizard's interactive `input()` prompts) is deliberately left unwrapped - only what gets printed is logged, not raw keystrokes.
- `web/jobs.py`'s `Job.append_output()` - the single function every `start_bv_*()` job-runner method already funnels all output through via `say = job.append_output` - now also calls `log_line()` after appending to the in-memory `Job.output` list. `prog` is recovered from `self.command.split(maxsplit=1)[0]` (every `start_bv_*()` sets `command=f"bv-... {...}"`, so this always yields the right CLI name) rather than threading a dedicated field through all eight methods just for this.

Docker: `docker-compose.yml`'s `bv-web` and `bv-cli` services both gained `BEYOND_VIDEO_LOGS_DIR=/data/logs` and a `./data/logs:/data/logs` mount pointing at the same host folder, mirroring how `BEYOND_VIDEO_CONFIG_DIR` already unifies camera configs across both containers - without this, a `bv-cli` container's transcript would vanish the instant its `docker-compose run --rm` container exits.

Tests: `tests/conftest.py` (new - the project's first) adds an autouse fixture isolating `BEYOND_VIDEO_LOGS_DIR` to a per-test `tmp_path` and resetting `joblog._logger`'s module-level singleton before/after every test in the whole suite - without it, the many `test_jobs.py` tests that spawn and run a real job would have started writing real log lines onto whatever machine runs the tests the moment `Job.append_output()` gained this call. `tests/blackvue/core/test_joblog.py` (new) covers the handler directly (file-per-month naming, directory auto-creation, rotation + gzip + content preservation, backup pruning with and without a cap, swallowed emit failures) and `get_logger()`/`log_line()`/`wrap_say()`/`wrap_warn()`. `test_camera_config.py` gained the same three-test pattern (`env var override` / `falls back to home when unset` / `falls back to home when empty`) `default_config_dir()` already had, for `default_logs_dir()`. `test_jobs.py` gained one integration test confirming `Job.append_output()` persists into the same logfile direct-CLI runs write to. All manually verified in the sandbox (no pytest available): a standalone harness ran every new test function with a small monkeypatch/tmp_path shim (12/12 `test_joblog.py` tests passed once an early harness bug in undoing `monkeypatch.setattr` was fixed - not a bug in the tests themselves), plus a direct end-to-end script confirming a `wrap_say()` call and a `Job.append_output()` call both land correctly tagged in the same `beyond-video-YYYY-MM.log` file. `ast.parse()` confirmed clean on all 12 touched/new source files.

Docs: `docs/WEB_ARCHITECTURE.md` gained a "Persistent output log" paragraph in the Job runner section; `docs/DEPLOY.md`'s step 3 folder list and explanation gained `data/logs`.

## Add persistent command-history file for bv-web + direct-CLI runs

Third piece of the `beyond-video-data/` restructure - the "history file of the command that has been executed, think history in pwsh or bash" half of Christer's original ask (the output-logfile half shipped above). This only *writes* the history; the `bv-history` command that *reads* it back is still a separate not-yet-built follow-on (see that note above).

New module `core/history.py`: a frozen `HistoryEntry` dataclass (`command`, `command_line`, `source`, `username`, `started_at`, `duration_seconds`, `status`) and `record(entry)`, which appends one JSON Lines record to `history.jsonl` - a sibling of `core/joblog.py`'s own rotating output logs, in the same `default_logs_dir()` (no new env var needed). JSON Lines (one complete, independently-parseable JSON object per line, append-only) chosen for the same crash-safety reason `core/joblog.py`'s design already leans on: a process killed mid-write can corrupt at most the last in-flight line, never anything written before it. `record()` never raises - a history-write failure should never break the command it's recording, matching `log_line()`'s own contract. `quote_for_display()`/`command_line_from_argv()` rebuild a paste-able command line from a prog name and argv, deliberately a separate copy of `web/jobs.py`'s own `_quote_for_replicate()` rather than a cross-import (`core/` shouldn't depend on `web/`).

Two call sites feed it, matching the "direct CLI calls too" scope decision - but via a cleaner hook than `core/joblog.py`'s per-file `wrap_say()`/`wrap_warn()` refactor needed:
- `cli/errors.py`'s `run_cli(prog, main, *, argv=None)` - the one wrapper every `bv-*` CLI's `main()` already calls as its final step - now records one entry in a `finally` block, so it fires exactly once regardless of whether the command succeeded, failed, hit `KeyboardInterrupt`, or raised something else entirely (SystemExit included, since `finally` runs before propagation). Only a one-line `argv=argv` addition was needed in each of the 8 primary `bv-*.py` CLIs' own `run_cli(...)` call, rather than a full refactor - `run_cli()` falls back to `sys.argv[1:]` when `argv` isn't passed, so `bv-web`/`bv-lang`/`bv-live` (not part of this feature's original scope) get accurate history for free without being touched at all.
- `web/jobs.py`'s `JobRunner._spawn()` - restructured its background thread's `target()` with an outer `try/finally` calling a new `_record_job_history(job)` helper, so a job's history entry is recorded exactly once whether it succeeds, fails, is cancelled, or hits an unhandled exception. `command_line` prefers `job.replicate_command` (the real paste-able command, task #676) and falls back to the bare `job.command` when a job type doesn't set one.

Tests: `tests/blackvue/core/test_history.py` (new, 12 tests) covers `record()`'s JSON-line format/append order/directory auto-creation/never-raises contract, and both quoting helpers. `tests/blackvue/cli/test_errors.py` gained 6 tests confirming `run_cli()` records succeeded/failed/interrupted/OS-error/unhandled-exception entries correctly, plus the `sys.argv` fallback. `tests/blackvue/web/test_jobs.py` gained 2 tests confirming `JobRunner._spawn()` records both a succeeded and a failed entry with the right `source`/`username`/`command_line`. All manually verified in the sandbox (no pytest available) via the same monkeypatch/tmp_path harness used for the output-logfile feature above - 99/99 across `test_history.py` + `test_errors.py` + `test_jobs.py` combined, run 4 times back-to-back with no flakes, plus a full pass of every touched `bv-*` CLI's own existing test suite (367 passed; the only 7 failures are a pre-existing sandbox limitation - the local `tomllib` stub used for this Python version doesn't implement real TOML parsing - unrelated to this change and present before it too). `ast.parse()` confirmed clean on all touched/new source files.

One genuine race surfaced and got fixed along the way, not just a test artifact: the new `test_jobs.py` tests originally polled `history.history_path().exists()` before reading the file back, but `open(path, "a")` creates the file on disk *before* `write()` lands - under load (the full suite spawning many background job threads at once) the poll could observe that brief empty-file window and fail a JSON-decode. Fixed by polling for non-empty content instead of mere existence.

Docs: none needed yet beyond the `history.py` module's own docstring - `docs/WEB_ARCHITECTURE.md`/`docs/CLI.md` will get a proper mention once `bv-history` (the command that actually surfaces this data) exists.

## Add bv-history command (CLI + bv-web)

Fourth piece of the `beyond-video-data/` restructure - the read side of the history file written above. `bv-history` (direct CLI) and bv-web's own `/history` + `/history/{number}` pages both browse the same `history.jsonl`, the way pwsh/bash's own `history` browses shell history - matching the "Settled" scope note above (combined record of bv-web-triggered and direct-CLI runs, one command reads both).

Two read-side additions to existing write-only modules, kept as additions rather than new duplicate modules: `core/history.py` gained `read_entries(path=None)` (JSON-Lines parse back into `HistoryEntry`s, oldest first, silently skipping a line that fails to parse rather than raising - one bad line can't take down an otherwise-fine history file); `core/joblog.py` gained a `LogLine` dataclass + `read_lines(since=, until=, source=)` (parses `beyond-video-YYYY-MM.log(.gz)` lines back via a regex on the `asctime [source] message` shape `log_line()` writes, treating an unmatched line as a continuation of the previous one rather than dropping it - handles a logged message with an embedded newline). Both modules' docstrings previously said "this module only writes" - updated now that they also read.

New top-level module `blackvue/history.py` (mirrors the existing `blackvue/search.py` precedent - shared filtering/formatting logic used by both the CLI and the web route, not duplicated between them): `NumberedEntry`/`HistoryFilter` dataclasses, `all_entries()`, `filtered_entries()`, `tail()`, `matching_log_lines()`. Entries are numbered by absolute 1-based position in the full, unfiltered, oldest-first history - the same convention bash/pwsh's own `history` uses, confirmed against Christer's own earlier "ordering - corrected" note above: a filtered view still shows each match's real original number, not a 1..N renumbering of the subset. Default listing is tail-style (`DEFAULT_TAIL_COUNT = 15`, `--all` to disable), matching the "I am more like a tail guy" note above. `--since`/`--until` reuse the existing `LexicalTimeParser` for parsing, but deliberately don't use its `TimeInterval.__contains__` - that method strips a trailing `_suffix` (built for recording-id tags like `_E`/`_P`) which would wrongly truncate a `YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS` timestamp down to date-only precision. `filtered_entries()` instead compares directly against `interval.first`/`interval.last` as strings. `matching_log_lines()` bridges a genuine timezone mismatch: `HistoryEntry.started_at` is UTC-aware ISO-8601, but `core/joblog.py`'s log lines use Python logging's naive-local-time `asctime` - converted via `.astimezone().replace(tzinfo=None)` before comparing, then matched by the entry's own command name as source tag within `[started - 2s, started + duration + 2s]`. Two documented limitations, both inherent to best-effort reconstruction rather than bugs: a rotated/pruned month has nothing left to show, and two concurrent runs of the *same* command share the same tag and can't be told apart.

New CLI `cli/bv_history.py`, registered as `bv-history` in `pyproject.toml`. Manually dispatches on `raw_argv[0] == "show"` before any argparse parsing (rather than argparse subparsers), because a bare `bv-history` with no subcommand needs to fall through to the default tail listing the same way bare `history` does in bash - subparsers and a bare-default positional don't coexist cleanly in argparse. `bv-history` lists with `--last N`/`--all`/`--command`/`--camera`/`--from`/`--until`/`--timestamp`/`--failed-only`/`--search`/`--source`; `bv-history show ID` dumps one entry plus its best-effort reconstructed output via `matching_log_lines()`. Goes through the same `run_cli()` every other CLI uses, so `bv-history` gets its own history entry recorded for free - confirmed by a test asserting exactly that.

bv-web: `GET /history` and `GET /history/{number}` added to `app.py`, both gated by the existing `require_owner` dependency (same as every other job/admin route - no partial-access tier exists yet, matching the still-open "let bv-web viewers run bv-search" note above, which this doesn't change). The routes call straight into `blackvue.history`'s functions rather than re-implementing filtering in the web layer. New templates `history_list.html` (filter form + numbered table, links each row to the detail page, shows a truncation hint when tail-limited) and `history_detail.html` (entry fields + logged-output block, or an empty-state message when nothing was found). `base.html` gained a "History" nav tab alongside the other owner-only job tabs.

Docs: `docs/man/bv-history.md` (new, follows the existing `bv-search.md` template); `docs/CLI.md` gained a short note that `bv-history` doesn't fit the recording-selection model the rest of the page documents; `docs/WEB_ARCHITECTURE.md`'s Job runner section - the paragraph that previously called `bv-history` "a separate, not-yet-built piece" now describes what it actually writes/reads, and a new paragraph documents the `/history` routes and the `blackvue/history.py` functions they share with the CLI.

Tests: `test_history.py` (core) gained 4 tests for `read_entries()` (missing file, oldest-first order, malformed-line skipping, explicit-path override independent of `history_path()`'s own env resolution). `test_joblog.py` gained 7 tests for `read_lines()` (missing dir, round-trip parse, source filter, since/until filter, continuation-line handling, reading a gzipped older month, chronological-not-lexical month ordering). New `tests/blackvue/test_history.py` (~17 tests) covers `all_entries()` numbering, every `filtered_entries()` filter individually and combined, `tail()`, and `matching_log_lines()`. New `tests/blackvue/cli/test_bv_history.py` (~14 tests) covers argument parsing, the empty-history message, numbered listing, default-tail truncation + note, `--all`, individual filters, a bad `--from` timestamp producing a clean error rather than a traceback, `show` on an unknown id, `show` with and without reconstructed output, and `main()`'s own invocation being recorded. All manually verified via the same sandbox harness used throughout this restructure (no pytest available) - 63 new tests passing.

bv-web verification took a different path than usual: `fastapi` isn't installable in this sandbox either (same proxy failure as `pytest`), so the new routes couldn't run through a `TestClient`. `jinja2` (3.0.3) is available though, so `history_list.html`/`history_detail.html` were verified by rendering them directly through a bare `jinja2.Environment` against hand-built fake `Request`/`User`/`NumberedEntry`/`LogLine` objects (including registering the `capitalize_first` filter and a `.cookies = {}` dict on the fake request - both things `base.html` needs that are normally supplied by `app.py`/Starlette) - covering populated-list, error-message, empty-list, output-found, and no-output-found paths. Matches the project's own established pattern for verifying bv-web changes without a live test client.

`ast.parse()` confirmed clean on all touched/new Python files.

## Add start/finished/duration reporting to bv-generate + bv-scribe

Fifth piece of this work stream - extends the `bv-search: started HH:MM:SS` / `bv-search: finished HH:MM:SS (N.Ns)` pattern (task #643) to bv-generate and bv-scribe, the two other long-running batch commands with no timing output at all. Directly resolves the "add timing/duration log to bv-scribe web jobs" and "add start/finished/duration reporting to bv-generate + bv-scribe" notes above - Christer's 902-recording bv-scribe run (half a day+) had no way to answer "how long did that take" short of checking `.scene.txt` file timestamps by hand.

Both CLIs now print `<prog>: started HH:MM:SS` up front and, wrapped in try/finally so every exit path hits it (argument errors, an empty selection, an unhandled per-recording exception), `<prog>: finished HH:MM:SS (N.Ns)` - same always-on, no-toggle-flag design bv-search already uses, and the same placement: timing wraps the interval-parse/empty-selection checks too, not just the main loop, so a bad `--timestamp` or an empty archive still gets a finished line (matches bv-search's own "started/finished lines around every exit path" test coverage).

`bv-generate`'s `_run()` timing wraps everything after archive resolution - interval parsing, the empty-recordings check, and the per-recording action loop (`--extract-audio`/`--get-duration`/`--transcribe`/`--translate`/`--describe-scene`).

`bv-scribe` needed a small split instead of a single wrap, because its existing `_run()` already dispatches to two very different code paths - `_run_raw()` for `--raw` mode (no archive, no LexicalTimeParser selection) and archive-mode selection/looping otherwise - and duplicating the timing wrapper in both would have meant keeping two copies in sync. Renamed the old `_run()` body to `_run_dispatch()` (still does exactly the raw/archive dispatch it always did) and made `_run()` itself just the started/finished wrapper calling `_run_dispatch()` - so both modes get identical timing coverage from one place.

Tests: `test_bv_generate.py` and `test_bv_scribe.py` each gained tests confirming started-before-finished ordering, that the finished line prints even when `--timestamp` is malformed (an args-error exit), and (bv-scribe only) that both `--raw` and archive mode get timing. All verified via the sandbox's manual pytest harness (no real pytest/fastapi here) - 120 passed, 2 failed, both pre-existing `tomllib`-stub gaps (real TOML parsing isn't implemented in the sandbox's minimal stub) unrelated to this change, present identically before it. `ast.parse()` confirmed clean on both touched CLI files.

Docs: `docs/man/bv-generate.md` and `docs/man/bv-scribe.md` each gained a sentence in their DESCRIPTION section documenting the started/finished lines, matching how `docs/man/bv-search.md` already documents its own.

Not yet covered by this change: bv-web's `job_detail.html` still shows no started-at timestamp or elapsed-time summary of its own outside of these printed lines now flowing into a job's captured output (and, since task #683, into `history.jsonl`'s own `duration_seconds` field per job) - a dedicated UI surface for "how long is this job taking" is still the separate, not-yet-built quick-tail-view idea (task #687).

## Let bv-web viewers run bv-search

Sixth piece of this work stream - implements option (a) from the note above: a one-off carve-out rather than a general per-job-type permission table, matching bv-web's existing very literal, explicit-per-route style (`require_owner` already applied route-by-route, not blanket-mounted).

`web/auth.py` gained `require_viewer_or_owner()`, a FastAPI dependency functionally identical to `require_login()` (ROLES is just `("owner", "viewer")` - see `users.py` - so "logged in" already means "viewer or owner") but named to document intent at each call site that uses it. `app.py`'s `GET`/`POST /jobs/bv-search` routes switched from `require_owner` to this new dependency.

The one wrinkle: `GET /jobs/{job_id}` (the job-detail/output page) is a single shared route for every job type, not just bv-search - it can't just swap its whole dependency to `require_viewer_or_owner`, or a viewer could load any job's output by guessing/reusing a job id (a download job's archive path, an export job's trip names, etc.). Kept the route open to any logged-in user, but added an explicit in-body check: `job.command.startswith("bv-search ")` - if false and the caller isn't the owner, 403 (same status/detail `require_owner` itself would have raised). `Job.command` already always starts with the literal CLI prog name (`start_bv_search()` sets it to `f"bv-search {camera_id}"`, matching every other `start_bv_*()` method's own convention) so this is a reliable check, not a guess.

`base.html`'s nav: the Search tab moved out of the `{% if user.role == "owner" %}` block (now right after "Browse archive", visible to any logged-in user) - every other job-trigger tab, plus the History tab (task #686, still owner-only - not in scope here), stayed inside it.

Verified via the same Jinja2-direct-render workaround used for prior bv-web-only changes (no fastapi in this sandbox): rendered `base.html` for both an "owner" and a "viewer" fake user and confirmed the owner sees every tab (including Search) while the viewer sees Search but none of the other job tabs or History. `ast.parse()` confirmed clean on `auth.py`/`app.py`. No route-level test suite exists for `app.py` in this sandbox (same fastapi-unavailable limitation noted throughout this restructure - see task #686's own entry), so the `job_detail` permission-check logic itself is unverified beyond manual code review; worth a real end-to-end check (or adding a fastapi-based test suite) once pytest/fastapi are available in a real environment.

Docs: `docs/WEB_ARCHITECTURE.md`'s "Job runner" section updated (the bullet listing owner-only jobs now calls out bv-search as the exception, and a new paragraph documents the `require_viewer_or_owner`/`job_detail` carve-out mechanics) - the file previously had no mention of per-route permission variation at all, every job route was described as uniformly `require_owner`-gated.

## Quick tail view for running bv-web jobs

Seventh piece of this work stream - option (a) from the note above: a lighter render of the existing `job_detail.html` page rather than a separate jobs-overview surface (that's a bigger, still-not-built change - there's still no page listing "what's currently running" across job types at all).

`app.py`'s `job_detail()` gained a `?tail=1` query param, checked alongside the existing `?paused=1`. When present on a still-running job whose output already exceeds `TAIL_LINE_COUNT` (200, a new module-level constant near `RECORDING_ID_RE`), only the last 200 lines are sliced out and passed to the template - the full `output` list from `job.snapshot()` is never touched otherwise, so nothing about a job's actual stored output changes, only what one particular page load renders. `tail=1` is silently ignored once a job reaches a terminal status (`tail_active = tail_requested and not job_status.is_finished`) - a finished job's output has stopped growing, so there's no auto-refresh cost left to save by tailing it, and showing the truncated view by leftover URL habit would just hide real content for no benefit.

`paused` and `tail` are independent toggles that can combine, so `job_detail()` builds all four link URLs (`tail_on_url`, `tail_off_url`, `pause_url`, `resume_url`) server-side and passes them as plain strings, rather than letting the template string-concatenate query params itself - flipping one toggle's link never silently drops the other one's own `?param=1`.

`job_detail.html`: the existing "Pause auto-refresh" line gained a second half - "Show only the last 200 lines" / "Showing only the last 200 lines - Show full output" depending on `tail_active` - plus a small hint line above the output block when lines are actually being hidden ("N earlier line(s) hidden - show full output"). Nothing here is JS - matches the rest of this app's deliberately JS-free, server-rendered-link pattern (the same one `?paused=1` already established).

Verified the same way as every other bv-web-only change in this restructure (no fastapi in this sandbox): rendered `job_detail.html` directly via a bare `jinja2.Environment` for three scenarios - running/untailed (full 300-line output shown, toggle link offered), running/tailed (only the last 200 of 300 lines present, "100 earlier line(s) hidden" note shown), and finished (no tail/pause toggle block at all, since that whole section is gated on `status == "running"`). `ast.parse()` confirmed clean on `app.py`.

## Surface scene/OCR text on the archive recording detail page

Eighth and final piece of this restructure work stream (task #681). Christer's own framing from the note above: after a `bv-search --text` hit against scene descriptions, there was no link from a recording to the described content itself - "the only way to read a scene description is opening the file directly on disk."

`web/archive_browser.py` gained `_SCENE_TEXTS = (("Front", Asset.SCENE_DESCRIPTION), ("Rear", Asset.SCENE_DESCRIPTION_REAR))`, the same front/rear pairing `blackvue/search.py`'s own `TEXT_SEARCH_ASSETS["scene"]` group already uses (there's no diarized equivalent for scene text the way transcript/translation have one, so unlike that dict entry this is just the two). `ArchiveRecording.scene_texts` (a new property, inserted after the existing `has_gsensor` property to match the file's established per-asset-group property convention) iterates that tuple, resolves each via `self.recording.file(asset)`, skips whichever direction isn't present, and reads the rest with `asset_file.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")` - wrapped in `try/except OSError` so a read failure (permissions, a half-written file) falls back to a bracketed `f"[could not read {asset_file.name}: {exc}]"` placeholder rather than 500ing the whole detail page, the same don't-break-the-page-over-one-sidecar posture `first_valid_gps_fix()` already established for the GPS link. Returns `list[tuple[str, str]]` - empty for the (currently most common) case where no `bv-generate --describe-scene`/`bv-scribe` run has ever touched that recording.

`archive_recording_detail.html` renders a new "Scene description" panel right after the existing "Show start location" link, one `<div class="scene-text">` block per `(label, text)` pair, wrapped in `{% if recording.scene_texts %}` so the panel is entirely absent rather than showing an empty heading when there's nothing to show. `base.html` gained matching `.scene-text`/`.scene-text-body` CSS, styled like `pre.job-output`'s own read-only text panel (same background/border/padding/max-height-with-scroll treatment) since both are "dump of a text file into a bordered box" - just `font-family: inherit` since scene descriptions are prose, not `job-output`'s monospace-friendly command transcript.

Deliberately *not* touched: `app.py`'s `archive_recording_detail` route. `scene_texts` lives on `ArchiveRecording` itself (computed on read, the same as `has_gps`/`sidecars`/every other per-asset-group property on that class), so the template reaches it via `recording.scene_texts` directly - no new context key, no route change, matching how `has_gps` already works for the "Show start location" link.

## Reuse a previous run's parameters (bv-scribe pilot)

Christer: "Another note, i would like to have a button or something like in bv-web to get the latest run parameters filled in for bv-web or maybe a list of the latest." Asked to choose between prefill-with-latest-only, pick-from-a-list-only, both, or just logging it as a note for later - he picked "Both": the form defaults to the latest run automatically, plus a list below it to pick an older run instead.

Scope: piloted on `bv-scribe`'s job-trigger form alone first, verified end-to-end, before rolling the identical pattern out to the other six commands (`bv-gps`, `bv-download`, `bv-generate`, `bv-export`, `bv-ls`, `bv-search`) as separate follow-up work. `bv-config` is excluded - it's an interactive wizard, not an ordinary field-form, so "reuse parameters" doesn't map onto it the same way.

Design chosen over the alternative (reconstructing an `argparse.Namespace` by re-parsing `Job.replicate_command`/`HistoryEntry.command_line`): capture the raw web-form field dict directly, at the point `app.py`'s own `POST /jobs/bv-scribe` route already has it, before `_clean()`/type-conversion/flag-inversion touches it. Confirmed feasible by checking FastAPI's `Form(...)` parameters use the Python parameter name as the HTML field's own `name=` attribute with no alias (grepped `job_new_bv_scribe.html`'s `name="from_"` etc. against the route's matching kwarg) - so the same dict, unmodified, is exactly what the `GET` form needs back to prefill itself.

`core/history.py`: `HistoryEntry` gained `params: dict | None = None` - `None` rather than defaulting to `{}` so "no params recorded" (a CLI entry, or an old bv-web entry from before this field existed) stays distinguishable from "recorded an empty dict". No changes needed to `record()`/`read_entries()` - both already generic enough (`asdict()`/`json.dumps()`, `HistoryEntry(**data)`) to carry a new optional field through transparently; old `history.jsonl` lines missing the key still load fine.

`web/jobs.py`: `Job` gained `params: dict = field(default_factory=dict)`. `_new_job()` gained a `params=None` keyword, passed through as `params=params or {}`. `_record_job_history()`'s `HistoryEntry(...)` call gained `params=job.params or None`. `start_bv_scribe()` gained a trailing `params: dict | None = None` keyword, threaded into its own `self._new_job(...)` call - otherwise unused by the method itself, which still runs the job from the `argv` its own typed kwargs build, not from `params`.

`web/app.py`: two new module-level helpers, `_recent_web_runs(command)` (every past bv-web run of `command` that has a `params` snapshot, newest first - filters `filtered_entries(HistoryFilter(command=..., source="bv-web"))` down to entries with `params` truthy, then reverses) and `_reuse_defaults(recent_runs, reuse_param)` (resolves the form's `defaults` dict plus which entry, if any, is "active" - `?reuse=<N>` if it names a real entry in `recent_runs`, otherwise the most recent entry, otherwise `({}, None)` when there's no history yet). `GET /jobs/bv-scribe` computes `recent_runs = _recent_web_runs("bv-scribe")[:5]` and passes `defaults`/`recent_runs`/`active_reuse_number` into the template context. `POST /jobs/bv-scribe` builds a `raw_params` dict from every raw (un-cleaned) `Form(...)` value, keyed identically to the route's own parameter names / the template's own `name=` attributes, and passes `params=raw_params` into `start_bv_scribe(...)`.

`job_new_bv_scribe.html`: every text/number `<input>` gained `value="{{ defaults.get('field_name', '') }}"`; every checkbox gained `{% if defaults.get('field_name') %}checked{% endif %}`; the `task`/`camera` `<select>` elements' `selected` logic now checks `defaults.get('task', 'both') == '<option value>'` / `defaults.get('camera', 'front') == '<option value>'` (falling back to the same hardcoded defaults the form always had when there's no history at all). A new "Reuse a previous run" panel sits above the form, shown only when `recent_runs` is non-empty, listing each entry as a link to `/jobs/bv-scribe?reuse={{ numbered.number }}` (`?reuse=<N>` mirrors the existing `?tail=1`/`?paused=1` toggle-link convention - a plain server-built URL, no JS), showing its raw `started_at` timestamp and its `command_line` as a paste-readable summary, with the currently-active entry highlighted. `base.html` gained matching `.reuse-panel`/`.reuse-list`/`.reuse-date`/`.reuse-command` CSS.

Verified: `ast.parse()` clean on `core/history.py`, `web/jobs.py`, `web/app.py`. Three Jinja2 direct-render scenarios (no fastapi in this sandbox, same workaround used throughout this restructure) confirmed the reuse panel is entirely absent with no history, shows "your most recent run" copy plus correct `value=`/`checked=`/`selected` prefills when auto-defaulting to the latest run, and shows "the run you picked below" copy plus the older entry's own values when `?reuse=<N>` names an older entry. `tests/blackvue/core/test_history.py` gained 3 new tests for `HistoryEntry.params` (defaults to `None`, round-trips through `record()`/`read_entries()`, old lines missing the key still default to `None`) - all passing via the sandbox's pytest-shim harness. `tests/blackvue/web/test_jobs.py` gained 2 new tests confirming `start_bv_scribe(params=...)` stores the dict unmodified on `Job.params`, and defaults to `{}` when not given - both passing (108 total passed, 0 failed, across `test_history.py`/`test_errors.py`/`test_jobs.py` combined). A new `tests/blackvue/web/test_app_reuse.py` covers `_recent_web_runs()`/`_reuse_defaults()` directly (newest-first ordering, excluding CLI/other-command/no-params entries, `?reuse=<N>` resolution including invalid/unknown/non-numeric fallback to latest) - kept in its own file since `web/app.py` imports fastapi (unlike `web/jobs.py`), so it can only be collected where the `web` extra is installed (CI has it; this sandbox doesn't) - logic double-checked by hand against `_recent_web_runs`/`_reuse_defaults`'s own implementation since it couldn't be executed here.

Docs: `docs/WEB_ARCHITECTURE.md` gained a new paragraph (right after the existing "Persistent command history" one, since this feature builds directly on `HistoryEntry.params`) covering the design choice, the data flow, and the pilot-then-rollout scope.

Not yet done: the same `params`/`_recent_web_runs`/`_reuse_defaults`/reuse-panel pattern for the other six job-trigger commands - separate follow-up work once this pilot's pattern is confirmed working in real use.

## Fix job-output pane not scrolling to bottom (?tail=1 looked stale)

Christer, on a running bv-scribe job: "The tail of bv-web job running... [Show only the last 30 lines](...?tail=1), should have the same size as the report window, and its still showing the first 30 rows. and it started on 50 instead of 203."

Diagnosis: `job_detail()`'s server-side `?tail=1` slicing (`output[-TAIL_LINE_COUNT:]`, task #687/its follow-up 200->30 tuning) was never actually wrong - it always sliced the real last 30 lines. The bug was purely visual: `pre.job-output` (`base.html`) is a fixed-height scrollable box (`max-height: 60vh`, ~24 visible rows before scrolling - the same measurement that justified lowering `TAIL_LINE_COUNT` from 200 to 30 in the first place) and a bare `<pre>` always starts scrolled to its own top. So even a correctly-sliced 30-line tail rendered with only its *oldest* ~24 lines visible above the fold - the newest, most-current lines (what Christer actually wanted to see) sat below an un-scrolled fold every single auto-refresh tick. "Started on 50 instead of 203" was him reading the oldest visible line in that unscrolled slice, not a real total-count/slicing bug.

Fix: `job_detail.html`'s `<pre class="job-output">` gained `id="job-output"`, plus a small inline `<script>` right after it that sets `box.scrollTop = box.scrollHeight` on load. Every job-detail page view is already a genuine full page reload (the existing `<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="2">`, same mechanism as a manual F5, not a partial DOM patch), so this scroll-to-bottom re-applies itself automatically on every 2-second auto-refresh tick with no extra "stay pinned while new lines stream in" logic needed - matches this app's existing minimal-JS-only-where-CSS-can't-do-it precedent (the replicate-command Copy button, the submarine easter egg).

Verified via a direct Jinja2 render of `job_detail.html` (no fastapi in this sandbox) with 30 fake output lines, `tail_active=True`, `tail_truncated_count=203`: confirmed `id="job-output"` and the `scrollTop = box.scrollHeight` script are both present, alongside the correct "203 earlier line(s) hidden" hint text. `ast.parse()` doesn't apply to a template file; no Python was touched by this fix.

Docs: `docs/WEB_ARCHITECTURE.md`'s `?tail=1` paragraph gained a new "pre.job-output scroll-to-bottom" paragraph right after it, documenting the root cause and fix.

## Cancelling a job in bv-web doesn't stop in-flight GPU compute

Christer, after clicking Cancel on a running bv-scribe job: "I cancelled the job, but its still running, i can see that in task manager and in the log."

Root cause, per `Job.cancel()`/`JobRunner.cancel()`'s own documented behavior (`docs/WEB_ARCHITECTURE.md`'s "Cancellation" paragraph): cancelling a job that's `waiting_for_input` is immediate - a sentinel goes onto the answer queue and the blocked `ask()` call raises `_JobCancelled` right there. But a job that's plain `running` with no open prompt has nothing to interrupt through - `cancel()` can only flip the job's own *displayed* status to `CANCELLED` in bv-web; the background daemon thread (`JobRunner._spawn()`'s `threading.Thread(..., daemon=True)`) keeps executing whatever it's actually doing until that finishes on its own. Python has no supported way to force-kill a thread from outside.

bv-scribe's specific case is worse than most: its per-recording loop (`cli/bv_scribe.py`) has no cooperative "was I cancelled?" check between recordings the way `bv-config`'s wizard is built around watching for a cancel signal between prompts. So a cancelled bv-scribe job doesn't just finish its current in-flight recording and stop - it has no way to even notice it was cancelled, and keeps running the entire remaining loop to real completion (or a crash), regardless of what bv-web's UI shows.

Also relevant: `JobRunner`'s background threads run inside the *same* Python process as the bv-web server itself (confirmed earlier this session while explaining why a server restart silently kills all running jobs) - so the only way to actually stop the compute right now is ending that whole process (Task Manager -> End Task on bv-web's `python`/`uvicorn` process), which takes bv-web itself down too, not just the one job. Restarting afterward is safe/expected, same as any other bv-web restart, since bv-scribe's `--overwrite`-gated `_should_write()` skip logic already makes it resumable.

Not yet built: a real mid-job cancellation check inside bv-scribe's loop (and likely the other long-running per-item commands) so a Cancel click can actually stop the loop cleanly after the current item finishes, without needing to kill the whole server. Christer hasn't yet said whether/when he wants this built - flagged here as a known gap, not started.

## Fix: multi-line sign reads truncated in Scene summary

Christer, pasting a real scene.txt against what the summary actually showed him: the raw file had a zoomed sign read spanning several lines - `227 DALARÖ` / `259 HUDDINGE` / `JORDBRÖ` / `500`, all one sign's OCR read - but the Scene summary panel only showed `227 DALARÖ`, silently dropping the rest.

Root cause: `zoom_into_signs()` (`generate/scene.py`) writes each bullet as `f"- [t=...] {label}: {read_text}"` with `read_text` taken verbatim from the model - a multi-row sign comes back with real embedded newlines, so the written file has continuation lines with no `"- "` prefix. `_extract_legible_sign_reads()` only ever looked at lines starting with `"- "`; every continuation line was silently skipped, not just left un-filtered.

Fixed by tracking the bullet currently being built (`current`) across lines: a line starting with `"- "` closes off and evaluates the previous bullet then starts a new one; any other non-blank line while inside the section gets appended (space-joined) onto `current` instead of being ignored; the bullet is finalized (and checked for `"not legible"`) whichever way the loop ends - hitting the next `"- "` bullet, the section's `#`/`---` terminator, or simply running out of lines.

Also flagged, not (yet) acted on: Christer's same example showed `## On-screen text` content (`327 BERGEN` / `359 JORDBRØ` / `600`, real destination signage) that never appears in the summary at all - by the original agreed scope (description + zoomed sign reads only), not a bug, but worth reconsidering since that section's content looked just as useful as the zoomed reads. No decision made yet.

Verified: added `test_scene_summary_keeps_a_multi_line_sign_read_intact` reproducing Christer's exact raw text - confirms the full multi-line read now comes through as one joined string. All 49 tests in `test_archive_browser.py` pass (156 total across the full harness run, no regressions). `ast.parse()` clean. Docs: `docs/WEB_ARCHITECTURE.md`'s scene summary paragraph gained a follow-up paragraph documenting the bug and fix.

## Note: HEVC recordings play audio-only in bv-web's video player

Christer: "For some reason i only get sound when playing the video in bv-web." Confirmed via `ffprobe` against a real file (`X:\files\2019\20190131_154520_NF.mp4`): `codec_name=hevc`, 3840x2160 - genuine 4K H.265 video. Root cause isn't a bv-web bug: the browser's `<video>` element can decode the AAC audio track fine but can't decode HEVC, so it shows a black/frozen frame while audio keeps playing. Chrome doesn't support HEVC playback regardless of OS codec packs; Edge can if the (free) "HEVC Video Extensions from Device Manufacturer" Microsoft Store package is installed; Safari supports it natively. Christer, on why this footage is HEVC at all: "The camera was new and i tested stuff like hevc, i thought it would create smaller files, but it didnt" - an early config experiment, not representative of his archive going forward.

Real fix, not yet started: bv-web could transcode (and cache) a browser-compatible H.264 preview for HEVC source files instead of serving the raw file directly for playback - Christer's GPU already does NVENC (established earlier this project, see the encode/stitch work), so this wouldn't be a slow CPU-bound transcode. Immediate workaround given instead: install the Edge HEVC extension, or just be aware only Safari/HEVC-capable browsers will show picture on this specific batch of test recordings.
